Jethro, priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard of everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Moses' wife Zipporah, whom Moses had sent back,
and her two sons. The first was named Gershom, for Moses had said, "I have been a foreign resident in a foreign land."
The second was named Eliezer, for he had said, "The God of my father was my help. He rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' sons and wife to him in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
He had sent word to Moses: "It is I, your father-in-law Jethro, coming to you with your wife and her two sons."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed low and kissed him, and each asked after the other's well-being. Then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship they had met on the way, and how the LORD had rescued them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the Egyptians' power.
Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the power of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who rescued this people from beneath the Egyptians' hand.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for in the very matter where they acted arrogantly against the people, he was above them."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to share a meal with Moses' father-in-law in God's presence.
The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around him from morning until evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, with all the people standing around you from morning until evening?"
Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to enquire of God.
When they have a dispute, it comes before me, and I decide between one person and another, and I make known God's rulings and teachings."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not right.
You will certainly wear yourself out, and these people with you. The task is too heavy for you. You cannot carry it alone.
Now listen to me. I will give you advice, and may God be with you. You yourself must stand for the people before God and bring their cases to him.
Instruct them in the rulings and teachings, and show them the road they are to take and the things they are to do.

But you yourself should look out among all the people for capable men who fear God, men of integrity who despise dishonest profit, and appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
Let them judge the people at all times. Any major case they bring to you, but every minor case they decide themselves. Make it lighter for yourself, and let them share the load with you.
If you do this, and God so directs you, you will be able to stand the strain, and all these people too will go home content."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people: leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
They judged the people at all times. The hard cases they brought to Moses, and the minor cases they decided themselves.
Then Moses saw his father-in-law off, and he went back to his own country.
In the third month after the Israelites had gone out from Egypt, on that very day, they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from Rephidim and entered the wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there, facing the mountain.
Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob, and tell to the Israelites:
'You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Now, if you will really listen to my voice and keep my covenant, then out of all the peoples you will be my own treasured possession. All the earth is mine,
but you will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites."
Moses came and called the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD had commanded him.
All the people answered together, "Everything the LORD has said we will do." Moses took the people's answer back to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, "I am coming to you in the thick of a cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you and will trust you for ever." Moses reported the people's words to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They are to wash their clothes
and be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
Mark out a boundary for the people all round, and say: 'Take care not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Anyone who touches the mountain will be put to death.
No hand is to touch him. He is to be stoned or shot, whether animal or person. He must not live.' When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain."
Moses went down from the mountain to the people. He consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.
He said to the people, "Be ready for the third day. Do not go near a woman."
On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and a very loud blast of a ram's horn. All the people in the camp trembled.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had come down on it in fire. Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain shook violently.
The sound of the horn grew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to the LORD to look, or many of them will perish.
Even the priests who come near to the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, because you warned us, saying, 'Set a boundary around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
The LORD said to him, "Go down, and come up again with Aaron. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and told them.
God spoke all these words:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You will have no other gods in my presence.
You will not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.
You will not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, bringing the guilt of parents on their children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
and showing faithful love to the thousandth generation of those who love me and keep my commands.
You will not use the name of the LORD your God for a worthless purpose, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who uses his name in that way.
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
For six days you are to labour and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath for the LORD your God. On it you will do no work, neither you, nor your son or your daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your livestock, nor the foreigner who lives within your gates.
For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, and on the seventh day he rested. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Honour your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You will not murder.
You will not commit adultery.
You will not steal.
You will not give false evidence against your neighbour.
You will not covet your neighbour's house. You will not covet your neighbour's wife, or his male or female servant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbour."
All the people saw the thunder and the lightning, and heard the horn, and saw the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they trembled and stood at a distance.
They said to Moses, "You speak to us, and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that the fear of him will be with you and you will not sin."
The people stood at a distance, while Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.
The LORD said to Moses, "This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from heaven.
You will not make gods of silver or gods of gold alongside me. You are not to make them for yourselves.

You are to make an altar of earth for me, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make an altar of stone for me, you are not to build it of cut stones, for if you use a chisel on it, you profane it.
You are not to go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness is not exposed on it.'
These are the rulings you are to set before them:
When you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years, and in the seventh he is to go out free, owing nothing.
If he came in single, he is to go out single. If he came in as the husband of a wife, his wife is to go out with him.
If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children belong to her master, and he is to go out alone.
But if the slave declares, "I love my master, my wife and my children. I do not want to go free,"
then his master is to bring him before God. He is to bring him to the door or the doorpost, and his master is to pierce his ear with an awl, and he will be his slave for life.
When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she is not to go out as the male slaves do.
If she displeases the master who had designated her for himself, he is to let her be bought back. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt unfairly with her.
If he designates her for his son, he is to deal with her as with a daughter.
If he takes another wife for himself, he is not to reduce the first one's food, her clothing or her marital rights.
If he does not do these three things for her, she is to go out without payment, without any money.
Whoever strikes a person and the person dies is to be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait for him, and God let it happen into his hand, I will appoint a place for you to which he may flee.
But if someone acts with premeditation against his neighbour and kills him by cunning, you are to take him even from my altar, to be put to death.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother is to be put to death.
Whoever kidnaps a person and sells him, or is found with him in his possession, is to be put to death.
Whoever curses his father or his mother is to be put to death.
When people quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with a fist, and he does not die but takes to his bed,
if he gets up and walks about outside on his staff, then the one who struck him is cleared. He is only to pay for his loss of time, and to have him thoroughly healed.
When a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, he is to be avenged.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be avenged, for the slave is his money.

When people fight and strike a pregnant woman so that her children come out, but there is no further harm, the one who struck her is to be fined as the woman's husband demands, and he is to pay as the judges decide.
But if there is harm, then you are to give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
When a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he is to let the slave go free in compensation for the eye.
If he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he is to let the slave go free in compensation for the tooth.
When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox is to be stoned and its flesh is not to be eaten, but the owner of the ox is not to be held responsible.
But if the ox has been in the habit of goring, and its owner has been warned but has not kept it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox is to be stoned, and its owner too is to be put to death.
If a ransom is imposed on him, he may pay the redemption price for his life, whatever is imposed on him.
If the ox gores a son or a daughter, this same ruling applies to him.
If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner is to give thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master, and the ox is to be stoned.
When a man opens a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit is to make it good. He is to pay money to the animal's owner, and the dead animal will be his.
When one man's ox hurts another's so that it dies, they are to sell the live ox and divide its price, and they are also to divide the dead animal.
Or, if it was known that the ox was in the habit of goring, and its owner did not keep it in, he is to pay in full, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
When a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he is to repay five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for the one who struck him,
but if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt for him. A thief must make full restitution. If he has nothing, he is to be sold for his theft.
If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether an ox or a donkey or a sheep, he is to repay double.

When a man lets a field or a vineyard be grazed, and lets his livestock loose so that they graze in another man's field, he is to make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
When a fire breaks out and catches in thorns, so that stacked grain or standing grain or the field is burned, the one who started the fire is to make full restitution.
When a man gives his neighbour silver or goods to keep, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he is to repay double.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house is to come before God, to swear that he has not laid a hand on his neighbour's property.

In every case of wrongdoing, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost thing about which someone says, "This is mine," the case of both parties is to come before God. The one whom God declares guilty is to repay double to his neighbour.
When a man gives his neighbour a donkey or an ox or a sheep or any animal to keep, and it dies or is hurt or driven away, with no one seeing it,
an oath by the LORD is to be between them both, that he has not laid a hand on his neighbour's property. The owner is to accept it, and the other is not to make restitution.
But if it was stolen from him, he is to make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn by a wild animal, he is to bring it as evidence. He is not to make restitution for what was torn.
When a man borrows an animal from his neighbour and it is hurt or dies while its owner is not with it, he is to make full restitution.
If its owner was with it, he is not to make restitution. If it was hired, the hire price covers the loss.
When a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he is to pay the bride-price for her and make her his wife.
If her father refuses to give her to him, he is to pay silver equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You are not to let a sorceress live.
Whoever lies with an animal is to be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone is to be devoted to destruction.
You are not to wrong a foreign resident or oppress him, for you were foreign residents in the land of Egypt.
You are not to afflict any widow or orphan.
If you do afflict them, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to my people, to the poor among you, you are not to act as a creditor to him. You are not to charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's cloak in pledge, you are to return it to him before the sun goes down,
for it is his only covering, the cloak for his body. What else will he sleep in? And when he cries out to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
You are not to curse God or put a curse on a leader of your people.
You are not to hold back the first of your harvest or of your vats. The firstborn of your sons you are to give to me.
You are to do the same with your oxen and with your sheep. For seven days it is to be with its mother, and on the eighth day you are to give it to me.
You are to be holy people to me. You are not to eat flesh torn by wild animals in the field. You are to throw it to the dogs.
You are not to pass on a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked person to be a malicious witness.
Do not follow the majority to do wrong, and do not give testimony in a dispute by siding with the majority to twist justice.
Do not favour a poor person in his dispute.
When you come across your enemy's ox or donkey straying, you must take it back to him.
When you see the donkey of someone who hates you collapsed under its load, you must not leave it alone. You must help him free it.
Do not twist the justice due to your needy people in their disputes.
Stay far from a false charge. Do not put to death the innocent and the righteous, for I will not acquit the guilty.
Do not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and distorts the words of the righteous.
Do not oppress a foreign resident. You yourselves know how it feels to be a foreigner, for you were foreign residents in the land of Egypt.
For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,

but in the seventh year you are to let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor of your people may eat, and what they leave the wild animals may eat. You are to do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you are to cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female servant and the foreign resident may be refreshed.
Be careful in all that I have said to you. You are not to mention the names of other gods, or let them be heard from your mouth.
Three times in the year you are to hold a festival for me.

You are to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.

You are to keep the Festival of the Harvest, of the first of your labours, of what you sow in the field. You are to keep the Festival of the Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your labour from the field.
Three times in the year all your males are to appear before the Lord, the LORD.
You are not to offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the fat of my festival offering is not to remain until morning.
The best of the first fruits of your ground you are to bring to the house of the LORD your God. You are not to boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
Pay attention to him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your rebellion, since my name is in him.
If you listen closely to his voice and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
My angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
You are not to bow down to their gods or serve them, and you are not to follow their practices. You are to demolish them completely and smash their pillars to pieces.
You are to serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from among you.
No woman will miscarry or be childless in your land. I will fill the number of your days.
I will send my terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every people you come to. I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
I will send hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out from before you in a single year, or the land would become desolate and the wild animals would multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and taken possession of the land.

I will set your boundary from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River. I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
You are not to make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They must not live in your land, or they will make you sin against me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.
To Moses he said, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. You are to worship from a distance.
Moses alone is to come near to the LORD. The others are not to come near, and the people are not to go up with him."
Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the rulings, and all the people answered with one voice, "Everything the LORD has said we will do."
Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent young men of the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he dashed against the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. They said, "Everything the LORD has said we will do, and we will obey."
Moses took the blood and threw it over the people and said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words."
Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
and they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet there was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the very heavens.
He did not lay his hand on the leaders of the Israelites. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and wait there. I will give you the tablets of stone, with the teaching and the commandment that I have written for their instruction."
Moses set out with his assistant Joshua, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever has a matter to settle may go to them."
Then Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day he called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
To the eyes of the Israelites the glory of the LORD was like a devouring fire on the top of the mountain.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites to take a contribution for me. You are to receive my contribution from everyone whose heart moves him to give.
This is the contribution you are to receive from them: gold, silver and bronze;
blue, purple and crimson yarn, fine linen and goats' hair;
rams' skins dyed red, fine leather and acacia wood;
oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
They are to make me a sanctuary, so that I may live among them.
You are to make it exactly according to the pattern I show you, both the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
They are to make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold moulding round it.
Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them on its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them.
The poles are to stay in the rings of the ark. They are not to be taken out.
You are to put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
Make a cover of atonement of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Make two cherubim of gold. Make them of hammered work, at the two ends of the cover.
Make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. Make the cherubim of one piece with the cover at its two ends.
The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, covering the cover with their wings, and their faces are to be towards one another. The faces of the cherubim are to be towards the cover.
Put the cover on top of the ark, and in the ark put the testimony that I will give you.
There I will meet with you. From above the cover, from between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the testimony, I will speak with you about all that I will command you for the Israelites.
You are to make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold moulding round it.
Make a rim for it a handbreadth wide, and a gold moulding for the rim all round.
Make four gold rings for it and fasten the rings at the four corners, at its four feet.
The rings are to be close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table is to be carried with them.
Make its plates and dishes, its flagons and bowls with which libations are poured out. Make them of pure gold.
You are to set the bread of the Presence on the table before me always.
You are to make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand is to be made of hammered work, its base and its shaft. Its cups, its buds and its petals are to be of one piece with it.
Six branches are to go out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and petals, are to be on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and petals, on the other branch. So it is to be for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and petals,
with a bud under the first pair of branches going out from it, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair, for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
Their buds and their branches are to be of one piece with it, the whole of it one hammered piece of pure gold.
You are to make its seven lamps and set them up so that they give light to the space in front of it.
Its tongs and trays are to be of pure gold.
It is to be made, with all these utensils, from a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern that is being shown you on the mountain.
"You are to make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue, purple and crimson yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled craftsman.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains are to be the same size.
Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five curtains are to be joined to one another.
Make loops of blue on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, so that the loops are opposite one another.
Make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is one whole.
You are to make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle. Make eleven curtains.
Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains are to be the same size.
Join five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain that joins the second set.
Make fifty clasps of bronze, put the clasps into the loops, and join the tent together so that it is one whole.
As for the extra length of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that is left over is to hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The cubit on one side and the cubit on the other of what is left over in the length of the curtains of the tent are to hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that, to cover it.
Make for the tent a covering of rams' skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
You are to make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame is to have two tenons for fitting together. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
Make twenty frames for the south side.
Make forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north, make twenty frames
and their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next.
For the rear of the tabernacle, to the west, make six frames.
Make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They are to be double at the bottom and joined at the top, to the first ring. It is to be the same for both of them. They are to be for the two corners.
There are to be eight frames with their silver bases, sixteen bases, two bases under each frame.
Make bars of acacia wood, five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames at the rear of the tabernacle on the west.
The middle bar, halfway up the frames, is to run from end to end.
Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings for them to hold the bars. Overlay the bars with gold.
Then set up the tabernacle according to the plan that you were shown on the mountain.
You are to make a curtain of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
Hang it on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with hooks of gold, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the curtain from the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, behind the curtain. The curtain will separate for you the holy place from the most holy place.
Put the cover of atonement on the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.
Set the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle. Put the table on the north side.
For the entrance of the tent you are to make a screen of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
For the screen make five posts of acacia wood and overlay them with gold. Their hooks are to be of gold, and you are to cast five bronze bases for them.
"Build the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five wide. The altar is to be square, three cubits high.
Make a horn at each of its four corners, formed as one piece with it, and cover it with bronze.
Make its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its flesh-forks and its fire pans. All its utensils you are to make of bronze.
Make a grating for it, a bronze network, and make four bronze rings on the network at its four corners.
Place it beneath the altar's ledge, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar of acacia wood, and cover them with bronze.
The poles are to go through the rings, so that they are on both sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make it hollow, of planks. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard is to have hangings of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long on that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
So also on the north side, along its length: hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The width of the courtyard on the west side is to have hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The width of the courtyard on the east side, towards the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits.
On one side of the gateway there are to be hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
For the gateway of the courtyard there is to be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases.
All the posts round the courtyard are to be joined with silver bands, with silver hooks and bronze bases.
The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long and fifty wide, with hangings of fine twisted linen five cubits high, set on bronze bases.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use of it, and all its tent pegs and all the pegs of the courtyard, are to be of bronze.
Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of crushed olives for the lamp, to keep a light burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that hangs before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend it, from evening to morning, before the LORD. This is a permanent rule for the Israelites, through their generations.
"Bring your brother Aaron near to you, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.
Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron, to give him honour and beauty.
Speak to all the skilled craftsmen whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aaron's garments, to set him apart to serve me as priest.

These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. They are to make these sacred garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve me as priests.
They are to use gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine linen.
They are to make the ephod of gold, of blue, purple and crimson yarn, and of fine twisted linen, in skilled work.
It is to have two shoulder pieces joined to its two upper edges, so that it can be fastened.
The woven waistband on it is to be of the same work and material: gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen.
Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel,
six names on one stone and the six remaining names on the other, in the order of their birth.
Engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel as a gem-cutter engraves a seal, and mount them in settings of gold.
Fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to carry their names before the LORD on his two shoulders as a reminder.
Make settings of gold,
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the twisted chains to the settings.
Make a breastpiece for decisions, in skilled work. Make it in the same work as the ephod: of gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It is to be square when folded double, a span long and a span wide.
Mount on it a setting of stones in four rows. The first row is to be a row of carnelian, chrysolite and emerald;
the second row a turquoise, a lapis lazuli and a moonstone;
the third row a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a topaz, an onyx and a jasper. They are to be set in gold mountings.
The stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve, one for each name. Each is to be engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
On the breastpiece make chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
Make two gold rings for the breastpiece and fasten them to the two upper corners of the breastpiece.
Fasten the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and fasten the other two ends of the cords to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
Make two gold rings and put them on the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on its inner edge next to the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and attach them to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front, near its seam, above the waistband of the ephod.
The breastpiece is to be tied by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rests above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing loose from the ephod.
Whenever Aaron enters the holy place, he is to carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece for decisions, as a constant reminder before the LORD.

Put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece for decisions, and they will be over Aaron's heart whenever he comes before the LORD. In this way Aaron will always carry the means of deciding for the Israelites over his heart before the LORD.
Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
There is to be an opening for the head in the middle of it, with a woven binding round the opening, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it will not tear.
Round its hem make pomegranates of blue, purple and crimson yarn, with gold bells between them all round,
a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all round the hem of the robe.
Aaron is to wear it when he serves, and its sound will be heard when he enters the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
Make a plate of pure gold and engrave it like the engraving of a seal: 'Holy to the LORD.'
Fasten it to the turban with a blue cord. It is to be on the front of the turban.

It will be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron will carry the guilt connected with the holy gifts the Israelites consecrate, whatever their sacred offerings. It is always to be on his forehead, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.
Weave the tunic in a checker pattern of fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and make the sash as embroidered work.
For Aaron's sons make tunics, sashes and headbands, to give them honour and beauty.
Put them on your brother Aaron and on his sons with him, and anoint them, install them and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their bare flesh, reaching from the hips to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they do not incur guilt and die. This is a permanent rule for him and for his descendants after him.
"This is what you are to do to set them apart, so that they may serve me as priests. Take one young bull and two rams without blemish,
and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Make them of fine wheat flour.
Put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod and the breastpiece, and fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
Put the turban on his head and fix the holy diadem on the turban.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head and anoint him.
Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics,
and wrap sashes round Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood will be theirs by a permanent rule. In this way you are to install Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull to the front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on the bull's head.
Slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the entrails, the long lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But the bull's flesh, its hide and its dung you are to burn outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the ram, take its blood and splash it against the sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.
Burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobes of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet, and splash the rest of the blood against the sides of the altar.

Take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be holy, and his sons and their garments with him.
Take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh, for it is a ram of installation,
and one loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and of his sons, and lift them up as an elevation offering before the LORD.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is a food offering to the LORD.
Take the breast of the ram of Aaron's installation and lift it up as an elevation offering before the LORD, and it will be your portion.
You are to set apart the breast that was lifted up and the thigh that was raised, from the ram of installation, from that which belongs to Aaron and to his sons.

It will be a permanent due for Aaron and his sons from the Israelites, for it is a contribution. It will be a contribution from the Israelites, from their peace offerings, their contribution to the LORD.
The sacred garments of Aaron will pass to his sons after him, to be anointed and installed in them.
The son who succeeds him as priest, who comes to the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place, will wear them for seven days.
Take the ram of installation and boil its flesh in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons are to eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They are to eat the things by which atonement was made at their installation and consecration, but no outsider may eat them, for they are holy.
If any of the flesh of the installation or any of the bread is left until morning, you are to burn what remains with fire. It must not be eaten, for it is holy.
Do for Aaron and his sons in just this way, all that I have commanded you. You are to take seven days to install them.
Each day you are to offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. Cleanse the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you are to make atonement for the altar and consecrate it, and the altar will be most holy. Whatever touches the altar will become holy.
This is what you are to offer on the altar: two year-old lambs each day, continually.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering, for the first lamb.
The second lamb you are to offer at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
This is to be a continual burnt offering through your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak with you.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be made holy by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons, to serve me as priests.
I will live among the Israelites and be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might live among them. I am the LORD their God.
"Make an altar for burning incense. Make it of acacia wood.
It is to be a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, and two cubits high, with its horns formed as one piece with it.
Cover its top, all its sides and its horns with pure gold, and make a gold moulding round it.
Make two gold rings for it beneath the moulding, on two opposite sides, to hold the poles by which it is carried.
Make the poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Place the altar in front of the curtain that hangs before the ark of the Testimony, in front of the cover of atonement that is over the Testimony, where I will meet with you.
Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it. Every morning when he tends the lamps he is to burn it,
and when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight he is to burn it, so that there will be incense before the LORD continually, through your generations.
You are not to offer on it any unauthorised incense, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering, and you are not to pour a drink offering on it.
Once a year Aaron is to make atonement on its horns. Once a year he is to make atonement on it with the blood of the sin offering of atonement, through your generations. It is most holy to the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each man is to give the LORD a ransom for his life when he is counted, so that no plague will strike them when they are counted.
Everyone who crosses over to the counted is to give this: half a shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary (a shekel is twenty gerahs). The half shekel is to be the LORD's contribution.
Everyone who crosses over to the counted, from twenty years old and upwards, is to give the LORD's contribution.
The rich are not to give more, and the poor are not to give less, than the half shekel, when you give the LORD's contribution to make atonement for your lives.

You are to take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting, so that it may be a reminder for the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Make a bronze basin for washing, with a bronze stand. Put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet from it.
When they go into the tent of meeting, they are to wash with water, so that they do not die. Also when they approach the altar to serve by burning a food offering to the LORD,
they are to wash their hands and their feet, so that they do not die. This is to be a permanent rule for them, for him and for his descendants through their generations."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take for yourself the finest spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much, 250 shekels, of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
and 500 shekels of cassia, by the shekel of the sanctuary, and a hin of olive oil.
Make of these a sacred anointing oil, a scented compound, the work of a perfumer. It is to be the sacred anointing oil.
With it you are to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the Testimony,
the table with all its utensils, the lampstand with its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
You are to consecrate them, so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
Say to the Israelites: 'This is to be my sacred anointing oil through your generations.
It is not to be poured on any person's body, and you are not to make any like it, in the same proportions. It is holy, and it is to be holy to you.
Whoever mixes anything like it, or puts any of it on someone who is not a priest, will be cut off from his people.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "Take sweet spices, gum resin, onycha and galbanum, sweet spices with pure frankincense, in equal parts.
Make an incense of them, a scented compound, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure and holy.
Grind some of it into fine powder and put part of it before the Testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It is to be most holy to you.
You are not to make for yourselves any incense of the same composition. It is to be holy to you, for the LORD.
Whoever makes any like it, to smell its fragrance, will be cut off from his people."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of craftsmanship,
to devise designs, to work in gold, in silver and in bronze,
in cutting stones for setting, and in carving wood, to work in every kind of craft.
I have also appointed with him Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. And in the heart of every skilled person I have put skill, so that they may make all that I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark of the Testimony and the cover of atonement that is on it, and all the furnishings of the tent,
the table and its utensils, the pure gold lampstand with all its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin and its stand,
the woven garments, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for their service as priests,
the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the holy place. They are to make them just as I have commanded you."
The LORD said to Moses,

"You are to speak to the Israelites and say: 'You must keep my Sabbaths, for this is a sign between me and you through your generations, so that you may know that I, the LORD, am the one who makes you holy.
You are to keep the Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Anyone who profanes it is to be put to death. Whoever does any work on it will be cut off from among his people.
Six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to keep the Sabbath, observing it through their generations as a lasting covenant.
It is a sign between me and the Israelites for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed.'"
When he had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, he gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone written with the finger of God.

The people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain. They gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Up, make us gods who will lead the way for us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up from Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold earrings from your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring them to me."
All the people took off the gold earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took what they handed him, worked it with an engraving tool and made it into a molten calf. They said, "Israel, here are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of it and proclaimed, "Tomorrow is a festival for the LORD."
They got up early the next morning, offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to revel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up from Egypt, have ruined themselves.

How quickly they have turned from the road I laid down for them! They have made themselves a molten calf, bowed down to it and sacrificed to it, and said, 'Israel, here are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "I have looked at this people, and they are a stubborn, stiff-necked people.
So now, let me be, so that my anger may blaze against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses tried to soften the LORD his God. "LORD," he said, "why should your anger blaze against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?

Why should the Egyptians be able to say, 'He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn back from your blazing anger, and change your mind about harming your people.

Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Israel, to whom you swore by your own self: 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars of the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I promised, to be theirs for ever.'"
And the LORD changed his mind about the harm he had threatened to bring on his people.
Moses turned and went down the mountain, the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands, tablets written on both sides, front and back.
The tablets were God's work, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
Joshua heard the people's noise as they shouted, and he said to Moses, "There is a sound of battle in the camp."
Moses answered, "That is not the sound of a victory cry, nor the sound of a cry of defeat. The sound I hear is singing."
As he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger blazed. He hurled the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered the powder on the water and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you brought such great guilt on them?"
Aaron said, "Do not let my lord's anger blaze. You know how bent on evil this people is.
They said to me, 'Make us gods to lead the way for us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up from Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' They gave it to me, I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were out of control, because Aaron had let them run wild, a laughing-stock for their enemies.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and called, "Whoever is for the LORD, to me!" All the Levites gathered to him.

He told them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Every man, strap on your sword. Go back and forth through the camp, from gate to gate, and kill your brother, your companion and your neighbour.'"
The Levites did what Moses said, and about three thousand of the people fell that day.
Moses said, "Today you have been set apart for the LORD, at the cost of your own sons and brothers, so that he may bless you today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD. Perhaps I can atone for your sin."
Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, this people has committed a great sin: they have made themselves a god of gold.
Now, if you will forgive their sin... but if not, wipe me out of the book you have written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe out of my book.
Now go, lead the people to the place I told you of. My angel will go ahead of you. But on the day I call them to account, I will hold them to account for their sin."
And the LORD struck the people with a plague because they had made the calf, the one Aaron made.

The LORD said to Moses, "Set out from here, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.'
I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stubborn people, and I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard this harsh word, they mourned, and none of them put on his ornaments.

The LORD had said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites: 'You are a stubborn people. If I went up in your midst even for a moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments from Mount Horeb onwards.

Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, a good distance away, and he called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wished to consult the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would stand up, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at its entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would all stand up and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant, Joshua son of Nun, never left the tent.
Moses said to the LORD, "You tell me, 'Lead this people up,' but you have not told me whom you will send with me. And yet you said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favour with me.'
So now, if I have found favour with you, please make your ways known to me, so that I may know you and go on finding favour with you. And remember that this nation is your people."
He said, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
He said to him, "If your presence does not go with us, do not take us up from here.

How else will it be known that I and your people have found favour with you? Will it not be by your going with us, so that we, I and your people, are set apart from every other people on the face of the earth?"
The LORD said to Moses, "I will do this too, the thing you have asked, for you have found favour with me, and I know you by name."
Moses said, "Show me your glory, I pray."

He said, "I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will call out the name 'the LORD' in front of you. I will be gracious to whom I choose to be gracious, and show compassion to whom I choose to show compassion."
He added, "But you cannot see my face, for no human can see me and live."
The LORD said, "Here is a place beside me. You are to stand on the rock,
and while my glory passes by, I will set you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back, but my face will not be seen."
The LORD said to Moses, "Carve out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you smashed.
Be ready by morning. In the morning you are to climb up Mount Sinai and present yourself to me there, on the top of the mountain.
No one is to go up with you, and no one is to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even flocks and herds are to graze in front of that mountain."
Moses carved out two stone tablets like the first ones, got up early in the morning and climbed Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, taking the two stone tablets in his hand.
The LORD came down in the cloud and stood beside him there, and he called out the name of the LORD.
The LORD passed in front of him and called out: "The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, rich in faithful love and truth,

keeping faithful love for thousands of generations, forgiving guilt, rebellion and sin, yet not leaving the guilty unpunished, holding the children and grandchildren to account for the guilt of their parents, to the third and fourth generation."
Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshipped.
He said, "My Lord, if I have found favour with you, let my Lord go with us. Though this is a stubborn people, forgive our guilt and our sin, and take us as your own possession."

He said, "See, I am making a covenant. In front of all your people I will do wonders such as have never been done anywhere on earth or among any nation. All the people around you will see the LORD's work, for what I am going to do with you is awe-inspiring.
Keep what I command you today. I am going to drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
Take care not to make a treaty with the people of the land you are entering, or it will become a trap in your midst.
Instead, tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars and cut down their sacred poles.
You must not bow down to any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
Do not make a treaty with the people of the land. When they chase after their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
You will take wives for your sons from among their daughters, and their daughters will chase after their gods and lead your sons to do the same.
You are not to make yourselves any molten gods.
Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
Everything that first opens the womb is mine, every male of your livestock, the firstborn of cattle and sheep.
A firstborn donkey you must redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. Redeem every firstborn among your sons. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
You may work for six days, but on the seventh day you must rest. Even at ploughing time and harvest time you must rest.
Keep the Festival of Weeks with the first of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times a year all your men are to appear before the Lord, the LORD, the God of Israel.
For I will drive out nations before you and extend your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
You are not to offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the Passover festival must not be left until morning.
Bring the best of the first produce of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You are not to boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words down, for on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with the LORD for forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hand, he did not know that the skin of his face was radiant because he had spoken with the LORD.
Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
After that all the Israelites came near, and he gave them all the commands that the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face.
But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he took the veil off until he came out. When he came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded,
the Israelites saw that the skin of Moses' face was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.
Moses assembled the whole community of the Israelites and said to them, "These are the things that the LORD has commanded you to do:
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day will be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of complete rest for the LORD. Anyone who does work on it is to be put to death.
You are not to light a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day."
Moses said to the whole community of the Israelites, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you a contribution for the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring the LORD's contribution: gold, silver and bronze;
blue, purple and crimson yarn, fine linen and goats' hair;
rams' skins dyed red, fine leather and acacia wood;
oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and the breastpiece.
Let every skilled person among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps, its frames, its bars, its posts and its bases;
the ark with its poles, the cover of atonement, and the curtain that screens it;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light, with its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, the basin with its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard, its posts and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
the pegs of the tabernacle and the pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for their service as priests."
Then the whole community of the Israelites went out from Moses' presence.

And everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him, came and brought the LORD's contribution for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service and for the sacred garments.
So they came, both men and women, all who had willing hearts, and brought brooches, earrings, rings and ornaments, all kinds of gold objects. Everyone presented an offering of gold to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple or crimson yarn, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, or fine leather, brought it.
Everyone who could make a contribution of silver or bronze brought it as the LORD's contribution, and everyone who had acacia wood for any work of the project brought it.
Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun, blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts moved them and who had the skill spun the goats' hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and the breastpiece,
and spices and oil for the light, for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.
All the Israelite men and women whose hearts moved them to bring something for all the work that the LORD, through Moses, had commanded to be done, brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
and he has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of craftsmanship,
to devise designs, to work in gold, in silver and in bronze,
in cutting stones for setting, and in carving wood, for work in every kind of skilled craft.
And he has put it in his heart to teach, both him and Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill to do every kind of work as engravers, as designers, and as embroiderers in blue, purple and crimson yarn and in fine linen, and as weavers, doing every kind of work and designing skilful work.

Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the LORD has given wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work in the service of the sanctuary are to work according to all that the LORD has commanded."
Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person in whose heart the LORD had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him to come to do the work.
They received from Moses all the contribution that the Israelites had brought for doing the work in the service of the sanctuary. And still they brought him freewill offerings every morning,
so that all the skilled people who were doing all the work on the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing,
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than is needed for the work that the LORD has commanded us to do."
So Moses gave a command, and word was sent throughout the camp: "Let no man or woman do any more work for the contribution for the sanctuary." So the people were restrained from bringing,
for what they had was enough for all the work, and more.
All the skilled among the workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains. They were made of fine twisted linen and blue, purple and crimson yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled craftsman.
The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width four cubits. All the curtains were the same size.
He joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.
He made loops of blue on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and did the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was in the second set, so that the loops were opposite one another.
And he made fifty clasps of gold, and joined the curtains one to the other with the clasps, so that the tabernacle was one whole.
He made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle. He made eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits. The eleven curtains were the same size.
He joined five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
And he made fifty loops on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together so that it might be one whole.
And he made for the tent a covering of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that.
Then he made the upright frames for the tabernacle, of acacia wood.
The length of each frame was ten cubits, and the width of each frame a cubit and a half.
Each frame had two tenons for fitting together. He made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
He made the frames for the tabernacle, twenty frames for the south side.
And he made forty bases of silver under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty frames
and their forty bases of silver, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
For the rear of the tabernacle on the west he made six frames.
He made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle in the rear.
They were separate beneath but joined at the top, at the first ring. He made two of them in this way for the two corners.
There were eight frames with their bases of silver: sixteen bases, two bases under every frame.
He made bars of acacia wood, five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the frames of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the tabernacle at the rear on the west.
He made the middle bar to run from end to end halfway up the frames.
And he overlaid the frames with gold, and made their rings of gold to hold the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the curtain of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
For it he made four posts of acacia and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold, and he cast for them four bases of silver.
He made a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen, embroidered,
and its five posts with their hooks. He overlaid their capitals and their bands with gold, but their five bases were of bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. It was two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide and a cubit and a half high.
He covered it with pure gold, inside and out, and made a gold moulding round it.
He cast four gold rings for it, fastened on its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
He made poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold,
and put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
He made a cover of atonement of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
He made two cherubim of gold. He made them of hammered work, at the two ends of the cover,
one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the cover, at its two ends.
The cherubim had their wings spread upward, covering the cover with their wings, their faces towards one another. The faces of the cherubim were towards the cover.
He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high.
He covered it with pure gold and made a gold moulding round it.
He made a rim for it a handbreadth wide, and a gold moulding for the rim all round.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened the rings at the four corners, at its four feet.
The rings were close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood to carry the table, and covered them with gold.
He made the utensils for the table of pure gold: its plates and dishes, its bowls and flagons with which libations were poured.
He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work, its base and its shaft. Its cups, its buds and its petals were of one piece with it.
Six branches went out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side of it and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

On one branch there were three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and petals, and on the other branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and petals. So it was for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and petals,
with a bud under the first pair of branches going out from it, a bud under the second pair and a bud under the third pair, for the six branches going out from it.
Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it, the whole of it a single hammered piece of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps and its tongs and its trays of pure gold.
He made it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. It was a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, and two cubits high, with its horns of one piece with it.
He covered it with pure gold, its top, its sides all round and its horns, and made a gold moulding round it.
He made two gold rings for it under the moulding, on two opposite sides, as holders for the poles with which to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He made the sacred anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood. It was five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high.
He made horns for it on its four corners, of one piece with it, and covered it with bronze.
He made all the utensils of the altar, the pots, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the flesh-forks and the fire pans. He made all its utensils of bronze.
He made for the altar a grating, a network of bronze, under its ledge, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it. He made it hollow, of planks.
He made the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze, from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits,
with their twenty posts and their twenty bronze bases, and the hooks and bands of the posts of silver.
For the north side there were hangings a hundred cubits long, with their twenty posts and their twenty bronze bases, and the hooks and bands of the posts of silver.
For the west side there were hangings fifty cubits long, with their ten posts and ten bases, and the hooks and bands of the posts of silver.
For the east side, towards the sunrise, it was fifty cubits.
The hangings for one side of the gate were fifteen cubits, with their three posts and three bases.
And so for the other side of the gate of the courtyard, hangings of fifteen cubits, with their three posts and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were of bronze, the hooks and bands of the posts of silver, and the overlaying of their tops of silver. All the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The screen for the gate of the courtyard was embroidered work in blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long and, like the hangings of the courtyard, five cubits high,
with four posts and four bases of bronze. Their hooks were of silver, and the overlaying of their tops and their bands were of silver.
All the pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard round it were of bronze.
This is the account of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony, as it was counted at Moses' command, the work of the Levites under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer and embroiderer in blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen.
All the gold that was used for the work in all the construction of the sanctuary, the gold from the contribution, was twenty-nine talents and 730 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
The silver from those of the community who were counted was a hundred talents and 1,775 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary:
a beka a head (that is, half a shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary), for everyone who crossed over to those counted, from twenty years old and upwards, 603,550 men.
