The hundred talents of silver were for casting the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain, a hundred bases for the hundred talents, a talent a base.
Of the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the posts and overlaid their capitals and made bands for them.
The bronze that was contributed was seventy talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and the bronze grating for it and all the utensils of the altar,
the bases round the courtyard, the bases of the gate of the courtyard, all the pegs of the tabernacle and all the pegs round the courtyard.
From the blue, purple and crimson yarn they made woven garments for serving in the holy place. They made the sacred garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen.
They hammered out gold leaf and cut it into threads, to work into the blue, purple and crimson yarn and the fine linen, in skilled work.
They made shoulder pieces for it, joined to it at its two upper edges.
The woven waistband on it was of the same work and material: gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the onyx stones, mounted in settings of gold, and engraved like the engravings of a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
He set them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece in skilled work, in the same work as the ephod: gold, blue, purple and crimson yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It was square. They made the breastpiece folded double, a span long and a span wide when folded.
They mounted on it four rows of stones. A row of carnelian, chrysolite and emerald was the first row;
the second row, a turquoise, a lapis lazuli and a moonstone;
the third row, a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
and the fourth row, a topaz, an onyx and a jasper. They were enclosed in settings of gold.
The stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve, according to their names. Each was engraved like a seal with its name, for the twelve tribes.
On the breastpiece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
They made two settings of gold and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two upper corners of the breastpiece.
They put the two gold cords in the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.
The other two ends of the two cords they fastened to the two settings, and so attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and put them on the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on its inner edge next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front, near its seam, above the waistband of the ephod.

They tied the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rested above the waistband of the ephod and did not swing loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod, woven, entirely of blue.
The opening of the robe in the middle of it was like the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding round the opening so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine twisted linen.
They also made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates all round the hem of the robe,
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all round the hem of the robe for serving, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics, woven of fine linen, for Aaron and his sons,
and the turban of fine linen, the headbands of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen and blue, purple and crimson yarn, embroidered, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the sacred diadem of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a seal: "Holy to the LORD."
They tied a blue cord to it, to fasten it on the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. They did it so.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its bars, its posts and its bases;
the covering of rams' skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the curtain for screening;
the ark of the Testimony with its poles, and the cover of atonement;
the table with all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps set in place, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the golden altar, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, the basin with its stand;

the hangings of the courtyard with its posts and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes and its pegs, and all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for their service as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses inspected all the work, and saw that they had done it. They had done it as the LORD had commanded. And Moses blessed them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
Put the ark of the Testimony in it, and screen the ark with the curtain.
Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
Put the golden altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony, and hang the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle.
Put the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
Put the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard round it, and hang the screen at the gate of the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and consecrate the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
Put the sacred garments on Aaron, and anoint him and consecrate him, so that he may serve me as priest.
Bring his sons and clothe them with tunics,
and anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will make them a priesthood for all time, through their generations."
Moses did this. He did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle. He placed its bases, set up its frames, put in its bars and set up its posts.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent over it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the Testimony and put it in the ark, fixed the poles to the ark and placed the cover of atonement on top of the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the curtain for screening, and screened the ark of the Testimony, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the curtain,
and set out the bread on it before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle,
and set up the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the tent of meeting in front of the curtain,
and burned fragrant incense on it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He hung the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle.
He put the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing,
and Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet from it.
When they went into the tent of meeting, and when they approached the altar, they washed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard round the tabernacle and the altar, and hung the screen at the gate of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud rested on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud did not lift, then they did not set out until the day it lifted.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel at every stage of their journey.
The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you are to bring your offering from the livestock, from the herd or from the flock.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to offer a male without blemish. He is to bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that it may be accepted before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf, to make atonement for him.
He is to slaughter the bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons, the priests, are to bring the blood and splash it against the sides of the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Then Aaron's sons, the priests, are to arrange the pieces, the head and the fat on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He is to wash the entrails and the legs with water, and the priest is to burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, he is to offer a male without blemish.
He is to slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons, the priests, are to splash its blood against the sides of the altar.
He is to cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest is to arrange them on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
The entrails and the legs he is to wash with water. The priest is to bring all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to bring his offering from the turtledoves or young pigeons.
The priest is to bring it to the altar, wring off its head and burn it on the altar. Its blood is to be drained out on the side of the altar.
He is to remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east side, in the place for ashes.
He is to tear it open by its wings, without dividing it. The priest is to burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering is to be of fine flour. He is to pour oil on it and put frankincense on it,

and bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. The priest is to take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all its frankincense, and burn this as its memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What is left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the food offerings to the LORD.
When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to be of fine flour: unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering made on a griddle, it is to be of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering made in a pan, it is to be made of fine flour with oil.
You are to bring the grain offering made of these things to the LORD, and present it to the priest, who will bring it to the altar.
The priest is to take from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What is left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the food offerings to the LORD.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD is to be made with leaven, for you are not to burn any leaven or any honey as a food offering to the LORD.
You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they are not to be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
Season every grain offering with salt. Do not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering. With all your offerings you are to offer salt.
If you bring a grain offering of first ripe produce to the LORD, you are to bring, as your grain offering of first ripe produce, new grain roasted on the fire, ground from fresh ears.
You are to put oil on it and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest is to burn as its memorial portion some of the ground grain and oil, with all its frankincense. It is a food offering to the LORD.
If his offering is a peace offering, and he offers an animal from the herd, whether male or female, he is to offer it without blemish before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons, the priests, are to splash the blood against the sides of the altar.
From the peace offering he is to present, as a food offering to the LORD, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat that is on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons are to burn it on the altar on top of the burnt offering, which is on the wood on the fire. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering for a peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, male or female, he is to offer it without blemish.
If he offers a lamb as his offering, he is to offer it before the LORD,
lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons are to splash its blood against the sides of the altar.

From the peace offering he is to present, as a food offering to the LORD, its fat, the whole fat tail, cut off close to the backbone, and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn it on the altar as food, a food offering to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he is to offer it before the LORD,
lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and the sons of Aaron are to splash its blood against the sides of the altar.
From it he is to present his offering, as a food offering to the LORD, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn them on the altar as food, a food offering with a pleasing aroma. All fat belongs to the LORD.
It is a permanent rule through your generations, in all your dwelling places: you are not to eat any fat or any blood."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: Suppose someone does wrong without meaning to, by breaking any of the LORD's commands about what must not be done, and does any one of them.
If it is the anointed priest who does wrong, bringing guilt on the people, he is to present to the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the wrong he has done.
He is to bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD, lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the LORD.
The anointed priest is to take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the tent of meeting.
He is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, towards the curtain of the sanctuary.

The priest is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting. All the rest of the bull's blood he is to pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to take all the fat from the sin offering bull: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on them,
the two kidneys with the fat on them by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys,
as these are taken from the ox of the peace offering. The priest is to burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
But the bull's hide and all its flesh, with its head, legs, entrails and dung,
the entire remains of the bull, he is to carry outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are dumped, and burn it on a wood fire. It is to be burned where the ashes are dumped.
If the whole community of Israel does wrong without knowing it, and the matter is hidden from the assembly, and they break any of the LORD's commands about what must not be done, and become guilty,
then when the wrong they have done becomes known, the assembly is to offer a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the tent of meeting.
The elders of the community are to lay their hands on the bull's head before the LORD, and the bull is to be slaughtered before the LORD.
The anointed priest is to bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting,
dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, towards the curtain.

He is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to take all its fat and burn it on the altar.
He is to do with this bull what he did with the sin offering bull. In this way the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
He is to carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
When a leader does wrong, breaking unintentionally any one of the commands of the LORD his God about what must not be done, and is guilty,
or if he is made aware of the wrong he has done, he is to bring as his offering a male goat without blemish.
He is to lay his hand on the goat's head and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
All its fat he is to burn on the altar, like the fat of the peace offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for his wrong, and he will be forgiven.
If an ordinary member of the people does wrong without meaning to, breaking any of the LORD's commands about what must not be done, and is guilty,
or if he is made aware of the wrong he has done, he is to bring as his offering a female goat without blemish for the wrong he has done.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
The priest is to take some of its blood on his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He is to take away all its fat, as the fat is taken from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he is to bring a female without blemish.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He is to take away all its fat, as the lamb's fat is taken from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar, on top of the food offerings to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the wrong he has done, and he will be forgiven.
If anyone does wrong by failing to speak when he has heard a public summons to testify and is a witness, having seen or learned of the matter, he will bear the consequences of his guilt.

Or if anyone touches something unclean, whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or of unclean livestock, or of unclean swarming creatures, and he does not realise it, he has become unclean and is guilty.
Or if he touches human uncleanness, whatever kind of uncleanness it may be, and he does not realise it, then when he comes to know it, he is guilty.

Or if anyone swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do harm or to do good, in any way that a person may swear thoughtlessly, and he does not realise it, then when he comes to know it, he is guilty in any of these matters.
When he is guilty in any of these ways, he is to confess the wrong he has done,
and bring to the LORD as his compensation for the wrong he has done a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, as a sin offering. The priest is to make atonement for him for his wrong.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he is to bring to the LORD, as compensation for his wrong, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
He is to bring them to the priest, who is to offer the sin offering first. He is to wring its head from its neck, but not tear it off.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second he is to offer as a burnt offering according to the rule. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the wrong he has done, and he will be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he is to bring as his offering for the wrong he has done a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He is not to put oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He is to bring it to the priest, and the priest is to take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, on top of the food offerings to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these wrongs he has done, and he will be forgiven. The rest will belong to the priest, as with the grain offering."
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"If anyone is unfaithful and does wrong without meaning to, in matters concerning the LORD's holy things, he is to bring to the LORD as his compensation a ram without blemish from the flock, valued by you in silver shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, as a guilt offering.

He is to make good what he has taken from the holy things, adding a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If anyone does wrong, breaking any of the LORD's commands about what must not be done, though he did not know it, he is guilty and will bear the consequences.

He is to bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, valued as a guilt offering. The priest is to make atonement for him for the wrong he did without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He was certainly guilty before the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"If anyone does wrong and is unfaithful to the LORD by deceiving his neighbour about something entrusted to him, or left in his keeping, or stolen, or by cheating his neighbour,
or has found a lost article and lied about it, or swears falsely about any of the things people do that are wrong,
then, since he has done wrong and is guilty, he is to give back what he took by theft or by cheating, or what was entrusted to him, or the lost article he found,
or whatever else he swore falsely about. He is to repay it in full, adding a fifth to it, and give it to its owner on the day he admits his guilt.
He is to bring to the priest, as his compensation to the LORD, a ram without blemish from the flock, valued as a guilt offering.
The priest is to make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he did that made him guilty."
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"Command Aaron and his sons: This is the teaching about the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to stay on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire is to be kept burning on it.

The priest is to put on his linen robe, with linen undergarments next to his body, and take up the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed on the altar, and place them beside the altar.
Then he is to take off his garments, put on other garments and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire on the altar is to be kept burning on it. It must not go out. The priest is to burn wood on it every morning, arrange the burnt offering on it and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
A fire is to be kept burning on the altar continually. It must not go out.
This is the teaching about the grain offering: Aaron's sons are to present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

One of them is to take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil of the grain offering, with all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and burn this as its memorial portion on the altar, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons are to eat what is left of it. It is to be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place. They are to eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It must not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their share of my food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron's descendants may eat it, as a permanent share through your generations from the food offerings to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become holy."
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"This is the offering that Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
It is to be made with oil on a griddle. You are to bring it well mixed, and present the grain offering in baked pieces, as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The anointed priest from among his sons who succeeds him is to prepare it. It is a permanent rule: the whole of it is to be burned to the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest is to be burned completely. It is not to be eaten."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the teaching about the sin offering. At the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering is to be slaughtered before the LORD. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin is to eat it. It is to be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of its blood is spattered on a garment, you are to wash the garment on which it was spattered in a holy place.
The clay pot in which it was boiled is to be broken. If it was boiled in a bronze pot, that pot is to be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place may be eaten. It is to be burned with fire.
This is the teaching about the guilt offering. It is most holy.
At the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered they are to slaughter the guilt offering, and its blood is to be splashed against the sides of the altar.
All its fat is to be offered: the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It is to be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering. There is one rule for both. The priest who makes atonement with it will have it.
The priest who presents anyone's burnt offering will have for himself the skin of the burnt offering he has presented.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and every one made in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron, equally.
This is the teaching about the sacrifice of peace offerings that a person may present to the LORD.
If he presents it as a thank offering, he is to present with the thank offering unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well mixed with oil.
With his thank offering of peace offerings he is to present his offering with loaves of leavened bread.
From each kind of offering he is to present one portion as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offerings.
The flesh of his thank offering is to be eaten on the day it is presented. He is not to leave any of it until morning.
If his sacrifice is a vow or a freewill offering, it is to be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and what is left of it may be eaten the next day.
But what is left of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day is to be burned with fire.

If any of the flesh of his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not count for the one who presented it. It will be foul, and the person who eats of it will bear the consequences of his guilt.
Flesh that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It is to be burned with fire. As for other flesh, anyone who is clean may eat it,
but if anyone eats flesh from the LORD's peace offering while he is unclean, that person will be cut off from his people.

If anyone touches something unclean, whether human uncleanness or an unclean animal or any unclean detestable creature, and then eats flesh from the LORD's peace offering, that person will be cut off from his people."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: You are not to eat any fat of an ox, a sheep or a goat.
The fat of an animal that has died naturally or been torn by wild animals may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD will be cut off from his people.
Wherever you live, you are not to eat any blood, whether of bird or of animal.
Anyone who eats any blood will be cut off from his people."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: Whoever presents a peace offering to the LORD is to bring his offering to the LORD from the peace offering itself.
With his own hands he is to bring the LORD's food offerings. He is to bring the fat with the breast, so that the breast may be lifted up as an elevation offering before the LORD.
The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aaron and his sons.
You are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offerings.
The son of Aaron who presents the blood of the peace offerings and the fat will have the right thigh as his share.

For I have taken the breast that is lifted up and the thigh that is contributed from the Israelites, from their peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent due from the Israelites."
This is the portion of Aaron and of his sons from the food offerings to the LORD, from the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
The LORD commanded that the Israelites give this to them from the day he anointed them, as a permanent due through their generations.
This is the teaching about the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the installation offering and the peace offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams and the basket of unleavened bread,
and gather the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the community gathered at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the community, "This is what the LORD has commanded to be done."
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on Aaron and wrapped the sash around him, clothed him with the robe and put the ephod on him. He fastened the ephod on him with its woven waistband, tying it to him.
He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece.
He set the turban on his head, and on the turban, at the front, he set the gold plate, the sacred diadem, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and so consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him, to consecrate him.
Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, wrapped sashes around them and tied headbands on them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he brought the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

Moses slaughtered it, took the blood and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar all round, to purify the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. In this way he consecrated it, to make atonement for it.
He took all the fat that was on the entrails, the long lobe of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and Moses burned them on the altar.
But the bull, with its hide, its flesh and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it and splashed the blood against the sides of the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the head, the pieces and the fat.
He washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the second ram, the ram of installation, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it, took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

Moses also brought Aaron's sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses splashed the blood against the sides of the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat on the entrails, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf of oiled bread and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He put all these in the hands of Aaron and of his sons, and lifted them up as an elevation offering before the LORD.
Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. This was an installation offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and lifted it up as an elevation offering before the LORD. It was Moses' portion of the ram of installation, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the flesh at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of installation offerings, as I was commanded: 'Aaron and his sons are to eat it.'
What is left of the flesh and the bread you are to burn with fire.
You are not to go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your installation are completed, for it will take seven days to install you.
What has been done today the LORD has commanded to be done, to make atonement for you.
You are to stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and keep the charge of the LORD, so that you do not die, for so I have been commanded."
So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take a bull calf for your sin offering and a ram for your burnt offering, both without blemish, and present them before the LORD.
Then say to the Israelites: Take a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without blemish, for a burnt offering,
and an ox and a ram for peace offerings to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will appear to you."
They brought what Moses commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole community drew near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you."

Then Moses said to Aaron, "Come near to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Present the people's offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded."
So Aaron came near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.
Aaron's sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering he burned on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The flesh and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp.
Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.
They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and burned them with the burnt offering on the altar.
Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat of the sin offering that was for the people, slaughtered it and offered it for sin, like the first one.
He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the rule.
He presented the grain offering, took a handful of it and burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning's burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the sacrifice of peace offerings for the people. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, which he splashed against the sides of the altar.
The fat portions of the ox and of the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver,
they laid on the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar,
but the breasts and the right thigh Aaron lifted up as an elevation offering before the LORD, as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted up his hands towards the people and blessed them, and he came down after offering the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting, and when they came out they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.
Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, put fire in it and added incense, and they offered unauthorised fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them.
Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD meant when he said: 'Among those who are near me I will be shown to be holy, and before all the people I will be honoured.'" And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, and said to them, "Come near. Carry your cousins away from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp."
They came near and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose, and do not tear your clothes, or you will die and wrath will come on the whole community. But your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may mourn for those whom the LORD has burned.
Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the LORD's anointing oil is on you." They did as Moses said.
The LORD spoke to Aaron:
"You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a permanent rule through your generations,
so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
and teach the Israelites all the rulings that the LORD has given them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings to the LORD and eat it beside the altar, made without yeast, for it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons' share of the food offerings to the LORD, for so I have been commanded.

But the breast that was lifted up and the thigh that was contributed you may eat in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you, for they are given as your share and your children's share from the peace offerings of the Israelites.

They must bring the thigh that was contributed and the breast that was lifted up with the food offerings of fat, to lift up as an elevation offering before the LORD. It will be yours and your children's by a permanent rule, as the LORD has commanded."
When Moses enquired carefully about the goat of the sin offering, he found that it had been burned up, and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said,
"Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and it was given to you to carry the guilt of the community, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Since its blood was not brought into the inner part of the sanctuary, you should have eaten the goat in the sanctuary area, as I commanded."

Aaron said to Moses, "Today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and yet such things as these have happened to me! If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been acceptable to the LORD?"
When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"Tell the Israelites: These are the creatures you may eat among all the animals of the land.
You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, completely split, and that brings up its cud.
But among those that bring up the cud or have a divided hoof, you are not to eat these: the camel, because it brings up its cud but does not have a divided hoof, is unclean for you;
the hyrax, because it brings up its cud but does not have a divided hoof, is unclean for you;
the hare, because it brings up its cud but does not have a divided hoof, is unclean for you;
and the pig, because it has a divided hoof, completely split, but does not bring up the cud, is unclean for you.
You are not to eat their flesh or touch their carcasses. They are unclean for you.
Of everything that lives in the water, you may eat this: anything in the seas or in the rivers that has fins and scales.
But anything in the seas or rivers that does not have fins and scales, whether among the swarming creatures of the waters or among the other living things in them, is detestable to you.
They are to be detestable to you. You are not to eat their flesh, and you are to treat their carcasses as detestable.
Anything in the waters that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
These are the birds you are to treat as detestable. They are not to be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the black kite of any kind,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the long-eared owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
All winged insects that go on all fours are detestable to you.
But among the winged insects that go on all fours you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet, for hopping on the ground.
Of these you may eat: every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket and every kind of grasshopper.
But all other winged insects that have four feet are detestable to you.
By these you will become unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
and whoever picks up any of their carcasses is to wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every animal that has a divided hoof that is not completely split, or does not bring up the cud, is unclean for you. Whoever touches them will be unclean.
Of all the animals that go on all fours, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
and whoever picks up their carcasses is to wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
Of the creatures that swarm on the ground, these are unclean for you: the mole-rat, the mouse, every kind of large lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink and the chameleon.
Of all the swarming creatures, these are unclean for you. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of them falls when dead will become unclean, whether it is an article of wood, or clothing, or leather, or sacking, any article that is put to any use. It is to be put into water, and it will be unclean until evening, and then it will be clean.
If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean, and you are to break the pot.
Any food in it that could be eaten, on which water has come, will be unclean, and any drink that could be drunk from such a vessel will be unclean.
Anything on which any part of their carcass falls will be unclean. An oven or a stove is to be broken in pieces. They are unclean, and they are to be unclean for you.
But a spring or a cistern holding water will be clean, though whoever touches a carcass in it will be unclean.
If any part of their carcass falls on any seed meant for sowing, it is clean,
but if water has been put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
Whoever eats some of its carcass is to wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. Whoever picks up its carcass is to wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every creature that swarms on the ground is detestable. It is not to be eaten.
Whatever crawls on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or has many feet, all the creatures that swarm on the ground, you are not to eat, for they are detestable.
Do not make yourselves detestable by any swarming creature. Do not make yourselves unclean with them, so that you become unclean through them.
For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, for I am holy. You are not to make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that crawls on the ground.
For I am the LORD who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. You are to be holy, for I am holy.
This is the teaching about animals and birds and every living creature that moves in the water and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a boy, she will be unclean for seven days, as she is unclean during the days of her monthly period.
On the eighth day the boy's foreskin is to be circumcised.
Then she is to wait thirty-three days for her blood to be purified. She is not to touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as during her period. She is to wait sixty-six days for her blood to be purified.

When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or for a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
He is to offer it before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from the flow of her blood. This is the teaching for a woman who gives birth, to a male or a female.

If she cannot afford a lamb, she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest is to make atonement for her, and she will be clean."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:

"When someone has on the skin of his body a swelling, a scab or a bright spot, and it turns into a skin disease on his body, he is to be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

The priest is to examine the affected patch on the skin of his body. If the hair in the patch has turned white and the patch appears to be deeper than the skin of his body, it is a skin disease. When the priest has examined him, he is to declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on the skin of his body is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest is to keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to examine him again. If in his eyes the patch has not changed and has not spread on the skin, the priest is to keep him apart for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest is to examine him again. If the patch has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest is to declare him clean. It is only a scab. He is to wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the scab spreads on the skin after he has shown himself to the priest to be declared clean, he is to appear before the priest again.
The priest is to examine him, and if the scab has spread on the skin, the priest is to declare him unclean. It is a skin disease.
When a person has a skin disease, he is to be brought to the priest.
The priest is to examine him, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a long-standing skin disease on the skin of his body. The priest is to declare him unclean. He is not to keep him apart, for he is already unclean.
If the disease breaks out all over the skin and covers all the skin of the person with the patch, from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
then the priest is to examine him, and if the disease has covered his whole body, he is to declare the person with the patch clean. It has all turned white. He is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he will be unclean.
The priest is to examine the raw flesh and declare him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean. It is a skin disease.
But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he is to come to the priest,
and the priest is to examine him, and if the patch has turned white, the priest is to declare the person with the patch clean. He is clean.
When someone has a boil on the skin of his body and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, he is to show it to the priest.
The priest is to examine it, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest is to declare him unclean. It is a skin disease that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it and it is not deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest is to keep him apart for seven days.
If it is spreading on the skin, the priest is to declare him unclean. It is a disease.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the priest is to declare him clean.
Or when someone has a burn on the skin of his body and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white or white,

the priest is to examine it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest is to declare him unclean. It is a skin disease.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the bright spot and it is no deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest is to keep him apart for seven days,
and the priest is to examine him on the seventh day. If it is spreading on the skin, the priest is to declare him unclean. It is a skin disease.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to declare him clean, for it is the scar of the burn.
When a man or a woman has a sore on the head or on the beard,

the priest is to examine the sore. If it appears deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest is to declare the person unclean. It is a scall, a skin disease of the head or beard.
If the priest examines the scall and it does not appear deeper than the skin and there is no black hair in it, the priest is to keep the person with the scall apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to examine the sore. If the scall has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it and the scall does not appear deeper than the skin,
he is to shave, but the scall he is not to shave. The priest is to keep the person with the scall apart for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest is to examine the scall. If the scall has not spread in the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest is to declare him clean. He is to wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the scall spreads in the skin after he has been declared clean,
the priest is to examine him. If the scall has spread in the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair. He is unclean.
But if in his eyes the scall has not changed and black hair has grown in it, the scall is healed. He is clean, and the priest is to declare him clean.
When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,
the priest is to examine them. If the bright spots on the skin of the body are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin. He is clean.
If a man loses the hair from his head, he is bald. He is clean.
If he loses hair from the front of his head, he has a bald forehead. He is clean.
But if there is on the bald head or the bald forehead a reddish-white sore, it is a skin disease breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.
The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the sore is reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, like the appearance of a skin disease on the skin of the body,
he is a man with a skin disease. He is unclean. The priest is to declare him unclean. His sore is on his head.
The person with the skin disease who has the sore is to wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose. He is to cover his upper lip and call out, 'Unclean! Unclean!'
As long as he has the sore, he will be unclean. He is unclean. He is to live alone. His dwelling is to be outside the camp.
When there is a case of mould in a garment, whether a wool garment or a linen garment,
in warp or weft of linen or wool, or in leather or in anything made of leather,
if the affected spot is greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the leather, or in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather, it is a case of mould, and it is to be shown to the priest.
The priest is to examine the affected spot and keep the article apart for seven days.
He is to examine the spot on the seventh day. If it has spread in the garment, in the warp or the weft, or in the leather, whatever its use, the mould is persistent. It is unclean.
He is to burn the garment, whether the warp or the weft, in wool or linen, or any article of leather that has the mould, for it is persistent mould. It is to be burned in the fire.
But if the priest examines it and the spot has not spread in the garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather,
the priest is to command that they wash the article that has the mould, and he is to keep it apart for another seven days.

After it has been washed, the priest is to examine the spot. If the spot has not changed its appearance, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. You are to burn it in the fire, whether the rot is on the back or on the front.
If the priest examines it and the spot has faded after it has been washed, he is to tear the piece out of the garment or the leather, from the warp or from the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather, it is spreading. You are to burn with fire whatever has the mould.
But the garment, warp or weft, or any article of leather from which the mould disappears when you have washed it, is to be washed a second time, and it will be clean.
This is the teaching for a case of mould in a garment of wool or linen, either in warp or weft, or in any article of leather, for deciding whether it is clean or unclean.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"This is the teaching for the person with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing. He is to be brought to the priest.
The priest is to go outside the camp and examine him. If the skin disease has healed in the person,
the priest is to command that two live clean birds, cedar wood, crimson yarn and hyssop be brought for the one who is to be cleansed.
The priest is to command that one of the birds be slaughtered over fresh water in a clay vessel.
He is to take the live bird, with the cedar wood, the crimson yarn and the hyssop, and dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water.
He is to sprinkle the blood seven times on the one to be cleansed of the skin disease. Then he is to declare him clean and release the live bird into the open country.

The one to be cleansed is to wash his clothes, shave off all his hair and bathe in water, and he will be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he is to stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he is to shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, his eyebrows, all his hair. He is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.

On the eighth day he is to take two male lambs without blemish and one year-old ewe lamb without blemish, along with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who cleanses him is to present the one to be cleansed and these things before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to take one of the male lambs and bring it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil, and lift them up as an elevation offering before the LORD.

He is to slaughter the lamb in the place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, in the holy place. For the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the priest. It is most holy.
The priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest is to take some of the log of oil and pour it into the palm of his own left hand,
and dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.

Some of the oil that remains in his hand the priest is to put on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest's hand he is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed. In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD.
The priest is to offer the sin offering, to make atonement for the one to be cleansed from his uncleanness. Afterwards he is to slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest is to offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

But if he is poor and cannot afford so much, he is to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be lifted up, to make atonement for him, and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whatever he can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he is to bring them for his cleansing to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
The priest is to take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and lift them up as an elevation offering before the LORD.

He is to slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand,
and with his right finger the priest is to sprinkle some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before the LORD.

The priest is to put some of the oil that is in his hand on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, in the place where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
The rest of the oil that is in the priest's hand he is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
He is to offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whatever he can afford,
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with a grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the one to be cleansed.
This is the teaching for the one who has a skin disease and who cannot afford the usual offering for his cleansing."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a case of mould in a house in the land you possess,
the owner of the house is to come and tell the priest, 'Something like mould has appeared in my house.'

The priest is to command that they empty the house before the priest goes in to examine the mould, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterwards the priest is to go in to examine the house.
He is to examine the mould, and if the mould in the walls of the house has greenish or reddish depressions and appears to be deeper than the wall,
the priest is to go out of the house to the doorway and close up the house for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to return and examine it. If the mould has spread in the walls of the house,
the priest is to command that they take out the stones with the mould in them and throw them into an unclean place outside the city.
He is to have the inside of the house scraped all round, and the plaster that is scraped off is to be dumped in an unclean place outside the city.
They are to take other stones and put them in the place of those stones, and take other plaster and plaster the house.
If the mould breaks out again in the house, after he has taken out the stones and scraped the house and plastered it,
the priest is to go and examine it. If the mould has spread in the house, it is persistent mould in the house. It is unclean.
He is to tear down the house, its stones and timber and all the plaster of the house, and take them out of the city to an unclean place.
Whoever enters the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening,
and whoever sleeps in the house is to wash his clothes, and whoever eats in the house is to wash his clothes.
But if the priest comes and examines it, and the mould has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest is to declare the house clean, for the mould is healed.
To cleanse the house he is to take two birds, with cedar wood, crimson yarn and hyssop,
and slaughter one of the birds in a clay vessel over fresh water.
He is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the crimson yarn and the live bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
In this way he is to cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, with the fresh water, with the live bird, and with the cedar wood, the hyssop and the crimson yarn.
He is to let the live bird go out of the city into the open country. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean."
This is the teaching for every case of skin disease, for a scall,
for mould in a garment or in a house,
for a swelling, a scab or a bright spot,
to teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the teaching for skin disease and mould.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"Tell the Israelites: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This is the rule of his uncleanness for a discharge: whether his body runs with the discharge or is blocked by it, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with a discharge lies will be unclean, and everything on which he sits will be unclean.
Whoever touches his bed is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on anything on which the man with the discharge has sat is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
An earthenware vessel that the man with the discharge touches is to be broken, and every wooden vessel is to be rinsed in water.
When the man with a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, he is to count seven days for his cleansing. He is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water, and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD to the entrance of the tent of meeting and give them to the priest.
The priest is to offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he is to bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
Every garment and every piece of leather on which the semen falls is to be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and has an emission of semen, both are to bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge in her body is blood, she will be in her monthly uncleanness for seven days, and whoever touches her will be unclean until evening.
Everything on which she lies during her uncleanness will be unclean, and everything on which she sits will be unclean.
Whoever touches her bed is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches anything on which she sits is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or anything on which she sits, when he touches it he will be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her monthly uncleanness is on him, he will be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies will be unclean.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days when it is not the time of her monthly uncleanness, or if she has a discharge that continues beyond that time, all the days of her unclean discharge she will be unclean, as in the days of her monthly uncleanness.

Every bed on which she lies all the days of her discharge will be to her like the bed of her monthly uncleanness, and everything on which she sits will be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her monthly period.
Whoever touches these things will be unclean and is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
But if she is cleansed of her discharge, she is to count seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
In this way you are to keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my tabernacle, which is in their midst.
This is the teaching for the man who has a discharge and for the man who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean by it,
and for the woman who is unwell with her monthly uncleanness, for anyone, male or female, who has a discharge, and for the man who lies with a woman who is unclean."
The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they came near the presence of the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come at just any time into the Holy Place, inside the curtain, in front of the cover of atonement that is on the ark, or he will die. For I appear in the cloud over the cover of atonement.
This is how Aaron is to enter the Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He is to put on the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body, wrap the linen sash round him and put on the linen turban. These are sacred garments. He is to bathe his body in water before he puts them on.
From the community of the Israelites he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron is to present the bull as a sin offering for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He is to take the two goats and place them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to cast lots for the two goats, one lot for the LORD and the other for Azazel.
Aaron is to bring forward the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell is to be presented alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it by sending it away into the wilderness to Azazel.
Aaron is to bring forward the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household. He is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
He is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the curtain.
He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense will cover the cover of atonement that is over the Testimony, or he will die.

He is to take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the cover of atonement, and in front of the cover he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

Then he is to slaughter the goat of the sin offering for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He is to do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on the cover of atonement and in front of it.

In this way he is to make atonement for the Holy Place because of the uncleanness of the Israelites and their rebellions, all their wrongs. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which remains with them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time he goes in to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out. He is to make atonement for himself, for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel.
Then he is to go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the blood of the bull and of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all round.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, to cleanse it and to consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
When he has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.

Aaron is to lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the guilt of the Israelites, all their rebellions, all their wrongs. He is to place them on the goat's head and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
The goat will carry all their guilt on itself to a barren land, and the man is to release the goat in the wilderness.
Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he put on when he went into the Holy Place, and leave them there.

He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place, put on his own garments and come out, and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
The fat of the sin offering he is to burn on the altar.
The man who released the goat to Azazel is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterwards he may come into the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Holy Place, are to be taken outside the camp, and their hides, their flesh and their dung are to be burned with fire.
The man who burns them is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterwards he may come into the camp.
This is to be a permanent rule for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you are to humble yourselves and do no work at all, whether native-born or a foreigner living among you,
because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you. You will be clean before the LORD from all your wrongs.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to humble yourselves. It is a permanent rule.
The priest who is anointed and installed to serve as priest in place of his father is to make atonement. He is to put on the linen garments, the sacred garments.
He is to make atonement for the Most Holy Place, for the tent of meeting and for the altar, and he is to make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This is to be a permanent rule for you: atonement is to be made for the Israelites once a year because of all their wrongs." And Moses did as the LORD commanded him.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and tell them: This is what the LORD has commanded:
Any Israelite who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat, whether inside the camp or outside it,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD in front of the LORD's tabernacle, will be held guilty of bloodshed. He has shed blood, and he is to be cut off from his people.

This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they now make in the open country. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest is to splash the blood against the LORD's altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat-demons to whom they have been unfaithful. This is to be a permanent rule for them and their descendants.
Say to them: Any Israelite or any foreigner living among them who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that person is to be cut off from his people.
If anyone from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood and cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives. It is the blood, as life, that makes atonement.
That is why I have said to the Israelites: None of you may eat blood, and no foreigner living among you may eat blood.
Any Israelite or any foreigner living among them who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten is to pour out its blood and cover it with earth,

because the life of every creature is its blood. That is why I have said to the Israelites: You are not to eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Anyone who eats it is to be cut off.

Anyone, native-born or foreigner, who eats an animal that has died naturally or been torn by wild animals is to wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening. Then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe his body, he will bear the consequences of his guilt."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God.
You are not to do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you are not to do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. You are not to follow their customs.
You are to keep my rulings and observe my statutes, walking by them. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and my rulings. The person who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
None of you is to approach any close relative to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father, which is the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother. You are not to uncover her nakedness.
