You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It is your father's nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, whether born in the same house or elsewhere.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She is your father's close relative.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close relative.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, that is, you are not to approach his wife. She is your aunt.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife. You are not to uncover her nakedness.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It is your brother's nakedness.

You are not to uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, and you are not to take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are close relatives. It is a shameful act.
You are not to take a woman as a rival to her sister, uncovering her nakedness in addition to the other while she is still alive.
You are not to approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she is in the uncleanness of her monthly period.
You are not to have intercourse with your neighbour's wife and so make yourself unclean with her.
You are not to give any of your children to be passed over to Molek, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You are not to lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is abhorrent.
You are not to have intercourse with any animal and so make yourself unclean with it. A woman is not to stand before an animal to mate with it. It is a perversion.
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these the nations that I am driving out before you have become unclean.
The land became unclean, so I called it to account for its guilt, and the land spewed out its inhabitants.
But you are to keep my statutes and my rulings and not do any of these abhorrent things, neither the native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you
(for the people who were in the land before you did all these abhorrent things, and the land became unclean),
so that the land will not spew you out when you make it unclean, as it spewed out the nation that was before you.
For anyone who does any of these abhorrent things, the persons who do them will be cut off from among their people.
Keep my charge, then, and do not practise any of the abhorrent customs that were practised before you, and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the whole community of the Israelites and tell them: You are to be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you is to revere his mother and his father, and you are to keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols or make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you offer a peace offering to the LORD, offer it so that it is accepted for you.
It is to be eaten on the day you offer it, or on the next day. Whatever is left until the third day is to be burned.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is foul. It will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear the consequences of his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person is to be cut off from his people.
When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap right to the edges of your field, and do not gather the leftover ears of your harvest.
Do not strip your vineyard a second time or gather the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not deceive one another.
Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not exploit your neighbour or rob him. Do not keep a hired worker's wages with you overnight until morning.
Do not curse the deaf or place an obstacle in front of the blind, but fear your God. I am the LORD.
Do not distort justice. Do not favour the poor or defer to the powerful, but judge your neighbour with fairness.
Do not go about spreading slander among your people. Do not stand by while your neighbour's life is at stake. I am the LORD.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. You must reason frankly with your neighbour, so that you do not share in his guilt.
Do not take revenge or hold a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbour as yourself. I am the LORD.
Keep my statutes. Do not breed two kinds of your livestock together. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear a garment made of two kinds of material.
If a man lies with a woman who is a slave, promised to another man but not yet bought back or given her freedom, there is to be an inquiry. They are not to be put to death, because she was not free.
The man is to bring a ram to the entrance of the tent of meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD.
The priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for the wrong he has done, and he will be forgiven the wrong he has done.
When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, you are to treat its fruit as forbidden for three years. It is not to be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield will increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
Do not eat anything with the blood still in it. Do not practise divination or look for omens.
Do not trim the hair at the sides of your head or cut off the edges of your beard.
Do not cut your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with shameful acts.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or seek out spirit-consulters, for you will be made unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.
Rise in the presence of the grey-haired, honour the elderly and fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not wrong him.
The foreigner who lives with you is to be treated like the native-born among you. Love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not use dishonest standards in measuring length, weight or quantity.
Use honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my statutes and all my rulings and do them. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Say to the Israelites: Any Israelite or any foreigner living in Israel who gives any of his children to Molek is to be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from his people, because he has given his children to Molek, making my sanctuary unclean and profaning my holy name.
If the people of the land close their eyes when that man gives one of his children to Molek and do not put him to death,
I myself will set my face against that man and his clan, and I will cut off from their people both him and all who follow him in being unfaithful to me by going after Molek.
If anyone turns to mediums and spirit-consulters, being unfaithful by going after them, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from his people.
Consecrate yourselves and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother is to be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother. His blood is on his own head.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, with the wife of his neighbour, both the adulterer and the adulteress are to be put to death.
If a man lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them are to be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them are to be put to death. They have committed a perversion. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done what is abhorrent. They are to be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man takes a woman and her mother as wives, it is a shameful act. He and they are to be burned with fire, so that there will be no shameful act among you.
If a man has intercourse with an animal, he is to be put to death, and you are to kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you are to kill the woman and the animal. They are to be put to death. Their blood is on their own heads.

If a man takes his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his, it is a disgrace. They are to be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness. He will bear the consequences of his guilt.

If a man lies with a woman during her monthly period and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed the source of her flow, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them are to be cut off from their people.
You are not to uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, for that is to expose a close relative. They will bear the consequences of their guilt.
If a man lies with his uncle's wife, he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They will bear the consequences of their sin. They will die childless.
If a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They will be childless.
Keep all my statutes and all my rulings and do them, so that the land to which I am bringing you to live will not spew you out.
You are not to follow the customs of the nation that I am driving out before you. They did all these things, and so I came to loathe them.
But I have said to you: You will inherit their land. I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.

So you are to make a distinction between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean. Do not make yourselves abhorrent by an animal or a bird or anything that crawls on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You are to be holy to me, for I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the peoples to be mine.
A man or a woman who is a medium or a spirit-consulter among you is to be put to death. They are to be stoned. Their blood is on their own heads."
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them: A priest is not to make himself unclean for any dead person among his people,
except for his nearest relatives: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
or his unmarried sister who is close to him because she has had no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.
He is not to make himself unclean for those related to him by marriage, and so profane himself.
Priests are not to shave their heads, trim the edges of their beards or cut gashes in their flesh.
They are to be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. For they present the food offerings of the LORD, the food of their God, and so they must be holy.
They are not to marry a woman made unclean by prostitution or a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You are to treat him as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, for I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy.
If a priest's daughter profanes herself by prostitution, she profanes her father. She is to be burned with fire.

The high priest, who is greater than his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been installed to wear the sacred garments, is not to let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes.
He must not go near any dead body. He is not to make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He is not to leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.
He is to marry a woman who is a virgin.
A widow, a divorced woman, or a woman made unclean by prostitution, these he is not to marry. He is to take as his wife a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not profane his offspring among his people. I am the LORD who makes him holy."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Say to Aaron: For all generations to come, no descendant of yours who has a defect may approach to present the food of his God.
No man who has a defect may approach: no one who is blind or lame, or has a disfigured face or a limb that is too long,
no man with a broken foot or a broken hand,
or who is a hunchback or a dwarf, or who has a defect in his eye, or who has an itching disease or scabs or damaged testicles.
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect is to come forward to present the food offerings to the LORD. He has a defect. He is not to come forward to present the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, the most holy as well as the holy,
but he is not to go in to the curtain or come near the altar, because he has a defect. He must not profane my sanctuaries, for I am the LORD who makes them holy."
So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with care the holy gifts of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them: For all generations to come, if any one of your descendants approaches the holy gifts that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while he is unclean, that person will be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.

If any descendant of Aaron has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat any of the holy gifts until he is clean. Likewise if he touches anything made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
or if he touches any swarming creature by which he is made unclean, or any person by whom he is made unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be,
the person who touches any such thing will be unclean until evening. He is not to eat any of the holy gifts unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down, he will be clean, and afterwards he may eat the holy gifts, for they are his food.
He is not to eat what has died naturally or been torn by wild animals, and so make himself unclean by it. I am the LORD.
The priests are to keep my charge, so that they do not bring guilt on themselves and die by treating it with contempt. I am the LORD who makes them holy.
No outsider may eat the holy gift. A priest's guest or hired worker may not eat the holy gift.
But if a priest buys a person with his money, that person may eat it, and so may those born in his house. They may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries a man who is not a priest, she may not eat the contribution of the holy gifts.
But if a priest's daughter is a widow or divorced and has no child, and she returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat her father's food. No outsider may eat it.
If anyone eats a holy gift by mistake, he is to add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy gift to the priest.
The priests are not to profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD,
by letting them eat the holy gifts and so bringing on them guilt that requires repayment. I am the LORD who makes them holy."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and tell them: If any of you, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living in Israel, presents an offering for a burnt offering to the LORD, in fulfilment of a vow or as a freewill offering,
to be accepted for you it must be a male without defect, from the cattle, the sheep or the goats.
You are not to present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted for you.

When someone presents a peace offering to the LORD from the herd or the flock, in fulfilment of a special vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without defect to be accepted. There must be no blemish in it.

Animals that are blind, injured or maimed, or that have a discharge or scabs or an itching disease, you are not to present to the LORD. You are not to put any of them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.
You may present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep that has a limb too long or too short, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
You are not to present to the LORD any animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn or cut. You are not to do this in your land,
and you are not to accept any such animals from a foreigner to offer as the food of your God. Because they are deformed and have defects, they will not be accepted for you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"When an ox, a sheep or a goat is born, it is to stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on it will be accepted as a food offering to the LORD.
You are not to slaughter an ox or a sheep and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.
It is to be eaten on the same day. You are not to leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep my commands and do them. I am the LORD.
Do not profane my holy name, so that I may be treated as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who makes you holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are my appointed festivals, the appointed festivals of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a sacred assembly. You are not to do any work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your homes.
These are the LORD's appointed festivals, the sacred assemblies you are to proclaim at their appointed times:
The LORD's Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month the LORD's Festival of Unleavened Bread begins. For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.
For seven days you are to present a food offering to the LORD. On the seventh day there is to be a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring to the priest a sheaf of the first of your harvest.
He is to lift the sheaf before the LORD so that it may be accepted for you. The priest is to lift it on the day after the Sabbath.
On the day you lift the sheaf you are to offer a year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD,
with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, a food offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, and its drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
You are not to eat any bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is a permanent rule through all your generations, in all your homes.
From the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the elevation offering, you are to count seven full weeks.
You are to count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
From your homes you are to bring two loaves to be lifted up, made of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with yeast, as first produce for the LORD.

With the bread you are to present seven year-old male lambs without defect, one young bull and two rams. They are to be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Then you are to offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old male lambs as a peace offering.
The priest is to lift them up with the bread of the first produce as an elevation offering before the LORD, together with the two lambs. They are to be holy to the LORD for the priest.
On that same day you are to proclaim a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work. This is a permanent rule through all your generations, in all your homes.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap right to the edges of your field, and do not gather the leftover ears of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of rest, a remembrance marked by trumpet blasts, a sacred assembly.
You are not to do any ordinary work, but you are to present a food offering to the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You are to hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves, and present a food offering to the LORD.
You are not to do any work on that day, because it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
Anyone who does not humble himself on that day is to be cut off from his people.
Anyone who does any work on that day, I will destroy from among his people.
You are not to do any work at all. This is a permanent rule through all your generations, in all your homes.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to keep your Sabbath."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month the LORD's Festival of Booths begins, and it lasts for seven days.
The first day is a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.

For seven days you are to present food offerings to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is a closing assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.

These are the LORD's appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies, to present food offerings to the LORD: burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its own day,
in addition to the LORD's Sabbaths, and in addition to your gifts, and in addition to all your vows and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you are to keep the festival of the LORD for seven days. The first day is a day of complete rest, and the eighth day is a day of complete rest.
On the first day you are to take the fruit of splendid trees, palm branches, boughs of leafy trees and willows of the stream, and you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You are to keep it as a festival to the LORD for seven days in the year. It is a permanent rule through all your generations. You are to keep it in the seventh month.
You are to live in booths for seven days. All the native-born in Israel are to live in booths,
so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses declared to the Israelites the appointed festivals of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of crushed olives for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually.
Outside the curtain of the Testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron is to tend it from evening to morning before the LORD continually. This is a permanent rule through your generations.
He is to tend the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
Set them in two rows, six in each row, on the table of pure gold before the LORD.
Put pure frankincense on each row, so that it may be a memorial portion for the bread, a food offering to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day he is to set it out before the LORD regularly, as a lasting covenant on behalf of the Israelites.
It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him, a portion from the food offerings to the LORD, a permanent due."
Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites. A fight broke out in the camp between this son of an Israelite woman and an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until the decision of the LORD could be made clear to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the whole community is to stone him.
Tell the Israelites: Anyone who curses his God will bear the consequences of his guilt.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD is to be put to death. The whole community is to stone him. Whether foreigner or native-born, when he blasphemes the Name he is to be put to death.
Anyone who takes the life of a human being is to be put to death.
Anyone who takes the life of an animal is to make it good, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbour, as he has done it is to be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever injury he has inflicted on another is to be inflicted on him.
Whoever kills an animal is to make it good, but whoever kills a human being is to be put to death.
You are to have one rule for the foreigner and for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God."
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land itself is to keep a Sabbath for the LORD.
For six years you may sow your field, and for six years you may prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
But in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath for the LORD. You are not to sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You are not to reap what grows by itself from your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines. It is to be a year of complete rest for the land.
Whatever the land yields during its Sabbath will be food for you, for yourself, for your male and female servants, for your hired worker and the resident foreigner who lives with you,
and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce may be eaten.
You are to count off seven Sabbath years, seven times seven years, so that the seven Sabbath years add up to forty-nine years.
Then you are to sound the ram's horn loudly on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you are to sound the horn throughout your land.

You are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim release throughout the land for all who live in it. It is to be a Jubilee for you. Each of you is to return to his own holding, and each to his own clan.
The fiftieth year is to be a Jubilee for you. You are not to sow, or reap what grows by itself, or gather the grapes of the untended vines.
For it is a Jubilee. It is to be holy to you. You may eat only what the fields produce.
In this Year of Jubilee each of you is to return to his own holding.
If you sell anything to your neighbour or buy anything from him, you are not to wrong one another.
You are to buy from your neighbour according to the number of years since the Jubilee, and he is to sell to you according to the number of years of crops that remain.
If the years are many, you are to increase the price, and if the years are few, you are to reduce the price, because what he is selling you is a number of harvests.
You are not to wrong one another, but fear your God. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and my rulings and do them, and you will live securely in the land.
The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live there securely.
If you ask, 'What will we eat in the seventh year, if we do not sow or gather our produce?'
I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that it yields a crop for three years.
In the eighth year you will sow, and you will eat from the old crop until the ninth year, until its produce comes in. You will eat the old crop until then.
The land is not to be sold permanently, for the land is mine. You are only foreigners and tenants with me.
In all the land you hold, you are to allow redemption of the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his holding, his nearest relative is to come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it, but he prospers and gains enough to redeem it himself,
he is to count the years since the sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his holding.
But if he does not gain enough to repay him, what he sold will stay in the hands of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. It will be released in the Jubilee, and he may return to his holding.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he has the right of redemption until a full year after its sale. For a full year he has the right of redemption.
If it is not redeemed within a full year, the house in the walled city will pass permanently to the buyer and his descendants. It will not be released in the Jubilee.
But the houses of villages that have no surrounding wall are to be treated as part of the open country. They may be redeemed, and they are released in the Jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right of redemption of the houses in the cities they hold.
Whatever one of the Levites redeems, a house sold in a city that they hold, will be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their holding among the Israelites.
But the open pasture land around their cities is not to be sold, for it is their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, you are to support him, as you would a foreigner or a resident, so that he can live among you.
Do not take interest or profit from him, but fear your God, so that your brother may live among you.
You are not to lend him your money at interest, or give him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you are not to make him work as a slave.
He is to be with you as a hired worker and a resident. He is to serve you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then he and his children with him are to go free from you, and he will return to his clan and to the holding of his ancestors.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They are not to be sold as slaves.
You are not to rule over him harshly, but fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves whom you may have, you may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy from the children of the foreign residents who live with you, and from their families who are with you, who have been born in your land. They may become your property.

You may leave them to your children after you as a holding, to inherit as property. You may make them work for you permanently. But over your brothers, the Israelites, you are not to rule one over another harshly.
If a foreigner or resident who lives with you grows rich, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the foreigner who lives with you, or to a member of the foreigner's clan,
he has the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle, or his uncle's son may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

He is to reckon with the one who bought him, from the year he sold himself to him until the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale is to be set according to the number of years, as the days of a hired worker are with him.
If there are many years left, he is to pay back part of his purchase price in proportion to them as his redemption.
If there are only a few years left until the Year of Jubilee, he is to reckon with him, and pay back the price of his redemption in proportion to his years.
He is to be with him like a worker hired year by year. He is not to rule over him harshly in your sight.
If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children with him are to go free in the Year of Jubilee,
for the Israelites are my servants. They are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

"You are not to make idols for yourselves, or set up a carved image or a standing stone for yourselves, or place a stone carved with figures in your land to bow down before it. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you walk by my statutes and keep my commands and do them,
I will give you your rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will yield their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until the time of sowing. You will eat your bread until you are full and live securely in your land.
I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will remove wild animals from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn towards you and make you fruitful and many, and I will keep my covenant with you.
You will be eating the old harvest, stored long, and you will have to clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will place my dwelling among you, and I will not reject you.
I will walk among you, and I will be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
But if you do not listen to me and do not do all these commands,
if you reject my statutes, and if you despise my rulings so that you do not do all my commands, and so break my covenant,

then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring on you sudden terror, wasting disease and fever that will make the eyes fail and the life ebb away. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is chasing you.
If after all this you still do not listen to me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
I will break your proud strength, and I will make the sky above you like iron and the earth beneath you like bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain, because your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not yield their fruit.
If you walk in opposition to me and refuse to listen to me, I will bring seven times more plagues on you, in keeping with your sins.
I will send wild animals among you, and they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock and make you so few that your roads will be deserted.
If by these things you are not corrected and you walk in opposition to me,
I myself will walk in opposition to you, and I myself will strike you seven times for your sins.
I will bring a sword on you to carry out the vengeance of the covenant. When you gather in your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be handed over to the enemy.
When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven, and they will bring your bread back by weight. You will eat, but you will not be satisfied.
If in spite of this you do not listen to me, but walk in opposition to me,
then I will walk in fury against you, and I myself will discipline you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense stands, and I will heap your corpses on the lifeless bodies of your idols, and I will loathe you.
I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will not smell your pleasing aromas.
I myself will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled.
I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw a sword after you. Your land will be a desolation, and your cities will be ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths all the days that it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
All the days that it lies desolate it will have the rest that it did not have on your Sabbaths when you lived in it.

As for those of you who are left, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will chase them, and they will flee as if fleeing from a sword, and they will fall when no one is chasing them.
They will stumble over one another as if before a sword, though no one is chasing them. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
Those of you who are left will rot away in the lands of your enemies because of their guilt, and because of the guilt of their ancestors they will rot away with them.
But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their ancestors, the unfaithfulness they showed towards me and the opposition they showed towards me,
which made me walk in opposition to them and bring them into the land of their enemies, if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they accept the punishment for their guilt,
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I will remember, and I will remember the land.

For the land will be left by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will accept the punishment for their guilt, because they rejected my rulings and their souls loathed my statutes.
Yet even then, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or loathe them so as to destroy them, breaking my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD."
These are the statutes, the rulings and the teachings that the LORD made between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai, through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When someone makes a special vow, the persons are to be the LORD's according to your valuation.
The valuation of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old is to be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
If the person is a female, your valuation is to be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, your valuation for a male is to be twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If the person is from one month old up to five years old, your valuation for a male is to be five shekels of silver, and for a female your valuation is to be three shekels of silver.
If the person is sixty years old or more, your valuation for a male is to be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

If the one who made the vow is too poor to pay your valuation, he is to be brought before the priest, and the priest is to value him. The priest is to set the valuation according to what the one who made the vow can afford.
If it is an animal that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, everything that any such person gives to the LORD is holy.
He is not to replace it or exchange it, a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If he does exchange one animal for another, then both it and its substitute will be holy.
If it is any unclean animal that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, he is to bring the animal before the priest,
and the priest is to value it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest values it, so it will be.
If he wishes to redeem it, he is to add a fifth to your valuation.
When a man dedicates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest is to value it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest values it, so it will stand.
If the one who dedicated it wishes to redeem his house, he is to add a fifth to your valuation, and it will be his.
If a man dedicates to the LORD part of the field that is his holding, your valuation is to be according to the seed needed for it: a homer of barley seed is to be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
If he dedicates his field from the Year of Jubilee, your valuation is to stand.
But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to reckon the price according to the years that remain until the next Year of Jubilee, and it is to be deducted from your valuation.
If the one who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, he is to add a fifth to your valuation, and it will be his.
But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it may not be redeemed any more.
When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD, like a field devoted. It will become the holding of the priest.
If he dedicates to the LORD a field that he has bought, which is not part of his own holding,
the priest is to reckon the amount of your valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man is to pay your valuation on that day as something holy to the LORD.
In the Year of Jubilee the field is to return to the one from whom it was bought, to the one whose holding the land was.
Every valuation is to be by the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
But a firstborn of the animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the LORD, no one may dedicate. Whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.
If it is an unclean animal, he may buy it back at your valuation, and add a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at your valuation.
But nothing that a man devotes to the LORD, of all that he has, whether man or animal or field of his holding, may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is most holy to the LORD.
No person devoted, who is to be devoted to destruction from among mankind, may be ransomed. He is to be put to death.
All the tithe of the land, whether of the grain of the land or of the fruit of the trees, is the LORD's. It is holy to the LORD.
If a man wishes to redeem some of his tithe, he is to add a fifth to it.
Every tithe of herd and flock, every tenth animal that passes under the rod, is to be holy to the LORD.
He is not to look to see whether it is good or bad, and he is not to exchange it. If he does exchange it, both it and its substitute will be holy. They may not be redeemed."
These are the commands that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt:
"Take a census of the whole community of the Israelites, by their clans and their families, counting every male by name, one by one.
You and Aaron are to number all in Israel who are twenty years old or more and able to go out to war, company by company.
One man from each tribe, the head of his family, is to be with you.
These are the names of the men who are to stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph, from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Okran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These were the ones called from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes. They were the heads of the clans of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named by name,

and they gathered the whole community together on the first day of the second month. The people declared their ancestry by clans and families, and the men twenty years old or more were counted by name, one by one,
as the LORD had commanded Moses. So he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.
The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, one by one, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.
The descendants of Simeon: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, one by one, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.
The descendants of Gad: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
The descendants of Judah: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
The descendants of Issachar: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
The descendants of Zebulun: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.
The descendants of Joseph, first the descendants of Ephraim: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
The descendants of Manasseh: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
The descendants of Benjamin: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
The descendants of Dan: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
The descendants of Asher: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
The descendants of Naphtali: all the men twenty years old or more who could go out to war were counted by name, by their clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
These were the ones counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, each one standing for his family.
All the Israelites twenty years old or more who could go out to war in Israel were counted by their families.
The total number counted was 603,550.
But the Levites were not counted among them by their ancestral tribe.
For the LORD had spoken to Moses:
"Only the tribe of Levi you are not to count. You are not to include them in the census of the Israelites.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the Testimony, over all its furnishings and all that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, and they are to tend it. They are to camp round the tabernacle.
When the tabernacle is to move on, the Levites are to take it down, and when the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites are to put it up. Any outsider who comes near it is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to camp by divisions, each man in his own camp and each under his own standard.
But the Levites are to camp round the tabernacle of the Testimony, so that no wrath will fall on the community of the Israelites. The Levites are to keep guard over the tabernacle of the Testimony."
The Israelites did this. They did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"The Israelites are to camp round the tent of meeting at some distance from it, each under his own standard, under the banners of their families.
On the east side, towards the sunrise, are to camp the divisions of the camp of Judah under their standard. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His division, those counted, numbers 74,600.
Next to him the tribe of Issachar is to camp. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His division, those counted, numbers 54,400.
Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His division, those counted, numbers 57,400.
All those counted in the camp of Judah, by their divisions, number 186,400. They are to set out first.
On the south side are to be the divisions of the camp of Reuben under their standard. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His division, those counted, numbers 46,500.
Next to him the tribe of Simeon is to camp. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His division, those counted, numbers 59,300.
Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Deuel.
His division, those counted, numbers 45,650.
All those counted in the camp of Reuben, by their divisions, number 151,450. They are to set out second.
Then the tent of meeting is to set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they are to set out, each in his place, by his standard.
On the west side are to be the divisions of the camp of Ephraim under their standard. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His division, those counted, numbers 40,500.
Next to him the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His division, those counted, numbers 32,200.
Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His division, those counted, numbers 35,400.
All those counted in the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions, number 108,100. They are to set out third.
On the north side are to be the divisions of the camp of Dan under their standard. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His division, those counted, numbers 62,700.
Next to him the tribe of Asher is to camp. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Okran.
His division, those counted, numbers 41,500.
Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His division, those counted, numbers 53,400.
All those counted in the camp of Dan number 157,600. They are to set out last, under their standards."
These are the Israelites, counted by their families. All those counted in the camps, by their divisions, were 603,550.
But the Levites were not counted among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each by his clan and his family.
These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, whom he installed to serve as priests.

But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorised fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Bring the tribe of Levi near and present them to Aaron the priest, so that they may serve him.
They are to carry out duties for him and for the whole community before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
They are to guard all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, and carry out duties for the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.
You are to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given to him, given from among the Israelites.
You are to appoint Aaron and his sons to keep their priesthood. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are mine,

for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, of people and of animals. They are to be mine. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai:
"Count the Levites by their families and clans. You are to count every male from a month old and upwards."
So Moses counted them, as he was commanded by the word of the LORD.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their families.
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These were the clans of the Gershonites.
Those counted, every male from a month old and upwards, numbered 7,500.
The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
The leader of the family of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
At the tent of meeting the Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its ropes, with all the work connected with them.
To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These were the clans of the Kohathites.
Counting every male from a month old and upwards, there were 8,600, responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the family of the clans of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the utensils of the sanctuary with which the priests serve, the screen, and all the work connected with them.
The chief of the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He was appointed over those who were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These were the clans of Merari.
Those counted, every male from a month old and upwards, numbered 6,200.
The leader of the family of the clans of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The appointed duty of the Merarites was the care of the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its posts and its bases, all its equipment and all the work connected with them,
and the posts of the courtyard round it with their bases, their pegs and their ropes.

Moses and Aaron and his sons were to camp in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting, responsible for the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
All the Levites who were counted, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD's command by their clans, every male from a month old and upwards, numbered 22,000.
The LORD said to Moses, "Count all the firstborn males of the Israelites from a month old and upwards, and take the number of their names.
Take the Levites for me in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites. I am the LORD."
So Moses counted all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
The total of the firstborn males from a month old and upwards, counted by name, was 22,273.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD.
For the redemption of the 273 firstborn of the Israelites who are more than the number of the Levites,
you are to take five shekels for each one, by the shekel of the sanctuary (a shekel is twenty gerahs).
Give the money for the redemption of those who are in excess to Aaron and his sons."
Moses took the redemption money from those who were in excess of those redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the silver, 1,365 shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, at the word of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty, all who come to take part in the work of the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the Kohathites in the tent of meeting: the care of the most holy things.
When the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons are to go in and take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
They are to put over it a covering of fine leather, and spread a cloth of pure blue on top, and put its poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and put on it the plates, the dishes, the bowls and the flagons for the drink offering. The regular bread is to remain on it.
They are to spread over them a crimson cloth and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its trays and all its oil vessels, with which they supply it.
They are to put it with all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and place it on the carrying frame.
Over the golden altar they are to spread a blue cloth and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take all the utensils of the service with which they serve in the sanctuary and put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather and place them on the carrying frame.
They are to clear the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

They are to put on it all the utensils with which they serve there: the fire pans, the flesh-forks, the shovels and the sprinkling bowls, all the utensils of the altar. They are to spread over it a covering of fine leather and put its poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary, when the camp is ready to set out, the Kohathites are to come to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things in the tent of meeting that the Kohathites are to carry.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil, with the oversight of the whole tabernacle and all that is in it, the sanctuary and its furnishings."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"Do not let the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites.
So that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his work and his load.
But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take a census of the Gershonites also, by their families and clans.
You are to count the men from thirty years old up to fifty, all who come to take part in the work of the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites, in serving and in carrying:
they are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, its covering and the covering of fine leather that is on top of it, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

and the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the gate of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and their ropes and all the equipment for their service. They are to do all that needs to be done with them.

All the service of the Gershonites, in all their carrying and in all their work, is to be under the direction of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign to them as their responsibility all that they are to carry.
This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and their duties are to be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
As for the Merarites, you are to count them by their clans and families.
You are to count them from thirty years old up to fifty, all who come to take part in the work of the tent of meeting.
This is what they are responsible for carrying, as the whole of their service in the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its posts and its bases,

and the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, their pegs and their ropes, with all their equipment and all their service. You are to assign by name the things they are responsible for carrying.
This is the service of the clans of the Merarites, for all their work in the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."
Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty, all who came to take part in the work of the tent of meeting.
Those counted by their clans numbered 2,750.
This was the total of those counted from the clans of the Kohathites, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD's command through Moses.
Those of the Gershonites who were counted, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty, all who came to take part in the work of the tent of meeting,
those counted by their clans and families numbered 2,630.
This was the total of those counted from the clans of the Gershonites, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD's command.
Those of the clans of the Merarites who were counted, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty, all who came to take part in the work of the tent of meeting,
those counted by their clans numbered 3,200.
This was the total of those counted from the clans of the Merarites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD's command through Moses.
All those of the Levites whom Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel counted, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty, all who came to do the work of service and the work of carrying in the tent of meeting,
those counted numbered 8,580.
At the LORD's command through Moses, each was assigned his service and his load. So they were counted, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone who has a skin disease or a discharge, and everyone who is unclean because of a dead body.
You are to send out both male and female. Send them outside the camp, so that they do not make the camp unclean, where I live in their midst."
The Israelites did so, and sent them outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had said to Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: When a man or a woman does any wrong to another person, by acting unfaithfully towards the LORD, that person is guilty.
He is to confess the wrong he has done. He is to make full restitution for his guilt, adding a fifth to it, and give it to the one he has wronged.

If the person has no close relative to whom restitution can be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt belongs to the LORD, for the priest, apart from the ram of atonement, with which atonement is made for him.
Every contribution from all the holy gifts of the Israelites, which they bring to the priest, will be his.
Each person's holy gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will be the priest's."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If any man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
and a man lies with her, and it is hidden from her husband's eyes and she is undetected, though she is unclean, and there is no witness against her, and she was not caught,
and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, who is unclean, or if a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, though she is not unclean,

then the man is to bring his wife to the priest. He is to bring the offering required for her, a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing guilt to remembrance.
The priest is to bring her near and have her stand before the LORD.
The priest is to take holy water in a clay vessel, and take some of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

The priest is to have the woman stand before the LORD and uncover her head, and put into her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. The priest is to hold in his hand the bitter water that brings a curse.

Then the priest is to put her under an oath and say to the woman, 'If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray into uncleanness while you were under your husband's authority, be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority, and if you have made yourself unclean, and some man other than your husband has lain with you,'

then the priest is to put the woman under the oath of the curse, and the priest is to say to the woman, 'May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, by making your thigh fall away and your belly swell.
May this water that brings a curse go into your body and make your belly swell and your thigh fall away.' And the woman is to say, 'Amen, amen.'
The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
He is to make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse will enter her and become bitter.
The priest is to take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, lift it up before the LORD and bring it to the altar.
The priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, and afterwards he is to make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, if she has made herself unclean and has been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her and become bitter, and her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean and is pure, then she will be free and will be able to conceive children.
This is the teaching about jealousy, when a woman goes astray while under her husband's authority and makes herself unclean,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. Then he is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to carry out all this teaching on her.
The man will be free from guilt, but that woman will bear the consequences of her guilt."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to set himself apart for the LORD,
he is to keep away from wine and strong drink. He is not to drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, and he is not to drink any grape juice or eat fresh or dried grapes.
All the days of his separation he is not to eat anything that is produced by the grapevine, from seeds to skins.

All the days of his vow of separation no razor is to pass over his head. Until the days are completed for which he separates himself to the LORD, he is to be holy. He is to let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.
All the days that he separates himself to the LORD he is not to go near a dead body.
Even for his father or for his mother, for his brother or for his sister, he is not to make himself unclean if they die, because the sign of his separation to God is on his head.
All the days of his separation he is holy to the LORD.
If someone dies very suddenly beside him and he defiles his consecrated head, he is to shave his head on the day of his cleansing. He is to shave it on the seventh day.
On the eighth day he is to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him because of the guilt he incurred through the dead body. That same day he is to consecrate his head again.
He is to separate himself to the LORD for the days of his separation and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days are lost, because his separation was defiled.
This is the teaching for the Nazirite when the days of his separation are completed: he is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

He is to present his offering to the LORD, one year-old male lamb without blemish as a burnt offering, one year-old ewe lamb without blemish as a sin offering, one ram without blemish as a peace offering,
and a basket of unleavened bread, loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil, with their grain offering and their drink offerings.
The priest is to present them before the LORD and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
He is to offer the ram as a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest is also to offer its grain offering and its drink offering.

Then the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and take the hair from his consecrated head and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the peace offerings.

The priest is to take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and put them in the hands of the Nazirite, after he has shaved his consecrated head.

The priest is to lift them up as an elevation offering before the LORD. They are holy for the priest, together with the breast that is lifted up and the thigh that is contributed. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the teaching for the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his separation, apart from whatever else he can afford. In keeping with the vow that he takes, so he is to do, according to the teaching for his separation."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Say to Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
May the LORD bless you and guard you.
May the LORD let his face shine on you and show you favour.
May the LORD lift up his face towards you and give you peace.
So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them."

On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it with all its furnishings, and also the altar with all its utensils. When he had anointed them and consecrated them,
the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families, made an offering. They were the leaders of the tribes, the ones who had been over those counted.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen, a cart for every two leaders and an ox for each one. They presented them before the tabernacle.
The LORD said to Moses:
"Accept these from them, so that they may be used in the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his work."
So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, according to their work,
and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, according to their work, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But to the Kohathites he gave none, because the work for the holy things that was theirs was to carry them on their shoulders.
The leaders also brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders presented their offering before the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, "Let one leader each day present his offering for the dedication of the altar."
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both by the shekel of the sanctuary, each full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel on the day it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver sprinkling bowls and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed a hundred and thirty shekels and each sprinkling bowl seventy. All the silver of the vessels came to two thousand four hundred shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
The twelve gold dishes full of incense weighed ten shekels each, by the shekel of the sanctuary. All the gold of the dishes came to a hundred and twenty shekels.
The total of the animals for the burnt offering was twelve young bulls, twelve rams and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offering. The twelve male goats were for the sin offering.

The total of the animals for the sacrifice of peace offerings was twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty male goats and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover of atonement that was on the ark of the Testimony, from between the two cherubim. And it spoke to him.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to Aaron and tell him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light in front of the lampstand."
Aaron did so. He set up the lamps to face forward on the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
This was how the lampstand was made: it was hammered work of gold, hammered from its base to its blossoms. Moses made the lampstand according to the pattern the LORD had shown him.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.
To cleanse them, do this: sprinkle them with the water of purification. Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean.
Then they are to take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you are to take a second young bull as a sin offering.
Bring the Levites forward before the tent of meeting and gather the whole community of the Israelites.
You are to bring the Levites forward before the LORD, and the Israelites are to lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as an elevation offering from the Israelites, so that they may be ready to do the work of the LORD.
When the Levites lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and present them as an elevation offering to the LORD.
In this way you are to set the Levites apart from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
After that the Levites may come in to do their work at the tent of meeting, once you have cleansed them and presented them as an elevation offering.
For they are given, wholly given, to me from among the Israelites. I have taken them for myself in place of all who open the womb, the firstborn of all the Israelites.
For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, of people and of animals. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.

And I have given the Levites, given from among the Israelites to Aaron and his sons, to do the work of the Israelites at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that there will be no plague among the Israelites when they come near the sanctuary."
Moses, Aaron and the whole community of the Israelites did this to the Levites. The Israelites did to them everything that the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.
The Levites cleansed themselves and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as an elevation offering before the LORD and made atonement for them, to cleanse them.
After that the Levites went in to do their work at the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons. As the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"This is the rule for the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upwards they are to come and take part in the work of the tent of meeting.
At fifty years of age they are to retire from the work and serve no longer.
They may assist their brothers at the tent of meeting by keeping watch, but they are not to do the work. This is how you are to arrange the duties of the Levites."
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt:
"Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
You are to keep it at its appointed time, on the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, according to all its statutes and all its rules."
So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.
They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But there were some men who were unclean because of the dead body of a person, and they could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron on that day,
and those men said to him, "We are unclean because of the dead body of a person. Why are we kept back from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time among the Israelites?"
Moses said to them, "Wait, and I will hear what the LORD commands concerning you."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the Israelites: If any of you or of your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a long journey, he may still keep the LORD's Passover.
They are to keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight. They are to eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
