They are not to leave any of it until morning, or break any of its bones. They are to keep it according to all the statute of the Passover.

But the man who is clean and is not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover, that person is to be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.

If a foreigner lives among you and keeps the LORD's Passover, he is to keep it according to the statute of the Passover and its rule. You are to have one statute for the foreigner and for the native-born."
On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the Testimony. From evening until morning it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire.
So it was always: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, the Israelites set out after it. In the place where the cloud settled, there the Israelites camped.
At the command of the LORD the Israelites set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
Even when the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud was a few days over the tabernacle. At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed from evening until morning. When the cloud lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, when the cloud lifted, they set out.
Whether it was two days, or a month, or a year, that the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, resting on it, the Israelites remained in camp and did not set out. But when it lifted, they set out.
At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out. They kept the charge of the LORD, at the command of the LORD through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Make two trumpets of silver. Make them of hammered work. You are to use them for summoning the community and for setting the camps in motion.
When both are blown, the whole community is to gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather to you.
When you blow an alarm, the camps on the east side are to set out.
When you blow a second alarm, the camps on the south side are to set out. An alarm is to be blown for their setting out.
But to gather the assembly, you are to blow, but not sound an alarm.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is to be a permanent rule for you through your generations.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who is oppressing you, you are to sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.

Also on your days of rejoicing, at your appointed festivals and at the beginnings of your months, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. They will be a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the Testimony.
The Israelites set out by stages from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD through Moses.
The standard of the camp of the people of Judah set out first, by their divisions. Nahshon son of Amminadab was over its division.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of the people of Issachar,
and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of the people of Zebulun.
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
The standard of the camp of Reuben set out, by their divisions. Elizur son of Shedeur was over its division.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of the people of Simeon,
and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of the people of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
The standard of the camp of the people of Ephraim set out, by their divisions. Elishama son of Ammihud was over its division.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of the people of Manasseh,
and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of the people of Benjamin.
Then the standard of the camp of the people of Dan set out, as the rear guard of all the camps, by their divisions. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over its division.
Pagiel son of Okran was over the division of the tribe of the people of Asher,
and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of the people of Naphtali.
This was the order of march of the Israelites by their divisions, when they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will do you good, for the LORD has promised good to Israel."
But he said to him, "I will not go. I will go to my own land and to my own kindred."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us, for you know where we can camp in the wilderness, and you will be our eyes.
And if you go with us, whatever good the LORD gives us, we will do the same for you."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD a three days' journey. The ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for the three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day, whenever they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said:
Rise up, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you.
And whenever it came to rest, he said:
Return, LORD, to the ten thousand thousands of Israel.
The people began to complain, and it was evil in the ears of the LORD. When the LORD heard it, his anger blazed, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed some at the edge of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was named Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
The mixed crowd among them was seized by craving, and the Israelites also began to weep again and said, "Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.
But now our appetite is gone. There is nothing at all but this manna to look at."
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like resin.
The people went about and gathered it and ground it in handmills or crushed it in mortars. They boiled it in pots and made cakes of it. It tasted like cakes baked with oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell with it.
Moses heard the people weeping by their families, each at the entrance of his tent. The anger of the LORD blazed hot, and Moses was troubled.
Moses said to the LORD, "Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I not found favour with you, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, 'Carry them in your arms, as a nurse carries a baby,' to the land that you swore to their ancestors?
Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep to me and say, 'Give us meat to eat.'
I am not able to carry all this people by myself. It is too heavy for me.
If this is how you are going to treat me, kill me at once, if I have found favour with you, so that I do not see my own misery."

The LORD said to Moses, "Gather for me seventy of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and officers over them. Bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them take their stand there with you.
I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them, so that they may bear the burden of the people with you, and you will not carry it alone.

Say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, for you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, 'Who will give us meat to eat? We were better off in Egypt.' The LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
You will not eat it for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,

but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you have rejected the LORD who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, 'Why did we ever come out of Egypt?'"
But Moses said, "The people among whom I am number six hundred thousand foot soldiers, and you say, 'I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.'
Would flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, and be enough for them? Or would all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, and be enough for them?"
The LORD said to Moses, "Is the LORD's hand too short? Now you will see whether my word will happen to you or not."
Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand round the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not do it again.

Two men had stayed in the camp, one named Eldad and the other named Medad. The spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."
Joshua son of Nun, who had served Moses from his youth, said, "My lord Moses, stop them."
But Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them."
Then Moses returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

A wind went out from the LORD and brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on the other side, all round the camp, about two cubits deep on the surface of the ground.
The people stayed up all that day and all night and all the next day and gathered the quail. The one who gathered least gathered ten homers. They spread them out for themselves all round the camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD blazed against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.
So that place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us also?" And the LORD heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more so than anyone else on the face of the earth.
At once the LORD said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, "Come out, you three, to the tent of meeting." So the three of them came out.
The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent, and he called Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
He said, "Hear my words:
When there is a prophet among you, I the LORD make myself known to him in a vision; I speak with him in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moses. He is trusted in all my house.
With him I speak mouth to mouth, plainly and not in riddles, and he sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
The anger of the LORD blazed against them, and he went away.
When the cloud moved away from over the tent, there was Miriam, with a skin disease, white as snow. Aaron turned to Miriam and saw that she had a skin disease.
Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not lay on us the sin that we have so foolishly committed.
Do not let her be like one born dead, whose flesh is half eaten away when it comes out of its mother's womb."
Moses cried out to the LORD, "O God, please heal her."
The LORD said to Moses, "If her father had spat in her face, would she not be shamed for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp for seven days, and after that she may be brought in again."
So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought in again.
After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am about to give to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a chief among his people."
Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran as the LORD directed. All of them were heads of the Israelites.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, that is, the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout the land. (Moses renamed Hoshea son of Nun, calling him Joshua.)
When Moses sent them to scout out Canaan, he told them, "Go up by way of the Negev and on into the hills.
Look at the land: what is it like? And at the people living there: are they strong or weak, few or many?
What is the land like where they live, good or poor? What are their towns like, open camps or fortified cities?
What is the ground like, rich or thin? Does it have trees or not? Take courage, and bring back some of the produce of the land." It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
They went up and scouted the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near the entrance to Hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
They came to the Valley of Eshcol and cut a branch there that carried a single cluster of grapes. Two men carried it on a pole, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was named the Valley of Eshcol, which means "cluster", because of the cluster the Israelites cut there.
After forty days they returned from scouting the land.
They came to Moses, Aaron and the whole community of Israel at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They gave their report to them and to the whole assembly, and showed them the produce of the land.
They told Moses, "We went to the land where you sent us, and it truly flows with milk and honey. Here is some of its produce.
But the people who live in the land are fierce, the cities are huge and heavily fortified, and we even saw descendants of Anak there.
Amalek lives in the Negev, the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites in the hills, and the Canaanites by the sea and along the Jordan."
Caleb hushed the people in front of Moses and said, "We should go up and take the land. We can certainly do it."
But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot go up against those people. They are too strong for us."
And they spread a discouraging report among the Israelites about the land they had scouted: "The land we crossed and scouted is a land that eats up its own people. Everyone we saw in it was huge.
We even saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak are part of the Nephilim). Next to them we looked like grasshoppers to ourselves, and that is how we looked to them."
That night the whole community cried out and wept aloud.
All the Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, "If only we had died in Egypt, or if only we had died here in the wilderness!
Why is the LORD bringing us to that land to be struck down by the sword? Our wives and children will be seized as spoil. Would it not be better to go back to Egypt?"
They said to one another, "Let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt."
Moses and Aaron threw themselves face down in front of the whole assembly of the Israelite community.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of those who had scouted the land, tore their clothes
and said to the whole Israelite community, "The land we crossed and scouted is wonderfully good.
If the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us into that land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of that land. They are no more than food for us. Their shelter has been taken from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them."
But the whole community was talking of stoning them, when the glory of the LORD appeared in the tent of meeting before all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people spurn me? How long will they refuse to trust me, after all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with plague and wipe them out, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are."
Moses said to the LORD, "The Egyptians will hear of it, since by your strength you brought these people up from among them.

They will tell it to the people who live in this land. They have heard that you, LORD, are in the midst of these people, that you, LORD, have shown yourself face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you put these people to death all at once, the nations that have heard of your fame will say,
'The LORD could not bring these people into the land he promised them by oath, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.'
So now, let the LORD's strength be shown, as you have said:

'The LORD is slow to anger, rich in faithful love, forgiving guilt and rebellion, though he does not simply let the guilty go unpunished. He holds children to account for the guilt of their parents, down to the third and fourth generation.'
By the greatness of your faithful love, please forgive the guilt of these people, as you have borne with them from Egypt until now."
The LORD said, "I forgive, as you have asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,
not one of those who have seen my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice,
will see the land I promised by oath to their ancestors. None who have spurned me will see it.
But my servant Caleb, because he has a different spirit and has followed me wholeheartedly, I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants will possess it.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are living in the valley. Tomorrow turn round and set out for the wilderness, along the road to the Red Sea."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"How long must I put up with this wicked community, murmuring against me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites make against me.
Tell them: 'As surely as I live, says the LORD, I will do to you exactly what I heard you say.
Your corpses will fall in this wilderness, every one of you counted in the census, from twenty years old and up, who murmured against me.
Not one of you will enter the land where I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
Your little ones, whom you said would be taken as spoil, I will bring in, and they will get to know the land you have spurned.
But your corpses will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will be wandering shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the cost of your unfaithfulness until the last of your corpses lies in the wilderness.
You scouted the land for forty days. For each day, a year: you will bear your guilt for forty years, and you will learn what it means to have me against you.'
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do this to this whole wicked community that has gathered against me. In this wilderness they will come to an end, and here they will die."
As for the men Moses sent to scout the land, who came back and made the whole community murmur against him by spreading a bad report about the land,
those men who spread the bad report about the land died by plague before the LORD.
Of the men who went to scout the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh stayed alive.
When Moses told these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned deeply.
Early the next morning they went up towards the heights of the hill country. "We are here," they said. "We will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned."
Moses said, "Why are you going against the LORD's command? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the LORD is not in your midst, and you will be struck down by your enemies.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there in front of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, the LORD will not be with you."
But in their arrogance they went up towards the heights of the hill country, though neither the ark of the LORD's covenant nor Moses left the camp.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them down and chased them all the way to Hormah.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Say to the Israelites: Once you have entered the land that I am giving you as your home,

you will offer to the LORD an offering made by fire. It may be a burnt offering or some other sacrifice, to fulfil a special vow, or as a gift freely given, or at one of your festivals, to send up a pleasing aroma to the LORD from your herd or flock.
Whoever presents his gift is to bring to the LORD, as a grain offering, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour blended with a quarter of a hin of oil,
and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Prepare this with each lamb, whether for the burnt offering or the sacrifice.
With a ram, prepare as a grain offering two tenths of an ephah of fine flour blended with a third of a hin of oil,
and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, to be offered as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to fulfil a special vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
bring with the bull a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour blended with half a hin of oil,
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering. This is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Follow this for every ox, every ram, and every lamb or kid.
Whatever the number you prepare, do it in this way for each one.
Every native-born Israelite is to follow this pattern whenever he presents a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Should a foreigner be living among you, or anyone else settled in your midst in generations to come, and he wishes to present a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do what you do.
There is to be one rule for the assembly, for you and for the foreigner living among you, a lasting rule through your generations. Before the LORD, you and the foreigner stand alike.
One teaching and one ruling will hold for you and for the foreigner who lives with you."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Say to the Israelites: When you come into the land where I am taking you,
and you eat the bread of that land, you are to set aside a contribution for the LORD.
Of the first of your coarse meal, set aside a loaf as a contribution. Present it as you would present a contribution from the threshing floor.
From the first of your coarse meal you are to give a contribution to the LORD, generation after generation.
Now suppose you go astray without meaning to, and fail to keep any one of these commands that the LORD gave Moses,
anything at all that the LORD commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and on through your generations.

If this was done unintentionally, and the community did not know, then the whole community is to present one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering as the rule requires, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest is to make atonement for the whole community of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, since it was unintentional, and they brought their gift, a food offering to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD, for their mistake.
The whole community of the Israelites will be forgiven, and the foreigner living among them as well, since the entire people were involved in the mistake.
If it is one person who goes astray without meaning to, he is to bring a female goat in her first year as a sin offering.
The priest is to make atonement before the LORD for the person who went astray, who erred unintentionally, so as to make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
There is to be one teaching for the one who acts unintentionally, whether he is native-born among the Israelites or a foreigner living among them.
But the person who acts defiantly, native-born or foreigner, insults the LORD. That person is to be cut off from his people.
He has despised the LORD's word and broken his command. That person is to be cut off completely. His guilt remains on him."
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses, Aaron and the whole community.
They held him in custody, because it had not been spelled out what was to be done to him.
The LORD said to Moses, "The man is certainly to die. The whole community is to stone him outside the camp."
The whole community led him outside the camp and stoned him, and he died, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Say to the Israelites: Through all your generations you are to make tassels for the corners of your garments, and attach to each corner tassel a cord of blue.

It will be your tassel, and when you look at it you will remember all the commands of the LORD and do them, and you will not wander after the desires of your own hearts and eyes, which draw you into unfaithfulness.
So you will remember and do all my commands, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took his stand along with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
They rose up against Moses together with 250 Israelites, community leaders, men called to the assembly, men of renown.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and told them, "You have taken too much on yourselves! The entire community, every one of them, is holy, and the LORD is in their midst. Why do you set yourselves above the LORD's assembly?"
When Moses heard this, he threw himself on his face.
He said to Korah and his whole company, "In the morning the LORD will make known who is his, and who is the holy one he will bring near to himself. Whomever he chooses, he will bring near.
Do this: Korah, and all your company, take censers,
put fire in them tomorrow and lay incense on the fire before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses is the one who is holy. It is you who have taken too much, sons of Levi!"
Moses said to Korah, "Listen now, sons of Levi.

Is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community of Israel, to bring you close to himself, to serve at the LORD's tabernacle and stand before the community to minister to them?
He has brought you close, you and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you are reaching for the priesthood as well!
It is against the LORD that you and all your company have gathered. As for Aaron, who is he that you should murmur against him?"
Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. They answered, "We will not come up.
Is it not enough that you have brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, and now you want to make yourself ruler over us as well?
You certainly have not brought us to a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us fields and vineyards to inherit. Do you think you can put out the eyes of these men? We will not come up."
Moses was furious. He said to the LORD, "Do not look favourably on their offering. I have not taken so much as one donkey from them, nor have I harmed any of them."
Moses said to Korah, "You and your whole company are to present yourselves before the LORD tomorrow, you, they and Aaron.
Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it, and bring his censer before the LORD, 250 censers. You and Aaron are to bring your censers as well."
Each man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron.
Korah had gathered the whole community against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole community.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"Stand apart from this community, and I will finish them in an instant."
They fell on their faces and said, "God, you who give breath to every living creature, will you be furious with the whole community when only one man has sinned?"
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell the community: Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan and Abiram."
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, with the elders of Israel following him.
He told the community, "Move away from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing that belongs to them, or you will be swept away in all their sins."
So they moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives, their sons and their small children.
Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD sent me to do all these things, and that I did not act on my own:
If these men die as all people die, and share the fate of all humankind, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD does something never done before, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and everything they have, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have scorned the LORD."
As soon as he had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, with their households, all Korah's people and all their property.
They went down alive into Sheol with everything they had. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from the assembly.
All the Israelites around them fled at their screams, crying, "The earth will swallow us too!"
And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Tell Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, to lift the censers out of the blaze and scatter the coals far off, for the censers have become holy,

the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their own lives. Let them be beaten into thin plates to cover the altar, since they were brought before the LORD and so are holy. They will be a sign to the Israelites."
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned had brought, and they were beaten into plates to cover the altar,

as a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not a descendant of Aaron, may come near to burn incense before the LORD, so that he will not end up like Korah and his company, as the LORD had told him through Moses.
The next day the whole community of the Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron: "You have killed the LORD's people!"
As the community gathered against Moses and Aaron and turned towards the tent of meeting, the cloud suddenly covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting,
and the LORD spoke to Moses:
"Stand apart from this community, and I will finish them in an instant." They fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer, put fire from the altar on it, lay incense on it and take it quickly to the community to make atonement for them. Wrath has gone out from the LORD. The plague has begun."
Aaron took the censer as Moses said and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people. He laid on the incense and made atonement for them.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
The dead from the plague numbered 14,700, besides those who died in the affair of Korah.
Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, for the plague had stopped.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and collect a staff from each of them, one for each ancestral house, twelve staffs from all their leaders. Write each man's name on his staff.
On the staff of Levi write Aaron's name, for there is to be one staff for each head of an ancestral house.
Lay them in the tent of meeting in front of the Testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout. Then I will put an end to the murmuring of the Israelites against you, which they keep up against you."
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader according to their ancestral houses, twelve staffs, and Aaron's staff was among them.
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the Testimony.
The next day Moses went into the tent of the Testimony, and there Aaron's staff, standing for the house of Levi, had sprouted. It had put out buds, opened blossoms and borne ripe almonds.
Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD's presence to all the Israelites. They looked at them, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's staff back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels, so that their murmuring against me may come to an end, and they may not die."
Moses did so. He did just as the LORD commanded him.
The Israelites said to Moses, "Look, we are dying! We are lost, all of us lost!
Everyone who comes near the LORD's tabernacle will die. Are we all going to perish?"

The LORD said to Aaron, "You and your sons and your ancestral house with you are to carry the guilt connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons alone are to carry the guilt connected with your priesthood.
Bring with you also your relatives from the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, so that they may join you and serve you, while you and your sons are before the tent of the Testimony.
They are to carry out your duties and the duties of the whole tent, but they must not come near the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or they and you will both die.
They are to join you and keep charge of the tent of meeting, for all the work of the tent, and no outsider may come near you.
You are to keep charge of the sanctuary and of the altar, so that wrath will not fall on the Israelites again.
I myself have taken your fellow Levites from among the Israelites as a gift to you, given to the LORD to do the work of the tent of meeting.

But you and your sons are to attend to your priesthood in everything that concerns the altar and what is behind the curtain. You are to do the work. I give you your priesthood as a gift for service, and any outsider who comes near is to be put to death."
The LORD said to Aaron, "I myself have given you charge of the contributions made to me. All the holy gifts of the Israelites I give to you and to your sons as your portion, a permanent share.

This is to be yours from the most holy gifts, kept back from the fire: every offering of theirs that they bring to me as most holy, whether grain offering, sin offering or guilt offering, will be yours and your sons'.
You are to eat it as most holy. Every male may eat it. It is to be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution of their gift, all the elevation offerings of the Israelites. I give them to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a permanent share. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the new wine and grain, the first produce that they give to the LORD, I give to you.
The first ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, will be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
Everything devoted in Israel will be yours.

Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh, that they present to the LORD, whether human or animal, will be yours. But you are to redeem the firstborn of humans, and the firstborn of unclean animals you are to redeem.
Their redemption price, from a month old, you are to set at five shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.
But the firstborn of an ox, a sheep or a goat you are not to redeem. They are holy. You are to splash their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Their flesh will be yours, just as the breast of the elevation offering and the right thigh are yours.

All the contributions from the holy gifts that the Israelites set aside for the LORD I give to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a permanent share. It is a covenant of salt for ever before the LORD, for you and for your descendants with you."
The LORD said to Aaron, "You are to have no inheritance in their land, and no portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
To the Levites I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for the work that they do, the work of the tent of meeting.
From now on the Israelites must not come near the tent of meeting, or they will bear the consequences of their sin and die.

It is the Levites who are to do the work of the tent of meeting, and they will carry the consequences of their guilt. This is a permanent rule through your generations. Among the Israelites they will have no inheritance.

For the tithe of the Israelites, which they present as a contribution to the LORD, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. That is why I have said of them that they are to have no inheritance among the Israelites."
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you are to present a contribution from it to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution will be counted for you as though it were grain from the threshing floor or the full yield of the winepress.
In this way you too are to present a contribution to the LORD from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites. From it you are to give the LORD's contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all that is given to you, you are to present every contribution due to the LORD, from all the best of it, the part that is holy.
Tell them: When you have presented the best of it, it will be counted for the Levites as the yield of the threshing floor and the yield of the winepress.
You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, for it is your wages for your work in the tent of meeting.
You will bring no guilt on yourselves by this, when you have presented the best of it. You will not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, and you will not die."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"This is the statute of the teaching that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer, one without defect, with no blemish, which has never carried a yoke.
You are to give it to Eleazar the priest. It is to be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in front of him.
Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times towards the front of the tent of meeting.
The heifer is to be burned in his sight: its hide, its flesh and its blood, with its dung, are to be burned.
The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop and crimson yarn and throw them into the fire where the heifer is burning.
Then the priest is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterwards he may come into the camp. The priest will be unclean until evening.
The one who burns it is also to wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water. He will be unclean until evening.

A man who is clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They are to be kept for the community of the Israelites for use in the water for impurity. It is a sin offering.

The one who gathers up the ashes of the heifer is to wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is to be a permanent rule for the Israelites and for the foreigner who lives among them.
Whoever touches the dead body of any person will be unclean for seven days.

He is to cleanse himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not cleanse himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.

Whoever touches a dead body, the body of anyone who has died, and does not cleanse himself, defiles the tabernacle of the LORD, and that person will be cut off from Israel. Because the water for impurity was not thrown over him, he is unclean. His uncleanness is still on him.
This is the teaching when someone dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent will be unclean for seven days.
Every open vessel that has no cover tied on it will be unclean.
Anyone in the open field who touches someone killed by the sword, or a body that has died naturally, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person they are to take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering and put fresh water over them in a vessel.

A clean person is to take hyssop, dip it in the water and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the furnishings, on the persons who were there, and on the one who touched the bone, or the person killed, or the one who died naturally, or the grave.

The clean person is to sprinkle it on the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day he is to cleanse him. The person is to wash his clothes and bathe in water, and in the evening he will be clean.

But the man who is unclean and does not cleanse himself, that person will be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water for impurity has not been thrown over him. He is unclean.
It is to be a permanent rule for them. The one who sprinkles the water for impurity is to wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water for impurity will be unclean until evening.
Whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
In the first month the whole community of Israel arrived in the wilderness of Zin, and the people settled at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
There was no water for the community, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people took Moses to task: "If only we had died when our kinsmen died before the LORD!
Why have you led the LORD's assembly into this wilderness, for us and our animals to die here?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this dreadful place? It is no place for grain, or figs, or vines, or pomegranates, and there is not even water to drink."
Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and fell on their faces. The glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"Take the staff and gather the assembly, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock in front of their eyes, and it will give its water. You will bring water out of the rock for them, and give the assembly and their animals something to drink."
Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and he said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses raised his arm and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out, and the assembly and their animals drank.
The LORD said to Moses and to Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to treat me as holy in the eyes of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them."
These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarrelled with the LORD, and where he showed himself holy among them.
From Kadesh Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has come to us.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians treated us and our ancestors harshly.
When we cried out to the LORD, he heard our voice and sent a messenger and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are in Kadesh, a town at the edge of your territory.

Please let us cross your land. We will not go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will go along the King's Road. We will not turn aside to the right or the left until we have crossed your territory."
But Edom said to him, "You will not cross through here, or I will come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will go along the highway, and if we or our animals drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We only want to cross on foot, nothing else."
But he said, "You will not cross." And Edom came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
The whole community of Israel set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron is to be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there."
Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole community saw that Aaron had died, the whole house of Israel mourned for Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the road of Atharim. He fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the LORD: "If you will truly hand this people over to us, we will devote their cities to destruction."
The LORD listened to Israel's plea and handed over the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction. So the place was called Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea, to go round the land of Edom. But the people grew short-tempered on the way,
and they spoke against God and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we loathe this wretched food!"
Then the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people, and they bit the people, and many in Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a poisonous snake and set it on a pole. Everyone who is bitten and looks at it will live."
So Moses made a snake of bronze and set it on a pole. When a snake bit someone, he would look at the bronze snake and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab towards the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
From there they set out and camped on the far side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that stretches out from the border of the Amorites. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD:
"Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys, the Arnon,
and the slope of the valleys that runs towards the seat of Ar and leans against the border of Moab."
From there they went on to Beer, the well of which the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song:
"Rise up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the leaders dug, that the nobles of the people hollowed out, with the sceptre, with their staffs."
From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the wasteland.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites:
"Let us cross your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will go along the King's Highway until we have crossed your territory."
But Sihon would not let Israel cross his territory. He gathered all his people and went out against Israel into the wilderness. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the edge of the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these cities and settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
That is why the ballad-singers say:
"Come to Heshbon, let it be built, let the city of Sihon be restored.
For a fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon. It devoured Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are ruined, people of Chemosh! He has made his sons fugitives, and his daughters captives, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
We have shot them down. Heshbon is ruined as far as Dibon. We have laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to Moses, "Do not fear him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon."
So they struck him down, with his sons and all his people, until no survivor was left to him. And they took possession of his land.
The Israelites set out and camped on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many. Moab was sick with dread of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "This horde is going to lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, by the River, in the land of his kinsmen, to summon him: "A people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the earth, and they are settling next to me.

Now come, put a curse on this people for me, for they are too strong for me. Perhaps I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land, for I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with the fee for divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak's words.
He said to them, "Spend the night here, and I will bring you back word, as the LORD speaks to me." So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent word to me:
'Look, a people has come out of Egypt, and it covers the face of the earth. Now come, put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"
God said to Balaam, "You are not to go with them. You are not to curse the people, for they are blessed."
Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak's officials, "Go back to your own land, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
The officials of Moab got up, went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
Balak sent officials again, more of them and more distinguished than the first.
They came to Balaam and said to him, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Please do not let anything stop you from coming to me.
I will honour you greatly and do whatever you say to me. Come, put a curse on this people for me."
But Balaam answered Balak's officials, "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.
Now you also stay here tonight, so that I may find out what more the LORD will say to me."
That night God came to Balaam and said to him, "If these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them. But you are to do only what I tell you."
Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey and went with the officials of Moab.
But God's anger blazed because he was going, and the angel of the LORD took his stand in the road as an adversary against him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. The donkey turned off the road and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, and she squeezed Balaam's foot against the wall. So he struck her again.
The angel of the LORD went further ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either to the right or to the left.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger blazed, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If there were a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing this to you?" He said, "No."
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bowed down and fell on his face.
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I came out as an adversary, because your way is reckless before me.
The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away from me, I would by now have killed you and let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know that you were standing in the road against me. Now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will go back."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but you are to speak only the word that I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send urgently to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honour you?"
Balaam said to Balak, "Look, I have come to you. But do I now have any power to say anything at all? The word that God puts in my mouth is the only one I will speak."
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and to the officials who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, and from there he saw the near edge of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go off. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me I will tell you." And he went to a bare height.
God met Balaam, and he said to him, "I have set out the seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram."
The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
He went back to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the officials of Moab.
He took up his poem and said:
"From Aram Balak has brought me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east: 'Come, curse Jacob for me, come, denounce Israel.'
How can I curse whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?
From the top of the rocks I see them, from the hills I behold them. Look, a people that dwells alone, not counted among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number a quarter of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like theirs."
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless them."
He answered, "Must I not take care to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Balak said to him, "Come with me to another place from which you can see them. You will see only the edge of them and not all of them. Curse them for me from there."
So he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here beside your burnt offering, while I meet him over there."
The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
He came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, with the officials of Moab. Balak said to him, "What has the LORD said?"
He took up his poem and said:
"Rise, Balak, and hear; listen to me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, to deceive, nor a son of man, to change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not make it come true?
I received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
No trouble is seen in Jacob, no distress is watched in Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of a king is in their midst.
God, who brings them out of Egypt, is for them like the horns of a wild ox.
For there is no spell against Jacob and no divination against Israel. At the right time it will be said to Jacob and to Israel, 'What has God done!'
Look, a people that rises like a lioness, and lifts itself like a lion. It does not lie down until it eats its prey and drinks the blood of the slain."
Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all."
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you, 'Whatever the LORD says, that I must do'?"
Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which looks down on the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go off, as at other times, to look for omens, but set his face towards the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the spirit of God came on him.
He took up his poem and said:
"The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
the oracle of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, falling down, with uncovered eyes:
How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwellings, Israel!
Like valleys they spread out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the water.
Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will have water in plenty. His king will be higher than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
God, who brings him out of Egypt, is for him like the horns of a wild ox. He will eat up the nations that oppose him and break their bones in pieces, and shoot them through with his arrows.
He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness. Who will rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you."
Balak's anger blazed against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. He said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you have blessed them these three times.
Now run off to your own place. I said I would honour you greatly, but the LORD has kept you back from honour."
Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not tell the messengers you sent to me,
'Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD to do good or bad of my own accord. Whatever the LORD speaks, that I will speak'?
Now I am going back to my people. Come, I will tell you what this people will do to your people in days to come."
He took up his poem and said:
"The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
the oracle of one who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, falling down, with uncovered eyes:
I see him, but not now. I behold him, but not near. A star will step out of Jacob, a sceptre will rise out of Israel. It will strike the brow of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will become a possession, Seir, his enemy, will become a possession, while Israel acts with strength.
One from Jacob will rule and destroy what is left of the city."
He looked at Amalek, took up his poem and said:
"Amalek was the first of the nations, but his end is destruction."
He looked at the Kenites, took up his poem and said:
"Your dwelling is firm, and your nest is set in the rock.
Yet Kain will be burned, when Asshur takes you captive."
He took up his poem and said:
"Alas, who will live when God does this?
Ships will come from the coast of Kittim and will oppress Asshur and oppress Eber, and he also will come to destruction."
Then Balaam got up and went back to his place, and Balak also went on his way.
While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to have sexual relations with the women of Moab,
who invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel was joined to the Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD blazed against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and have them exposed before the LORD in the sun, so that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel."
Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you is to put to death those of his men who have joined themselves to the Baal of Peor."

Just then one of the Israelites came and brought a Midianite woman to his family, in the sight of Moses and of the whole community of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he got up from the middle of the assembly and took a spear in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the inner room and drove the spear through both of them, the man of Israel and the woman through her belly. Then the plague on the Israelites was stopped.
Those who died by the plague were 24,000.
The LORD spoke to Moses:

"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back my wrath from the Israelites, because he was zealous with my own zeal among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore tell him that I am giving him my covenant of peace,
and it will be for him and for his descendants after him a covenant of a lasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites."
The name of the Israelite who was killed, who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, the head of a father's house of the Simeonites.
The name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur, the head of the people of a father's house in Midian.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Treat the Midianites as enemies, and strike them.

For they have treated you as enemies by the trickery they used against you in the affair of Peor, and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the plague in the affair of Peor."
After the plague the LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
"Take a census of the whole community of the Israelites, by their ancestral houses, of everyone twenty years old and upwards who is able to go out to war in Israel."
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, and said:
"Count the men twenty years old and upwards, as the LORD commanded Moses." These were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. The descendants of Reuben: from Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; from Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; from Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These were the clans of the Reubenites. Those counted numbered 43,730.
The son of Pallu was Eliab.
The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, chosen from the community, who defied Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah when they defied the LORD,
and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with Korah, when that company died and the fire consumed 250 men. They became a warning.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon by their clans: from Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; from Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; from Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
from Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; from Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These were the clans of the Simeonites, 22,200.
The descendants of Gad by their clans: from Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; from Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; from Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
from Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; from Eri, the clan of the Erites;
from Arod, the clan of the Arodites; from Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Gad. Those counted numbered 40,500.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah by their clans: from Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; from Perez, the clan of the Perezites; from Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
The descendants of Perez: from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; from Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These were the clans of Judah. Those counted numbered 76,500.
The descendants of Issachar by their clans: from Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; from Puvah, the clan of the Punites;
from Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; from Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These were the clans of Issachar. Those counted numbered 64,300.
The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: from Sered, the clan of the Seredites; from Elon, the clan of the Elonites; from Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These were the clans of the Zebulunites. Those counted numbered 60,500.
The descendants of Joseph by their clans, Manasseh and Ephraim.
The descendants of Manasseh: from Machir, the clan of the Machirites (Machir was the father of Gilead); from Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These were the descendants of Gilead: from Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; from Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
from Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; from Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;
from Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; from Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but only daughters. The names of Zelophehad's daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
These were the clans of Manasseh. Those counted numbered 52,700.
These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: from Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; from Becher, the clan of the Becherites; from Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
These were the descendants of Shuthelah: from Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim. Those counted numbered 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: from Bela, the clan of the Belaites; from Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; from Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
from Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; from Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: from Ard, the clan of the Ardites; from Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans. Those counted numbered 45,600.
These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: from Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These were the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, those counted, numbered 64,400.
The descendants of Asher by their clans: from Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; from Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; from Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the descendants of Beriah: from Heber, the clan of the Heberites; from Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
The name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
These were the clans of the descendants of Asher. Those counted numbered 53,400.
The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: from Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; from Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
from Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; from Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These were the clans of Naphtali by their clans. Those counted numbered 45,400.
This was the total of the Israelites who were counted: 601,730.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"To these the land is to be divided as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
To a larger group you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group a smaller inheritance. Each is to be given its inheritance according to the number of those counted.
But the land is to be divided by lot. They are to inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
Their inheritance is to be divided by lot between the larger and the smaller."
These were the Levites counted by their clans: from Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; from Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; from Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These were the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam.
To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorised fire before the LORD.
Those counted of the Levites, every male from a month old and upwards, numbered 23,000. They were not counted among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These were the ones counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
Among these there was not one of those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, "They will surely die in the wilderness." Not one of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders and the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said:
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company that gathered against the LORD in the company of Korah, but he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name be lost to his clan because he had no son? Give us a holding among our father's brothers."
Moses brought their case before the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. You are to give them a holding as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and pass on their father's inheritance to them.
Tell the Israelites: When a man dies and has no son, you are to pass his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, you are to give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

If his father has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to his nearest relative in his clan, and he will possess it. This is to be a legal rule for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and look at the land that I have given to the Israelites.
When you have seen it, you also will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was,

because you both rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin, when the community quarrelled, and you did not treat me as holy at the waters before their eyes." (These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
Moses spoke to the LORD:
"May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint someone over this community
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the community of the LORD may not be like sheep without a shepherd."
The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community, and commission him in their sight.
Give him some of your own authority, so that the whole community of the Israelites may obey.

He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will enquire for him by the decision of the Urim before the LORD. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, he and all the Israelites with him, the whole community."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole community.
He laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and tell them: You are to take care to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food for my food offerings, a pleasing aroma to me.
Tell them: This is the food offering that you are to present to the LORD: two male lambs a year old without defect, each day, as a regular burnt offering.
You are to offer one lamb in the morning and the other lamb at twilight,
with a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil.
It is a regular burnt offering, ordained at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin for each lamb. In the holy place you are to pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD.
The other lamb you are to offer at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
On the Sabbath day, two male lambs a year old without defect, with a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for each Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
At the beginnings of your months you are to present a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect,
with a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for the one ram,
and a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb. It is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.

Their drink offerings are to be half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering of each month through the months of the year.
Also one male goat as a sin offering to the LORD, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering.
On the fourteenth day of the first month there is to be a Passover to the LORD.
On the fifteenth day of this month there is to be a festival. For seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.
You are to present a food offering, a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old. They are to be without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for a bull and two-tenths for the ram.
For each of the seven lambs you are to offer a tenth,
and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You are to offer these in addition to the burnt offering of the morning, which is the regular burnt offering.
In this way you are to offer the food daily for seven days, as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.
On the day of the first produce, when you present a grain offering of new grain to the LORD at your Festival of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.
You are to present a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old,
with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and a tenth for each of the seven lambs,
with one male goat to make atonement for you.
You are to present them in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. They are to be without defect, together with their drink offerings."
"On the first day of the seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work. It is a day of trumpet blasts for you.
You are to present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect,
with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs,
and one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you,

in addition to the burnt offering of the new moon and its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings, according to the rule. They are a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves. You are not to do any work.
