You are to present a burnt offering to the LORD as a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old. They are to be without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the one ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, with their drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work. You are to keep a festival to the LORD for seven days.
You are to present a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old. They are to be without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams,
and one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offerings.
On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the eighth day you are to hold a closing assembly. You are not to do any ordinary work.
You are to present a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, the ram and the lambs, according to their number, as the rule requires,
and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.

These you are to offer to the LORD at your appointed festivals, in addition to your vows and your freewill offerings, as your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings and your peace offerings."
And Moses told the Israelites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites: "This is what the LORD has commanded.
When a man makes a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself with a pledge, he is not to break his word. He is to do everything that comes out of his mouth.
When a woman makes a vow to the LORD and binds herself with a pledge in her youth, while she is in her father's house,

and her father hears her vow and the pledge by which she has bound herself, and her father says nothing to her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or her pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will release her, because her father forbade her.
If she marries while under her vows, or a rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows will stand, and her pledges by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if on the day her husband hears of it he forbids her, then he nullifies her vow that was on her, and the rash utterance of her lips by which she bound herself. The LORD will release her.
The vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound herself, will stand against her.
If she made a vow in her husband's house or bound herself by a pledge with an oath,
and her husband heard of it and said nothing to her and did not forbid her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.

But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that comes from her lips, whether vows or pledges, will stand. Her husband has made them void, and the LORD will release her.
Every vow and every binding oath to deny herself, her husband may confirm or her husband may nullify.

But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or all her pledges that are on her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard of them.
But if he nullifies them after he has heard of them, then he will bear her guilt."
These are the rules that the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth, while she is in her father's house.
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midianites. After that you will be gathered to your people."
Moses said to the people, "Arm men from among you for war, so that they may go against Midian and carry out the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
You are to send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, into the war."
So out of the thousands of Israel a thousand from each tribe were handed over, twelve thousand armed for war.
Moses sent them into the war, a thousand from each tribe, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took in his hand the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and they took as plunder all their cattle, all their flocks and all their goods.
All their towns where they lived, and all their encampments, they burned with fire.
They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals,
and brought the captives, the plunder and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the community of the Israelites, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the community went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had come back from the service of war.
Moses said to them, "Have you let all the women live?
Look, these women, on Balaam's advice, caused the Israelites to act unfaithfully against the LORD in the affair of Peor, so that the plague came on the community of the LORD.
Now kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.
But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him you may keep alive for yourselves.
You are to camp outside the camp for seven days. Whoever has killed anyone or touched any who were killed, purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day.
You are to purify every garment, every article of leather, everything made of goats' hair and every wooden article."
Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had gone into battle, "This is the statute of the teaching that the LORD commanded Moses:
gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead,

everything that can stand fire, you are to pass through the fire, and it will be clean. Nevertheless it is to be purified with the water for impurity. And whatever cannot stand fire, you are to pass through the water.
You are to wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. Afterwards you may come into the camp."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"You and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the ancestral houses of the community are to count the plunder that was captured, both people and animals.
Divide the plunder into two parts, between the warriors who went out to battle and all the rest of the community.
From the men of war who went out to battle, set apart a tribute for the LORD, one in five hundred, of the persons, the cattle, the donkeys and the flocks.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's contribution.

From the Israelites' half you are to take one in every fifty, of the persons, the cattle, the donkeys, the flocks and all the animals, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The plunder remaining from the spoil that the army had taken was 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 persons in all, women who had not known a man by lying with him.
The half, the share of those who had gone out to war, was in number 337,500 sheep,
and the LORD's tribute from the sheep was 675.
The cattle were 36,000, of which the LORD's tribute was 72.
The donkeys were 30,500, of which the LORD's tribute was 61.
The persons were 16,000, of whom the LORD's tribute was 32.
Moses gave the tribute, which was the LORD's contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD commanded Moses.
As for the Israelites' half, which Moses separated from that of the men who had gone to war,
the community's half was 337,500 sheep,
36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys
and 16,000 persons.
From the Israelites' half Moses took one in every fifty, both of persons and of animals, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
Then the officers who were over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, came near to Moses
and said to him, "Your servants have counted the men of war who are in our charge, and not one of us is missing.
So we have brought as an offering to the LORD what each man found of gold ornaments: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and pendants, to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all of it in worked ornaments.
All the gold of the contribution that they presented to the LORD, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was 16,750 shekels.
The men of war had each taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
The Reubenites and the Gadites had very large herds and flocks. They saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead were a good place for livestock.
So the Gadites and the Reubenites came and said to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the community:
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon,
the land that the LORD struck down before the community of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.
If we have found favour in your eyes," they said, "let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, "Are your brothers to go to war while you sit here?
Why do you discourage the Israelites from crossing over into the land that the LORD has given them?
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and they discouraged the Israelites from going into the land that the LORD had given them.
The LORD's anger blazed on that day, and he swore an oath:
'None of the men who came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upwards, will see the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, because they have not followed me fully,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have followed the LORD fully.'
The anger of the LORD blazed against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the sight of the LORD was finished.
And now you have risen up in place of your fathers, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the burning anger of the LORD against Israel.
If you turn away from following him, he will once more abandon them in the wilderness, and you will bring ruin on all this people."
They came up to him and said, "We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones,
but we will arm ourselves and go ahead of the Israelites, until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones will live in the fortified cities, because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every one of the Israelites has taken possession of his inheritance.
We will not inherit with them across the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan to the east."
Moses said to them, "If you will do this, if you will arm yourselves for the war before the LORD,
and every armed man of you crosses the Jordan before the LORD, until he has driven out his enemies from before him,
and the land is subdued before the LORD, then afterwards you may return and be free of obligation to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be your possession before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, then you have sinned against the LORD, and be sure that your sin will find you out.
Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, but do what you have said."
The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, "Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our flocks and all our livestock will stay there in the cities of Gilead,
but your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over before the LORD to battle, as my lord says."
So Moses gave a command about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites.

Moses said to them, "If the Gadites and the Reubenites, every man armed for battle, cross over the Jordan with you before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you are to give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
But if they do not cross over armed with you, they are to receive possessions among you in the land of Canaan."
The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, "What the LORD has said to your servants, we will do.
We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance will remain with us on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with its cities and the territories of the surrounding cities.
The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo and Baal-meon (their names were changed) and Sibmah. They gave other names to the cities that they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were in it.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled in it.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages, and called them Havvoth-jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and called it Nobah, after his own name.
These are the stages of the Israelites, when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Moses wrote down their starting places, stage by stage, at the command of the LORD. These are their stages according to their starting places:
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them. On their gods also the LORD executed judgements.
So the Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which is east of Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from before Hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness. They went a three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the Israelites.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the territory of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim on the plains of Moab.
The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you are to drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you. Destroy all their carved figures and destroy all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.
You are to take possession of the land and live in it, for I have given the land to you to possess.

You are to divide the land by lot according to your clans. To a larger group you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that will be his. You are to inherit according to the tribes of your ancestors.

But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those you let remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they will trouble you in the land where you live.
And what I planned to do to them I will do to you."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and tell them: When you come into the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan with its borders.
Your southern side will be from the wilderness of Zin alongside Edom. Your southern border will run from the end of the Dead Sea on the east.
Your border will turn south of the ascent of Akrabbim, cross to Zin and run south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go on to Hazar-addar and cross to Azmon.
The border will turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea.
For your western border you will have the Great Sea and its coast. This will be your western border.
This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea you are to draw a line to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you are to draw a line to Lebo-hamath, and the border will reach Zedad.
The border will go on to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
For your eastern border you are to draw a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. The border will go down and reach the slope of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east.
The border will go down to the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea. This will be your land, with its borders all round."
Moses commanded the Israelites: "This is the land that you are to inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes.
For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral houses, and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, towards the sunrise."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"These are the names of the men who are to divide the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
You are to take one leader from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance.
These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of the Simeonites, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of the Danites, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli;
from the sons of Joseph, from the tribe of the Manassites, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod;
from the tribe of the Ephraimites, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
from the tribe of the Zebulunites, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of the Issacharites, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan;
from the tribe of the Asherites, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of the Naphtalites, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance among the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Command the Israelites to give to the Levites, from the inheritance that they possess, towns in which to live. You are also to give the Levites pasture land round the towns.
The towns will be theirs to live in, and the pasture land will be for their cattle, their goods and all their animals.
The pasture land of the towns that you give to the Levites is to reach from the wall of the town outwards a thousand cubits all round.

You are to measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand cubits on the south side, two thousand cubits on the west side and two thousand cubits on the north side, with the town in the middle. This will be the pasture land for their towns.
The towns that you give to the Levites will be the six cities of refuge, which you are to give for the one who has killed to flee to, and in addition to them you are to give forty-two towns.
All the towns that you give to the Levites will be forty-eight towns, with their pasture lands.

As for the towns that you give from the possession of the Israelites, you are to take more from the larger tribes and fewer from the smaller. Each tribe, according to the inheritance it receives, is to give some of its towns to the Levites."
The LORD spoke to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you are to choose towns to be your cities of refuge, so that a person who has killed another by mistake may flee there.
The towns will be for you a refuge from the avenger, so that the one who has killed may not die until he stands before the assembly for judgement.
The towns that you give are to be six cities of refuge for you.
You are to give three towns across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan, to be cities of refuge.
These six towns are to be a refuge for the Israelites, for the foreigner and for the resident among them, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake may flee there.
But if he strikes him with an iron tool so that he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer is to be put to death.
If he strikes him with a stone in the hand, by which a person could die, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer is to be put to death.
Or if he strikes him with a wooden tool in the hand, by which a person could die, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer is to be put to death.
The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he is to put him to death.
If he pushes him out of hatred, or throws something at him on purpose, so that he dies,
or strikes him with his hand in enmity so that he dies, the one who struck him is to be put to death. He is a murderer. The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death when he meets him.
But if he pushes him suddenly without enmity, or throws something at him without lying in wait,
or, without seeing him, drops on him any stone by which a person could die, so that he dies, though he was not his enemy and did not seek his harm,
then the assembly is to judge between the one who struck and the avenger of blood, according to these rulings.

The assembly is to protect the one who killed from the hand of the avenger of blood, and the assembly is to return him to his city of refuge, to which he fled. He is to live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the one who killed ever goes outside the border of his city of refuge to which he fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the border of his city of refuge and kills him, the avenger is not guilty of blood,
because the one who killed was to live in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest the one who killed may return to the land of his possession.
These are to be a legal rule for you through your generations, in all your dwellings.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer is to be put to death on the evidence of witnesses. But a single witness is not enough for a person to be put to death.
You are not to take a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, but he is to be put to death.
You are not to take a ransom for someone who has fled to his city of refuge, to allow him to return and live in the land before the death of the high priest.
You are not to pollute the land where you live. Blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
You are not to defile the land in which you live, in the midst of which I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell in the midst of the Israelites."

The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.

They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

But if they are married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. So it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.

And when the Jubilee of the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our ancestors."
Moses commanded the Israelites at the word of the LORD: "The tribe of the sons of Joseph is right in what they say.
This is what the LORD commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whom they think best, only they must marry within the clan of their father's tribe.
No inheritance of the Israelites is to be passed from one tribe to another, for every one of the Israelites is to hold on to the inheritance of the tribe of his ancestors.

Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the Israelites is to be married to one from the clan of her father's tribe, so that every one of the Israelites may possess the inheritance of his ancestors.
No inheritance is to be passed from one tribe to another, for each of the tribes of the Israelites is to hold on to its own inheritance."
The daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married to their cousins on their father's side.
They were married into the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father's clan.
These are the commands and the rulings that the LORD commanded the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel on the far side of the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Dizahab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of the hill country of Seir.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
On the far side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to set out this teaching. He said:
"At Horeb the LORD our God said to us, 'You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Break camp and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all the places near it: the Arabah, the hills, the lowland, the Negev and the coast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.

Look, I have placed the land in front of you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD promised by oath to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to give to them and to their descendants after them.'
At that time I told you, 'I cannot carry you by myself.
The LORD your God has made you many, and today you are as numerous as the stars of the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you as he promised.
But how can I alone bear your burden, your load and your quarrels?
Choose for each of your tribes men who are wise, discerning and respected, and I will make them your heads.'
You answered me, 'What you propose is good.'
So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as your leaders: commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of tens, and officers for your tribes.
At that time I instructed your judges: 'Listen to the disputes between your kinsmen, and judge fairly between one man and another, whether he is a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living with him.
Do not show favouritism in judging. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgement belongs to God. Bring me any case too hard for you, and I will hear it.'
At that time I also told you everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and crossed all that vast and fearsome wilderness that you saw, on the road to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we reached Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, 'You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
Look, the LORD your God has placed the land in front of you. Go up and take possession of it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.'
Then all of you came to me and said, 'Let us send men ahead of us to search the land for us and bring back word about the road we should take and the cities we will come to.'
The idea seemed good to me, so I chose twelve of you, one man for each tribe.
They set out and went up into the hills and came to the Valley of Eshcol and scouted it.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They reported, 'It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us.'
But you refused to go up. You rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
You murmured in your tents and said, 'The LORD hates us. He brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.

Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt. They say, "The people are bigger and taller than we are. The cities are huge, with walls up to the sky. We even saw the sons of the Anakites there."'
I said to you, 'Do not be terrified and do not be afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who goes ahead of you, will fight for you himself, as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way you travelled until you reached this place.'
Yet in spite of this word, you did not trust the LORD your God,
who went ahead of you on the road to find you a place to camp, in fire by night and in a cloud by day, to show you the way you were to go.
The LORD heard what you said and was angry, and he swore an oath:
'Not one of these men, this wicked generation, will see the good land that I promised by oath to give to your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his descendants the land he has walked on, because he has followed the LORD fully.'
With me too the LORD was angry because of you. He said, 'You also will not go in there.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands in your service, will go in. Encourage him, for he will lead Israel to inherit it.
As for your little ones, whom you said would be taken as spoil, and your children, who do not yet know good from evil, they will go in. I will give the land to them, and they will possess it.
But you, turn round and set out for the wilderness, on the road to the Red Sea.'

Then you answered me, 'We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, as the LORD our God commanded us.' Each of you strapped on his weapons of war, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hills.
The LORD said to me, 'Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, and you will be struck down by your enemies.'
I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command and, in your arrogance, you went up into the hills.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees, and they beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD would not hear your voice or turn his ear to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh for many days, as long as you stayed."
"We turned and set out for the wilderness on the road to the Red Sea, as the LORD had told me, and for many days we went round the hill country of Seir.
Then the LORD said to me:
'You have gone round this hill country long enough. Turn north.
Give the people this command: You are about to pass through the territory of your kinsmen, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so take great care.
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a foot's width, because I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his possession.
You may buy food from them with silver, so that you can eat, and you may buy water from them with silver, so that you can drink.

For the LORD your God has blessed you in everything you have done. He has watched over your journey through this great wilderness. For these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.'
So we passed by our kinsmen, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the road of the Arabah, away from Elath and Ezion-geber. We turned and went by the road of the wilderness of Moab.
The LORD said to me, 'Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.'
(The Emites had lived there before, a people great and many and as tall as the Anakites.
They too are counted as Rephaim, like the Anakites, though the Moabites call them Emites.

The Horites also lived in Seir before, but the descendants of Esau drove them out and destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did to the land of its possession that the LORD gave them.)
'Now get up and cross the valley of the Zered.' So we crossed the valley of the Zered.

The time from our leaving Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the valley of the Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men had died out from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
The hand of the LORD was against them to remove them from the camp, until they had all died.
When all the fighting men had died and were gone from among the people,
the LORD said to me:
'Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.

When you come near the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as a possession, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.'
(That also is counted as a land of the Rephaim. The Rephaim lived there before, though the Ammonites call them Zamzummites,
a people great and many and as tall as the Anakites. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place,
just as he did for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, and they drove them out and settled in their place, as they are to this day.
As for the Avvites, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorites, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.)
'Get up, set out and cross the valley of the Arnon. Look, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession of it, and engage him in battle.
This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you on the peoples under all the heavens. When they hear the report of you, they will tremble and be in anguish because of you.'
From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace:
'Let me pass through your land. I will keep to the road, and I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
You will sell me food for silver, so that I may eat, and you will give me water for silver, so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.'
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through, for the LORD your God made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, in order to hand him over to you, as he is today.
The LORD said to me, 'Look, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession of it, so that you may occupy his land.'
Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.
The LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down, with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his towns, and we devoted to destruction every town, men, women and little ones. We left no survivor.
Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, with the spoil of the towns we had captured.
From Aroer, on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and from the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was not a town too high for us. The LORD our God gave everything over to us.
Only to the land of the Ammonites you did not go near, to all the banks of the Jabbok and the towns of the hill country, or to anything the LORD our God had forbidden."
"Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.'
So the LORD our God also handed over to us Og king of Bashan and all his people. We struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
At that time we captured all his towns. There was not one of the towns we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these were towns fortified with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town, men, women and little ones.
But all the livestock and the plunder from the towns we took as spoil for ourselves.
So at that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land east of the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),
all the towns of the plateau, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
(Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was an iron bed. Is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the standard cubit.)

When we took possession of this land at that time, I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the land from Aroer, on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
The rest of Gilead, and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (The whole region of Argob, all that Bashan, used to be called a land of the Rephaim.

Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called the villages after his own name, Havvoth-jair, as they are still called today.)
To Machir I gave Gilead.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the land from Gilead down to the valley of the Arnon, with the middle of the valley as the border, as far as the Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites,
and the Arabah, with the Jordan as its border, from Chinnereth down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you: 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your kinsmen the Israelites.
Only your wives, your little ones and your livestock (I know you have a great deal of livestock) are to stay in the towns I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your kinsmen as he has to you, and they too possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you.'
I also commanded Joshua at that time: 'Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to cross into.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.'
At that time I pleaded with the LORD:
'Lord GOD, you have only begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. What god in heaven or on earth can do deeds and mighty acts like yours?
Please let me cross over and see the good land across the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.'
But the LORD was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, 'Enough! Do not speak to me again about this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes to the west, the north, the south and the east, and look at it with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
But commission Joshua, and encourage him and make him strong, for he will cross over at the head of this people and will bring them into possession of the land you will see.'
So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

"Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the rulings that I am teaching you, and do them, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
You are not to add anything to the word that I am commanding you, and you are not to take anything away from it, so that you may keep the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
Your own eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for the LORD your God destroyed from among you every man who followed the Baal of Peor.
But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all alive today.
See, I have taught you statutes and rulings, as the LORD my God commanded me, for you to do in the land that you are entering to take possession of it.

Keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples. When they hear all these statutes, they will say, 'This great nation is surely a wise and understanding people.'
For what great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has statutes and rulings as just as all this teaching that I am setting before you today?

Only be careful, and guard yourselves closely, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not slip from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and to your children's children,

how on the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, the LORD said to me, 'Gather the people to me, so that I may let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach their children.'
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain burned with fire up to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud and thick gloom.
The LORD spoke to you out of the middle of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form. There was only a voice.
He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to keep, the Ten Words, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
And at that time the LORD commanded me to teach you statutes and rulings, for you to do in the land that you are crossing over to possess.
So be very careful, for you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb out of the middle of the fire.
Take care that you do not act corruptly by making for yourselves a carved image in the shape of any figure: the likeness of a male or a female,
the likeness of any animal on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the likeness of anything that crawls on the ground, the likeness of any fish in the waters below the earth.

And take care that you do not lift up your eyes to the sky and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, and are drawn away to bow down to them and serve them, things that the LORD your God has given to all the peoples under all the heavens.
But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be a people for his own possession, as you are today.
The LORD was angry with me because of you, and he swore that I would not cross the Jordan and not enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am going to die in this land. I will not cross the Jordan. But you are going to cross over and take possession of that good land.
Take care that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God that he made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image in the shape of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have children and grandchildren and have lived long in the land, if you act corruptly and make a carved image in the shape of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, to make him angry,

I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will soon perish from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long in it, but will be completely destroyed.
The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will be left among the nations where the LORD will drive you.
There you will serve gods made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him, if you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
In your distress, when all these things have come upon you, in the later days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.

Ask now about the days of long ago, before your time, from the day God created humankind on the earth, and ask from one end of the sky to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has a people ever heard the voice of a god speaking out of the middle of the fire, as you have, and lived?

Or has a god ever tried to come and take a nation for himself from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs and wonders, by war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great and terrifying acts, as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God. There is no other besides him.
From heaven he let you hear his voice to instruct you. On earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words out of the middle of the fire.
And because he loved your ancestors and chose their descendants after them, he brought you out of Egypt himself, with his own presence, by his great power,
driving out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
So know today, and take it to heart: the LORD is God in the heavens above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Keep his statutes and his commands, which I am giving you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time."
Then Moses set apart three towns east of the Jordan,
so that someone who killed another person without intending it, and had not been his enemy in the past, could flee there. Fleeing to one of these towns, he could save his life:
Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the teaching that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the decrees, the statutes and the rulings that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
across the Jordan in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites defeated when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan to the east,
from Aroer, on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, as far as Mount Sirion (that is, Hermon),
together with all the Arabah on the east side of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: "Hear, Israel, the statutes and rulings that I am speaking in your hearing today. Learn them, and take care to do them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
The LORD did not make this covenant with our ancestors, but with us, with all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke with you face to face at the mountain, out of the middle of the fire.
At that time I stood between the LORD and you, to tell you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You will have no other gods in my presence.
You will not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.
You will not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, bringing the guilt of parents on their children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
and showing faithful love to the thousandth generation of those who love me and keep my commands.
You will not use the name of the LORD your God for a worthless purpose, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who uses his name in that way.
Keep the Sabbath day and make it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
For six days you are to labour and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath for the LORD your God. On it you will do no work, neither you, nor your son or your daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner who lives within your gates, so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honour your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You will not murder.
You will not commit adultery.
You will not steal.
You will not give false evidence against your neighbour.
You will not covet your neighbour's wife. You will not desire your neighbour's house, his field, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbour.'

These words the LORD spoke to your whole assembly at the mountain, out of the middle of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, in a great voice, and he added nothing more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

and said, 'Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the middle of the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being, and the human being still lives.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any more, we will die.
For what mortal has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near, and hear all that the LORD our God says. Then tell us everything that the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and do it.'
The LORD heard what you said when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they said was right.
If only their hearts were always like this, so that they would fear me and keep all my commands, so that it would go well with them and with their children for ever!
Go and tell them, "Return to your tents."
But you, stay here beside me, and I will tell you the whole command, the statutes and the rulings that you are to teach them, so that they may do them in the land that I am giving them to possess.'
So take care to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. You are not to turn aside to the right or to the left.
You are to walk in the whole way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and that it may go well with you, and that you may live long in the land that you will possess."
"This is the command, the statutes and the rulings that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may do them in the land you are crossing into to possess,
so that you may fear the LORD your God, you and your son and your grandson, all the days of your life, by keeping all his statutes and commands that I am giving you, and so that you may live long.

Listen, Israel, and take care to do it, so that it may go well with you, and so that you may become very many, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
You are to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
These words that I am commanding you today are to be on your heart.
You are to repeat them to your children, and talk about them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
You are to tie them as a sign on your hand, and they are to be as bands between your eyes.
You are to write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you, a land with great and good cities that you did not build,
with houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, with cisterns cut out of the rock that you did not cut, with vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant, and you eat and are full,
take care that you do not forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You are to fear the LORD your God. You are to serve him, and you are to swear by his name.
You are not to follow other gods, any of the gods of the peoples around you,
for the LORD your God, who is in your midst, is a jealous God. Otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will blaze against you, and he will wipe you off the face of the earth.
You are not to put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested him at Massah.
You are to keep carefully the commands of the LORD your God, and his decrees and statutes that he has commanded you.

You are to do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you, and so that you may go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to give to your ancestors,
driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has promised.
When your son asks you in time to come, 'What is the meaning of the decrees, the statutes and the rulings that the LORD our God has commanded you?'
you are to tell your son, 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
The LORD sent signs and wonders, great and harsh, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and against all his household, before our eyes.
And he brought us out from there, so that he could bring us in and give us the land he had sworn to our ancestors.
The LORD commanded us to do all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, so that he might keep us alive, as we are today.
It will be righteousness for us if we are careful to keep this whole command before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us.'"

"When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, and clears away many nations ahead of you, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, seven nations larger and stronger than you,
and when the LORD your God hands them over to you and you strike them down, you are to devote them to destruction. You are not to make a treaty with them or show them favour.
You are not to marry into them. You are not to give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons,
for they would turn your children away from following me, to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD would blaze against you, and he would destroy you quickly.
This is what you are to do to them: pull down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their sacred poles and burn their carved images in the fire.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his own treasured people.
The LORD did not set his heart on you and choose you because you were more numerous than other peoples. You were the smallest of all peoples.

It was because the LORD loved you, and because he was keeping the oath he swore to your ancestors, that the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
So know that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and faithful love to the thousandth generation with those who love him and keep his commands,
but who repays to their face those who hate him, destroying them. He does not delay with one who hates him. He repays him to his face.
So keep the command, the statutes and the rulings that I am giving you today, and do them.
If you listen to these rulings and keep them and do them, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the faithful love that he swore to your ancestors.

He will love you and bless you and make you many. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, your new wine and your oil, the young of your cattle and the lambs of your flock, in the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. There will be no barren man or woman among you, and none among your livestock.
The LORD will take away all sickness from you. He will not lay on you any of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you knew, but will lay them on all who hate you.
You are to consume all the peoples that the LORD your God hands over to you. Show them no pity, and do not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
If you say to yourselves, 'These nations are stronger than I am. How can I drive them out?'
do not be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt,

the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the strong hand and outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you fear.
Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet against them, until even those who survive and hide from you are destroyed.
Do not be terrified by them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and awe-inspiring God.
The LORD your God will clear away these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to finish them off all at once, or the wild animals would multiply against you.
But the LORD your God will hand them over to you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will give their kings into your hand, and you will wipe out their names from under the heavens. No one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You are to burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. You are not to covet the silver and gold on them or take it for yourselves, or you will be trapped by it, for it is abhorrent to the LORD your God.
You are not to bring an abhorrent thing into your house, or you will be devoted to destruction like it. You are to loathe it completely and utterly detest it, for it is devoted to destruction."
"Take care to keep the whole command that I am giving you today, so that you may live and increase and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors.

Remember the whole road that the LORD your God has led you along these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you and to test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commands or not.

He humbled you and let you go hungry, and then fed you with manna, which you did not know and your ancestors did not know, to make you understand that a person does not live on bread alone, but lives on everything that comes out of the mouth of the LORD.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell, these forty years.
Know in your heart that, as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
So keep the commands of the LORD your God, by walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of springs and underground waters welling up in valleys and hills,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
a land where you will eat bread without scarcity, where you will lack nothing, a land whose rocks are iron, and from whose hills you can dig copper.
You will eat and be full, and you are to bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
Take care that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, his rulings and his statutes that I am giving you today,
so that, when you have eaten and are full, and have built good houses and lived in them,
and your herds and flocks have multiplied, and your silver and gold have multiplied, and everything you have has multiplied,
your heart does not become proud, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty land with no water, who brought water for you out of the flinty rock,
who fed you in the wilderness with manna that your ancestors did not know, to humble you and test you, so as to do you good in the end.
Beware of saying in your heart, 'My own strength and the power of my own hand have won me this wealth.'
Remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you the power to gain wealth, to confirm his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as he does today.
If you forget the LORD your God and follow other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will certainly perish.
Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you will perish, because you would not listen to the voice of the LORD your God."
"Hear, Israel: today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations larger and stronger than you, with great cities fortified up to the sky,
a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anakites, whom you know and about whom you have heard it said, 'Who can stand against the descendants of Anak?'

Know today that the LORD your God is the one who goes over ahead of you, as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and bring them down before you, and you will drive them out and destroy them quickly, as the LORD has promised you.

After the LORD your God has pushed them out before you, do not say in your heart, 'It is because of my righteousness that the LORD has brought me in to possess this land.' It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to possess their land. It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is driving them out before you, and in order to keep the word that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
So know that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stubborn people.
Remember, and do not forget, how you made the LORD your God angry in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
Even at Horeb you made the LORD angry, and the LORD was so furious with you that he was ready to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.

The LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the middle of the fire on the day of the assembly.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, 'Get up and go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them. They have made a cast image for themselves.'
The LORD also said to me, 'I have looked at this people, and they are a stubborn people.
Let me be, so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens. Then I will make a nation of you that is stronger and greater than they are.'
So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire. The two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
I looked, and there you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves a cast calf. You had quickly turned aside from the way the LORD had commanded you.
So I took hold of the two tablets and threw them from my two hands and broke them before your eyes.

Then I fell down before the LORD as before, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all the sin you had committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and making him angry.
For I was afraid of the anger and fury that the LORD had against you, so that he was ready to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time also.
The LORD was so angry with Aaron that he was ready to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

I took the thing you had made, your sin, the calf, and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it thoroughly, until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.
At Taberah too, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you made the LORD angry.

When the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said, 'Go up and take possession of the land that I have given you,' you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
You have been rebelling against the LORD from the day I first knew you.
So I fell down before the LORD those forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD: 'Lord GOD, do not destroy your people, your own inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness or their sin,

or the land from which you brought us out will say, "Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land he promised them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness."
They are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.'"
"At that time the LORD said to me, 'Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Make a wooden chest also.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you smashed, and you are to put them in the chest.'
So I made a chest of acacia wood and cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

He wrote on the tablets what had been written the first time, the Ten Words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the middle of the fire on the day of the assembly. And the LORD gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the chest I had made. They are there still, as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites set out from Beeroth-bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they set out for Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve him and to bless in his name, as they do to this day.
That is why Levi has no portion or inheritance with his kinsmen. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God told him.)
I stayed on the mountain, as I had the first time, forty days and forty nights. The LORD listened to me that time also, and the LORD did not choose to destroy you.
The LORD said to me, 'Get up and go on your way ahead of the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.'

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? Only this: to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commands and statutes of the LORD that I am giving you today, for your own good.
Look, to the LORD your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it.
Yet the LORD set his heart in love on your ancestors alone, and chose their descendants after them, you, out of all the peoples, as you are today.
So circumcise your hearts, and do not be stubborn any longer.
For the LORD your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awe-inspiring, who shows no favouritism and takes no bribe.
He brings justice for the orphan and the widow, and loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
So you also are to love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You are to fear the LORD your God. You are to serve him, hold fast to him and swear by his name.
He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awe-inspiring things that your own eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt, seventy persons in all, and now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars of the sky.
"So you are to love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his rulings and his commands always.

Know today that it is not your children, who have not known and have not seen, but you yourselves who have seen the discipline of the LORD your God, his greatness, his strong hand and outstretched arm,
his signs and his deeds that he did in the middle of Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,
what he did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and chariots, how he made the water of the Red Sea flow over them as they chased you, and how the LORD destroyed them, as is plain to this day,
what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and their tents and every living creature that belonged to them, in the middle of all Israel.
For your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did.
So keep the whole command that I am giving you today, so that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land you are crossing into,
and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where you sowed your seed and watered it by foot, like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are crossing into to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water from the rain of heaven,
a land that the LORD your God looks after. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you listen carefully to my commands that I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I will give the rain for your land at its proper time, the autumn rain and the spring rain, so that you may gather in your grain, your new wine and your oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be full.
Take care that your heart is not led astray, so that you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

Then the anger of the LORD would blaze against you, and he would shut up the sky so that there would be no rain and the land would yield no produce, and you would soon perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you.
Put these words of mine on your heart and on your soul. Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be as bands between your eyes.
Teach them to your children, talking about them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children may be many in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them, as many as the days of the heavens above the earth.
For if you take care to keep all this command that I am giving you, to do it, loving the LORD your God, walking in all his ways and holding fast to him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations larger and stronger than you.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your territory will reach from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the river, the Euphrates, to the western sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will put the fear and dread of you on all the land you tread on, as he promised you.
See, today I am setting before you a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today,
