and the curse, if you do not listen to the commands of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the road I am commanding you today, to follow other gods that you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, you are to set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not across the Jordan, beyond the western road, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, near the oaks of Moreh?
For you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
Take care to do all the statutes and rulings that I am setting before you today."
"These are the statutes and rulings that you are to take care to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, all the days that you live on the earth.
You are to destroy completely all the places where the nations you are driving out served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills and under every leafy tree.
Pull down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn their sacred poles in the fire, cut down the carved images of their gods, and wipe out their names from that place.
You are not to worship the LORD your God in that way.
Instead, you are to look for the place that the LORD your God will choose out of all your tribes, to put his name there and make his dwelling, and there you are to go.

There you are to bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution from your hand, your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
There you and your households are to eat before the LORD your God and rejoice in everything you have put your hand to, in which the LORD your God has blessed you.
You are not to do as we are doing here today, each one doing whatever is right in his own eyes,
for you have not yet reached the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and he gives you rest from all your enemies around you, so that you live in safety,

then to the place that the LORD your God will choose, to make his name live there, you are to bring everything I am commanding you: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution from your hand, and all the choice offerings you have vowed to the LORD.

You are to rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who lives within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance with you.
Take care that you do not offer your burnt offerings in any place you see,
but only in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes. There you are to offer your burnt offerings, and there you are to do everything I am commanding you.

You may, however, slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates, as much as you wish, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as with the gazelle and the deer.
Only you are not to eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, your new wine or your oil, or the firstborn of your herds or flocks, or any of the offerings you have vowed, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution from your hand.

You are to eat these before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God will choose, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite who lives within your gates. You are to rejoice before the LORD your God in everything you put your hand to.
Take care that you do not neglect the Levite for as long as you live in your land.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he has promised you, and you say, 'I want to eat meat,' because you have a craving for meat, you may eat meat whenever you wish.

If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name is too far from you, you may slaughter any of your herd or flock that the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and eat within your gates whenever you wish.
Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you may eat it. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
Only be sure not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you are not to eat the life with the meat.
You are not to eat it. Pour it out on the ground like water.
You are not to eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
But your holy gifts and your vow offerings you are to take and bring to the place that the LORD will choose,

and offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices is to be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.

Be careful to listen to all these words that I am commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you for ever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations that you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

take care that you are not trapped into following them, after they have been destroyed before you, and that you do not ask about their gods, saying, 'How did these nations serve their gods? I will do the same.'
You are not to worship the LORD your God in that way, for every abhorrent thing that the LORD hates they have done for their gods. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
Everything that I am commanding you, take care to do. You are not to add anything to it or take anything from it."
"If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams appears among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or the wonder that he spoke of comes true, and he says, 'Let us follow other gods,' which you have not known, 'and let us serve them,'
you are not to listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer of dreams. For the LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
It is the LORD your God you are to follow and fear. You are to keep his commands and listen to his voice, serve him and hold fast to him.

That prophet or dreamer of dreams is to be put to death, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to draw you away from the way that the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife you hold in your arms, or your friend who is like your own self, secretly entices you, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods,' which neither you nor your ancestors have known,
any of the gods of the peoples around you, near to you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other,
you are not to give in to him or listen to him. Do not let your eye pity him, do not spare him, and do not cover for him.
You must kill him. Your hand is to be the first against him to put him to death, and afterwards the hands of all the people.
You are to stone him to death, because he tried to draw you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and never again do such an evil thing among you.
If you hear it said about one of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
that worthless men have gone out from among you and led the people of their town astray, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods,' which you have not known,
then you are to enquire, search out and ask carefully. If it is true and certain that this abhorrent thing has been done among you,
you are to strike down the people of that town with the sword, devoting it to destruction, with everything in it and its livestock, with the edge of the sword.

You are to gather all its plunder into the middle of its open square and burn the town and all its plunder completely, as an offering to the LORD your God. It is to be a heap for ever. It is never to be rebuilt.
Nothing from what is devoted is to stay in your hand, so that the LORD may turn from his fierce anger and show you mercy and have compassion on you and make you many, as he swore to your ancestors,
when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commands that I am giving you today, and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God."
"You are children of the LORD your God. You are not to cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be a people for his own possession.
You are not to eat anything abhorrent.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and that brings up the cud.

But among those that bring up the cud or have a divided hoof, you are not to eat these: the camel, the hare and the hyrax. They bring up the cud but do not have a divided hoof, so they are unclean for you.
The pig is also unclean for you, because it has a divided hoof but does not bring up the cud. You are not to eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
Of everything that lives in the water, you may eat these: you may eat whatever has fins and scales.
But you are not to eat anything that does not have fins and scales. It is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these are the ones you are not to eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the falcon, the kite of any kind,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the long-eared owl, the white owl,
the desert owl, the osprey, the cormorant,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
All winged insects are unclean for you. They are not to be eaten.
You may eat any clean winged creature.

You are not to eat anything that has died naturally. You may give it to the foreigner living in your towns, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. You are not to boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Every year you are to set aside a tenth of all the produce of your seed that comes from the field.

In the presence of the LORD your God, in the place he will choose to make his name live there, you are to eat the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, so that you may learn always to fear the LORD your God.
If the journey is too long for you, and you cannot carry it, because the place the LORD your God will choose to put his name is too far from you, when the LORD your God has blessed you,
then you may exchange it for silver, bind up the silver in your hand and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.

There you may spend the silver on anything you want: oxen, sheep, wine or strong drink, anything you crave. You are to eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
Do not neglect the Levite who lives in your towns, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
At the end of every three years you are to bring out the whole tithe of your produce for that year and store it in your towns.

Then the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the foreigner, the orphan and the widow who live in your towns, may come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
"At the end of every seven years you are to grant a release.

This is how the release is to be done: every creditor is to release what he has lent to his neighbour. He is not to press his neighbour, his fellow Israelite, for repayment, because a release for the LORD has been proclaimed.
You may press a foreigner for it, but whatever your fellow Israelite owes you, your hand is to release.
But there will be no poor among you, for the LORD will certainly bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
if only you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and take care to keep all this command that I am giving you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you as he promised. You will lend to many nations but will not borrow, and you will rule over many nations but they will not rule over you.

If there is a poor person among you, one of your fellow Israelites, in any of the towns of the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor kinsman.
Instead, open your hand to him and lend him enough to meet his need, whatever it may be.

Take care that no worthless thought enters your mind, saying, 'The seventh year, the year of release, is near,' so that you look with ill will on your poor kinsman and give him nothing, and he cries out to the LORD against you, and it becomes sin for you.
Give to him freely, and do not let your heart be grudging when you give, because for this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.
For there will always be poor people in the land. That is why I am commanding you: open your hand wide to your kinsman, to the needy and to the poor in your land.
If your fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you, he is to serve you for six years, and in the seventh year you are to let him go free.
When you let him go free, do not send him away empty-handed.
Provide for him generously from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress. Give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I am commanding you this today.
But if he says to you, 'I do not want to leave you,' because he loves you and your household, since he is well off with you,
then take an awl and push it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same with your female servant.
Do not think it hard to let him go free, because in six years he has given you the service of a hired worker at half the cost. And the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
Every firstborn male born in your herd and flock you are to set apart for the LORD your God. You are not to work the firstborn of your herd or shear the firstborn of your flock.
You and your household are to eat it every year before the LORD your God, in the place the LORD will choose.
But if it has a defect, if it is lame or blind or has any serious defect, you are not to sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
You may eat it within your towns. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as with the gazelle and the deer.
Only you are not to eat its blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
"Keep the month of Abib and hold the Passover for the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You are to sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God, from the flock or the herd, in the place the LORD will choose to make his name live there.

Do not eat anything leavened with it. For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, because you came out of the land of Egypt in a hurry, so that all the days of your life you may remember the day you came out of Egypt.
For seven days no yeast is to be seen with you anywhere in your territory, and none of the meat that you sacrifice on the evening of the first day is to be left until morning.
You are not to sacrifice the Passover in any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you,
but only in the place the LORD your God will choose to make his name live. There you are to sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at sunset, at the time of day you came out of Egypt.
You are to cook it and eat it in the place the LORD your God will choose. In the morning you may turn back and go to your tents.
For six days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there is to be a closing assembly for the LORD your God. You are not to do any work.
You are to count seven weeks. Begin to count the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Then you are to keep the Festival of Weeks for the LORD your God, with a freewill offering from your hand, which you are to give according to the way the LORD your God has blessed you.

You are to rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite who lives in your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan and the widow among you, in the place the LORD your God will choose to make his name live.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and take care to keep these statutes.
You are to keep the Festival of Booths for seven days, after you have gathered in the produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
You are to rejoice in your festival, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite, and the foreigner, the orphan and the widow who live in your towns.

For seven days you are to keep the festival for the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you will be completely joyful.

Three times a year all your men are to appear before the LORD your God in the place he will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths. They are not to appear before the LORD empty-handed.
Each is to give as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
You are to appoint judges and officers for yourselves in all your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they are to judge the people with right judgement.
You are not to twist justice. You are not to show favouritism, and you are not to take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and distorts the words of the righteous.
Justice, only justice, you are to pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You are not to plant any wooden pole of Asherah beside the altar that you build for the LORD your God.
And you are not to set up a sacred pillar, which the LORD your God hates."
"You are not to sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect, any serious flaw, for that is abhorrent to the LORD your God.
If a man or a woman is found among you, in any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you, who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God and breaks his covenant,
and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have forbidden,
and it is reported to you and you hear of it, you are to make a thorough enquiry. If it is true and certain that this abhorrent thing has been done in Israel,
you are to bring out to your gates that man or that woman who has done this evil thing, and stone that man or woman to death.
A person is to be put to death on the evidence of two witnesses or three. He is not to be put to death on the evidence of one witness alone.
The hands of the witnesses are to be the first against him to put him to death, and afterwards the hands of all the people. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.

If a case is too hard for you to decide, whether between one kind of bloodshed and another, one kind of legal claim and another, or one kind of assault and another, any matter of dispute in your towns, you are to get up and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Ask them, and they will tell you the verdict.
You are to do what they tell you from that place that the LORD will choose. Take care to do everything they instruct you.
You are to act according to the instruction they give you and the verdict they pronounce for you. Do not turn aside from what they tell you, to the right or to the left.
The man who acts with arrogance and refuses to listen to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, that man is to die. So you are to clear the evil out of Israel.
All the people will hear and be afraid, and will not act with arrogance again.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and take possession of it and live in it, and then say, 'I want to set a king over me, like all the nations around me,'
you may set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. You are to set over you a king from among your own kinsmen. You are not to put a foreigner over you, one who is not your kinsman.
Only he is not to build up many horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to build up many horses, since the LORD has told you, 'You are never to go back that way again.'
He is not to build up many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away. He is not to build up large amounts of silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this teaching, taken from the one that is in the care of the Levitical priests.

It is to stay with him, and he is to read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, and take care to keep all the words of this teaching and these statutes, and do them,

so that his heart is not raised up above his kinsmen, and so that he does not turn aside from the command to the right or to the left, and so that he and his sons may reign long over his kingdom in Israel.
"The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, are to have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the LORD's food offerings as their inheritance.
They are to have no inheritance among their kinsmen. The LORD is their inheritance, as he promised them.
This is to be the priests' due from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they are to give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks and the stomach.
You are to give him the first of your grain, your new wine and your oil, and the first fleece of your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the name of the LORD for ever.
If a Levite comes from any of your towns, from any place in Israel where he is living, and comes with all the longing of his heart to the place the LORD will choose,
he may serve in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They are to have equal shares to eat, apart from what he receives from the sale of his family property.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you are not to learn to do the abhorrent practices of those nations.
No one is to be found among you who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or who practises divination, or tells fortunes, or reads omens, or is a sorcerer,
or casts spells, or consults a medium or a spirit-consulter, or enquires of the dead.
Anyone who does these things is abhorrent to the LORD, and because of these abhorrent practices the LORD your God is driving them out before you.
You are to be wholly devoted to the LORD your God.
For these nations that you are about to dispossess listen to fortune-tellers and diviners. But as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do this.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your own kinsmen. You are to listen to him,
just as you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, 'Do not let me hear the voice of the LORD my God again or see this great fire any more, or I will die.'
The LORD said to me, 'They are right in what they have said.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their kinsmen. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
If anyone does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will call that person to account.
But the prophet who presumes to speak in my name a word that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet is to die.'
You may say in your heart, 'How can we know a word that the LORD has not spoken?'
When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the word does not happen or come true, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it with arrogance. Do not be afraid of him.
"When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their cities and houses,
you are to set apart three towns for yourselves in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
You are to prepare the roads and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God is giving you as a possession, so that anyone who has killed a person may flee there.
This is the rule for the one who kills and may flee there and live: he is someone who kills his neighbour unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.

For example, a man goes into the forest with his neighbour to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down a tree, and the iron head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbour so that he dies. That man may flee to one of these towns and live,

so that the avenger of blood, in the heat of his anger, does not chase the killer and overtake him, because the way is long, and strike him dead, though he does not deserve to die, since he had not hated him in the past.
That is why I am commanding you: set apart three towns for yourselves.
If the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your ancestors, and gives you all the land he promised to give to your ancestors,
if you take care to keep all this command that I am giving you today, by loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always, then you are to add three more towns to these three,
so that innocent blood is not shed in your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and so that the guilt of bloodshed does not rest on you.
But if someone hates his neighbour and lies in wait for him, attacks him and strikes him dead, and then flees to one of these towns,
the elders of his town are to send and take him from there and hand him over to the avenger of blood, so that he may die.
Do not let your eye pity him. You are to clear the guilt of innocent blood out of Israel, so that it may go well with you.
You are not to move your neighbour's boundary stone, which former generations have set, in the inheritance you will receive in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness is not enough to convict anyone of any crime or any wrong in respect of any offence. A matter is to be established on the evidence of two witnesses or three.
If a malicious witness stands up against someone to accuse him of wrongdoing,
both parties to the dispute are to stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office at that time.
The judges are to investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is a false witness who has made a false accusation against his kinsman,
you are to do to him what he meant to do to his kinsman. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.
The rest will hear and be afraid, and never again do such an evil thing among you.
Do not let your eye pity. It is to be life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

"When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and speak to the people.
He is to say to them: 'Hear, Israel. Today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart grow faint. Do not be afraid or panic or tremble before them,
for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.'
Then the officers are to say to the people: 'Is there anyone who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go home, or he may die in the battle and someone else dedicate it.
Is there anyone who has planted a vineyard and has not yet enjoyed it? Let him go home, or he may die in the battle and someone else enjoy it.
Is there anyone who is engaged to a woman and has not yet married her? Let him go home, or he may die in the battle and someone else marry her.'
The officers are to go on and say to the people: 'Is there anyone who is afraid and fainthearted? Let him go home, so that he does not make the hearts of his fellows melt as his own has.'
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, they are to appoint commanders at the head of the people.
When you approach a town to attack it, make an offer of peace to it.
If it accepts your offer of peace and opens its gates to you, all the people in it are to serve you in forced labour.
But if it will not make peace with you and makes war against you, you are to besiege it.
When the LORD your God hands it over to you, you are to put all its males to the sword.

But the women, the little ones, the livestock and everything else in the town, all its plunder, you may take as spoil for yourselves. You may enjoy the plunder from your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.
This is how you are to treat all the towns that are very far from you, those that are not towns of the nations nearby.
But in the towns of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you are not to leave alive anything that breathes.
You are to devote them to destruction: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they do not teach you to do all the abhorrent practices that they do for their gods, and you sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a town for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, you are not to destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them. You may eat from them, but you are not to cut them down. Are the trees of the field human beings, that you should besiege them?
Only the trees that you know are not fruit trees may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the town that is making war with you, until it falls."
"If someone is found killed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, lying in the open country, and it is not known who struck him down,
your elders and your judges are to go out and measure the distances to the towns around the body.
The town nearest the body is to take a heifer that has never been worked and has never pulled in a yoke.
The elders of that town are to bring the heifer down to a valley with a flowing stream, one that has not been ploughed or sown, and break the heifer's neck there in the valley.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, are to come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and every dispute and every case of assault is to be settled by their word.
All the elders of the town nearest the body are to wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
and declare: 'Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it done.
LORD, forgive your people Israel, whom you redeemed. Do not let the guilt of innocent blood remain among your people Israel.' Then the bloodshed will be forgiven them.
So you are to clear the guilt of innocent blood from among you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take captives,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and you desire her and want to take her as your wife,
you are to bring her into your house. She is to shave her head and trim her nails,

and take off the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She is to stay in your house and mourn for her father and mother for a full month. After that you may go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
But if you are not pleased with her, you are to let her go wherever she wishes. You are not to sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have humiliated her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and both the loved and the unloved bear him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the unloved wife,
then on the day he divides his property among his sons, he is not allowed to treat the son of the loved wife as the firstborn in place of the son of the unloved wife, who is the firstborn.
He is to acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the unloved wife, by giving him a double share of all he has, for he is the first sign of his strength. The right of the firstborn is his.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son, who will not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and does not listen to them even when they discipline him,
his father and mother are to take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his town, to the gate of the place where he lives,
and say to the elders of his town, 'This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not listen to us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.'
Then all the men of his town are to stone him to death. So you are to clear the evil out from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
If a man has committed a sin that carries the death penalty and is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his body is not to stay on the tree overnight. You must bury him that same day, for anyone hung on a tree is under God's curse. You are not to defile the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
"You are not to see your kinsman's ox or sheep straying and ignore it. You must take it back to your kinsman.
If your kinsman does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take it to your own house and keep it until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him.
Do the same with his donkey, his cloak, or anything else your kinsman has lost and you find. You are not to ignore it.
You are not to see your kinsman's donkey or ox fallen on the road and ignore it. You must help him lift it up again.
A woman is not to wear a man's clothing, and a man is not to put on a woman's garment, for anyone who does this is abhorrent to the LORD your God.

If you come across a bird's nest beside the road, in any tree or on the ground, with young birds or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, you are not to take the mother together with the young.
You may take the young, but you must let the mother go, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
When you build a new house, make a parapet around your roof, so that you do not bring the guilt of bloodshed on your house if someone falls from it.
You are not to plant your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeit, the seed you sowed and the produce of the vineyard.
You are not to plough with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
You are not to wear cloth made of wool and linen woven together.
You are to make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
If a man marries a woman, and after sleeping with her turns against her,
and charges her with shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, 'I married this woman, but when I came near her I did not find the proofs of her virginity,'
then the young woman's father and mother are to take the proofs of her virginity and bring them to the elders of the town, at the gate.
The young woman's father is to say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has turned against her.

Now he has charged her with shameful conduct, saying, "I did not find the proofs of virginity in your daughter." But these are the proofs of my daughter's virginity.' Then they are to spread the cloth before the elders of the town.
The elders of that town are to take the man and punish him.

They are to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman's father, because he has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She is to remain his wife. He is not allowed to divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true, and the proofs of the young woman's virginity were not found,

then they are to bring the young woman to the door of her father's house, and the men of her town are to stone her to death. She has done a disgraceful thing in Israel, by acting as a prostitute in her father's house. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.
If a man is found lying with a woman who is married to another man, both of them are to die, the man who lay with the woman and the woman. So you are to clear the evil out of Israel.
If there is a young woman who is a virgin, engaged to a man, and another man finds her in the town and lies with her,

you are to bring both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them to death, the young woman because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he violated his neighbour's wife. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.
But if the man finds the engaged young woman in the open country, and the man seizes her and lies with her, only the man who lay with her is to die.
You are to do nothing to the young woman. She has committed no sin that deserves death. This case is like that of someone who attacks his neighbour and murders him,
for he found her in the open country, and the engaged young woman cried out, but there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a young woman who is a virgin, who is not engaged, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,

the man who lay with her is to give fifty shekels of silver to the young woman's father, and she is to become his wife, because he has violated her. He is not allowed to divorce her as long as he lives.
A man is not to take his father's wife, so that he does not uncover his father's skirt.
"No man whose testicles are crushed or whose penis is cut off may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No one born of a forbidden union may enter the assembly of the LORD. None of his descendants, even to the tenth generation, may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD. None of their descendants, even to the tenth generation, may enter the assembly of the LORD, ever,
because they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. The LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.
You are never to seek their peace or their good, as long as you live.
You are not to despise an Edomite, for he is your kinsman. You are not to despise an Egyptian, because you were a foreigner in his land.
Children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you march out as a camp against your enemies, keep away from every evil thing.
If there is a man among you who is unclean because of an emission in the night, he is to go outside the camp and not come into it.
When evening comes he is to wash with water, and when the sun has set he may come back into the camp.
You are to have a place outside the camp where you can go.
You are to have a small tool among your equipment, and when you squat outside, you are to dig with it and then turn and cover what has come from you.

For the LORD your God walks about in your camp, to save you and to hand your enemies over to you. So your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
If a slave escapes from his master to you, you are not to hand him back to his master.
He is to live with you, in your midst, in the place he chooses within one of your towns, wherever suits him. You are not to oppress him.
No Israelite woman is to become a temple prostitute, and no Israelite man is to become a temple prostitute.
You are not to bring the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God for any vow, because both of these are abhorrent to the LORD your God.
You are not to charge interest to your kinsman, interest on money, interest on food, interest on anything that is lent for interest.
You may charge interest to a foreigner, but not to your kinsman, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you put your hand to in the land you are entering to possess.
When you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not delay in paying it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and it would be sin in you.
But if you refrain from making a vow, it will not be sin in you.
You are to keep what has gone out of your lips and do what you have vowed, as a freewill offering that you promised with your own mouth to the LORD your God.
When you go into your neighbour's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, until you are full, but you are not to put any into your basket.
When you go into your neighbour's standing grain, you may pick ears with your hand, but you are not to swing a sickle against your neighbour's standing grain.

"When a man takes a wife and marries her, and she does not please him, because he has found something indecent about her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house,
and she leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's wife,
and the latter husband turns against her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her as his wife dies,

then her first husband, who sent her away, is not allowed to take her again to be his wife, since she has been made unclean. That would be abhorrent to the LORD. You are not to bring sin on the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man has newly married a wife, he is not to go out with the army or have any duty laid on him. He is to be free at home for one year, to bring happiness to the wife he has taken.
No one is to take a pair of millstones or even the upper millstone as a pledge, for that would be taking a life as a pledge.
If a man is found kidnapping any of his kinsmen, the Israelites, and treats him as a slave or sells him, that kidnapper is to die. So you are to clear the evil out from among you.
In a case of skin disease, take great care to do exactly as the Levitical priests instruct you. As I commanded them, so you are to take care to do.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the road after you came out of Egypt.
When you make your neighbour a loan of any kind, you are not to go into his house to take his pledge.
You are to stand outside, and the man to whom you are lending is to bring the pledge outside to you.
If he is a poor man, you are not to go to sleep holding his pledge.
You are to return the pledge to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. And it will count as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
You are not to oppress a poor and needy hired worker, whether he is one of your kinsmen or a foreigner who lives in your land in one of your towns.
You are to give him his wages on the same day, before the sun goes down, for he is poor and his life depends on it. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and it would be sin in you.
Parents are not to be put to death because of their children, and children are not to be put to death because of their parents. Each is to be put to death for his own sin.
You are not to twist the justice due to a foreigner or an orphan, or take a widow's garment as a pledge.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I am commanding you to do this.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you are not to go back to get it. It is to be for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, you are not to go over the branches again. What is left is to be for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you are not to glean it afterwards. What is left is to be for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I am commanding you to do this.
"When there is a dispute between people, they are to go to court, and the judges are to decide between them, declaring the innocent in the right and the guilty in the wrong.
If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge is to have him lie down and be beaten in his presence, with the number of blows his offence deserves.
He may give him forty blows, but not more. If he is beaten with more blows than these, your kinsman would be shamed in your sight.
You are not to muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

When brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the dead man's wife is not to marry outside the family to a stranger. Her husband's brother is to go to her and take her as his wife and carry out the duty of a brother-in-law to her.
The first son she bears is to carry on the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to take his brother's wife, his brother's wife is to go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, 'My husband's brother refuses to keep his brother's name alive in Israel. He is unwilling to carry out the duty of a brother-in-law to me.'
Then the elders of his town are to summon him and speak to him. If he stands firm and says, 'I do not want to take her,'

then his brother's wife is to go up to him in the sight of the elders, pull off his sandal from his foot, spit in his face and declare, 'This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house.'
His family is to be known in Israel as the House of the Unsandalled.
When two men are fighting with each other and the wife of one comes up to rescue her husband from the one who is hitting him, and puts out her hand and seizes him by his private parts,
you are to cut off her hand. Do not let your eye pity her.
You are not to have in your bag two different weights, a heavy and a light.
You are not to have in your house two different measures, a large and a small.
You are to have a full and honest weight, a full and honest measure, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who acts dishonestly, is abhorrent to the LORD your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the road when you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the road and attacked from behind all who were straggling at the rear, when you were tired and worn out, and he did not fear God.

So when the LORD your God has given you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you are to wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
"When you have entered the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it and live in it,

you are to take some of the first of all the produce of the ground that you harvest from your land that the LORD your God is giving you, and put it in a basket and go to the place the LORD your God will choose to make his name live there.
You are to go to the priest who is in office at that time and say to him, 'Today I declare to the LORD your God that I have come into the land that the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.'
The priest is to take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.

Then you are to answer and say before the LORD your God: 'My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner, few in number, and there he became a great nation, strong and many.
The Egyptians treated us badly and oppressed us and put hard labour on us.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our misery, our toil and our oppression.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now I have brought the first of the produce of the ground that you, LORD, have given me.' You are to set it down before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.
Then you are to rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given to you and to your household, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who lives among you.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tenth of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied,

you are to say before the LORD your God: 'I have cleared the holy portion out of my house, and I have also given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan and the widow, according to all your command that you gave me. I have not broken your commands or forgotten them.

I have not eaten any of it while in mourning. I have not cleared any of it away while unclean, and I have not given any of it for the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God. I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.'
Today the LORD your God is commanding you to do these statutes and rulings. You are to keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commands and his rulings, and listen to his voice.
And the LORD has declared today that you are his people, his treasured possession, as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commands,
and that he will set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise, fame and honour, and that you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised."
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: "Keep the whole command that I am giving you today.
On the day you cross over the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you are to set up large stones and coat them with plaster.

Write on them all the words of this teaching when you have crossed over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, you are to set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and coat them with plaster.
There you are to build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You are not to use an iron tool on them.
You are to build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones, and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
You are to sacrifice peace offerings and eat them there, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
You are to write on the stones all the words of this teaching, plainly and clearly."
Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel: "Be silent, Israel, and listen. Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
So listen to the voice of the LORD your God and do his commands and statutes that I am giving you today."
That same day Moses commanded the people:
"When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.
And these tribes are to stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
The Levites are to declare in a loud voice to every Israelite:
'Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast image, an abhorrent thing to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' All the people are to answer, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who dishonours his father or his mother.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbour's boundary stone.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who misleads a blind person on the road.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who twists the justice due to a foreigner, an orphan or a widow.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who lies with his father's wife, because he has uncovered his father's skirt.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who lies with any animal.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who lies with his mother-in-law.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who strikes down his neighbour in secret.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to strike down an innocent person.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this teaching by doing them.' All the people are to say, 'Amen.'"
"If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and take care to keep all his commands that I am giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come on you and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God:
You will be blessed in the city, and blessed in the field.
The fruit of your womb will be blessed, and the produce of your ground, and the young of your livestock, the calves of your herd and the lambs of your flock.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in, and blessed when you go out.
The LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against you to be struck down before you. They will come out against you by one road and flee before you by seven.
The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your storehouses and in everything you put your hand to, and he will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will set you up as a holy people for himself, as he swore to you, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.
The LORD will give you great prosperity, in the fruit of your womb, in the young of your livestock and in the produce of your ground, in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you.
The LORD will open for you his good storehouse, the heavens, to give your land its rain in season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

The LORD will make you the head and not the tail. You will be only at the top, and never at the bottom, if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today, and take care to do them,
and do not turn aside from any of the words that I am commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and serve them.
But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God and take care to do all his commands and statutes that I am giving you today, all these curses will come on you and overtake you:
You will be cursed in the city, and cursed in the field.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be cursed.
The fruit of your womb will be cursed, and the produce of your ground, the calves of your herd and the lambs of your flock.
You will be cursed when you come in, and cursed when you go out.
The LORD will send on you curse, confusion and rebuke in everything you put your hand to, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the evil of your deeds in leaving me.
The LORD will make the plague cling to you until he has finished you off from the land you are entering to possess.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, with blight and mildew. They will pursue you until you perish.
The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth under you iron.
The LORD will make the rain of your land powder and dust. It will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
The LORD will let you be struck down before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee before them by seven, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpses will be food for all the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth, and there will be no one to scare them away.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumours, with scurvy and with the itch, from which you cannot be healed.
The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness and confusion of heart.
At noon you will grope about like a blind man in the dark. You will not succeed in anything you do. You will be oppressed and robbed all the time, and no one will save you.
You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will lie with her. You will build a house, but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken away from you by force and not returned. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will save them.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all day, and there will be nothing you can do.
A people you do not know will eat the produce of your ground and all your labour, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all your days.
What you see with your eyes will drive you mad.
The LORD will strike you on the knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
The LORD will drive you and the king you set over you to a nation neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone.
You will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
You will carry much seed out to the field but gather little, because the locust will eat it.
You will plant vineyards and work them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because the worm will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with the oil, because your olives will drop off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, because they will go into captivity.
The whirring locust will take over all your trees and the produce of your ground.
The foreigner who lives among you will rise higher and higher above you, and you will sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come on you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commands and statutes that he commanded you.
They will be a sign and a wonder against you and your descendants for ever.
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart in the midst of abundance,
you will serve your enemies, whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle, a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation of fierce face, that will not respect the old or show favour to the young.

It will eat the young of your livestock and the produce of your ground, until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine or oil, no calves of your herd or lambs of your flock, until it has made you perish.

It will besiege you in all your towns, until your high and fortified walls, in which you trusted, come down throughout your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout the land that the LORD your God has given you.
In the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you, you will eat the fruit of your own womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the LORD your God has given you.
The man among you who is the most gentle and refined will look with a hard eye on his brother, on the wife he holds in his arms and on the rest of his children who are left,

so that he will not give to any of them any of the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing left, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you in all your towns.

The most gentle and refined woman among you, so refined and gentle that she would never try to set the sole of her foot on the ground, will look with a hard eye on the husband she holds in her arms, and on her son and her daughter,

and on the afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and on the children she bears, because she will eat them in secret, for lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will press you in your towns.
If you do not take care to do all the words of this teaching that are written in this book, and fear this glorious and awe-inspiring name, the LORD your God,
then the LORD will bring on you and your descendants extraordinary plagues, great and lasting plagues, and grievous and lasting sicknesses.
He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt, which you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
Every sickness and every plague that is not written in this book of the teaching, the LORD will also bring on you, until you are destroyed.
You will be left few in number, though you were as many as the stars of the sky, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

And as the LORD took delight in you to do you good and to make you many, so the LORD will take delight in you to destroy you and wipe you out. You will be torn from the land you are entering to possess.
The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods, of wood and stone, that neither you nor your ancestors have known.
Among those nations you will find no rest, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes and a languishing spirit.
Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day, and have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening you will say, 'If only it were morning!' because of the fear in your heart that you fear, and because of the sight that your eyes will see.

The LORD will take you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I said to you, 'You will never see it again.' There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no buyer."
These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: "You have seen everything the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
the great trials that your own eyes saw, those signs and great wonders.
But to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.
I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You have not eaten bread or drunk wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.
When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us for battle, and we struck them down.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
So keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may succeed in everything you do.
All of you are standing today before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, your officers, all the men of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and the foreigner in your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, and into his oath, which the LORD your God is making with you today,
so that he may set you up today as his people and be your God, as he promised you and as he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
but with those who stand here with us today before the LORD our God, and also with those who are not here with us today.
You know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the nations you crossed.
You have seen their loathsome things, their idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold, that they kept.

Make sure there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe among you today, whose heart turns away from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations. Make sure there is no root among you that produces poison and bitterness.

When such a person hears the words of this oath, he may bless himself in his heart and say, 'I will be safe, even if I go on in the stubbornness of my heart,' sweeping away the watered land with the dry.

The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Rather, the anger of the LORD and his jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will settle on him, and the LORD will wipe out his name from under the heavens.
The LORD will single him out for disaster from all the tribes of Israel, in keeping with all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the teaching.
The coming generation, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses that the LORD has laid on it,

all its soil sulphur and salt, a burned waste, not sown and not producing, with no plant growing on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger and fury.
All the nations will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land? Why this great burning anger?'
And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods they had not known and that he had not given them.
So the anger of the LORD blazed against this land, bringing on it every curse written in this book.
In anger, in fury and in great wrath the LORD uprooted them from their land and threw them into another land, as it is today.'
The hidden things belong to the LORD our God, but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children for ever, so that we may do all the words of this teaching.
"When all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart in all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you,
and you return to the LORD your God, you and your children, and listen to his voice with all your heart and with all your soul, according to everything I am commanding you today,
then the LORD your God will turn your captivity around and have compassion on you, and he will gather you again from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.
Even if your outcasts are at the farthest edge of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you and from there he will bring you back.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land that your ancestors possessed, and you will possess it. He will do you good and make you more numerous than your ancestors.
The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you may love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies, on those who hate you and pursued you.
You will return and listen to the voice of the LORD, and do all his commands that I am giving you today.

The LORD your God will make you abound in all the work of your hands, in the fruit of your womb, in the young of your livestock and in the produce of your ground, for the LORD will again delight in doing you good, as he delighted in your ancestors,

when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God and keep his commands and statutes that are written in this book of the teaching, and when you turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
This command that I am giving you today is not too hard for you, and it is not far off.
It is not in heaven, so that you need to say, 'Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and do it?'
Nor is it across the sea, so that you need to say, 'Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and do it?'
The word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to do it.
See, today I have set before you life and good, death and evil.

If you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today, by loving the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his commands, his statutes and his rulings, then you will live and become many, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you will certainly perish. You will not live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, so that you and your descendants may live,

loving the LORD your God, listening to his voice and holding fast to him. For he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may live in the land that the LORD swore to give to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob."
Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them: "I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go out and come in, and the LORD has told me, 'You will not cross this Jordan.'
The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD has said.
The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you are to do to them everything I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you. He will not fail you or abandon you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you are the one who will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them, and you are the one who will give it to them as their inheritance.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you. He will be with you. He will not fail you or abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged."
Moses wrote down this teaching and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses commanded them: "At the end of every seven years, in the year of release, at the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God in the place he will choose, you are to read this teaching aloud in the hearing of all Israel.

Gather the people, the men, the women and the little ones, and the foreigner who lives in your towns, so that they may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God, and take care to do all the words of this teaching.
Their children, who do not know it, will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

The LORD said to Moses, "The days of your death are near. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him." So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves in the tent of meeting.
The LORD appeared in the tent, in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to lie down with your ancestors. This people will get up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and break my covenant that I made with them.

On that day my anger will blaze against them, and I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be consumed. Many evils and troubles will come on them, and on that day they will say, 'Have these evils not come on us because our God is not among us?'
On that day I will surely hide my face, because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods.
Now write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the Israelites. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for me against the Israelites.

When I bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to their ancestors, and they eat and are full and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them, and despise me and break my covenant.

And when many evils and troubles have come on them, this song will testify against them as a witness, because it will not be forgotten by the mouths of their descendants. For I know the way they are inclined, even before I bring them into the land that I swore to give."
So Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.
The LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and courageous, for you are the one who will bring the Israelites into the land that I swore to give them, and I will be with you."
When Moses had finished writing the words of this teaching in a book, to the very end,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD:
"Take this book of the teaching and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and let it be there as a witness against you.
For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. If you have been rebelling against the LORD while I am still alive with you today, how much more after my death!
Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after my death you will certainly act corruptly and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. Evil will meet you in the days to come, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD and make him angry by the work of your hands."
Then Moses spoke the words of this song from beginning to end in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel:
Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Hear, earth, the words of my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, let my speech flow down like dew, like showers on fresh grass, like downpours on tender plants.
For I will call out the name of the LORD. Give greatness to our God.
The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness, with no wrong in him, righteous and upright is he.
They have acted corruptly towards him. They are not his children, the blemish is theirs, a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish people, without wisdom? Is he not your father, who made you, who formed you and set you firm?
Remember the days of long ago. Understand the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will explain it to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated the children of humankind, he set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD's portion is his people, Jacob is his allotted inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in the empty howling waste. He encircled him, he cared for him, he guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that hovers over its young, spreading its wings, taking them, carrying them on its feathers,
the LORD alone led him, and no foreign god was with him.
He made him ride on the heights of the earth and he ate the produce of the field. He let him suck honey from the crag and oil from the flinty rock,
curds of cattle and milk of the flock, with the fat of lambs, rams of the breed of Bashan and goats, with the very finest wheat, and you drank wine, the blood of the grape.
Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, you grew thick, you grew sleek. He abandoned the God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange gods, they angered him with abhorrent things.
They sacrificed to demons, not to God, to gods they had not known, new ones, who came in recently, whom your ancestors did not dread.
You neglected the Rock who fathered you. You forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw it and spurned them, provoked by his sons and daughters.
He said, "I will hide my face from them. I will see what their end will be, for they are a generation of upside-down ways, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
They have made me jealous with what is not a god. They have angered me with their empty idols. So I will make them jealous with those who are not a people. I will anger them with a foolish nation.
For a fire has been kindled by my anger, and it burns to the lowest Sheol. It will consume the earth and its produce and set fire to the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap disasters on them. I will use up my arrows on them.
Wasting hunger, burning fever and bitter plague, and the teeth of beasts I will send against them, with the venom of crawling things in the dust.
Outside, the sword will bereave them, and inside, terror, for young man and young woman, for nursing child with the grey-haired man.
I said, 'I will cut them to pieces. I will wipe out their memory from among humankind,'
had I not feared the provoking of the enemy, lest their foes misjudge, lest they say, 'Our hand is high, and the LORD has not done all this.'"
For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise, they would understand this. They would see what their end will be.
How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock, as even our enemies judge.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of poison, their clusters bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, the cruel poison of asps.
"Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my treasuries?
Vengeance and repayment are mine, for the time when their foot slips. For the day of their disaster is near, and what is to come hurries towards them."
