For the LORD will give justice to his people, and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that their strength is gone, and none is left, bond or free.
He will say, "Where are their gods, the rock in which they took shelter,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you. Let them be your shelter.
See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death and I make alive. I have wounded and I heal, and there is no one who can deliver from my hand.
I raise my hand to heaven and say, As I live for ever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword, and my hand takes hold of judgement, I will take vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will eat flesh, with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the leaders of the enemy."
Nations, shout for joy with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will take vengeance on his adversaries and cleanse his land and his people.
Moses came, with Joshua son of Nun, and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words that I am declaring to you today, so that you may command your children to take care to do all the words of this teaching.
For it is not an empty word for you. It is your life, and by this word you will live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
On that same day the LORD spoke to Moses:
"Go up this mountain of the Abarim range, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab across from Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as a possession.
You will die on the mountain that you go up, and be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
because both of you broke faith with me in the midst of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy among the Israelites.
You will see the land from a distance, but you will not go there, into the land that I am giving to the Israelites."
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the Israelites before his death.
He said:
The LORD came from Sinai and dawned on them from Seir. He shone out from Mount Paran, and came from the myriads of holy ones, with fire flashing at his right hand.
Truly he loves the peoples. All their holy ones are in your hand. They bow down at your feet, and each receives your words,
the teaching that Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
There was a king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together.
May Reuben live and not die, though his people be few.
And this he said of Judah:
Hear, LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him in to his people. With his own hands he fights for them. Be a help against his foes.
And of Levi he said:
Give Levi your Thummim, and your Urim to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you quarrelled at the waters of Meribah,
who said of his father and mother, "I have not seen them," who did not acknowledge his brothers or recognise his own children. For they kept your word and guarded your covenant.
They teach your rulings to Jacob and your teaching to Israel. They put incense before you and whole offerings on your altar.
LORD, bless his substance, and accept the work of his hands. Strike the loins of those who rise against him, and of those who hate him, so that they do not rise.
Of Benjamin he said:
May the beloved of the LORD live safely by him. He covers him all day long, and dwells between his shoulders.
And of Joseph he said:
Blessed by the LORD be his land, with the best of heaven, with the dew, and of the deep that crouches below,
with the best of the yield of the sun, and the best of the produce of the months,
with the finest of the ancient mountains, and the best of the everlasting hills,
with the best of the earth and its fullness, and the favour of him who lived in the bush. May it come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

His firstborn bull, majesty is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore the peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth. They are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
And of Zebulun he said:
Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call peoples to the mountain. There they will offer right sacrifices, for they will draw on the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.
And of Gad he said:
Blessed be the one who enlarges Gad. Gad lives like a lion and tears off an arm and even a head.
He chose the first part for himself, for there a commander's portion was kept. He came with the heads of the people, and he carried out the LORD's justice and his rulings with Israel.
And of Dan he said:
Dan is a lion's cub that leaps out from Bashan.
And of Naphtali he said:
Naphtali, full of favour, full of the blessing of the LORD, take possession of the lake and the south.
And of Asher he said:
Most blessed of sons be Asher. May he be favoured by his brothers, and dip his foot in oil.
Your bolts will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as your days.
There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to help you, through the skies in his majesty.
The God of old is a dwelling place, and underneath are the arms that last for ever. He drove out the enemy before you and said, "Destroy."
So Israel lives in safety, the spring of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drip dew.
You are happy, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help, and the sword of your majesty? Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread on their backs.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is across from Jericho. The LORD showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
the Negev, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

The LORD said to him, "This is the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over there."
So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said.
He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor, but no one knows where his grave is to this day.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eye was not dim, and his vigour had not left him.
The Israelites wept for Moses on the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were over.
Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Since then no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
for all the signs and wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
and for all the mighty power and all the great and terrifying deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
After the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, the assistant of Moses:
"Moses my servant is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the Israelites.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, as I promised Moses.
Your territory will reach from the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the Great Sea in the west.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you or abandon you.
Be strong and courageous, for you will lead this people to inherit the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.
Only be strong and very courageous, and take care to do all the teaching that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.
This book of the teaching is not to leave your mouth. You are to recite it day and night, so that you take care to do everything written in it. Then your way will prosper, and then you will succeed.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people:

"Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get food ready for yourselves, for in three days you are to cross this Jordan, to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
To the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said:
"Remember the word that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and has given you this land.'

Your wives, your little ones and your livestock may stay in the land that Moses gave you across the Jordan, but all your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your kinsmen, and you are to help them,

until the LORD gives rest to your kinsmen as he has to you, and they also take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your own possession and take possession of it, the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you across the Jordan, towards the sunrise."
They answered Joshua: "Everything you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
Just as we listened to Moses in everything, so we will listen to you. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as he was with Moses.
Anyone who rebels against your command and does not listen to your words, in whatever you command him, will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous."

Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men from Shittim as scouts, saying, "Go and look over the land, especially Jericho." They went and came to the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and stayed there.
The king of Jericho was told, "Some Israelites have come here tonight to search out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who have come to you, who came into your house, for they have come to search out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men did come to me, but I did not know where they were from.
At dusk, when it was time to shut the gate, the men went out. I do not know where they went. Chase after them quickly, and you may catch them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
So the men chased after them on the road to the Jordan, to the fords, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.
Before the men lay down, she came up to them on the roof
and said to them, "I know that the LORD has given you the land, and that terror of you has fallen on us, and that all who live in the land are melting in fear before you.

For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, to Sihon and Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no one had any courage left because of you, for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.
Now, please swear to me by the LORD that, since I have shown you faithful love, you will also show faithful love to my father's household, and give me a sure sign
that you will let my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them live, and save our lives from death."
The men said to her, "Our lives for yours! If you do not tell this business of ours, then when the LORD gives us the land we will deal with you in faithful love and truth."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, and she lived on the wall.
She said to them, "Go to the hill country, so that the pursuers do not meet you. Hide there for three days, until the pursuers return. Then go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will be released from this oath you have made us swear

unless, when we come into the land, you tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and gather into your house your father and mother, your brothers and all your father's household.

If anyone goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be free of guilt. But for anyone who is with you in the house, his blood will be on our heads if a hand is laid on him.
And if you tell this business of ours, we will be released from the oath you made us swear."
She said, "Let it be as you say." She sent them away, and they left. Then she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers had searched all along the road and had not found them.
Then the two men came back down from the hill country, crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has given all the land into our hands. All who live in the land are melting in fear before us."
Joshua got up early in the morning, and he and all the Israelites set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan. They stayed there before they crossed over.
After three days the officers went through the camp
and commanded the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the Levitical priests carrying it, you are to set out from your place and follow it.
But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and it. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not been this way before."
Joshua said to the people, "Make yourselves holy, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."
Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that, as I was with Moses, I will be with you.
You are to command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand still in the Jordan.'"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."

Joshua said, "This is how you will know that the living God is among you, and that he will certainly drive out from before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites and the Jebusites:
the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to cross over ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man for each tribe.

When the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, the waters flowing down from above, and they will stand in a heap."
So when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of the people,
and when those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying the ark touched the edge of the water (the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the harvest),

the waters flowing down from above stood still and rose up in a heap, far off at Adam, the town beside Zarethan, and the waters flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. The people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua:
"Choose twelve men from the people, one man for each tribe,

and command them: 'Take twelve stones from here, out of the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm, and carry them over with you and put them down in the place where you will spend the night.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the Israelites, one man for each tribe,
and said to them, "Go over ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you is to lift a stone on his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites,
so that this may be a sign among you. When your children ask you in time to come, 'What do these stones mean to you?'

you are to tell them that the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. So these stones will be a memorial for the Israelites for ever."

The Israelites did as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites, as the LORD had told Joshua, and carried them over with them to the place where they camped, and put them down there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. They are there to this day.

The priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that the LORD had commanded Joshua to tell the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua. The people hurried across.
When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over in front of the people.
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had told them.
About forty thousand men ready for war crossed over before the LORD, to the plains of Jericho, for battle.
On that day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they stood in awe of him all the days of his life, as they had of Moses.
The LORD said to Joshua:
"Command the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

When the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of their feet were lifted onto dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.
Those twelve stones that they had taken out of the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.
He said to the Israelites, "When your children ask their parents in time to come, 'What do these stones mean?'
you are to tell your children, 'Israel crossed over this Jordan on dry ground.'
For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up before us until we had crossed over,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is strong, and so that you may fear the LORD your God for ever."

When all the kings of the Amorites on the west side of the Jordan and all the kings of the Canaanites by the sea heard how the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted, and there was no courage left in them because of the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath-haaraloth.
This is why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, died in the wilderness on the road after they came out of Egypt.
All the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness on the road after they came out of Egypt had not been circumcised.

For the Israelites walked in the wilderness forty years, until all the nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, had died, because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD. The LORD had sworn to them that he would not let them see the land that he had sworn to their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
It was their sons, whom he raised up in their place, that Joshua circumcised. They were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the road.
When the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they were healed.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you." So the place is called Gilgal to this day.
While the Israelites were camped at Gilgal, they kept the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, on the plains of Jericho.
On the day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land, unleavened bread and roasted grain.
The manna stopped on the day after they ate the produce of the land. The Israelites no longer had manna, but ate the crops of the land of Canaan that year.

When Joshua was near Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and there was a man standing in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, "Are you for us, or for our enemies?"
He said, "Neither. I am the commander of the army of the LORD. I have come now." Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and said to him, "What does my lord say to his servant?"
The commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, "Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
The LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have handed Jericho over to you, with its king and its fighting men.
You are to march round the city, all the men of war, going round it once. Do this for six days.
Seven priests are to carry seven ram's-horn trumpets in front of the ark. On the seventh day you are to march round the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.

When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn, and you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people are to shout a great shout. Then the wall of the city will fall down flat, and the people are to go up, each man straight ahead."
So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram's-horn trumpets in front of the ark of the LORD."
He said to the people, "Go forward and march round the city, and let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the LORD."
As Joshua had told the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the LORD went forward and blew the trumpets, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD following them.
The armed men went in front of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard came after the ark, while the trumpets sounded all the time.
But Joshua had commanded the people, "You are not to shout or let your voice be heard, and no word is to come out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout.' Then you are to shout."
So he had the ark of the LORD go round the city, circling it once. Then they came back to the camp and spent the night in the camp.
Joshua got up early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark of the LORD went on, blowing the trumpets all the time. The armed men went in front of them, and the rear guard came after the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets sounded all the time.
On the second day they marched round the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they got up early, at daybreak, and marched round the city in the same way seven times. That was the only day they marched round the city seven times.
At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout, for the LORD has given you the city.
The city and everything in it is to be devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house are to live, because she hid the messengers we sent.

But you are to keep yourselves from what is devoted, so that you do not covet it and take some of what is devoted, and so make the camp of Israel a thing devoted to destruction and bring trouble on it.
All the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD. They are to go into the treasury of the LORD."

So the people shouted, and the trumpets were blown. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, they shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, and the people went up into the city, each man straight ahead, and they captured the city.
They devoted to destruction everything in the city, men and women, young and old, ox, sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
Joshua said to the two men who had scouted the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring the woman out of it, with all who belong to her, as you swore to her."

So the young men who had been the scouts went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers and all who belonged to her. They brought out all her family and put them outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city with fire, and everything in it. Only the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

But Rahab the prostitute, with her father's household and all who belonged to her, Joshua let live. She has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua swore an oath: "Cursed before the LORD is the man who gets up and builds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates."
So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread through all the land.

But the Israelites broke faith over what was devoted. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted, and the anger of the LORD blazed against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.
They returned to Joshua and said to him, "Do not send all the people up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for they are few."
So about three thousand men went up there from the people, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them and chased them from the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down on the slope. The hearts of the people melted and became like water.
Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD, why did you bring this people across the Jordan at all, only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
What can I say, Lord, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all who live in the land will hear of it, and they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up. Why are you lying on your face?
Israel has sinned. They have broken my covenant that I commanded them. They have taken some of what was devoted. They have stolen, they have lied, and they have put it among their own things.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is devoted from among you.

Get up. Make the people holy, and say, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is something devoted among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted from among you.

In the morning you are to come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe that the LORD takes by lot is to come forward clan by clan. The clan that the LORD takes is to come forward household by household. The household that the LORD takes is to come forward man by man.
The one who is taken with what is devoted is to be burned with fire, he and everything he has, because he has broken the covenant of the LORD and done a disgraceful thing in Israel.'"
Joshua got up early in the morning and brought Israel forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
He brought forward the clans of Judah, and the clan of the Zerahites was taken. He brought forward the clan of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
He brought forward his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make your confession to him. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

when I saw among the plunder a fine cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I wanted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and there it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took them out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and laid them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua and all Israel with him took Achan son of Zerah, with the silver, the cloak and the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his ox, donkey and sheep, his tent and everything he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD brings trouble on you today." And all Israel stoned him with stones. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
They raised over him a great heap of stones, which is there to this day. Then the LORD turned from his burning anger. So that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.

The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take all the fighting men with you, and get up and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land.
You are to do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may take its plunder and its livestock as spoil for yourselves. Set an ambush against the city, behind it."
So Joshua and all the fighting men set out to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.
He commanded them: "Listen, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind it. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you be ready.
I and all the people with me will approach the city. When they come out against us as they did the first time, we will run away from them.
They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are running away from us as they did the first time.' So we will run away from them.
Then you are to rise from the ambush and take the city, for the LORD your God will hand it over to you.
When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do it according to the word of the LORD. See, I have commanded you."
So Joshua sent them off, and they went to the place of the ambush and lay in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
Joshua got up early in the morning and mustered the people, and he went up, he and the elders of Israel, ahead of the people to Ai.
All the fighting men who were with him went up and came near and arrived in front of the city and camped on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
So they took up their positions, the main camp north of the city and its rear guard west of the city. But Joshua spent that night in the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people, the men of the city, hurried and got up early and went out to meet Israel in battle at the appointed place facing the Arabah. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten by them and ran away in the direction of the wilderness.
So all the people in the city were called together to chase after them, and as they chased Joshua they were drawn away from the city.
Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and chased Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the javelin that is in your hand towards Ai, for I will give it into your hand." So Joshua held out the javelin in his hand towards the city.
As soon as he stretched out his hand, the men in the ambush rose quickly from their place and ran, and entered the city and captured it. They quickly set the city on fire.

When the men of Ai looked back, they saw the smoke of the city going up to the sky. They had no strength to run this way or that, for the people who had been running to the wilderness turned back on their pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city was going up, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
The others came out of the city to meet them, so that they were in the middle of Israel, some on this side and some on that. Israel struck them down until none were left who survived or escaped.
But the king of Ai they took alive, and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the people of Ai in the open country, in the wilderness where they chased them, and all of them had fallen by the edge of the sword to the very last man, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it down with the edge of the sword.
All who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.
For Joshua did not draw back his hand, with which he had held out the javelin, until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
Only the livestock and the plunder of that city Israel took as spoil for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a heap of ruins for ever, a desolation to this day.

The king of Ai he hanged on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua commanded, and they took his body down from the tree and threw it down at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the book of the teaching of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, on which no iron had been used. They offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the teaching of Moses, which Moses had written.

All Israel, foreigner and native alike, with their elders, officers and judges, stood on both sides of the ark in front of the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded at the first, to bless the people of Israel.
After that he read aloud all the words of the teaching, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the teaching.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read aloud in front of the whole assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones and the foreigners who lived among them.

When all the kings west of the Jordan heard of this, in the hill country, in the lowland and along the whole coast of the Great Sea towards Lebanon, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites,
they gathered together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel.
But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
they too acted with cunning. They went and disguised themselves as envoys, with worn-out sacks on their donkeys and wineskins, worn out, split and mended,
with worn and patched sandals on their feet and old clothes on their bodies. All the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbly.
They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant country. Now make a treaty with us."
But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you live near us. How could we make a treaty with you?"
They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
They said to him, "Your servants have come from a very distant country, because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard a report of him, and of all that he did in Egypt,
and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
So our elders and all who live in our country said to us, 'Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them and say to them, "We are your servants. Now make a treaty with us."'
This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses as our food, on the day we set out to come to you. Now look, it is dry and crumbly.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, and look, they are split. These clothes and sandals of ours are worn out from the very long journey."
The men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask for the LORD's decision.
Joshua made peace with them and made a treaty with them, to let them live, and the leaders of the community swore an oath to them.
Three days after they had made the treaty with them, they heard that they were neighbours and lived among them.
The Israelites set out and reached their towns on the third day. Their towns were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.
But the Israelites did not strike them down, because the leaders of the community had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole community grumbled against the leaders.
But all the leaders said to the whole community, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
This is what we will do to them: we will let them live, so that no wrath comes on us because of the oath we swore to them."
The leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water-carriers for the whole community, as the leaders had said of them.
Joshua called them and said to them, "Why did you deceive us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you live among us?
Now you are cursed, and some of you will always be slaves, woodcutters and water-carriers for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "It was told to your servants for certain that the LORD your God commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and to destroy all who live in the land before you. So we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and we did this.
Now we are in your hand. Do to us what seems good and right to you."
So he did this to them: he saved them from the hand of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
But Joshua made them that day woodcutters and water-carriers for the community and for the altar of the LORD, in the place that he would choose, as they are to this day.

When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, having done to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
he and his people were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was larger than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."

So the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon, gathered together and went up with all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the fighting men with him, and all the mighty warriors.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over to you. Not one of them will stand against you."
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.

The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who struck them down with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the road that goes up to Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel, on the way down from Beth-horon, the LORD threw large stones down from the sky on them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
On the day when the LORD handed the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD, and in the sight of Israel he said:
"Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon."
And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took revenge on its enemies.
Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
Those five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found, hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and post men by it to guard them,
but do not stay there yourselves. Chase your enemies and attack their rear. Do not let them enter their towns, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
When Joshua and the Israelites had finished striking them down with a very great slaughter, until they were wiped out, and the survivors had reached their fortified towns,
all the people returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah. No one dared say a word against the Israelites.
Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me from the cave."
They did so, and brought those five kings out to him from the cave, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

When they brought those kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the soldiers who had gone with him, "Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came near and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for this is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight."
After that Joshua struck them down and put them to death, and hanged them on five trees. They hung on the trees until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave a command, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They set large stones against the mouth of the cave, and they are there to this very day.

Joshua captured Makkedah on that day and struck it and its king with the edge of the sword. He devoted to destruction everyone in it. He left no survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

The LORD also gave it and its king into the hand of Israel. He struck it with the edge of the sword, and everyone in it. He left no survivor in it. And he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish, and camped against it and fought against it.
The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, who captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and everyone in it, as they had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people down until he left him no survivor.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped against it and fought against it.
They captured it on that day and struck it with the edge of the sword. He devoted to destruction everyone in it that day, as he had done to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

They captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king and all its towns and everyone in it. He left no survivor, as he had done to Eglon. He devoted it to destruction, with everyone in it.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and fought against it.

He captured it with its king and all its towns. They struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction everyone in it. He left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, and as he had done to Libnah and its king, so he did to Debir and its king.

So Joshua struck the whole land, the hill country, the Negev, the lowland and the slopes, and all their kings. He left no survivor, but devoted to destruction everything that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them down from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings in the northern hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
to the Canaanites in the east and the west, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They came out, they and all their armies with them, a great army, as many as the sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
All these kings joined forces and came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for by this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel, struck down. You are to cripple their horses and burn their chariots with fire."
So Joshua and all his fighting men came against them suddenly at the waters of Merom and fell on them.

The LORD handed them over to Israel, who struck them down and chased them as far as Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and east as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. They struck them down until no survivor was left.
Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him. He crippled their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and struck its king down with the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the head of all those kingdoms.
They struck down everyone in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction. No one who breathed was left, and he burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the towns of those kings, and all their kings, and struck them down with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the towns that stood on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

The Israelites took all the plunder of these towns and the livestock as spoil for themselves. But they struck down every person with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them. They left no one who breathed.
As the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took all that land, the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its lowland,
from Mount Halak, which rises towards Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon, below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down and put them to death.
Joshua fought a long time against all those kings.
There was not a town that made peace with the Israelites, except the Hivites living in Gibeon. They took all the others in battle.

For it was the LORD's doing to harden their hearts, so that they would meet Israel in battle, in order that they might be devoted to destruction and given no mercy, but be wiped out, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakites from the hill country, from Hebron, Debir and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction with their towns.
No Anakites were left in the land of the Israelites. Only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did some remain.
So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had told Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by tribes. And the land had rest from war.

These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites struck down and whose land they took as a possession across the Jordan towards the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, with all the Arabah on the east:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, as far as the Jabbok, the boundary of the Ammonites, half of Gilead,
and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth on the east, and towards Beth-jeshimoth, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, on the east, and southwards to the foot of the slopes of Pisgah.
And Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
and ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah and all Bashan, as far as the boundary of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, as far as the boundary of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the LORD and the Israelites struck them down, and Moses the servant of the LORD gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites struck down west of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises towards Seir. (Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,
in the hill country, the lowland, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness and the Negev, the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites):
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one: thirty-one kings in all.
Joshua was old, advanced in years, and the LORD said to him, "You are old, advanced in years, and a very great deal of the land still remains to be taken.
This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all those of the Geshurites
(from the Shihor, east of Egypt, to the border of Ekron in the north, counted as Canaanite; the five rulers of the Philistines, in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and the Avvites),
in the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah of the Sidonians as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites,
the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon towards the sunrise, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath,

all who live in the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will drive them out before the Israelites. Only divide it by lot as an inheritance for Israel, as I have commanded you.
Now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With the other half of Manasseh the Reubenites and the Gadites had received the inheritance that Moses gave them across the Jordan, to the east, as Moses the servant of the LORD gave it to them:
from Aroer, on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites,
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah,
the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei (he alone was left of the last of the Rephaim). Moses had struck them down and driven them out.
But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.
To the tribe of Levi alone Moses gave no inheritance. The offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he promised them.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the Reubenites by their clans.
Their territory was from Aroer, on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau by Medeba,
Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau, Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth-jeshimoth,

all the towns of the plateau and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down with the chiefs of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.
Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the Israelites also killed with the sword among the rest of their slain.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan and its edge. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites by their clans, the towns and their villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites by their clans.
Their territory was Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah,
and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Debir,

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan as its border, to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth, across the Jordan to the east.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites by their clans, the towns and their villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It was for the half-tribe of the Manassites by their clans.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim, all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty towns,
and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. These were for the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the descendants of Machir by their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moses distributed on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan east of Jericho.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he promised them.

These are the inheritances that the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites gave them.
Their inheritance was by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses for the nine and a half tribes.
For Moses had given an inheritance to the two and a half tribes across the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.
The descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received no share in the land, only towns to live in, with pasture lands for their livestock and their property.
The Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea about you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back word to him as it was in my heart.
But my brothers who went up with me made the hearts of the people melt, yet I followed the LORD my God fully.
On that day Moses swore: 'The land on which your foot has walked will surely be an inheritance for you and for your children for ever, because you have followed the LORD my God fully.'

Now look, the LORD has kept me alive, as he promised, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel was walking in the wilderness. Now look, today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me. My strength now is as my strength was then, for war and for going out and coming in.

So now give me this hill country about which the LORD spoke on that day. You yourself heard on that day that the Anakites were there, with great fortified towns. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, as the LORD said."
Then Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, fully.
The name of Hebron was formerly Kiriath-arba. (Arba was the greatest man among the Anakites.) And the land had rest from war.
The lot for the tribe of Judah by their clans reached to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin in the far south.
Their southern border began at the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces south.
It goes out south of the ascent of Akrabbim, crosses to Zin, goes up south of Kadesh-barnea, passes by Hezron, goes up to Addar and turns to Karka,
crosses to Azmon and goes out at the Wadi of Egypt. The border ends at the sea. This will be your southern border.
The eastern border is the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The border on the north side begins at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
The border goes up to Beth-hoglah and passes north of Beth-arabah. The border goes up to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

The border goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turns north towards Gilgal, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, south of the stream. The border passes the waters of En-shemesh and ends at En-rogel.

Then the border goes up the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to the southern slope of the Jebusites (that is, Jerusalem). The border goes up to the top of the mountain that lies west of the Valley of Hinnom, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the top of the mountain the border bends to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to the towns of Mount Ephron. Then the border bends to Baalah (that is, Kiriath-jearim).
From Baalah the border turns west to Mount Seir, passes along the northern slope of Mount Jearim (that is, Chesalon), goes down to Beth-shemesh and passes by Timnah.
The border goes out to the slope north of Ekron, then bends to Shikkeron, passes on to Mount Baalah and goes out at Jabneel. The border ends at the sea.
The western border is the Great Sea and its coast. This is the border all round the Judahites by their clans.
As the LORD had commanded Joshua, he gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a share among the Judahites, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron (Arba was the father of Anak).
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
From there he went up against the people of Debir. The name of Debir was formerly Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Judahites by their clans.
The towns of the tribe of the Judahites in the far south, towards the border of Edom, were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor-hadattah, Kerioth-hezron (that is, Hazor),
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet,
Hazar-shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon: twenty-nine towns in all, with their villages.
In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen towns with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad,
Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmam, Chitlish,
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen towns with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Achzib and Mareshah: nine towns with their villages.
Ekron, with its towns and villages;
from Ekron to the sea, all that were beside Ashdod, with their villages.
Ashdod, with its towns and villages; Gaza, with its towns and villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the Great Sea with its coast.
In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Dannah, Kiriath-sannah (that is, Debir),
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh: eleven towns with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Janim, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) and Zior: nine towns with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah: ten towns with their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six towns with their villages.
Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim) and Rabbah: two towns with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi: six towns with their villages.
But the Judahites could not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites live with the Judahites in Jerusalem to this day.
The lot for the descendants of Joseph went out from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, up through the wilderness, from Jericho up into the hill country of Bethel.
Then it goes from Bethel to Luz, crosses to the border of the Archites at Ataroth,
goes down west to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer, and ends at the sea.
The descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
The border of the Ephraimites by their clans was as follows: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon,
and the border goes out to the sea. On the north it is Michmethath. Then the border turns east to Taanath-shiloh and passes it on the east to Janoah,
then goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, touches Jericho and ends at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border goes west to the Wadi Kanah and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites by their clans,
together with the towns set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all those towns with their villages.
But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. So the Canaanites live among Ephraim to this day, but they have been put to forced labour.

Then the lot was cast for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. To Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead, were given Gilead and Bashan, because he was a man of war.

Lots were also cast for the rest of the Manassites by their clans: the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph by their clans.
Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

They came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the leaders and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our kinsmen." So, at the command of the LORD, he gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers.
So ten shares fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the Manassites.
The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which is east of Shechem. Then the border goes south to the people of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.

Then the border went down to the Wadi Kanah. These towns south of the wadi, among the towns of Manasseh, belong to Ephraim. The border of Manasseh goes along the north side of the wadi and ends at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. They touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

In Issachar and in Asher, Manasseh also had Beth-shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, the people of Dor and its villages, the people of Endor and its villages, the people of Taanach and its villages, and the people of Megiddo and its villages: the third is Naphath.
But the Manassites could not take possession of those towns, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When the Israelites grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labour, but they did not drive them out completely.
The descendants of Joseph spoke to Joshua: "Why have you given me only one lot and one share as an inheritance, when I am a numerous people, because the LORD has blessed me so far?"

Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear land for yourselves there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

The descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us. And all the Canaanites who live in the valley land have iron chariots, both those in Beth-shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
Then Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and have great strength. You will not have only one lot,

but the hill country will be yours. Although it is forest, you will clear it, and its farthest edges will be yours. For you will drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they are strong."
The whole community of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land lay subdued before them.
But seven tribes of the Israelites were left whose inheritance had not yet been divided.
So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you put off going in to take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?

Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They are to set out and go through the land and write a description of it, according to their inheritances. Then they are to come back to me.
They are to divide it into seven parts. Judah is to stay in his territory on the south, and the house of Joseph in theirs on the north.
You are to write a description of the land in seven parts and bring it here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

The Levites have no share among you, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."

As the men were setting out to write the description of the land, Joshua commanded them, "Go and walk through the land and write a description of it, and come back to me. Here at Shiloh I will cast lots for you before the LORD."
So the men went and passed through the land and wrote a description of it in a book, town by town, in seven parts. Then they came back to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land among the Israelites, to each their share.
The lot of the tribe of the Benjaminites by their clans came up, and the territory of their lot lay between the Judahites and the descendants of Joseph.
On the north side their border began at the Jordan. The border goes up to the slope north of Jericho, then up through the hill country westward, and ends at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the border crosses to Luz, to the southern slope of Luz (that is, Bethel). Then the border goes down to Ataroth-addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.

Then the border turns and bends round on the western side southward, from the hill that lies south of Beth-horon, and ends at Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim), a town of the Judahites. This is the western side.
The southern side begins at the edge of Kiriath-jearim, and the border goes out westward, and goes to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

Then the border goes down to the edge of the mountain that faces the Valley of Ben-hinnom, which is at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim. It goes down the Valley of Hinnom, south of the slope of the Jebusites, and down to En-rogel.
Then it bends northward and goes to En-shemesh, and from there to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim. Then it goes down to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben,
and passes along the north side of the slope of Beth-arabah and goes down to the Arabah.
Then the border passes along the north side of the slope of Beth-hoglah and ends at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This is the southern border.
The Jordan forms its border on the east side. This was the inheritance of the Benjaminites, by its borders all round, by their clans.
The towns of the tribe of the Benjaminites by their clans were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
Chephar-ammoni, Ophni and Geba: twelve towns with their villages;
Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
Zela, Haeleph, Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah and Kiriath: fourteen towns with their villages. This is the inheritance of the Benjaminites by their clans.
The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans, and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the Judahites.
Their inheritance included Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,
Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen towns with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four towns with their villages,
together with all the villages round these towns as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans.
The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the share of the Judahites. Because the share of the Judahites was too large for them, the Simeonites received their inheritance within theirs.
The third lot came up for the Zebulunites by their clans. The border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
Then their border goes up westward to Maralah, and touches Dabbesheth, then the wadi that is east of Jokneam.
From Sarid it turns the other way, east, towards the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-tabor, then goes to Daberath, then up to Japhia.
From there it passes eastward to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin, and goes on to Rimmon, where it bends to Neah.
Then the border turns round it on the north to Hannathon, and ends at the Valley of Iphtah-el,
with Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve towns with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the Zebulunites by their clans, these towns with their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the Issacharites by their clans.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah and Beth-pazzez.
The border touches Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-shemesh, and ends at the Jordan: sixteen towns with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Issacharites by their clans, the towns with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the Asherites by their clans.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad and Mishal. On the west it touches Carmel and Shihor-libnath,
then turns east towards Beth-dagon, touches Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el on the north, then Beth-emek and Neiel, and goes on north to Cabul,
Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
Then the border turns to Ramah, to the fortified town of Tyre. The border turns to Hosah and ends at the sea, with Mehebel, Achzib,
Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two towns with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Asherites by their clans, these towns with their villages.
The sixth lot came out for the Naphtalites, for the Naphtalites by their clans.
Their border ran from Heleph, from the oak at Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
Then the border turns west to Aznoth-tabor and goes from there to Hukkok, touching Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west and the Jordan on the east.
The fortified towns are Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor,
Yiron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh: nineteen towns with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Naphtalites by their clans, the towns with their villages.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the Danites by their clans.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon,
Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory opposite Joppa.

When the territory of the Danites was lost to them, the Danites went up and fought against Leshem, and after capturing it and striking it down with the sword, they took possession of it and settled there. They called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Danites by their clans, these towns with their villages.
When they had finished dividing the land into its territories as inheritances, the Israelites gave an inheritance among them to Joshua son of Nun.
At the command of the LORD they gave him the town that he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the town and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites distributed by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
Then the LORD said to Joshua:
"Tell the Israelites: Set apart the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you through Moses,
so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally, without meaning to, may flee there. They will be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

The one who flees to one of these cities is to stand at the entrance of the city gate and state his case in the hearing of the elders of that city. They are to take him into the city and give him a place, and he will live among them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they are not to hand over the one who killed, because he killed his neighbour without meaning to, and had not hated him in the past.

He is to stay in that city until he has stood trial before the assembly, and until the death of the high priest who is in office at that time. Then the one who killed may go back to his own town and his own home, to the town he fled from."
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.

Across the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the towns designated for all the Israelites and for the foreigner living among them, so that anyone who killed a person unintentionally could flee there and not die at the hand of the avenger of blood until he stood before the assembly.
Then the heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites
at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said to them, "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given towns to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock."
So, as the LORD had commanded, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns with their pasture lands out of their own inheritance.
The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. The Levites who were descendants of Aaron the priest received thirteen towns by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.
The rest of the descendants of Kohath received ten towns by lot from the clans of the tribes of Ephraim, Dan and half of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received thirteen towns by lot from the clans of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, by their clans, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave these towns with their pasture lands to the Levites by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
