The LORD is my crag and my fortress, my rescuer,
my God, my rock where I take shelter, my shield and the horn of my safety, my high refuge and my place of escape. My saviour, you save me from violence.
I call on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
For the waves of death closed round me, the torrents of ruin terrified me.
The cords of Sheol wound round me, the snares of death met me.
In my distress I called on the LORD, I called to my God. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry came to his ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, the foundations of the heavens trembled. They shook because he was angry.
Smoke rose from his nostrils, fire from his mouth devoured, glowing coals blazed out from him.
He bent the heavens and came down, with thick darkness under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew. He appeared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness a canopy round himself, a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the sky.
From the brightness before him coals of fire blazed.
The LORD thundered from heaven. The Most High gave his voice.
He shot arrows and scattered them, lightning, and threw them into confusion.
Then the channels of the sea were seen, the foundations of the world were laid bare, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He reached down from on high and took hold of me. He drew me out of mighty waters.
He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.
They met me on the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
He brought me out into a wide place. He rescued me, because he delighted in me.
The LORD rewarded me for my righteousness. He repaid me for the cleanness of my hands.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not turned wickedly from my God.
All his rules were before me, and I did not turn away from his statutes.
I was blameless before him, and I kept myself from guilt.
So the LORD repaid me for my righteousness, for my cleanness in his sight.
With the faithful you show yourself faithful. With the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless.
With the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself twisted.
You save a humble people, but your eyes are on the proud, to bring them down.
You, LORD, are my lamp. The LORD lights up my darkness.
With you I can run at a troop. With my God I can leap a wall.
As for God, his way is perfect. The word of the LORD is tested. He is a shield for all who take refuge in him.
For who is God besides the LORD? Who is a rock except our God?
God is my strong refuge, and he makes my way safe.
He makes my feet like a deer's and sets me on my high places.
He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your help makes me great.
You made room for my steps under me, and my ankles did not slip.
I chased my enemies and destroyed them. I did not turn back until they were finished.
I finished them. I struck them down so that they could not rise. They fell under my feet.
You armed me with strength for battle. You made those who rose against me sink beneath me.
You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and I destroyed those who hated me.
They looked, but there was no one to save them. They looked to the LORD, but he did not answer them.
I ground them fine like the dust of the earth. I crushed them and stamped them down like mud in the streets.
You rescued me from the quarrels of my people. You kept me as head of nations. People I did not know serve me.
Foreigners cringe before me. As soon as they hear of me, they obey me.
Foreigners lose heart. They come trembling out of their strongholds.
The LORD lives. Blessed be my rock. Exalted be my God, the rock of my salvation,
the God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples under me,
who brings me out from my enemies. You lift me above those who rise against me. You rescue me from violent men.
So I will thank you, LORD, among the nations, and sing praises to your name.
He gives great victories to his king, and shows faithful love to his anointed, to David and his descendants for ever.
These are the last words of David:
The saying of David son of Jesse, the saying of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet singer of Israel.
The spirit of the LORD spoke through me, and his word was on my tongue.
The God of Israel spoke. The Rock of Israel said to me: "One who rules over people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, like the grass that springs from the earth after the rain.
Is my house not like this with God? He has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in every part and secure. Will he not make all my help and my desire grow?
But the worthless are all like thorns thrown away, for no one can take them in the hand.
Whoever touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they are burned with fire where they lie."
These are the names of David's warriors. Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the three, wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
After him among the three warriors was Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi. He was with David when they defied the Philistines gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.

He stood his ground and struck down the Philistines until his hand was tired and stuck to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the army came back after him only to strip the dead.
After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at Lehi, where there was a field full of lentils, and the army fled from the Philistines.
But he took his stand in the middle of the field and defended it and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down and came to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.
David said longingly, "If only someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate."

Then the three warriors broke through the Philistine camp and drew water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But he would not drink it. He poured it out to the LORD,
and said, "The LORD forbid that I should do this. Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he would not drink it. These are the things the three warriors did.
Abishai, the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was chief of the thirty. He wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and won a name beside the three.
He was the most honoured of the thirty and became their commander, but he did not reach the three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel, who did great deeds. He struck down two lion-like warriors of Moab. He also went down and killed a lion in a pit on a day when snow had fallen.

He also killed an Egyptian, a fine-looking man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
These are the things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he won a name beside the three warriors.
He was honoured among the thirty, but he did not reach the three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty, with Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammah of Harod, Elika of Harod,
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh of Tekoa,
Abiezer of Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai of Netophah,
Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites,
Benaiah of Pirathon, Hiddai of the wadis of Gaash,
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth of Bahurim,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai of Maacah, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezro of Carmel, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai of Beeroth, the armour-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
and Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.
Again the anger of the LORD blazed against Israel, and he stirred up David against them, saying, "Go and count Israel and Judah."

So the king said to Joab and the commanders of the army who were with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people, so that I may know the number of the people."

But Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as there are, while the eyes of my lord the king can see it. But why does my lord the king want to do this?"
But the king's word overruled Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army left the king's presence to register the people of Israel.
They crossed the Jordan and began from Aroer and from the town in the middle of the valley, towards Gad and on to Jazer.
Then they came to Gilead and to Kadesh in the land of the Hittites, and to Dan, and from Dan they went round to Sidon,
and came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Then they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.
So when they had gone through the whole land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
Joab gave the total of the registration of the people to the king. In Israel there were eight hundred thousand brave men who drew the sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand.

But David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, LORD, please take away the guilt of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
When David got up in the morning, the word of the LORD had come to the prophet Gad, David's seer:
"Go and say to David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am offering you three things. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall three years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you run for three months from your enemies while they chase you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now think, and decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for his mercy is great. But do not let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.

When the angel stretched out his hand towards Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD changed his mind about the disaster and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "That is enough. Now stop." The angel of the LORD was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

When David saw the angel who was striking the people, he spoke to the LORD and said, "I am the one who has sinned. I am the one who has done wrong. But these sheep, what have they done? Let your hand be against me and against my father's house."
Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
So David went up, as Gad had told him, as the LORD commanded.
When Araunah looked down, he saw the king and his servants coming towards him. Araunah went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.

Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, so that I can build an altar to the LORD, and the plague may be stopped among the people."
Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer whatever seems good to him. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the oxen's yokes for the wood.
All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you."

But the king said to Araunah, "No, I will buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
David built an altar there to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD answered the plea for the land, and the plague was stopped in Israel.
King David was old, well on in years, and though they covered him with clothes, he could not get warm.
So his servants said to him, "Let a young woman, a virgin, be found for my lord the king, to wait on the king and look after him. Let her lie in your arms, so that my lord the king may be warm."
So they searched all through the land of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very beautiful. She looked after the king and served him, but the king did not have sex with her.
Now Adonijah son of Haggith put himself forward and said, "I will be king." He got himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run in front of him.
His father had never once crossed him by asking, "Why do you do this?" He was also very handsome, and he had been born next after Absalom.
He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah and helped him.
But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and David's warriors did not side with Adonijah.
Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle and fattened calves at the Serpent's Stone, beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were the king's servants.
But he did not invite Nathan the prophet or Benaiah or the warriors or his brother Solomon.
Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
Now come, let me give you advice, so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

Go at once to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, "Your son Solomon will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
While you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."
So Bathsheba went in to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was looking after him.
Bathsheba bowed and did homage to the king, and the king said, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "My lord, you swore to your servant by the LORD your God, 'Your son Solomon will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne.'
But now, look, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.

He has sacrificed oxen, fattened calves and sheep in great numbers, and has invited all the king's sons, and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he has not invited your servant Solomon.
As for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be treated as criminals."
While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came before the king and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne'?

For today he has gone down and sacrificed oxen, fattened calves and sheep in great numbers, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest. Look, they are eating and drinking in front of him, and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah.'
But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
Has this been done by my lord the king, without letting your servants know who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
King David answered, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came into the king's presence and stood before the king.
The king swore, "As the LORD lives, who has rescued me from every trouble,
as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, 'Your son Solomon will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,' so I will do this day."
Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and did homage to the king and said, "May my lord King David live for ever."
King David said, "Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came before the king.
The king said to them, "Take my servants with you, and have my son Solomon ride on my own mule, and take him down to Gihon.
There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Blow the trumpet and say, 'Long live King Solomon.'
Then come up after him, and let him come in and sit on my throne, for he will be king in my place. I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen. May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.
As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and had Solomon ride on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the trumpet, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon."
All the people went up after him, playing pipes and rejoicing so loudly that the ground split open with the noise.
Adonijah and all the guests with him heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "Why is the town in such an uproar?"
While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and you bring good news."
Jonathan answered Adonijah, "No. Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they have had him ride on the king's mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing, and the town is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.
Solomon is now sitting on the royal throne.

The king's servants also came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make the name of Solomon more famous than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowed in worship on his bed.
The king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has today given one to sit on my throne, and my own eyes see it.'"
Then all the guests of Adonijah were terrified, and they got up and each went his own way.
Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, and he got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon, and he has taken hold of the horns of the altar and says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
Solomon said, "If he proves to be a worthy man, not one hair of his will fall to the ground. But if wickedness is found in him, he will die."
So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
When David's time to die drew near, he gave a charge to his son Solomon:
"I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong and be a man.

Keep what the LORD your God requires: walk in his ways and keep his statutes, his commands, his rules and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may succeed in all you do and wherever you turn,

and so that the LORD may carry out the promise he made to me: 'If your sons take care how they live, walking before me in faithfulness with all their heart and all their soul, you will never lack a man on the throne of Israel.'

You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, and shed the blood of war in a time of peace, and put the blood of war on the belt round his waist and on the sandals on his feet.
So act with your wisdom, and do not let his grey head go down to Sheol in peace.
But show faithful love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they stood by me in the same way when I ran away from your brother Absalom.

And there is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, with you. He cursed me with a bitter curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
Now do not let him go unpunished, for you are a wise man. You will know what to do to him, and you will bring his grey head down to Sheol with blood."
Then David lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David.
The time that David ruled over Israel was forty years. He ruled seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.
Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She said, "Do you come in peace?" He said, "In peace."
Then he said, "I have something to say to you." She said, "Say it."
He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel looked to me to be king. But the kingdom has turned round and become my brother's, for it was his from the LORD.
Now I have one request to make of you. Do not refuse me." She said to him, "Say it."
He said, "Please ask King Solomon, for he will not refuse you, to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."
Bathsheba said, "Very well. I will speak to the king for you."

So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat on his throne, and a throne was set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
She said, "I have one small request to make of you. Do not refuse me." The king said to her, "Make your request, my mother, for I will not refuse you."
She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."

King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for the kingdom for him as well, for he is my older brother, and he has Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah on his side."
Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, "May God do this to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at the cost of his life.
Now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of my father David, and who has made a house for me, as he promised, Adonijah will be put to death today."
So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.

To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to your fields at Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and because you shared in all the hardships my father went through."
So Solomon removed Abiathar from being priest of the LORD, and so fulfilled the word of the LORD that he spoke about the house of Eli at Shiloh.
When the news came to Joab (for Joab had supported Adonijah, though he had not supported Absalom), Joab ran to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
King Solomon was told, "Joab has run to the tent of the LORD, and he is there beside the altar." Then Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go and strike him down."

So Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "The king says, 'Come out.'" He said, "No, I will die here." Then Benaiah took word back to the king: "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."
The king said, "Do as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so take away from me and from my father's house the guilt for the blood that Joab shed without cause.

The LORD will bring his blood back on his own head, for he attacked two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword, without my father David knowing: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
Their blood will come back on the head of Joab and on the head of his descendants for ever. But for David and his descendants and his house and his throne there will be peace from the LORD for ever."
So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and killed him. And he was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in his place, and the king put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.
Then the king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there to any place at all.
For on the day you go out and cross the Wadi Kidron, know for certain that you will die. Your blood will be on your own head."
Shimei said to the king, "What you say is good. Your servant will do as my lord the king has said." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for many days.
But at the end of three years two of Shimei's servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your servants are in Gath."
Shimei got up and saddled his donkey and went to Achish at Gath to look for his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and come back.

So the king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and solemnly warn you, 'Know for certain that on the day you go out and go to any place at all, you will die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is good. I will obey.'
Why then have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?"
The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the wrong you did to my father David. The LORD will bring your wrong back on your own head.
But King Solomon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be established before the LORD for ever."
Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him down, and he died. So the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the city of David, until he had finished building his own house and the house of the LORD and the wall round Jerusalem.
The people were sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD.
Solomon loved the LORD and followed the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night, and God said, "Ask what I should give you."

Solomon said, "You showed great and faithful love to your servant, my father David, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness and in uprightness of heart. You have kept this great and faithful love for him and have given him a son to sit on his throne today.
Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, though I am only a young boy and do not know how to go out or come in.
Your servant is in the middle of your people, whom you chose, a great people, too many to be counted or numbered.
So give your servant a listening heart to judge your people and to tell good from evil, for who can judge this great people of yours?"
It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked for this.

God said to him, "Because you have asked for this, and have not asked for long life for yourself, or riches, or the lives of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to hear what is right,
I now do what you have said. I give you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and no one like you will rise after you.
I also give you what you have not asked for, both riches and honour, so that no other king will be like you, all your days.
And if you walk in my ways and keep my statutes and my commands, as your father David did, I will give you a long life."
Solomon woke up, and it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and gave a feast for all his servants.
Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
One woman said, "Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.
On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together. There was no one else with us in the house, only the two of us.
This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.
She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was asleep, and laid him in her arms, and laid her dead son in my arms.
When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, I saw that he was not the son I had borne."
But the other woman said, "No. The living one is my son, and the dead one is yours." The first said, "No. The dead one is your son, and the living one is mine." So they argued before the king.
The king said, "This one says, 'This is my son who is alive, and your son is dead,' and that one says, 'No, your son is dead, and my son is the one who is alive.'"
The king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword to the king.
The king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other."

Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king, because her heart burned for her son. She said, "Please, my lord, give her the living child, and do not kill him." But the other said, "He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two."
Then the king answered, "Give the living child to the first woman, and do not kill him. She is his mother."
All Israel heard of the judgement that the king had given, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do justice.
King Solomon was king over all Israel,
and these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah son of Nathan was over the officers; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's friend;
Ahishar was over the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda was over the forced labour.
Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided food for the king and his household. Each one had to provide for one month in the year.
These were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed, in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);
Ben-abinadab, in all Naphath-dor (he had Taphath, Solomon's daughter, as his wife);
Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead (the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to him, and the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty great towns with walls and bronze bars);
Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he too took a daughter of Solomon as his wife);
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. And there was one officer over the land of Judah.
Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea. They ate and drank and were happy.
Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
Solomon's food for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,
ten fattened oxen, twenty oxen from the pastures and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks and fattened birds.
For he ruled over everything west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the Euphrates. And he had peace on all sides round him.
Judah and Israel lived in safety, from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree, all the days of Solomon.
Solomon also had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
Those officers provided food for King Solomon and for all who came to the king's table, each in his month. They let nothing be lacking.
They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift steeds to the place where it was needed, each according to his duty.
God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding beyond measure, and breadth of mind as wide as the sand on the seashore,
so that Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
He was wiser than anyone, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol, and his fame spread through all the surrounding nations.
He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also of animals, birds, reptiles and fish.
People of all nations came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father, and Hiram had always been a friend of David.
Solomon sent this message to Hiram:
"You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God, because of the wars that surrounded him, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of his feet.
But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is no enemy and no disaster.
So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the house for my name.'

Now give the order that cedars from Lebanon be cut for me. My servants will work with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wage you set, for you know that none of us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
When Hiram heard Solomon's words, he was very glad and said, "Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this great people."
Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have heard the message you sent me. I will do all you want about the cedar and cypress timber.

My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will have it made into rafts to go by sea to the place you name. There I will have them broken up, and you can take it away. And you will meet my need by providing food for my household."
So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pressed oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year after year.
The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as he had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
King Solomon raised a labour force from all Israel, and the force numbered thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in turns. They spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the labour force.
Solomon also had seventy thousand carriers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
besides three thousand three hundred chief officers of Solomon who were over the work and in charge of the people doing it.
At the king's command they quarried large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stone.
So Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the men of Gebal cut the stone and prepared the timber and the stone for building the house.

In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and thirty cubits high.
The porch in front of the main hall of the house was twenty cubits long, the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.
He made windows for the house, with narrowing frames.
Against the wall of the house he built a structure all round the walls of the house, round both the main hall and the inner room. And he made side rooms all round.

The lowest storey was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits wide and the third seven cubits wide. For he made ledges in the outer wall of the house all round, so that the beams would not be fixed into the walls of the house.
When the house was being built, it was built with stone prepared at the quarry, so that no hammer or axe or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
The entrance to the lowest side rooms was on the south side of the house, and a stairway went up to the middle storey, and from the middle to the third.
So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.
He built the side structure against the whole house, each storey five cubits high, and it was joined to the house with cedar timbers.
The word of the LORD came to Solomon:

"As for this house that you are building, if you walk in my statutes and carry out my rules and keep all my commands by walking in them, then I will keep with you my word that I spoke to your father David.
I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel."
So Solomon built the house and finished it.

He lined the walls of the house on the inside with cedar boards. From the floor of the house to the ceiling beams he covered them on the inside with wood, and he covered the floor of the house with cypress boards.
He built twenty cubits at the back of the house with cedar boards from floor to ceiling beams, and he built it inside as an inner room, the most holy place.
The house, that is, the main hall in front of the inner room, was forty cubits long.
The cedar inside the house was carved with gourds and open flowers. All was cedar. No stone could be seen.
He prepared the inner room inside the house, at the back, to put there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
The inner room was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it with pure gold. He also overlaid an altar of cedar.
Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold, and he stretched chains of gold across the front of the inner room, and overlaid it with gold.
He overlaid the whole house with gold, until the whole house was finished. He also overlaid with gold the whole altar that belonged to the inner room.
In the inner room he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long, ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
The second cherub also measured ten cubits. Both cherubim had the same size and shape.
The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the other.

He put the cherubim in the innermost part of the house. Their wings were spread out so that a wing of one touched one wall and a wing of the other touched the other wall, and their other wings touched each other in the middle of the house.
He overlaid the cherubim with gold.
On all the walls of the house all round he carved figures of cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, in the inner and outer rooms.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, in the inner and outer rooms.
For the entrance to the inner room he made doors of olive wood. The lintel and doorposts were five-sided.
He carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers on the two doors of olive wood, and overlaid them with gold, spreading gold over the cherubim and the palm trees.
In the same way he made for the entrance to the main hall doorposts of olive wood, four-sided,
and two doors of cypress. The two leaves of one door turned on hinges, and the two leaves of the other door turned on hinges.
He carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers on them, and overlaid them with gold, fitted evenly to the carving.
He built the inner court with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams.
In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv.
In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts and according to all its plans. He took seven years to build it.
Solomon was building his own house for thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide and thirty cubits high, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
It was roofed with cedar above the rooms that were on the forty-five pillars, fifteen to a row.
There were window frames in three rows, with window facing window in three tiers.
All the doorways and doorposts were square-framed, and window faced window in three tiers.
He made the Hall of Pillars, fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. In front of it was a porch with pillars, and a canopy in front of them.
He made the Hall of the Throne where he would give judgement, the Hall of Judgement. It was panelled with cedar from floor to rafters.
His own house, where he was to live, in the other court behind the hall, was of the same work. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.
All these buildings were of costly stone, cut to size and trimmed with saws on the inner and outer sides, from the foundation to the top course, and from the outside to the great court.
The foundation was of costly stones, huge stones, some ten cubits and some eight cubits.
Above were costly stones, cut to size, and cedar.
The great court had three courses of dressed stone all round and one course of cedar beams, like the inner court of the house of the LORD and the porch of the house.
King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was full of wisdom, understanding and skill for every kind of work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.
He cast two pillars of bronze. One pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits measured the other round.
He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. One capital was five cubits high, and the other capital was five cubits high.
There were nets of lattice work with wreaths of chain work for the capitals on top of the pillars, one net for one capital and one net for the other.
He made the pomegranates in two rows round one network to cover the capitals on top of the pillars, and he did the same for the other capital.
The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
The capitals were on the two pillars, and also above the rounded part beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows all round the other capital.
He set up the pillars at the porch of the main hall. He set up the pillar on the south side and named it Jachin, and he set up the pillar on the north side and named it Boaz.
On top of the pillars was lily work. So the work of the pillars was finished.
Then he made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured it round.
Under its rim were gourds, for ten cubits, going all round the sea. The gourds were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was set on top of them, and all their hindquarters were towards the middle.
It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.
He also made the ten stands of bronze. Each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide and three cubits high.
This is how the stands were made: they had panels, and the panels were set within frames,
and on the panels within the frames were lions, oxen and cherubim. On the frames there was a base above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and at its four corners were supports for a basin. The supports were cast with wreaths at the side of each.
Its opening was inside a crown that stood up a cubit. Its opening was round, shaped like a stand, a cubit and a half deep. There were carvings at its opening, and its panels were square, not round.
The four wheels were under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were fixed to the stand. The height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
The wheels were made like chariot wheels. Their axles, rims, spokes and hubs were all cast.
There were four supports at the four corners of each stand. The supports were part of the stand.
At the top of the stand there was a round band half a cubit high, and on top of the stand its stays and its panels were part of it.
On the surfaces of its stays and on its panels he carved cherubim, lions and palm trees, wherever there was space, with wreaths all round.
This is how he made the ten stands. All of them were cast alike, with the same size and shape.
He made ten basins of bronze. Each basin held forty baths and measured four cubits across, and each of the ten stands had a basin.
He put five of the stands on the south side of the house and five on the north side. And he put the sea on the south side of the house, towards the south-east.
Hiram also made the pots, the shovels and the bowls. So Hiram finished all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:
the two pillars, the two bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars,
the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars,
the ten stands with the ten basins on the stands,
the one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea.
The pots, the shovels and the bowls, all these vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon in the house of the LORD, were of polished bronze.
The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be found out.
So Solomon made all the furnishings that were in the house of the LORD: the golden altar and the golden table for the bread of the Presence,
the lampstands of pure gold, five on the south side and five on the north, in front of the inner room, with the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold,

the cups, snuffers, bowls, dishes for incense and fire pans, of pure gold, and the hinges for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the main hall of the house, of gold.

So all the work that King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was finished. Then Solomon brought in the things that his father David had dedicated, the silver, the gold and the furnishings, and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

Then Solomon summoned the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the festival in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
When all the elders of Israel had come, the priests lifted the ark.
They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy furnishings that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
King Solomon and the whole community of Israel, who had gathered round him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner room of the house, in the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, so that they covered the ark and its poles.
The poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place in front of the inner room, but they could not be seen from outside. They are there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt.
When the priests came out of the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD,
so that the priests could not stand to do their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would live in thick darkness.
I have built you a house to be your home, a place for you to live in for ever."
Then the king turned round and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to my father David and has fulfilled it with his hand. He said,

'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no town out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, but I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, 'You had it in your heart to build a house for my name, and you did well that it was in your heart.
But you will not build the house. Your son who will be born to you will build the house for my name.'

Now the LORD has kept the word that he spoke. I have taken the place of my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have made a place there for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with our ancestors when he brought them out of the land of Egypt."
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands towards heaven,
and said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below, keeping covenant and showing faithful love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept for your servant, my father David, what you promised him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled it today.

Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, what you promised him: 'You will never lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons take care how they live, walking before me as you have walked before me.'
Now, God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, the word that you spoke to your servant, my father David.
But will God really live on the earth? Look, heaven, and the highest heaven, cannot contain you. How much less this house that I have built.
Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, LORD my God, and listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying before you today,
that your eyes may be open night and day towards this house, the place of which you said, 'My name will be there,' and that you may listen to the prayer that your servant prays towards this place.
Listen to the plea of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray towards this place. Listen in heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.
If someone wrongs his neighbour and is made to swear an oath, and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this house,
then hear in heaven and act and judge your servants, bringing down the guilty by putting his conduct on his own head, and clearing the innocent by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
When your people Israel are beaten by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave to their ancestors.
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray towards this place and acknowledge your name and turn from their sin when you afflict them,

then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, and teach them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.
If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, blight, mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, if their enemy besieges them in the land at their gates, whatever disaster or sickness there is,
whatever prayer or plea is made by anyone or by all your people Israel, each knowing the pain in his own heart and stretching out his hands towards this house,
then hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive, and act, and repay each one according to all his ways, since you know his heart (for you alone know the hearts of all human beings),
so that they may fear you all the days that they live in the land that you gave to our ancestors.
Also when a foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, comes from a distant land for the sake of your name
(for they will hear of your great name and your strong hand and your outstretched arm), and comes and prays towards this house,

hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and do all that the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and may know that this house that I have built is called by your name.
When your people go out to battle against their enemy, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD towards the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then hear in heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
When they sin against you (for there is no one who does not sin) and you are angry with them and hand them over to an enemy, so that they are taken captive to the land of the enemy, far or near,

and they come to their senses in the land where they have been taken captive, and turn back and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

and turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and pray to you towards their land, which you gave to their ancestors, the city that you have chosen, and the house that I have built for your name,
then hear in heaven, your dwelling place, their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause,
and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their offences against you, and make their captors show them mercy,
for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace.
May your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, and may you listen to them whenever they call to you.
For you set them apart from all the peoples of the earth to be your inheritance, as you said through your servant Moses, when you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, Lord GOD."
When Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and plea to the LORD, he got up from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling with his hands spread out towards heaven.
He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice:
"Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promise that he spoke through his servant Moses.
May the LORD our God be with us, as he was with our ancestors. May he not leave us or abandon us,
so that he turns our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commands, his statutes and his rules, which he commanded our ancestors.

May these words of mine, with which I have pleaded before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that he upholds the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel, as each day requires,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other.
Let your hearts be wholly true to the LORD our God, walking in his statutes and keeping his commands, as you do today."
Then the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifices before the LORD.
Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.

On the same day the king made holy the middle of the court in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.
So Solomon held the festival at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt, before the LORD our God, for seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away. They blessed the king and went to their homes, joyful and glad at heart for all the good that the LORD had done for his servant David and for his people Israel.
When Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the king's house and everything else that Solomon wanted to build,
the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

The LORD said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your plea that you made before me. I have made this house that you have built holy, by putting my name there for ever. My eyes and my heart will be there at all times.
As for you, if you walk before me as your father David did, with a whole heart and with honesty, doing all that I have commanded you, and keeping my statutes and my rules,
then I will establish your royal throne over Israel for ever, as I promised your father David: 'You will never lack a man on the throne of Israel.'
But if you or your sons turn away from following me and do not keep my commands and my statutes that I have set before you, but go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

then I will cut Israel off from the land that I have given them, and the house that I have made holy for my name I will throw out of my sight, and Israel will become a proverb and a taunt among all peoples.
This house will become a heap of ruins. Everyone who passes by it will be shocked and will whistle, and they will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

Then they will say, 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of the land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them. That is why the LORD has brought all this disaster on them.'"
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD and the king's house,
and Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar and cypress timber and gold, as much as he wanted, King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the land of Galilee.
But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns that Solomon had given him, he was not pleased with them.
He said, "What kind of towns are these that you have given me, my brother?" So they are called the land of Cabul to this day.
Hiram had sent the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.
This is the account of the forced labour that King Solomon raised to build the house of the LORD and his own house, the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer
(Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it down and killed the Canaanites who lived in the town, and had given it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife),
and Solomon rebuilt Gezer, and Lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath, and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land of Judah,

and all the storage towns that Solomon had, and the towns for his chariots and the towns for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land under his rule.
All the people who were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, who were not Israelites,
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not been able to devote to destruction, Solomon raised as forced labour, and so they are to this day.
But of the Israelites Solomon made no slaves. They were his soldiers, his officials, his commanders, his captains and the commanders of his chariots and horsemen.
These were the chief officers over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty, who were in charge of the people doing the work.
But Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her own house that Solomon had built for her. Then he built the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he had built for the LORD, and burned incense with them before the LORD. So he finished the house.
King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, sailors who knew the sea, to work with Solomon's servants.
They went to Ophir and brought from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and delivered it to King Solomon.
When the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, and of his connection with the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions.
She came to Jerusalem with a very large caravan, with camels carrying spices and a great deal of gold and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she told him everything that was on her mind.
Solomon answered all her questions. There was nothing hidden from the king that he could not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, the house that he had built,

the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings that he offered at the house of the LORD, she was left breathless.
She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own land of your words and your wisdom was true.
But I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. And look, not even half was told me. Your wisdom and wealth go beyond the report that I heard.
How happy your people are. How happy these servants of yours are, who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.
Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel. Because the LORD loved Israel for ever, he made you king, to do justice and righteousness."

Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices come as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
(Hiram's fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought from Ophir a very great amount of almug wood and precious stones.
The king used the almug wood to make supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day.)
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her out of his royal generosity. Then she turned and went back to her own land with her servants.
The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents,
besides what came from the traders and the merchants' trade, and from all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold, with six hundred shekels of gold in each shield.
He also made three hundred smaller shields of beaten gold, with three minas of gold in each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with fine gold.
The throne had six steps, and a round top at the back, and arms on each side of the seat, with a lion standing beside each arm.
Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one at each end of a step. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.

All King Solomon's drinking cups were of gold, and all the vessels in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None were of silver, for silver was thought of no value in the days of Solomon.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish ships at sea with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came back, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and baboons.
So King Solomon was greater than all the other kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
The whole world wanted to see Solomon and hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
Each one brought a gift, articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules, year after year.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot towns and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore fig trees in the lowland.
Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue, and the king's traders bought them from Kue at a price.

A chariot imported from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse a hundred and fifty, and they were exported through the king's traders to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides Pharaoh's daughter: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite women,

from the nations about which the LORD had said to the Israelites, "You must not go in to them, and they must not come in to you, for they will surely turn your hearts away after their gods." Solomon held on to these in love.
He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines. And his wives turned his heart away.
For when Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart away after other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
So Solomon did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and did not follow the LORD fully, as his father David had done.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, on the hill east of Jerusalem, and for Molech, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
The LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had commanded him about this very thing, that he should not follow other gods. But he did not keep what the LORD commanded.

So the LORD said to Solomon, "Because this is what you have done, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
But for the sake of your father David I will not do it in your lifetime. I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
Yet I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give your son one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite. He was of the royal family in Edom.
When David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the dead, he struck down every male in Edom
(for Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom).
But Hadad ran away to Egypt with some Edomites who were his father's servants. Hadad was still a young boy.
They set out from Midian and came to Paran, and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him food and gave him land.
Hadad found great favour with Pharaoh, so that he gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
The sister of Tahpenes bore him his son Genubath, whom Tahpenes brought up in Pharaoh's house. Genubath lived in Pharaoh's house among Pharaoh's sons.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his ancestors and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, so that I can go to my own country."
Pharaoh said to him, "What do you lack with me, that you now want to go to your own country?" He answered, "Nothing. But please let me go."
God also raised up another adversary against him, Rezon son of Eliada, who had run away from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men round him and became leader of a raiding band, after David killed the men of Zobah. They went to Damascus and lived there and made him king in Damascus.
He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon, adding to the harm that Hadad did. He hated Israel and ruled over Aram.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother was a widow named Zeruah, also raised his hand against the king.
This is why he raised his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed up the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
The man Jeroboam was very capable, and when Solomon saw how hard the young man worked, he put him in charge of all the forced labour of the house of Joseph.
At that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road. Ahijah had put on a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open country.
Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
He said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes
(but he will keep one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the town that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel),

because he has abandoned me and bowed down to Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab and to Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and has not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes and keeping my statutes and my rules, as his father David did.
But I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand. I will keep him as ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose and who kept my commands and my statutes.
I will take the kingdom from his son's hand and give it to you, ten tribes.
To his son I will give one tribe, so that my servant David may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the town where I chose to put my name.
I will take you, and you will rule over all that you desire, and you will be king over Israel.

If you listen to all that I command you, and walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commands, as my servant David did, I will be with you and will build you a lasting house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
I will punish David's descendants because of this, but not for ever."
Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam got up and ran away to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and stayed in Egypt until Solomon's death.
The rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
The time that Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
Then Solomon lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it (he was still in Egypt, where he had run away from King Solomon), Jeroboam came back from Egypt.
They sent and called him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."
He said to them, "Go away for three days, and then come back to me." So the people went away.
King Rehoboam took advice from the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was still alive. He said, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
They said to him, "If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them, and speak kind words to them when you answer them, then they will be your servants for ever."
But he rejected the advice that the elders gave him and took advice from the young men who had grown up with him and who served him.
He said to them, "What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"

The young men who had grown up with him said to him, "This is what you should say to this people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must lighten it for us.' Say to them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father loaded you with a heavy yoke, but I will make your yoke heavier. My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions.'"
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said, "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered the people harshly, rejecting the advice that the elders had given him,
and spoke to them as the young men advised: "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will make your yoke heavier. My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people, for the turn of events was from the LORD, to carry out the word that the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
When all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king:
"What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel. Now look after your own house, David."
So Israel went to their tents.
But Rehoboam ruled over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labour, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. No one followed the house of David, except the tribe of Judah alone.

When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he gathered the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people,

'This is what the LORD says: You must not go up and fight against your kinsmen the Israelites. Each of you go back to his home, for this is from me.'" So they listened to the word of the LORD and went back, as the LORD had said.
Then Jeroboam built up Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built up Penuel.
Jeroboam said to himself, "Now the kingdom will go back to the house of David.

If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, the heart of this people will turn back to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and go back to Rehoboam king of Judah."
So the king took advice and made two golden calves. He said to the people, "You have gone up to Jerusalem for long enough. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
He set one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
This became a sin, for the people went as far as Dan to worship before the one.
He also made houses on the high places and appointed priests from all the people, who were not Levites.

Jeroboam appointed a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar. He did this at Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made. And he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.

He went up to the altar that he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in the month that he had chosen on his own, and he held a festival for the Israelites, and went up to the altar to burn incense.
By the word of the LORD, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel, while Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

By the word of the LORD he cried out against the altar: "Altar, altar, this is what the LORD says: A son will be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and on you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you."
He gave a sign that same day: "This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: the altar will be torn apart, and the ashes on it will be poured out."

When the king heard what the man of God cried out against the altar at Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar and said, "Seize him." But the hand that he stretched out against him dried up, so that he could not pull it back.
The altar was also torn apart and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

The king said to the man of God, "Please seek the favour of the LORD your God, and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God sought the favour of the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.
The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."
But the man of God said to the king, "If you gave me half your house, I would not go with you. I will not eat bread or drink water in this place,
for this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: 'You must not eat bread or drink water or go back by the way you came.'"
So he went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.
Now an old prophet was living in Bethel. His sons came and told him all that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words he had spoken to the king.
Their father said to them, "Which way did he go?" His sons showed him the way that the man of God from Judah had gone.
He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him and he got on it.
