He went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak. He said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He said, "I am."
He said to him, "Come home with me and eat something."
But he said, "I cannot go back with you or go with you. I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place,
for it was said to me by the word of the LORD: 'You must not eat bread or drink water there, or go back by the way you came.'"

He said to him, "I am a prophet too, as you are, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD: 'Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" But he was lying to him.
So he went back with him and ate bread in his house and drank water.
While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.
He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have disobeyed the word of the LORD and have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you,
but have come back and eaten bread and drunk water in the place where he told you, 'Do not eat bread or drink water,' your body will not come to the tomb of your ancestors."
After he had eaten bread and drunk, he saddled the donkey for the prophet whom he had brought back.
As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body was thrown down on the road, and the donkey stood beside it. The lion also stood beside the body.
Some men passed by and saw the body thrown down on the road and the lion standing beside the body. They went and told it in the town where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard it, he said, "It is the man of God who disobeyed the word of the LORD. The LORD has handed him over to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, as the word of the LORD said to him."
He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled it.
He went and found the body thrown down on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
The prophet picked up the body of the man of God and laid it on the donkey and brought it back, to mourn for him and bury him in the town.
He laid the body in his own grave. They mourned over him and said, "Alas, my brother."
After he had buried him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the grave where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.
For the word that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places in the towns of Samaria, will certainly come true."

Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but again appointed priests for the high places from all the people. Anyone who wanted to be one, he installed as a priest of the high places.
This became sin for the house of Jeroboam, so that it was cut off and wiped from the face of the earth.
At that time Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, fell ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up and disguise yourself, so that no one will know you are Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, who told me I would be king over this people.
Take with you ten loaves, some cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did so. She got up and went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were fixed with age.
The LORD had said to Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. This is what you are to say to her. When she comes, she will be pretending to be someone else."
When Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you pretending to be someone else? I have been sent to you with hard news.
Go and tell Jeroboam, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I raised you up from among the people and made you leader over my people Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commands and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
You have done more evil than all who were before you. You have gone and made for yourself other gods and cast images, to make me angry, and you have thrown me behind your back.

So I will bring disaster on the house of Jeroboam and cut off from Jeroboam every male, slave and free, in Israel. I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung, until it is all gone.
Anyone of Jeroboam's family who dies in the town, the dogs will eat, and anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat. For the LORD has spoken.'
Now get up and go home. When your feet enter the town, the child will die.
All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He alone of Jeroboam's family will come to a grave, because in him something pleasing to the LORD, the God of Israel, was found in the house of Jeroboam.
The LORD will raise up for himself a king over Israel, who will cut off the house of Jeroboam this very day. What is it even now?

The LORD will strike Israel, so that it sways like a reed in the water. He will pull Israel up out of this good land that he gave to their ancestors, and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles and made the LORD angry.
He will give Israel up because of the sins that Jeroboam committed and caused Israel to commit."
Jeroboam's wife got up and left and came to Tirzah. As she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.
All Israel buried him and mourned for him, as the word of the LORD said through his servant the prophet Ahijah.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he made war and how he ruled, are written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel.
The time that Jeroboam ruled was twenty-two years. Then he lay down with his ancestors, and his son Nadab became king in his place.

Rehoboam son of Solomon was king in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the town that the LORD chose out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and with their sins they made him jealous, more than all that their ancestors had done.
They also built for themselves high places and pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree,
and there were male shrine prostitutes in the land. They acted according to all the detestable practices of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything. He also took away all the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and put them in the care of the officers of the guard, who kept watch at the entrance of the king's house.
Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards carried them, and then took them back to the guardroom.
The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the time.
Rehoboam lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. And his son Abijam became king in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
He walked in all the sins that his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as the heart of his ancestor David had been.
Yet for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, by raising up his son after him and keeping Jerusalem secure,
because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and did not turn aside from anything that he commanded him, all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
The rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David. His son Asa became king in his place.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah,
and he ruled for forty-one years in Jerusalem. His grandmother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done.
He drove the male shrine prostitutes out of the land and removed all the idols that his ancestors had made.
He also removed his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother, because she had made a horrible image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Wadi Kidron.
But the high places were not removed. Even so, Asa's heart was wholly true to the LORD all his days.
He brought into the house of the LORD the gifts that his father and he himself had dedicated: silver, gold and vessels.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built up Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the treasuries of the king's house and handed it to his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

"Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the towns of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building up Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.

Then King Asa gave an order to all Judah, with no exceptions, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building. With them King Asa built up Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

The rest of all the acts of Asa, all his power, and all that he did, and the towns that he built, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah? But in his old age he was diseased in his feet.
Asa lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of his ancestor David. His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.
Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he ruled over Israel for two years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father, and in the sin that he made Israel commit.
Baasha son of Ahijah, from the house of Issachar, plotted against him. Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.

As soon as he was king, he struck down the whole house of Jeroboam. He left no one alive of the family of Jeroboam, until he had destroyed it, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
because of the sins that Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit, and because of the anger with which he made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
The rest of the acts of Nadab and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel at Tirzah, and he ruled for twenty-four years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in the sin that he made Israel commit.
The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha:
"I lifted you out of the dust and made you leader over my people Israel, but you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, and made me angry with their sins.
So I will sweep Baasha and his house away completely, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Anyone of Baasha's family who dies in the town, the dogs will eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."
The rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did and his power, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Baasha lay down with his ancestors and was buried at Tirzah, and his son Elah became king in his place.

The word of the LORD also came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of the LORD, making him angry by the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah, and he ruled for two years.
His servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, plotted against him. Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was in charge of the household at Tirzah.
Zimri came in and struck him down and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and became king in his place.
When he became king and sat on his throne, he struck down the whole house of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, relative or friend.
So Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke against Baasha through the prophet Jehu,
because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of his son Elah, which they committed and made Israel commit, making the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their idols.
The rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri ruled in Tirzah for seven days. The army was camped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines,
and the soldiers in the camp heard it said, "Zimri has plotted and has killed the king." So that day in the camp all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the town was taken, he went into the stronghold of the king's house and burned the king's house down over himself, and died,
because of the sins that he committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin that he committed, making Israel sin.
The rest of the acts of Zimri, and the plot that he made, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel were split into two parts. Half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.
But the people who followed Omri overcame the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel, and he ruled for twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and he built on the hill, and he named the town that he built Samaria, after Shemer, the owner of the hill.
Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all who were before him.
He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in the sin that he made Israel commit, making the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their idols.
The rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the power that he showed, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Omri lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel, and Ahab son of Omri ruled over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
As if it were a small thing to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he married Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.
Ahab also made an Asherah pole. Ahab did more to make the LORD, the God of Israel, angry than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, as the word of the LORD had said through Joshua son of Nun.
Elijah the Tishbite, from Tishbe in Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain in these years, except at my word."
Then the word of the LORD came to him:
"Leave here and turn east, and hide yourself by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
You will drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
So he went and did as the LORD had said. He went and lived by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
After a while the wadi dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
Then the word of the LORD came to him:
"Get up and go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and live there. I have commanded a widow there to feed you."
So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. He called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I can drink."
As she was going to get it, he called to her, "Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand."

She said, "As the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked, only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks, to go home and make something for myself and my son, so that we can eat it and die."
Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small loaf from it and bring it to me, and then make something for yourself and your son.
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not fail, until the day the LORD sends rain on the earth."
She went and did as Elijah said. And she and he and her household ate for many days.
The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not fail, as the word of the LORD said through Elijah.
After this the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. His illness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
She said to Elijah, "What do you have against me, man of God? Have you come to remind me of my guilt and to kill my son?"
He said to her, "Give me your son." He took him from her arms and carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
He cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on the widow I am staying with, by killing her son?"
Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried to the LORD, "LORD my God, let this child's life come back into him."
The LORD listened to Elijah's voice, and the child's life came back into him, and he lived.
Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, "Look, your son is alive."
The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is true."
After many days the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year: "Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain on the earth."
So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine in Samaria was severe.
Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the palace. (Obadiah feared the LORD greatly,
and when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them fifty to a cave and fed them with bread and water.)

Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the wadis. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive, so that we do not have to kill any of the animals."
So they divided the land between them to cover it. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
While Obadiah was on the way, Elijah met him. Obadiah recognised him and fell on his face and said, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?"
He answered, "It is. Go and tell your lord, 'Elijah is here.'"
He said, "What wrong have I done, that you hand your servant over to Ahab to be killed?

As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to look for you. When they said, 'He is not here,' he made that kingdom or nation swear that they had not found you.
And now you say, 'Go and tell your lord, "Elijah is here."'

As soon as I leave you, the spirit of the LORD will carry you off to a place I do not know. When I come and tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me, though I, your servant, have feared the LORD from my youth.
Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD, how I hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets, fifty to a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
And now you say, 'Go and tell your lord, "Elijah is here."' He will kill me."
Elijah said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will show myself to him today."
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, "Is it you, the troubler of Israel?"
He answered, "I have not troubled Israel, but you have, and your father's house, because you have abandoned the commands of the LORD and followed the Baals.
Now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."
So Ahab sent word to all the Israelites and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.
Elijah came near to all the people and said, "How long will you limp between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is, follow him." But the people did not answer him a word.
Then Elijah said to the people, "I am the only prophet of the LORD left, but Baal's prophets number four hundred and fifty.

Let two bulls be given to us. Let them choose one bull for themselves and cut it in pieces and put it on the wood, but not set fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and put it on the wood, and not set fire to it.
Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The god who answers by fire, he is God." All the people answered, "What you say is good."
Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many, and call on the name of your god, but do not set fire to it."

They took the bull that was given them and prepared it, and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, "Baal, answer us." But there was no voice, and no one answered. They limped round the altar that they had made.
At noon Elijah mocked them: "Shout louder, for he is a god. Perhaps he is deep in thought, or he has gone aside, or he is on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and needs to be woken."
They shouted louder and cut themselves with swords and spears, as was their custom, until the blood poured over them.
When midday had passed, they raved on until the time for the evening offering, but there was no voice, no answer, and no one paid attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." All the people came near to him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come, "Israel will be your name."
With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD. He dug a trench round the altar, large enough to hold two measures of seed.
He arranged the wood and cut the bull in pieces and laid it on the wood. He said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood."
He said, "Do it a second time." And they did it a second time. He said, "Do it a third time." And they did it a third time.
The water ran round the altar and filled the trench as well.

At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet came near and said, "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things at your word.
Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you are turning their hearts back."
Then the fire of the LORD fell and burned up the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench.
When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, "The LORD, he is God. The LORD, he is God."
Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal. Do not let one of them escape." They seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon and killed them there.
Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of heavy rain."
So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah went up to the top of Carmel and bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
He said to his servant, "Go up and look towards the sea." He went up and looked and said, "There is nothing." Seven times Elijah said, "Go back."
The seventh time he said, "Look, a small cloud like a man's hand is rising from the sea." Elijah said, "Go and say to Ahab, 'Harness your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.'"
In a little while the sky grew black with clouds and wind, and there was heavy rain. Ahab rode off to Jezreel.
The hand of the LORD was on Elijah, and he tucked up his clothes and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.
Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "May the gods do this to me, and more also, if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the life of one of them."
He was afraid, and he got up and ran for his life, and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.

But he went a day's journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a broom bush. He asked that he might die, saying, "It is enough now, LORD. Take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors."
He lay down and slept under the broom bush. Then an angel touched him and said to him, "Get up and eat."
He looked, and there by his head was a loaf baked on hot stones, and a jar of water. He ate and drank and lay down again.
The angel of the LORD came a second time and touched him and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."
He got up and ate and drank, and on the strength of that food he walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he came to a cave and spent the night in it. And the word of the LORD came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He said, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are trying to take my life."

He said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD, for the LORD is about to pass by." Then a great and strong wind tore the mountains apart and broke the rocks in pieces before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire there was a sound of thin silence.
When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And a voice came to him and said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He said, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are trying to take my life."
The LORD said to him, "Go back on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah as prophet in your place.
Whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill, and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will kill.
Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."
So he left there and found Elisha son of Shaphat, who was ploughing with twelve pairs of oxen ahead of him, and he was with the twelfth. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak over him.
He left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, "Let me kiss my father and my mother goodbye, and then I will follow you." He said to him, "Go back. What have I done to you?"

Elisha went back from following him, and took the pair of oxen and killed them and boiled their flesh using the ploughing equipment as fuel, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up and followed Elijah and served him.
Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army, with thirty-two kings and their horses and chariots. He went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.
He sent messengers into the town to Ahab king of Israel and said to him, "This is what Ben-hadad says:
'Your silver and your gold are mine. Your wives and your best children are mine too.'"
The king of Israel answered, "As you say, my lord the king, I and all that I have are yours."
The messengers came again and said, "This is what Ben-hadad says: 'I sent word to you, saying,"Hand over to me your silver and gold, your wives and your children."
But by this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants and take away whatever they like.'"

Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land and said, "See how this man is looking for trouble. He sent to me for my wives and children, and for my silver and gold, and I did not refuse him."
All the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen to him or agree."
So he said to Ben-hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king, 'I will do all that you first demanded of your servant, but this I cannot do.'" The messengers left and took the answer back.
Ben-hadad sent to him and said, "May the gods do this to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria is enough for a handful for each of the people who follow me."
The king of Israel answered, "Tell him, 'The one who puts on his armour should not boast like the one who takes it off.'"
When Ben-hadad heard this message, as he was drinking with the kings in the shelters, he said to his men, "Take your places." And they took their places against the town.
Then a prophet came to Ahab king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: Do you see this whole great crowd? Today I will hand it over to you, and you will know that I am the LORD."
Ahab said, "By whom?" He said, "This is what the LORD says: By the young men of the district governors." He said, "Who will begin the battle?" He answered, "You."
So he counted the young men of the district governors, and they were two hundred and thirty-two. After them he counted all the people, all the Israelites, seven thousand.
They went out at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the shelters with the thirty-two kings who were helping him.
The young men of the district governors went out first. Ben-hadad sent out scouts, and they reported to him, "Men are coming out of Samaria."
He said, "If they have come out for peace, take them alive. If they have come out for war, take them alive."
So these went out of the town, the young men of the district governors and the army following them.
Each struck down his man. The Arameans ran away, and Israel chased them, but Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on a horse with some horsemen.
The king of Israel went out and struck the horses and chariots, and struck the Arameans a great blow.

Then the prophet came to the king of Israel and said to him, "Go and strengthen yourself, and think carefully about what you must do, for in the spring the king of Aram will come up against you again."

The servants of the king of Aram said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills, and that is why they were stronger than we. But let us fight them on the plain, and we will surely be stronger than they.
And do this: remove the kings, each from his post, and put commanders in their place,
and raise an army like the one you lost, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. Then we will fight them on the plain, and we will surely be stronger than they." He listened to them and did so.
In the spring Ben-hadad gathered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
The Israelites were also gathered and supplied, and went to meet them. The Israelites camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans filled the countryside.

A man of God came and said to the king of Israel, "This is what the LORD says: Because the Arameans have said, 'The LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys,' I will hand all this great crowd over to you, and you will know that I am the LORD."
They camped opposite each other for seven days. On the seventh day the battle began, and the Israelites struck down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
The rest ran to the town of Aphek, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of those who were left. Ben-hadad also ran away and went into an inner room in the town.

His servants said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth round our waists and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will spare your life."

So they put sackcloth round their waists and ropes on their heads and went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" He said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
The men were watching for a sign, and quickly took it from him and said, "Yes, your brother Ben-hadad." He said, "Go and bring him." Ben-hadad came out to him, and he had him get up into his chariot.

Ben-hadad said to him, "I will give back the towns that my father took from your father, and you may set up markets for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab said, "On these terms I will let you go." So he made a treaty with him and let him go.
One of the company of the prophets said to another by the word of the LORD, "Strike me, please." But the man refused to strike him.
Then he said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, as soon as you leave me a lion will strike you down." As soon as he left him, a lion met him and struck him down.
He found another man and said, "Strike me, please." So the man struck him and wounded him.
Then the prophet went and waited for the king by the road, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passed by, he called out to the king, "Your servant went out into the middle of the battle, and a soldier turned aside and brought a man to me and said, 'Guard this man. If he is missing, your life will be for his life, or you will pay a talent of silver.'
While your servant was busy here and there, he was gone." The king of Israel said to him, "That is your sentence. You have decided it yourself."
He quickly took the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognised him as one of the prophets.
He said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people."
The king of Israel went home to Samaria, sullen and angry.
Some time later Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard, so that I can have it as a vegetable garden, because it is close to my house. I will give you a better vineyard for it, or, if you prefer, I will pay you its value in silver."
But Naboth said to Ahab, "The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my ancestors."

Ahab went home sullen and angry because of what Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him, for he had said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my ancestors." He lay down on his bed and turned his face away and would not eat.
His wife Jezebel came to him and said, "Why are you so low in spirit that you will not eat?"

He said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver, or, if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard for it.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
His wife Jezebel said to him, "Do you not now rule over Israel? Get up and eat and be cheerful. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
So she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and the leading men who lived in Naboth's town.
In the letters she wrote: "Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
Seat two worthless men opposite him, and have them bring a charge against him: 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him to death."
The men of his town, the elders and the leading men who lived in his town, did as Jezebel had told them, as written in the letters she had sent them.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

The two worthless men came in and sat opposite him. And the worthless men brought a charge against Naboth in front of the people: "Naboth has cursed God and the king." So they took him outside the town and stoned him to death.
Then they sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."

As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is no longer alive. He is dead."
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
"Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. He is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession.

Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered and also taken possession?' And say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lick up your blood too.'"
Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" He answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
I will bring disaster on you. I will sweep you away and cut off from Ahab every male, slave and free, in Israel.
I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the anger you have provoked and because you have made Israel sin.
And about Jezebel the LORD also says: 'The dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
Anyone of Ahab's family who dies in the town, the dogs will eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."
(There was never anyone like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, urged on by his wife Jezebel.
He acted most vilely in following idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the Israelites.)
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his body and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and walked about subdued.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
"Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days. I will bring the disaster on his house in his son's days."
For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.
In the third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his officials, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, and we are doing nothing to take it back from the king of Aram?"
He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "First, please ask for the word of the LORD."

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall I go to fight against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" They said, "Go up, for the Lord will hand it over to the king."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no other prophet of the LORD here, that we may ask through him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can ask the LORD, Micaiah son of Imlah. But I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only bad." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, "This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore the Arameans until they are finished."
All the prophets prophesied the same: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and win, for the LORD will hand it over to the king."
The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the words of the prophets are all one in favour of the king. Let your word be like theirs, and speak favourably."
But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, I will speak what the LORD says to me."
When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to fight at Ramoth-gilead, or shall we hold back?" He answered him, "Go up and win. The LORD will hand it over to the king."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
Then he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, 'These have no master. Let each go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good about me, only bad?"
Micaiah said, "Then hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing round him, on his right and on his left.
The LORD said, 'Who will persuade Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and another said another.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will persuade him.'
The LORD said to him, 'How?' He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' He said, 'You will persuade him, and you will succeed. Go out and do it.'
So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has declared disaster against you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the spirit of the LORD go when it left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "You will see on the day when you go into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Seize Micaiah and take him back to Amon the governor of the town and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and feed him only a little bread and a little water until I come back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you ever come back safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." And he said, "Listen, all you peoples."
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.
Now the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel alone."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "It must be the king of Israel." So they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from chasing him.
But someone drew his bow without aim and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armour. So he said to his chariot driver, "Turn round and take me out of the fighting, for I am wounded."
The battle grew fierce that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans. He died in the evening, and the blood from the wound ran down to the floor of the chariot.
About sunset a cry went through the army: "Each man to his town, and each man to his land."
So the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.
They washed out the chariot at the pool of Samaria, where the prostitutes washed, and the dogs licked up his blood, as the word of the LORD had said.
The rest of the acts of Ahab and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the towns that he built, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Ahab lay down with his ancestors, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

He walked in all the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD. But the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and the power that he showed, and how he made war, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
He also wiped out of the land the remnant of the male shrine prostitutes who were left from the days of his father Asa.
There was no king in Edom. A deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, because the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat was not willing.
Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of his ancestor David. His son Jehoram became king in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he ruled over Israel for two years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
He served Baal and bowed down to him and made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry, just as his father had done.
After Ahab's death, Moab rebelled against Israel.
Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers and told them, "Go and ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury."

But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up and go to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?'
Therefore this is what the LORD says: You will not come down from the bed that you have gone up to, but you will certainly die." So Elijah went.
The messengers went back to the king, and he said to them, "Why have you come back?"

They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him, This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not come down from the bed that you have gone up to, but you will certainly die.'"
He said to them, "What was the man like who came to meet you and told you these things?"
They answered him, "He was wearing a garment of hair, with a leather belt round his waist." He said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
Then the king sent a captain of fifty with his fifty men to him. The captain went up to Elijah, who was sitting on top of a hill, and said to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down.'"
Elijah answered the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and burn you up, you and your fifty." Then fire came down from heaven and burned him up, and his fifty.
The king sent another captain of fifty with his fifty to him. He said to him, "Man of God, this is what the king says: 'Come down at once.'"
Elijah answered them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and burn you up, you and your fifty." Then the fire of God came down from heaven and burned him up, and his fifty.

Again the king sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up and came and fell on his knees before Elijah and begged him, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
Look, fire came down from heaven and burned up the two earlier captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your eyes."
The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him." So he got up and went down with him to the king,

and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Because you sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel to ask for his word, you will not come down from the bed that you have gone up to, but you will certainly die."
So he died, as the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken said. Jehoram became king in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because Ahaziah had no son.
The rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
The company of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from you?" He said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
The company of the prophets who were at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from you?" He answered, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Elijah said to him, "Stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
Fifty of the company of the prophets also went and stood at a distance opposite them, as the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Then Elijah took his cloak and rolled it up and struck the water, and the water divided to one side and the other, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I may do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let me have a double share of your spirit."
He said, "You have asked a hard thing. Yet if you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you, but if not, it will not."
As they were walking on and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen." And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
He picked up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He took the cloak that had fallen from Elijah and struck the water and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he struck the water, it divided to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.
When the company of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him opposite, they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

They said to him, "Look, there are fifty strong men among your servants. Please let them go and look for your master. Perhaps the spirit of the LORD has taken him up and thrown him down on some mountain or in some valley." He said, "Do not send them."
But when they pressed him until he was embarrassed, he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and for three days they searched but did not find him.
They came back to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not tell you not to go?"
The men of the town said to Elisha, "Look, the town is well placed, as my lord can see, but the water is bad and the land is unfruitful."
He said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
Then he went out to the spring and threw salt into it and said, "This is what the LORD says: I have healed this water. From now on neither death nor miscarriage will come from it."
So the water has been healed to this day, as Elisha's word said.
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up the road, some small boys came out of the town and jeered at him, saying, "Go up, baldhead. Go up, baldhead."
He turned round and looked at them and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two she-bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.
From there he went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for twelve years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and mother, for he removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
Even so, he held on to the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit, and did not turn away from it.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to deliver to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So King Jehoram marched out of Samaria at that time and called out all Israel.

He went and sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" He said, "I will go. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
Then he said, "By which way shall we go up?" Jehoram answered, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
So the king of Israel went with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. When they had gone round by a seven-day route, there was no water for the army or for the animals that followed them.
The king of Israel said, "Oh no. The LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."

Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, through whom we can ask the LORD?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah."
Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have you and I in common? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No. It is the LORD who has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if I did not have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you.
But now bring me someone to play the harp." While the harpist played, the hand of the LORD came on him.
He said, "This is what the LORD says: Make this valley full of ditches.
For this is what the LORD says: You will not see wind or rain, but that valley will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your cattle and your animals.
This is a small thing in the eyes of the LORD. He will also hand Moab over to you.
You will strike every fortified town and every important town. You will cut down every good tree, stop up every spring of water and ruin every good field with stones."
The next morning, at the time of the offering, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
When all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, everyone who could put on armour, young and old, was called out and stood at the border.
When they got up early in the morning and the sun shone on the water, the Moabites saw the water opposite them as red as blood.
They said, "That is blood. The kings must have fought each other and struck each other down. Now to the plunder, Moab."
But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, who ran away from them. The Israelites went forward into the land, striking the Moabites as they went.

They pulled down the towns, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was covered. They stopped every spring and cut down every good tree, until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left, and the slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took seven hundred men with swords to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.
Then he took his firstborn son, who was to rule in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. There was great anger against Israel. So they left him and went back to their own land.

The wife of one of the company of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. But now the creditor has come to take my two sons as his slaves."
Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil."
He said, "Go and borrow vessels from all your neighbours, empty vessels, as many as you can.
Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all those vessels. As each one is full, put it to one side."
So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." He said to her, "There are no more." Then the oil stopped.
She went and told the man of God, and he said, "Go and sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha went on to Shunem, where a wealthy woman lived, who urged him to eat some food. So whenever he passed that way, he would turn in there to eat.
She said to her husband, "Look, I know that this man who often passes by us is a holy man of God.
Let us make a small room on the roof, with walls, and put a bed there for him, with a table, a chair and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us he can stay there."
One day he came there, and he went up to the room and lay down there.
He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call this Shunammite woman." He called her, and she stood before him.

He said to him, "Say to her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Shall a word be put in for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."
He said, "What then can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
He said, "Call her." He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
He said, "At this time next year you will be holding a son." She said, "No, my lord, man of God. Do not lie to your servant."
But the woman conceived, and she bore a son at that time the next year, as Elisha had told her.
When the child was older, he went out one day to his father among the reapers.
He said to his father, "My head, my head." The father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
He picked him up and brought him to his mother, and the child sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door behind him and went out.
She called to her husband and said, "Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I can hurry to the man of God and come back."
He said, "Why go to him today? It is not the new moon or the sabbath." She said, "It will be all right."
Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and do not slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, "Look, there is the Shunammite.
Run to meet her and ask her, 'Are you well? Is your husband well? Is the child well?'" She answered, "Well."

When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for she is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."
Then she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"
He said to Gehazi, "Tie up your clothes, take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the face of the child."
The child's mother said, "As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the face of the child, but there was no sound and no sign of life. So he went back to meet him and told him, "The child has not woken."
When Elisha came into the house, there was the child, lying dead on his bed.
He went in and shut the door on the two of them and prayed to the LORD.
Then he got on the bed and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands. As he stretched himself over him, the child's flesh became warm.
Then he got up and walked once up and down in the house, and went up and stretched himself over him again. The child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her. When she came to him, he said, "Pick up your son."
She came in and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

Elisha went back to Gilgal when there was a famine in the land. While the company of the prophets were sitting in front of him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on and make a stew for the company of the prophets."

One of them went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered as many wild gourds from it as his cloak would hold, and came and cut them into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
They served it for the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot." And they could not eat it.
He said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Serve it for the people to eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread from the first harvest, twenty barley loaves and fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."
But his servant said, "How can I set this in front of a hundred men?" He said again, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: They will eat and have some left over."
So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, as the word of the LORD said.

Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master's eyes and highly respected, because through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. He was a brave warrior, but he had a skin disease.
On one of their raids the Arameans had taken captive a young girl from the land of Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "If only my master were with the prophet who is in Samaria. He would cure him of his skin disease."
So Naaman went in and told his master, "This is what the girl from the land of Israel said."
The king of Aram said, "Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and ten changes of clothes.
He brought the letter to the king of Israel. It read: "When this letter reaches you, know that I have sent my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his skin disease."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to kill and to give life, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his skin disease? Just think, and see how he is looking for a quarrel with me."

When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent word to the king: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, so that he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh will be restored and you will be clean."
But Naaman was angry and went away, saying, "I thought he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot and cure the disease.
Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage.
But his servants came near and said to him, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more when he says to you, 'Wash and be clean.'"
So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, as the man of God had said, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

Then he went back to the man of God, he and all his company, and stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant."
But he said, "As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept anything." He urged him to take it, but he refused.

Then Naaman said, "If not, please let your servant be given as much earth as a pair of mules can carry, for from now on your servant will not offer burnt offering or sacrifice to any god except the LORD.

But may the LORD forgive your servant in this one thing: when my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there and leans on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant in this thing."
He said to him, "Go in peace." But when Naaman had gone a short distance from him,

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself, "My master has spared this Aramean Naaman by not accepting what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi went after Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is everything all right?"

He said, "Everything is all right. My master has sent me to say, 'Two young men of the company of the prophets have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

Naaman said, "Please take two talents." He urged him and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them ahead of Gehazi.
When he came to the hill, he took them from them and put them in the house, and sent the men away, and they left.
He went in and stood before his master, and Elisha said to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere."

But he said to him, "Did my heart not go with you when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept money and clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, male and female servants?
So Naaman's skin disease will cling to you and to your descendants for ever." Gehazi left his presence with a skin disease, as white as snow.
The company of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live with you is too small for us.
Let us go to the Jordan, and each of us get a beam from there, and let us make a place there for us to live." He said, "Go."
One of them said, "Please come with your servants." He said, "I will come."
So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down trees.
While one was felling a beam, the iron axe head fell into the water, and he cried out, "Oh no, my master. It was borrowed."
The man of God said, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there, and the iron floated.
He said, "Lift it out." So he reached out his hand and took it.
When the king of Aram was at war with Israel, he took counsel with his officers and said, "My camp will be in such and such a place."
But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Be careful not to pass this place, for the Arameans are going down there."
So the king of Israel sent word to the place that the man of God had told him about. He warned him again and again, so that he was on his guard there, not just once or twice.
The king of Aram was very troubled about this, and he called his officers and said to them, "Will you not tell me which of us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
One of his officers said, "No one, my lord the king. But Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."
He said, "Go and find out where he is, so that I can send and capture him." It was reported to him, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses and chariots and a large force there, and they came by night and surrounded the town.

When the servant of the man of God got up early in the morning and went out, there was an army with horses and chariots all round the town. His servant said to him, "Oh no, my master. What shall we do?"
He said, "Do not be afraid, for there are more with us than with them."
Then Elisha prayed, "LORD, please open his eyes, so that he may see." The LORD opened the servant's eyes, and he saw that the hill was full of horses and chariots of fire all round Elisha.
When the Arameans came down towards him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Please strike this people with blindness." So he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.
Elisha said to them, "This is not the road, and this is not the town. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men, so that they can see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw that they were inside Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?"

He answered, "You must not strike them down. Do you strike down those you have captured with your own sword and bow? Set bread and water in front of them, so that they can eat and drink and go back to their master."

So he prepared a great feast for them, and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went back to their master. And the Aramean raiding bands did not come again into the land of Israel.
Some time later Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army and went up and besieged Samaria.
There was a great famine in Samaria during the siege, until a donkey's head was sold for eighty shekels of silver and a quarter of a cab of dove's dung for five shekels of silver.
As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king."
He said, "If the LORD does not help you, how can I help you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"
Then the king asked her, "What is the matter?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son so that we can eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
So we boiled my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son so that we can eat him.' But she has hidden her son."
When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. (He was passing by on the wall, and the people looked, and there was sackcloth underneath, next to his skin.)
He said, "May God do this to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on his shoulders today."

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king had sent a man from his presence, but before the messenger arrived, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this murderer's son has sent to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it shut against him. Is the sound of his master's feet not behind him?"
While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him, and the king said, "This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

Elisha said, "Listen to the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: By this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

The officer on whose arm the king leaned said to the man of God, "Even if the LORD made windows in the sky, could this happen?" He said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
Now there were four men with a skin disease at the entrance of the gate. They said to each other, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

If we say, 'Let us go into the town,' the famine is in the town, and we will die there. And if we stay here, we die too. So now, come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live, and if they kill us, we will only die."
So they got up at dusk to go to the camp of the Arameans. When they came to the edge of the camp, there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the Aramean army hear the sound of chariots and horses, the sound of a great army, and they said to each other, "The king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us."
So they got up and ran away at dusk and abandoned their tents, their horses and their donkeys, leaving the camp as it was, and ran for their lives.

When these men with the skin disease came to the edge of the camp, they went into a tent and ate and drank, and carried off silver, gold and clothing, and went and hid them. Then they came back and went into another tent and carried things off from it, and went and hid them.

Then they said to each other, "What we are doing is not right. Today is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, punishment will catch up with us. Now come, let us go and tell the king's household."

So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the town and told them, "We went to the Aramean camp, and there was no one there, no sound of anyone, just the horses tied up and the donkeys tied up and the tents as they were."
The gatekeepers called out, and it was told inside the king's household.

The king got up in the night and said to his officers, "I will tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country, thinking, 'When they come out of the town, we will take them alive and get into the town.'"

One of his officers answered, "Let some men take five of the horses that are left in the town. They will be like the whole crowd of Israel that is left, or like the whole crowd of Israel that has already died. Let us send them and see."
So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, "Go and see."
They went after them as far as the Jordan, and the whole road was full of clothing and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers went back and told the king.
Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, as the word of the LORD said.
The king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
For when the man of God had said to the king, "Two measures of barley will be sold for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, by this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria,"
the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD made windows in the sky, could such a thing happen?" And he had said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
And that is what happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gateway and he died.

Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, "Get up and go with your household and live as a foreigner wherever you can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will come on the land for seven years."
So the woman got up and did as the man of God had said. She went with her household and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
At the end of the seven years the woman came back from the land of the Philistines, and she went to appeal to the king for her house and her land.
The king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and saying, "Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done."

While he was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead to life, the woman whose son he had brought back to life came to appeal to the king for her house and her land. Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha brought back to life."

When the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed an official for her and said, "Give back everything that was hers, with all the income from her fields from the day she left the land until now."
Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-hadad king of Aram was ill, and it was told to him, "The man of God has come here."
The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go to meet the man of God, and ask the LORD through him: 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

So Hazael went to meet him, taking a gift with him, all kinds of the good things of Damascus, forty camel loads. He came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"
Elisha said to him, "Go and say to him, 'You will certainly recover.' But the LORD has shown me that he will certainly die."
He fixed his gaze and stared at him until he was ashamed. Then the man of God wept.
