Hazael said, "Why does my lord weep?" He answered, "Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites. You will set fire to their fortresses, and kill their young men with the sword, and smash their little children and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael said, "What is your servant, a mere dog, that he should do this great thing?" Elisha answered, "The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram."
Then he left Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He answered, "He told me that you would certainly recover."
But the next day he took the blanket and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, became king.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married a daughter of Ahab. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of his servant David, since he had promised to give him a lamp for ever, for his descendants.
In his days Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of their own.
Then Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He got up by night and struck down the Edomites who had surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but his army ran away home.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled at the same time.
The rest of the acts of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Joram lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.
He also walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab did, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

King Joram went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.
The prophet Elisha called one of the company of the prophets and said to him, "Tie up your clothes, take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in and have him get up from among his companions, and take him to an inner room.
Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run. Do not wait."
So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together. He said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu said, "For which of us?" He said, "For you, commander."
Jehu got up and went into the house. The young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I anoint you king over the LORD's people, over Israel.
You are to strike down the house of Ahab your master, so that I may take revenge on Jezebel for the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the LORD's servants.
The whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male, slave and free, in Israel.
I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
The dogs will eat Jezebel in the plot of Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then he opened the door and ran.
When Jehu came out to the officers of his master, one said to him, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" He said to them, "You know the man and what he says."
They said, "That is a lie. Tell us." He said, "This is what he said to me: 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
Then they quickly took their cloaks and spread them under him on the bare steps, and blew the trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king."
So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, plotted against Joram. (Joram and all Israel had been defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,

but King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had given him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram.) Jehu said, "If this is how you feel, do not let anyone slip out of the town to go and tell the news in Jezreel."
Then Jehu got into his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there. Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's company coming and said, "I see a company." Joram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him ask, 'Is it peace?'"

So the horseman went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."
Then he sent a second horseman, who came to them and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me."
The watchman reported, "He reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman."

Joram said, "Harness the horses." They harnessed his chariot, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his chariot, to meet Jehu, and met him on the plot of land that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answered, "What peace can there be, as long as the prostitution and the witchcraft of your mother Jezebel go on?"
Joram turned his chariot and fled, calling to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah."
Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and shot Joram between the shoulders, and the arrow went through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him on the plot of Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember, when you and I were riding side by side behind his father Ahab, how the LORD spoke this word against him:

'As surely as I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, declares the LORD, I will repay you on this plot.' Now pick him up and throw him on the plot, as the word of the LORD said."

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu chased him and said, "Shoot him too." They shot him in the chariot at the ascent of Gur, by Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants took him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the city of David.
In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it. She painted her eyes and arranged her hair and looked out of a window.
As Jehu came in at the gate, she said, "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"
He looked up at the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three officials looked down at him.
He said, "Throw her down." So they threw her down, and some of her blood splashed on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
Then he went in and ate and drank. He said, "Take care of this cursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet and the palms of her hands.
They came back and told him, and he said, "This is the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the plot of Jezreel the dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel,
and the body of Jezebel will be like dung on the surface of the field in the plot of Jezreel, so that no one can say, This is Jezebel.'"
Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders and to the guardians of Ahab's sons, saying,
"Now as soon as this letter comes to you, since your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a fortified town and weapons,
choose the best and most suitable of your master's sons and put him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
But they were very afraid and said, "Look, two kings could not stand against him. How can we?"

So the man in charge of the palace and the man in charge of the town, with the elders and the guardians, sent word to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do all you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think is good."

Then he wrote them a second letter: "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." The king's sons, seventy of them, were with the leading men of the town, who were bringing them up.
When the letter came to them, they took the king's sons and killed them, seventy people, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
A messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He said, "Put them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
In the morning he went out and stood and said to all the people, "You are innocent. I plotted against my master and killed him, but who killed all these?
So know that not one word of the LORD that the LORD spoke against the house of Ahab will fall to the ground. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah."
So Jehu killed all who were left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his leading men, his close friends and his priests, until he had left no survivor.
Then he set out and went to Samaria. On the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are relatives of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
He said, "Take them alive." They took them alive and killed them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men. He left none of them.

When he left there, he met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said, "Is your heart as true to my heart as mine is to yours?" Jehonadab answered, "It is." Jehu said, "If it is, give me your hand." So he gave him his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot with him.
He said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So he had him ride in his chariot.
When he came to Samaria, he killed all who were left of Ahab's family in Samaria, until he had wiped them out, as the word of the LORD said to Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him much.

Now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshippers and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to offer to Baal. Anyone who is missing will not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning, in order to destroy the worshippers of Baal.
Jehu said, "Call a sacred assembly for Baal." And they called it.

Jehu sent word throughout Israel, and all the worshippers of Baal came, so that there was no one left who did not come. They went into the temple of Baal, and the temple of Baal was filled from one end to the other.
He said to the man in charge of the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for all the worshippers of Baal." So he brought out robes for them.

Then Jehu went into the temple of Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab, and said to the worshippers of Baal, "Look carefully and make sure that there is no servant of the LORD here with you, only worshippers of Baal."

Then they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, "If any of the men I put in your hands escapes, the one who lets him go will pay with his own life."

As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards and officers, "Go in and strike them down. Let no one escape." The guards and officers struck them down with the sword and threw them out, and went into the inner room of the temple of Baal.
They brought out the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal and burned it.
They smashed the sacred pillar of Baal and smashed the temple of Baal and made it a latrine, as it is to this day.
So Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.
But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit: the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab all that was in my heart, your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."
But Jehu was not careful to follow the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, which he made Israel commit.
In those days the LORD began to cut off parts of Israel. Hazael struck them throughout the territory of Israel,
from the Jordan eastwards, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer by the Wadi Arnon, that is, Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of the acts of Jehu and all that he did, and all his power, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Jehu lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became king in his place.
The time that Jehu ruled over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she got up and destroyed all the royal family.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being killed, and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not killed.
He stayed with her six years, hidden in the house of the LORD, while Athaliah ruled over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the captains of the Carites and of the guards and brought them to him in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and showed them the king's son.
He commanded them, "This is what you are to do: one third of you, those who come on duty on the sabbath, will guard the king's house,
one third will be at the Sur Gate, and one third at the gate behind the guards. You will guard the palace and keep watch.
The two divisions of you who go off duty on the sabbath will guard the house of the LORD for the king.
You will surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes near the ranks must be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."

The captains did all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those who were to come on duty on the sabbath and those who were to go off duty on the sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the captains the spears and shields that had belonged to King David and were in the house of the LORD.
The guards stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, round the altar and the house, for the king.
Then he brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the testimony. They made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king."
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she went to the people in the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there was the king, standing by the pillar, as was the custom, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason. Treason."

Then Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains who were over the army, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest said, "She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
So they seized her, and she went by the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they would be the LORD's people, and also between the king and the people.

Then all the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed his altars and his images to pieces, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. The priest posted guards over the house of the LORD.

He took the captains, the Carites, the guards and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD, and came by way of the gate of the guards to the king's house. And he took his seat on the throne of the kings.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the town was quiet, for Athaliah had been put to death with the sword at the king's house.
Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he ruled for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Even so, the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money from the holy gifts that is brought into the house of the LORD, the money from those who are counted, the money set for each person, and all the money that anyone freely chooses to bring into the house of the LORD,
let the priests take it, each from his own supporter, and let them repair the damage to the house wherever any is found."
But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.

So King Jehoash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? Now take no more money from your supporters, but hand it over for the repair of the house."
So the priests agreed that they would take no more money from the people and would not repair the house themselves.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar, on the right as one enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
Whenever they saw that there was a lot of money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest came up and bagged and counted the money that was found in the house of the LORD.
They would give the weighed money to those in charge of the work who supervised the house of the LORD. They paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,
and to the masons and stonecutters, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and for all that was spent on the repairs.
But no silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets or any gold or silver vessels were made for the house of the LORD from the money brought into the house of the LORD,
for it was given to those who did the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
They did not ask for an account from those into whose hands they gave the money to pay the workers, because they acted honestly.
The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD. It belonged to the priests.
At that time Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy gifts that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy gifts, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then he went away from Jerusalem.
The rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
His servants got up and plotted and struck down Joash at the house of the Millo, on the road down to Silla.

It was Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit. He did not turn away from them.
The anger of the LORD blazed against Israel, and he kept handing them over to Hazael king of Aram and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael.
Then Jehoahaz sought the favour of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw how the king of Aram oppressed Israel.
So the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the power of Aram, and the Israelites lived in their homes as before.
But they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, which he made Israel commit, but walked in them. The Asherah pole also remained standing in Samaria.
For nothing was left of Jehoahaz's army except fifty horsemen, ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz and all that he did, and his power, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Jehoahaz lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria, and his son Joash became king in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for sixteen years.
He also did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit, but walked in them.
The rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, and the power with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Joash lay down with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now when Elisha was suffering from the illness of which he was to die, Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over him, crying, "My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen."
Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." He put his hand on it, and Elisha put his hands on the king's hands.

He said, "Open the window to the east." He opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot." He shot. Then he said, "The LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram. You will strike down the Arameans at Aphek until you have finished them."
He said, "Take the arrows." He took them. He said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." He struck it three times and stopped.

The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times. Then you would have struck down Aram until you had finished it. But now you will strike down Aram only three times."
Elisha died, and they buried him. Now bands of Moabite raiders used to come into the land every spring.
Once, as some men were burying a man, they saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into Elisha's grave. When the man touched the bones of Elisha, he came back to life and stood on his feet.
Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them, and turned to them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and he was not willing to destroy them or to throw them out from his presence, even until now.
When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the towns that he had taken in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated him, and recovered the towns of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his ancestor David. He did everything as his father Joash had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he put to death the servants who had killed the king his father.

But he did not put to death the children of the killers, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Parents are not to be put to death for their children, or children for their parents. Each person is to die for his own sin."
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle, and named it Joktheel, which is its name to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us meet face to face."

Jehoash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' Then a wild animal of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You have struck down Edom, and your heart has made you proud. Enjoy your glory, and stay at home. Why ask for trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah met face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was beaten by Israel, and every man ran home.

Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. Then he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages as well, and went back to Samaria.
The rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did, and his power, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Jehoash lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam became king in his place.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
They plotted against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They brought him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
All the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, became king in Samaria, and he ruled for forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, as the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, said, which he spoke through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
For the LORD saw that the suffering of Israel was very bitter, for there was no one left, slave or free, and no one to help Israel.
But the LORD had not said that he would wipe out the name of Israel from under heaven, so he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

The rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did, and his power, how he fought, and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel, which had belonged to Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Jeroboam lay down with his ancestors, the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah became king in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, became king.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Amaziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
The LORD struck the king, so that he had a skin disease until the day he died, and he lived in a separate house. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Azariah lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David, and his son Jotham became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for six months.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit.
Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against him and struck him down in front of the people and killed him and became king in his place.
The rest of the acts of Zechariah are written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel.
(This was the word of the LORD that he spoke to Jehu: "Your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel." And so it happened.)
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he ruled for one month in Samaria.
Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him and became king in his place.
The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the plot that he made, are written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel.

At that time Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territory from Tirzah onwards, because they would not open to him. He attacked it, and he ripped open all the pregnant women in it.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and he ruled for ten years in Samaria.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. All his days he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver to help him strengthen his hold on the kingdom.
Menahem raised the money from Israel, from all the wealthy, fifty shekels of silver from each one, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria went back and did not stay in the land.
The rest of the acts of Menahem and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Menahem lay down with his ancestors, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for two years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, plotted against him, and with fifty men of Gilead he struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house, along with Argob and Arieh. He killed him and became king in his place.
The rest of the acts of Pekahiah and all that he did, are written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for twenty years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel commit.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh and Hazor, Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he carried the people off to Assyria.
Then Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah son of Remaliah and struck him down and killed him and became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The rest of the acts of Pekah and all that he did, are written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Uzziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.
The rest of the acts of Jotham and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of his ancestor David, and his son Ahaz became king in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, became king.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as his ancestor David had done,
but walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to make war on Jerusalem, and they besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
At that time the king of Edom recovered Elath for Edom, and drove the men of Judah out of Elath, and the Edomites came to Elath and have lived there to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are attacking me."
Ahaz also took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house and sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria went up against Damascus and captured it, and carried its people off to Kir, and killed Rezin.

When King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, he saw the altar that was in Damascus. King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest a drawing of the altar and a plan of it, with all its details.
Uriah the priest built an altar, following all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. Uriah the priest made it before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
When the king came back from Damascus, the king looked at the altar. Then the king went up to the altar and went up on it
and burned his burnt offering and his grain offering and poured out his drink offering and splashed the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
The bronze altar that stood before the LORD he moved from the front of the house, from between the new altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of the new altar.

King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, "On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, and the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering and their drink offerings. Splash on it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice. But the bronze altar will be for me to consult."
Uriah the priest did all that King Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cut off the frames of the stands and removed the basin from them, and he took the sea down from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone pavement.
He also removed from the house of the LORD the covered way for the sabbath that had been built in the house, and the outer entrance for the king, because of the king of Assyria.
The rest of the acts of Ahaz that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Ahaz lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David, and his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for nine years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria discovered a plot in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and did not send tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year. So the king of Assyria seized him and put him in prison in chains.
Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land and came to Samaria and besieged it for three years.

In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and took the Israelites away to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes.
This happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods
and followed the practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites, and the practices that the kings of Israel had introduced.
The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built high places for themselves in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified town.
They set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree,
and there on all the high places they burned incense, like the nations whom the LORD had driven out before them. They did wicked things that made the LORD angry,
and they served idols, about which the LORD had said to them, "You must not do this."

The LORD warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer: "Turn back from your evil ways and keep my commands and my statutes, in keeping with all the law that I commanded your ancestors and that I sent to you through my servants the prophets."
But they would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who did not trust the LORD their God.

They rejected his statutes and his covenant that he made with their ancestors and the warnings that he gave them. They followed worthless things and became worthless themselves, and followed the nations round them, though the LORD had commanded them not to do as they did.
They abandoned all the commands of the LORD their God and made for themselves two cast calves. They made an Asherah pole and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served Baal.
They made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, and practised divination and omens, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, making him angry.
So the LORD was very angry with Israel and removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah was left.
Judah also did not keep the commands of the LORD their God, but followed the practices that Israel had introduced.
The LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel and afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until he had thrown them out of his presence.
When he had torn Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam drew Israel away from following the LORD and made them commit a great sin.
The Israelites walked in all the sins that Jeroboam committed. They did not turn away from them
until the LORD removed Israel from his presence, as he had said through all his servants the prophets. So Israel was taken from their own land into exile in Assyria, and is there to this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
When they first lived there, they did not fear the LORD, so the LORD sent lions among them, which killed some of them.

The king of Assyria was told, "The nations that you carried off and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know the rules of the god of the land. So he has sent lions among them, and they are killing them, because they do not know the rules of the god of the land."
Then the king of Assyria commanded, "Send back one of the priests whom you took away from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the rules of the god of the land."
So one of the priests whom they had taken away from Samaria came and lived in Bethel and taught them how to fear the LORD.
But each nation still made gods of its own and put them in the shrines on the high places that the people of Samaria had made, each nation in the towns where they lived.
The people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the people of Cuth made Nergal, the people of Hamath made Ashima,
the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They also feared the LORD and appointed from among themselves all kinds of people as priests of the high places, who offered sacrifices for them in the shrines on the high places.
So they feared the LORD, and also served their own gods, following the practices of the nations from which they had been taken.

To this day they follow their former practices. They do not fear the LORD, and they do not keep the statutes or the rules or the law or the command that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
The LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them: "You must not fear other gods or bow down to them or serve them or sacrifice to them.
But you must fear the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm. You must bow down to him and sacrifice to him.
You must always take care to keep the statutes and the rules and the law and the command that he wrote for you. You must not fear other gods.
You must not forget the covenant that I made with you. You must not fear other gods.
But you must fear the LORD your God, and he will rescue you from the hand of all your enemies."
But they did not listen, but followed their former practices.
So these nations feared the LORD and also served their carved images. Their children did the same, and their children's children. As their ancestors did, so they do to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done.

He removed the high places and smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah pole. He also broke into pieces the bronze snake that Moses had made, for until those days the Israelites had been burning incense to it. It was called Nehushtan.
He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah after him, or among those before him.
He held fast to the LORD and did not turn away from following him, but kept the commands that the LORD had given to Moses.
The LORD was with him, and he was successful wherever he went. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and would not serve him.
He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified town.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it,
and at the end of three years he captured it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
The king of Assyria took the Israelites away to Assyria and settled them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes,
because they did not obey the voice of the LORD their God but broke his covenant, all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded. They would neither listen nor obey.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified towns of Judah and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have done wrong. Withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand of me." The king of Assyria demanded of Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house.
At that time Hezekiah stripped off the gold with which he had covered the doors and doorposts of the temple of the LORD and gave it to the king of Assyria.

But the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rabsaris and the Rabshakeh with a large army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem and stood by the channel of the upper pool, which is on the road to the Washerman's Field.
When they called for the king, Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace, and Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.
The Rabshakeh said to them, "Say to Hezekiah: 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence of yours?
Do you think that words alone are strategy and strength for war? Who are you relying on, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are relying on Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which will go into the hand of anyone who leans on it and pierce it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who rely on him.

But if you say to me, "We rely on the LORD our God," is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem"?
Now make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you can put riders on them.
How can you turn back even one officer among the least of my master's servants, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
And did I come up against this place to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, and Shebna and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people on the wall."

But the Rabshakeh said to them, "Did my master send me to say these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?"
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah: "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
This is what the king says: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot rescue you from my hand.
Do not let Hezekiah make you rely on the LORD by saying, "The LORD will certainly rescue us, and this town will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."'

Do not listen to Hezekiah. For this is what the king of Assyria says: 'Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree and drink water from his own cistern,

until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, so that you may live and not die. But do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, "The LORD will rescue us."
Has any of the gods of the nations ever rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?'"
But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace, and Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the palace, and Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to bring them out.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. So pray for the remnant that is left.'"
When the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have insulted me.
Look, I will put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and go back to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
The Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
Now the king heard it said about Tirhakah king of Cush, "He has set out to fight against you." So he sent messengers to Hezekiah again, saying,
"This is what you are to say to Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let your God, on whom you rely, deceive you by saying,"Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."
You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations rescue them, the nations that my ancestors destroyed: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Tel-assar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the town of Sepharvaim, of Hena or of Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Turn your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to mock the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,
and have thrown their gods into the fire, for they were not gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone. So they destroyed them.
Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, LORD, are God alone."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria.
This is the word that the LORD has spoken against him:
The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you mocked and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes so high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

Through your messengers you have mocked the Lord. You have said, 'With my many chariots I have gone up the heights of the mountains, to the far reaches of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, its finest cypresses. I have reached its farthest lodging, its thickest forest.
I dug wells and drank foreign water, and with the soles of my feet I dried up all the streams of Egypt.'
Have you not heard? Long ago I did it. In days of old I planned it, and now I have brought it about, that you should turn fortified towns into heaps of ruins.
Their people had little strength. They were dismayed and ashamed. They were like plants in the field, like green grass, like grass on the roofs, scorched before it grows up.
I know where you sit, and when you go out and come in, and how you rage against me.
Because you rage against me, and your arrogance has come to my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will make you go back by the road you came on.

This will be the sign for you: this year you will eat what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs up from that. But in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root downwards and bear fruit upwards.
For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD will do this.
So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not come into this town or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
He will go back by the way he came, and he will not come into this town, declares the LORD.
I will defend this town and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
That night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up early in the morning, there were all the dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria left and went back and stayed at Nineveh.

One day, as he was worshipping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.

In those days Hezekiah became ill and was close to death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: Put your house in order, for you will die. You will not recover."
Then he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD:
"Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Before Isaiah had left the middle court, the word of the LORD came to him:

"Go back and say to Hezekiah, the leader of my people: This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Look, I will heal you. On the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD.
I will add fifteen years to your life. I will rescue you and this town from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this town for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
Isaiah said, "Bring a cake of figs." They brought it and put it on the boil, and he recovered.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
Isaiah said, "This will be the sign for you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he has said: Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?"
Hezekiah said, "It is easy for the shadow to lengthen by ten steps. No, let the shadow go back ten steps."
The prophet Isaiah called on the LORD, and he made the shadow go back the ten steps that it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz.
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.

Hezekiah welcomed them, and showed them all his treasury, the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his whole armoury and everything found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and where did they come from?" Hezekiah said, "They came from a far country, from Babylon."
He said, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah answered, "They saw everything in my palace. There is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:
The days are coming when everything in your palace, and all that your ancestors have stored up until today, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
Some of your own descendants, who come from you, whom you father, will be taken away, and they will be officials in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "Why not, if there will be peace and security in my days?"
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and all his power, and how he made the pool and the channel and brought water into the town, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and his son Manasseh became king in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed, and set up altars for Baal and made an Asherah pole, as Ahab king of Israel had done, and he bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will put my name."
He built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
He made his son pass through the fire and practised soothsaying and divination and dealt with mediums and spirit-consulters. He did great evil in the eyes of the LORD, making him angry.

He put the carved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which the LORD had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever.

I will not again make the feet of the Israelites wander from the land that I gave to their ancestors, if only they take care to do all that I have commanded them, and all the law that my servant Moses commanded them."
But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
The LORD spoke through his servants the prophets:
"Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these detestable things, and has done more evil than all that the Amorites did before him, and has made Judah sin with his idols,
this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am bringing such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.
I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
I will abandon the remnant of my inheritance and hand them over to their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil for all their enemies,
because they have done what is evil in my eyes and have made me angry from the day their ancestors came out of Egypt until today."

Manasseh also shed a great deal of innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to the other, besides the sin that he made Judah commit, so that they did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh and all that he did, and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Manasseh lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the garden of his house, the garden of Uzza, and his son Amon became king in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done.
He walked in all the way that his father had walked, and served the idols that his father had served and bowed down to them.
He abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.
The servants of Amon plotted against him and killed the king in his palace.
But the people of the land struck down all those who had plotted against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
The rest of the acts of Amon that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah became king in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in all the way of his ancestor David, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the secretary, to the house of the LORD with this order:
"Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and have him count the money that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have collected from the people.
Let it be handed to those in charge of the work, who supervise the house of the LORD, and let them pay it to the workers who are at the house of the LORD, repairing the damage to the house,
that is, to the carpenters, the builders and the masons, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the house.
But no account is to be asked of them for the money that is handed to them, for they act honestly."
Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

Shaphan the secretary came to the king and reported to the king, "Your servants have poured out the money that was found in the house and have handed it to those in charge of the work, who supervise the house of the LORD."
Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it in the presence of the king.
When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.
The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go and ask the LORD for me, and for the people and for all Judah, about the words of this book that has been found. For great is the anger of the LORD that has been kindled against us, because our ancestors did not listen to the words of this book and do all that is written about us."

So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophet, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter, and they spoke with her.
She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me:
This is what the LORD says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and on those who live here, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read.
Because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, to make me angry with all the work of their hands, my anger will be kindled against this place, and it will not be put out.
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask the LORD, say this: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: As for the words that you have heard,

because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and those who live here, that they would become a desolation and a curse, and because you tore your clothes and wept before me, I have heard you, declares the LORD.

So I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am going to bring on this place." They took the word back to the king.
Then the king sent word, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem were gathered to him.

The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him all the men of Judah and all who lived in Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets, and all the people, small and great. He read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD, to follow the LORD and to keep his commands, his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, and to carry out the words of this covenant that were written in this book. All the people joined in the covenant.

The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and the keepers of the threshold to bring out of the temple of the LORD all the objects that had been made for Baal, for Asherah and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.

He removed the priests of the idols whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the towns of Judah and round Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and the moon and the constellations and all the host of heaven.

He brought the Asherah pole out of the house of the LORD to the Wadi Kidron, outside Jerusalem, and burned it at the Wadi Kidron and ground it to dust and threw the dust on the graves of the common people.
He pulled down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah.

He brought all the priests from the towns of Judah and made unclean the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He pulled down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the Gate of Joshua the governor of the town, which was on the left of the town gate.
The priests of the high places, however, did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but ate unleavened bread among their fellow priests.
He made Topheth unclean, which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one could make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance to the house of the LORD, by the room of the official Nathan-melech, which was in the precincts. And he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

The altars on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king pulled down and smashed to pieces there, and threw the dust into the Wadi Kidron.

The king made unclean the high places that were east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the detestable goddess of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the detestable god of Moab and for Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
He smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah poles and filled their places with human bones.
He also pulled down the altar at Bethel, the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin. He burned the high place and ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah pole.

As Josiah turned, he saw the tombs that were there on the hill. He sent and took the bones out of the tombs and burned them on the altar and made it unclean, as the word of the LORD said, which the man of God had proclaimed, who had foretold these things.

Then he said, "What is that monument that I see?" The men of the town told him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and foretold these things that you have done to the altar at Bethel."
He said, "Leave him alone. Let no one move his bones." So they left his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
Josiah also removed all the shrines of the high places in the towns of Samaria that the kings of Israel had made, making the LORD angry. He did to them just as he had done at Bethel.
He killed on the altars all the priests of the high places who were there, and burned human bones on them. Then he went back to Jerusalem.
The king commanded all the people, "Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant."
No Passover like it had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, or in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.

Josiah also removed the mediums, the spirit-consulters, the household gods, the idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, so as to carry out the words of the law that were written in the book that the priest Hilkiah found in the house of the LORD.
Before him there was no king like him, who turned back to the LORD with all his heart and all his soul and all his strength, in keeping with all the law of Moses. And after him no one like him arose.
Even so, the LORD did not turn from the heat of his great anger, which had been kindled against Judah because of all that Manasseh had done to make him angry.
The LORD said, "I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I removed Israel. I will reject this town that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
The rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the River Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.

His servants carried his body in a chariot from Megiddo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in his father's place.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done.
Pharaoh Neco put him in chains at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he could not rule in Jerusalem, and imposed on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away, and he went to Egypt and died there.

Jehoiakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he taxed the land to pay the money at Pharaoh's command. He collected the silver and gold from the people of the land, from each according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

The LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, as the word of the LORD said, which he had spoken through his servants the prophets.
This came on Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh, and all that he had done,
and also because of the innocent blood that he had shed. He had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
Jehoiakim lay down with his ancestors, and his son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
The king of Egypt did not come out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Wadi of Egypt to the River Euphrates.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father had done.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the town was besieged.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the town while his servants were besieging it,

and Jehoiachin king of Judah gave himself up to the king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his commanders and his officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.

He carried off from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house, and cut up all the gold objects that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had said.
He took into exile all Jerusalem, all the commanders and all the warriors, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and metalworkers. No one was left except the poorest people of the land.
He took Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon. He took the king's mother, the king's wives, his officials and the leading men of the land into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
The king of Babylon also took into exile to Babylon all the seven thousand warriors, and a thousand craftsmen and metalworkers, all of them strong and fit for war.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Jehoiakim had done.
It was because of the anger of the LORD that this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until he threw them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
In the ninth year of his reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem and camped against it and built siege works all round it.
The town was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the town was so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then the town wall was broken through, and all the soldiers fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden, though the Chaldeans were round the town. They went in the direction of the Arabah.
But the Chaldean army chased the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they passed judgement on him.
They killed the sons of Zedekiah in front of his eyes. Then they put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in bronze chains and took him to Babylon.

On the seventh day of the fifth month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the LORD and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every large house he burned down.
The whole Chaldean army that was with the captain of the guard broke down the walls round Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took into exile the rest of the people who were left in the town, and the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the crowd.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest people of the land to be vine-dressers and farmers.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and carried the bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes for incense and all the bronze vessels used in the service of the temple.
The captain of the guard took away the fire pans and the bowls, whatever was of gold or of silver.
As for the two pillars, the one sea and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels was too much to weigh.

One pillar was eighteen cubits high, and it had a bronze capital on top. The capital was three cubits high, with a network and pomegranates all round the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar was like it, with a network.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

From the town he took an officer who had been in command of the soldiers, and five of the king's advisers who were found in the town, and the secretary of the army commander who called up the people of the land, and sixty of the people of the land who were found in the town.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
Over the people who were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as governor.

When all the army commanders and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, with their men.
Gedaliah swore an oath to them and their men: "Do not be afraid of the Chaldean officials. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."

But in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down Gedaliah and killed him, with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, small and great, and the army commanders, got up and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes and ate at the king's table every day of his life.
For his allowance, a regular allowance was given to him by the king, a portion every day, as long as he lived.
Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Rodanim.
