The secretary Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, wrote them down in the presence of the king and the officials and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites, one father's house being taken for Eleazar and one for Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
These were the groups for their service when they came into the house of the LORD, according to the rule laid down for them by their ancestor Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
As for the rest of the descendants of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael. Of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth. Of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah. Of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah. Of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari, from Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri.
From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
From Kish, the sons of Kish: Jerahmeel.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of the Levites by their fathers' houses.

They also cast lots, just as their relatives the descendants of Aaron did, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites, the family of the oldest as well as that of the youngest.

David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service some of the descendants of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with lyres, harps and cymbals. This is the list of those who did the work and of their duty:
From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asharelah, sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.

From Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
From Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman the king's seer, to raise up his horn, according to the promises of God. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the direction of their father for the music in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman were under the direction of the king.
Their number, with their relatives who were trained in singing to the LORD, all of them skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their duties, small and great alike, teacher and student.
The first lot fell to Joseph, of Asaph's sons, the second to Gedaliah, he and his relatives and sons, twelve,
the third to Zaccur, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the fourth to Izri, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the tenth to Shimei, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and relatives, twelve,
the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons and relatives, twelve.
As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: from the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the descendants of Asaph.
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth and Eliehoenai the seventh.
Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh and Peullethai the eighth, for God had blessed him.
His son Shemaiah also had sons, who ruled in their father's house, for they were men of great ability.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed and Elzabad, whose relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also able men.
All these were descendants of Obed-edom, they and their sons and relatives, able men with the strength for the service: sixty-two from Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and relatives, able men, eighteen.
Hosah, of the descendants of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (although he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief),
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third and Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and relatives of Hosah were thirteen.
These divisions of the gatekeepers, by their chief men, had duties like their relatives, serving in the house of the LORD.
They cast lots for each gate, small and great alike, by their fathers' houses.
The lot for the east gate fell to Meshelemiah. Then they cast lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counsellor, and his lot came out for the north gate.
Obed-edom's lot came out for the south, and his sons were given the storehouse.
For Shuppim and Hosah it came out for the west, at the Shalleketh Gate on the upper road. Guard stood beside guard.
There were six each day on the east, four each day on the north, four each day on the south, and two at a time at the storehouse.
For the colonnade on the west there were four on the road and two at the colonnade.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers from the Korahites and the descendants of Merari.
Of the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the holy gifts.
The descendants of Ladan, the Gershonites who belonged to Ladan, the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites and the Uzzielites:
Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was the chief officer in charge of the treasuries.
His relatives from Eliezer were his son Rehabiah, his son Jeshaiah, his son Joram, his son Zichri and his son Shelomoth.

Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy gifts that King David and the heads of the fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army had dedicated.
They dedicated some of the plunder from battles for the upkeep of the house of the LORD.
Also everything that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated, all the holy gifts, were in the care of Shelomith and his relatives.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to work outside for Israel, as officials and judges.
Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, seventeen hundred able men, were in charge of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites, Jeriah was the chief of the Hebronites, by their family records and fathers' houses. (In the fortieth year of David's rule a search was made, and able men among them were found at Jazer in Gilead.)

King David appointed him and his relatives, two thousand seven hundred able men, heads of fathers' houses, to be in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter of God and for the affairs of the king.

This is the list of the Israelites, the heads of fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in everything to do with the divisions that came on and went off duty month by month through the year. Each division had twenty-four thousand.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was over the first division, for the first month, and his division had twenty-four thousand.
He was a descendant of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite was over the division of the second month, and Mikloth was the leader of his division. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief. His division had twenty-four thousand.
This is the Benaiah who was a warrior among the thirty and over the thirty. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the Ephraimites. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer of Anathoth, a Benjaminite. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai of Netophah, of the Zerahites. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah of Pirathon, an Ephraimite. His division had twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai of Netophah, of Othniel. His division had twenty-four thousand.
Over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, Eliezer son of Zichri was the chief officer. For the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah.
For Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel. For Aaron, Zadok.
For Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers. For Issachar, Omri son of Michael.
For Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah. For Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel.
For the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah. For the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah.
For the other half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah. For Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner.
For Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the officers of the tribes of Israel.
David did not count those below twenty years of age, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as many as the stars of heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count but did not finish. Anger came on Israel because of this, and the number was not entered in the records of King David.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was over the king's treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was over the storehouses in the countryside, in the towns, in the villages and in the towers.
Ezri son of Chelub was over those who did the work of the fields, farming the land.
Shimei the Ramathite was over the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was over what the vineyards produced for the wine cellars.
Baal-hanan the Gederite was over the olive and sycamore trees in the lowland, and Joash was over the stores of oil.
Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that grazed in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai was over the herds in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite was over the camels, Jehdeiah the Meronothite was over the donkeys, and Jaziz the Hagrite was over the flocks.
All these were officials in charge of King David's property.
Jonathan, David's uncle, was an adviser, a man of understanding and a scribe. He and Jehiel son of Hachmoni took care of the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king's adviser, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king's army.

David gathered at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel, the officers of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, the officials in charge of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the palace officials, the warriors and all the brave fighting men.

King David rose to his feet and said: "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations to build it.
But God said to me, 'You are not to build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel for ever. For he chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah my father's house, and among my father's sons he was pleased with me and made me king over all Israel.
Of all my sons (for the LORD has given me many sons) he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
He said to me, 'It is your son Solomon who will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish his kingdom for ever if he is firm in keeping my commands and my rules, as he is today.'

So now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, keep and search out all the commands of the LORD your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your descendants after you for ever.

And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you abandon him, he will reject you for ever.
Take care now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house as a sanctuary. Be strong and do it."
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the porch of the temple, its buildings, its storerooms, its upper rooms, its inner rooms and the room for the mercy seat,
and the plans of all that he had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, and all the rooms round it, the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries for the holy gifts,
and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the vessels used in the service of the house of the LORD,
the weight of gold for all the gold vessels for each service, and the weight of silver for all the silver vessels for each service,

the weight of gold for the lampstands and their lamps, the weight of gold for each lampstand and its lamps, and the weight of silver for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand,
the weight of gold for each table for the bread of the Presence, and silver for the silver tables,
and pure gold for the forks, the bowls and the cups, the gold bowls and the weight of each, the silver bowls and the weight of each,
and refined gold for the altar of incense, with its weight, and the plan for the chariot of gold, the cherubim that spread their wings and covered the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
"All this," David said, "was given to me in writing from the hand of the LORD, to make me understand all the details of the plan."

David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and brave, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or abandon you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

Here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God. Every willing person who has skill in any kind of work will be with you for all the work, and the officials and all the people will do whatever you command."
King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great, for the palace is not for a human being but for the LORD God.

With all my strength I have provided for the house of my God: gold for the things of gold, silver for the things of silver, bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron and wood for the things of wood, and onyx and stones to be set, stones for mosaic, all kinds of precious stones and slabs of marble in great amounts.
Besides all that I have provided for the holy house, I now give my own treasure of gold and silver to the house of my God, because of my love for the house of my God:
three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the buildings,
for the things of gold and the things of silver, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who is willing to give himself today to the LORD?"
Then the heads of the fathers' houses, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials over the king's work gave willingly.

For the service of the house of God they gave five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
Anyone who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people rejoiced at their willing giving, for they had given to the LORD with a whole heart. King David also rejoiced greatly.
Then David blessed the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly. David said:
Blessed are you, LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

Yours, LORD, are the greatness and the power, the glory, the victory and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and you are lifted up as head over all.
Riches and honour come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are power and strength, and in your hand is the power to make great and to give strength to all.
Now, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so willingly? For everything comes from you, and we have given you only what is yours.
We are foreigners before you, and strangers, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope of staying.
LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and all of it is yours.

I know, my God, that you test the heart and take pleasure in honesty. With an honest heart I have given all these things willingly, and now I have seen with joy your people who are here giving willingly to you.
LORD, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Israel, keep this for ever in the thoughts and purposes of your people's hearts, and direct their hearts towards you.
Give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep your commands, your testimonies and your statutes, to do all of them, and to build the palace for which I have made provision.

Then David said to the whole assembly, "Now bless the LORD your God." And the whole assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and bowed their heads and bowed down to the LORD and to the king.

The next day they offered sacrifices to the LORD and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in great numbers for all Israel.
They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. They made Solomon son of David king a second time, and anointed him as leader for the LORD, and Zadok as priest.
Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the officials and the warriors, and all the sons of King David as well, pledged their loyalty to King Solomon.
The LORD made Solomon very great in the eyes of all Israel and gave him a royal majesty such as no king before him in Israel had had.
David son of Jesse ruled over all Israel.
The time that he ruled over Israel was forty years. He ruled for seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of years, riches and honour, and his son Solomon became king in his place.
The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, and in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Gad the seer,
with all the details of his rule and his power, and of the events that happened to him and to Israel and to all the kingdoms of the lands.
Solomon son of David was firmly established in his kingdom, for the LORD his God was with him and made him very great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to all the leaders in all Israel, the heads of the fathers' houses.
Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness, was there.
(David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.)
The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was also there, in front of the tabernacle of the LORD. Solomon and the assembly came to it.
Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."
Solomon said to God, "You have shown great and faithful love to my father David, and have made me king in his place.
Now, LORD God, let your word to my father David be fulfilled, for you have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.
Give me now wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this great people of yours?"

God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for possessions, wealth or honour, or for the lives of those who hate you, and did not even ask for long life, but asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself so that you can judge my people over whom I have made you king,
wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you riches, possessions and honour, such as none of the kings before you had, and none after you will have."
So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem. And he ruled over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot towns and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore fig trees in the lowland.
Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue, and the king's traders bought them from Kue at a price.

A chariot imported from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse a hundred and fifty, and they were exported through the king's traders to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
Solomon decided to build a house for the name of the LORD, and a royal palace for himself.
Solomon assigned seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to supervise them.
Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre: "Do for me as you did for my father David, when you sent him cedar to build a house to live in.

I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God and to make it holy to him, for burning fragrant incense before him, for the regular arrangement of the bread of the Presence, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths and the new moons and the appointed festivals of the LORD our God, as ordained for ever in Israel.
The house that I am to build will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
But who can build him a house, since heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain him? Who am I to build a house for him, except as a place to burn offerings before him?

So now send me a man skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, crimson and blue cloth, and trained in engraving, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
Also send me cedar, cypress and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. My servants will work with yours
to prepare a large amount of timber for me, for the house I am to build will be great and wonderful.
I will give your servants, the woodcutters who cut the timber, twenty thousand cors of ground wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine and twenty thousand baths of oil."
Hiram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them."

Hiram also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
I am now sending a skilled man, who has understanding, Huram-abi,

the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, whose father was from Tyre. He is trained to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone and wood, and in purple, blue and crimson cloth and fine linen, and to do any kind of engraving and carry out any design given to him, with your craftsmen and the craftsmen of my lord David your father.
Now let my lord send to his servants the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine that he has promised.
We will cut all the timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you can take it up to Jerusalem."
Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, following the count that his father David had made, and there were a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
He assigned seventy thousand of them to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to be overseers to make the people work.

Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
These are the measurements Solomon laid down for building the house of God. The length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
The porch in front of the main hall was twenty cubits long, the width of the house, and its height was a hundred and twenty. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
He lined the main hall with cypress and covered it with fine gold, and put palm trees and chains on it.
He decorated the house with precious stones. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
He covered the house with gold, its beams, thresholds, walls and doors, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
He made the most holy place. Its length, matching the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits. He covered it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also covered the upper rooms with gold.
In the most holy place he made two cherubim of wood and covered them with gold.

The wings of the cherubim together were twenty cubits long. One wing of the first, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.
One wing of the other cherub, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, also five cubits long, joined the wing of the first cherub.
The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.
He made the curtain of blue, purple and crimson cloth and fine linen, and worked cherubim into it.
In front of the house he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits high, with a capital on top of each, five cubits high.
He made chains like a necklace and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. The one on the south he named Jachin, and the one on the north Boaz.
He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.
Then he made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured it round.
Under it were figures of oxen, ten to a cubit, going all round the sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was set on top of them, and all their hindquarters were towards the middle.
It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held three thousand baths.
He also made ten basins for washing, and put five on the right and five on the left. In them they rinsed what was used for the burnt offering, but the sea was for the priests to wash in.
He made ten gold lampstands as prescribed and put them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
He also made ten tables and put them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. And he made a hundred gold bowls.
He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and covered their doors with bronze.
He put the sea on the south side, towards the south-east corner.
Huram also made the pots, the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of God:
the two pillars, the bowls and the two capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars,
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars.
He made the stands and the basins on the stands,
the one sea and the twelve oxen under it,
and the pots, the shovels, the forks and all the equipment. Huram-abi made all these of polished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made all these things in such great numbers that the weight of the bronze could not be found out.
Solomon also made all the furnishings that were in the house of God: the golden altar and the tables for the bread of the Presence,
the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to burn as prescribed in front of the inner room,
the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of purest gold,
the snuffers, bowls, dishes for incense and fire pans, of pure gold, and the doors of the house, the inner doors to the most holy place and the doors of the main hall, were of gold.

So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the things that his father David had dedicated, the silver, the gold and all the furnishings, and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled in Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the Israelites, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel assembled before the king at the festival in the seventh month.
When all the elders of Israel had come, the Levites lifted the ark.
They brought up the ark and the tent of meeting and all the holy furnishings that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
King Solomon and the whole community of Israel, who had gathered round him before the ark, sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, in the inner room of the house, in the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, so that they covered the ark and its poles.
The poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place in front of the inner room, but they could not be seen from outside. They are there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
When the priests came out of the holy place (for all the priests who were present had made themselves holy, whatever their divisions,

and all the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, dressed in fine linen, stood east of the altar with cymbals, harps and lyres, and with them a hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets,

and the trumpeters and the singers were to sound as one, to praise and give thanks to the LORD), when the sound was raised with trumpets, cymbals and other instruments, in praise of the LORD, "For he is good, for his faithful love lasts for ever," the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
so that the priests could not stand to do their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would live in thick darkness.
I have built you a house to be your home, a place for you to live in for ever."
Then the king turned and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to my father David and has fulfilled it with his hands. He said,

'From the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no town from all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, and I chose no man to be leader over my people Israel.
But I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.'
Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, 'You had it in your heart to build a house for my name, and you did well that it was in your heart.
But you will not build the house. Your son who will be born to you will build the house for my name.'

Now the LORD has kept the word that he spoke. I have taken the place of my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have put the ark there, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with the Israelites."
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court. He stood on it, and then knelt down in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands towards heaven,
and said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and showing faithful love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept for your servant, my father David, what you promised him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled it today.

Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, what you promised him: 'You will never lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons take care how they live, walking in my law as you have walked before me.'
Now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, the word that you spoke to your servant David.
But will God really live with human beings on the earth? Look, heaven, and the highest heaven, cannot contain you. How much less this house that I have built.
Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, LORD my God, and listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying before you,
that your eyes may be open day and night towards this house, the place where you said you would put your name, and that you may listen to the prayer that your servant prays towards this place.
Listen to the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray towards this place. Listen from heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.
If someone wrongs his neighbour and is made to swear an oath, and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this house,
then hear from heaven and act and judge your servants, bringing down the guilty by putting his conduct on his own head, and clearing the innocent by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
When your people Israel are beaten by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back and acknowledge your name and pray and plead before you in this house,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their ancestors.
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray towards this place and acknowledge your name and turn from their sin when you afflict them,

then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, and teach them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.
If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, blight, mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, if their enemies besiege them in the land at their gates, whatever disaster or sickness there is,
whatever prayer or plea is made by anyone or by all your people Israel, each knowing his own pain and his own sorrow and stretching out his hands towards this house,
then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive, and repay each one according to all his ways, since you know his heart (for you alone know the hearts of all human beings),
so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days that they live in the land that you gave to our ancestors.

Also when a foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, comes from a distant land for the sake of your great name and your strong hand and your outstretched arm, and comes and prays towards this house,

hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do all that the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and may know that this house that I have built is called by your name.
When your people go out to battle against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to you towards this town that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
When they sin against you (for there is no one who does not sin) and you are angry with them and hand them over to an enemy, so that they are taken captive to a land far or near,

and they come to their senses in the land where they have been taken captive, and turn back and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

and turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray towards their land, which you gave to their ancestors, the town that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.
Now rise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let your faithful people rejoice in your goodness.
LORD God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember the faithful love promised to David your servant."
When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and burned up the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
The priests could not enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

When all the Israelites saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD on the temple, they knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement and bowed down and gave thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his faithful love lasts for ever."
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites also, with the instruments for the music of the LORD that King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD, "for his faithful love lasts for ever," whenever David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests blew trumpets, and all Israel stood.

Solomon also made holy the middle of the court in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat.
At that time Solomon held the festival for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.
On the eighth day they held a closing assembly, for they had kept the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.
On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad at heart for the good that the LORD had done for David and Solomon and for his people Israel.
So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king's house. All that Solomon had planned to do in the house of the LORD and in his own house he carried out successfully.
Then the LORD appeared to Solomon at night and said to him: "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
When I shut up the sky so that there is no rain, or order locusts to eat up the land, or send a plague among my people,
if my people, who are called by my name, humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn back from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.
For now I have chosen and made this house holy, so that my name may be there for ever. My eyes and my heart will be there at all times.
As for you, if you walk before me as your father David did, doing all that I have commanded you and keeping my statutes and my rules,
then I will establish your royal throne, as I made a covenant with your father David: 'You will never lack a man to rule over Israel.'
But if you turn away and abandon my statutes and my commands that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
then I will pull you up from my land that I have given you, and this house that I have made holy for my name I will throw out of my sight, and I will make it a proverb and a taunt among all peoples.
And this house, which was so high, will be shocking to everyone who passes by, and they will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

Then they will say, 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them. That is why he has brought all this disaster on them.'"
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,
Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him, and settled Israelites in them.
Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and overpowered it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the storage towns that he built in Hamath.
He also built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified towns with walls, gates and bars,

and Baalath, and all Solomon's storage towns, and all the towns for his chariots and the towns for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land under his rule.
All the people who were left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, who were not Israelites,
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed, Solomon raised as forced labour, and so they are to this day.
But Solomon made no slaves of the Israelites for his work. They were his soldiers, his officers, the commanders of his chariots and horsemen.
These were the chief officers of King Solomon, two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.

Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to the house that he had built for her, for he said, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, for the places where the ark of the LORD has come are holy."
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the porch,

as each day required, offering according to the command of Moses for the sabbaths, the new moons and the three annual festivals: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths.

In keeping with the ruling of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties of praise and of serving alongside the priests as each day required, and the gatekeepers in their divisions at each gate, for this was what David the man of God had commanded.
They did not turn aside from the king's command to the priests and Levites in any matter, or about the treasuries.
So all the work of Solomon was carried out, from the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid until it was finished. So the house of the LORD was completed.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth on the shore of the sea, in the land of Edom.

Huram sent him ships and servants who knew the sea, by the hands of his own servants. They went to Ophir with Solomon's servants and brought from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and delivered it to King Solomon.

When the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, she came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions, with a very large retinue, and with camels carrying spices, a great deal of gold and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she told him everything that was on her mind.
Solomon answered all her questions. There was nothing hidden from Solomon that he could not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen Solomon's wisdom and the house he had built,

the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the steps by which he went up to the house of the LORD, she was left breathless.
She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom was true.
But I did not believe their reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. And look, I was not told half of the greatness of your wisdom. You go beyond the report I heard.
How happy your people are, and how happy these servants of yours, who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.

Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for the LORD your God. Because your God loved Israel and would establish them for ever, he made you king over them, to do justice and righteousness."
Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very large amount of spices and precious stones. There were no spices like those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
(The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
The king used the algum wood to make steps for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.)
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted, whatever she asked, more than she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own land with her servants.
The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents,
besides what the traders and merchants brought. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold, with six hundred shekels of beaten gold in each shield.
He also made three hundred smaller shields of beaten gold, with three hundred shekels of gold in each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great ivory throne and covered it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps and a gold footstool attached to the throne, and arms on each side of the seat, with a lion standing beside each arm,
and twelve lions standing there, one at each end of a step on the six steps. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.
All King Solomon's drinking cups were of gold, and all the vessels in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. Silver was thought of no value in the days of Solomon.
For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish came back, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and baboons.
So King Solomon was greater than all the other kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
All the kings of the earth wanted to see Solomon and hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
Each one brought a gift, articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules, year after year.
Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot towns and with the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore fig trees in the lowland.
Horses were imported for Solomon from Egypt and from all lands.

The rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer about Jeroboam son of Nebat?
Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
Solomon lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of his father David, and his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it (he was in Egypt, where he had run away from King Solomon), Jeroboam came back from Egypt.
They sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."
He said to them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.
King Rehoboam took advice from the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was still alive. He said, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
They said to him, "If you are kind to this people and please them and speak kind words to them, then they will be your servants for ever."
But he rejected the advice that the elders gave him and took advice from the young men who had grown up with him and who served him.
He said to them, "What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"

The young men who had grown up with him said to him, "This is what you should say to the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must lighten it for us.' This is what you should say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father loaded you with a heavy yoke, but I will make your yoke heavier. My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions.'"
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said, "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders
and spoke to them as the young men advised: "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will make it heavier. My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people, for the turn of events was from God, so that the LORD might carry out his word that he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
When all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king:
"What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each to your tents, Israel. Now look after your own house, David."
So all Israel went to their tents.
But Rehoboam ruled over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labour, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he gathered the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against Israel and to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam.
But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin,

'This is what the LORD says: You must not go up and fight against your kinsmen. Each of you go back to his home, for this is from me.'" So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built towns for defence in Judah.
He built up Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Soco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, fortified towns in Judah and Benjamin.
He strengthened the fortresses and put commanders in them, with stores of food, oil and wine.
In every town he put shields and spears and made them very strong. So he held Judah and Benjamin.
The priests and the Levites throughout Israel came to him from all their districts.
The Levites left their pasturelands and their property and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had dismissed them from serving as priests of the LORD,
and he had appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat demons and for the calves that he had made.
Those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, followed them to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and for three years made Rehoboam son of Solomon secure, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
Rehoboam married Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and of Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
After her he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines. (He had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and had twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.)
Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, the leader among his brothers, for he planned to make him king.
He acted wisely and spread out some of his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified towns, and gave them plenty of supplies and found many wives for them.
When Rehoboam's rule was established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem
with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. The people who came with him from Egypt were without number: Libyans, Sukkites and Cushites.
He captured the fortified towns of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned me, so I have abandoned you to the hand of Shishak."
The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will give them some deliverance, and my anger will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
But they will become his servants, so that they may know the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem. He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything. He also took away the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and put them in the care of the officers of the guard, who kept watch at the entrance of the king's house.
Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards came and carried them, and then took them back to the guardroom.
Because he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, and he did not destroy him completely. There was also some good in Judah.

So King Rehoboam grew strong in Jerusalem and ruled. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the town that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
He did what was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.

The acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the family records? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah became king in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went into battle with an army of brave warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men. Jeroboam drew up his battle line against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, brave warriors.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel.
Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel for ever to David and his descendants by a covenant of salt?
Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Worthless men gathered round him and stood up against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and timid and could not stand against them.

And now you think you can stand against the kingdom of the LORD in the hands of David's descendants, because you are a great crowd and have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the descendants of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves, like the peoples of other lands? Anyone who comes to be installed with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned him. The priests who serve the LORD are descendants of Aaron, and the Levites do the work.

Every morning and every evening they offer burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD, and set out the bread of the Presence on the pure gold table, and light the lamps of the gold lampstand every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.

Look, God is with us at our head, and his priests with their trumpets to sound the battle cry against you. People of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed."
But Jeroboam had sent an ambush round to come on them from behind. So his troops were in front of Judah and the ambush was behind them.
When Judah turned, there was battle in front and behind. Then they cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
The men of Judah raised the battle cry. And when the men of Judah shouted, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The Israelites ran from Judah, and God handed them over to them.
Abijah and his people struck them with great slaughter, so that five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell dead.
So the Israelites were beaten at that time, and the people of Judah won, because they relied on the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Abijah chased Jeroboam and captured towns from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages and Ephron with its villages.
Jeroboam did not recover his power in the days of Abijah. The LORD struck him down, and he died.
But Abijah grew strong. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his words, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king in his place. In his days the land had peace for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah poles,
and commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to keep the law and the command.
He also removed the high places and the incense altars from all the towns of Judah, and the kingdom had peace under him.
He built fortified towns in Judah, for the land had peace. He had no war in those years, for the LORD gave him rest.

He said to Judah, "Let us build these towns and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, armed with small shields and bows. All these were brave warriors.
Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

Asa called to the LORD his God: "LORD, there is no one but you to help, whether the mighty or the weak. Help us, LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this crowd. LORD, you are our God. Do not let a mere human prevail against you."
So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites ran away.

Asa and the army with him chased them as far as Gerar, and so many Cushites fell that none were left alive, for they were crushed before the LORD and his army. The men of Judah carried off a great amount of plunder.
They struck all the towns round Gerar, for the fear of the LORD had come on them. They plundered all the towns, for there was a great deal of plunder in them.
They also struck down the tents of the herdsmen and carried off sheep in large numbers, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
The spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you when you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without law.
But in their distress they turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him, and he was found by them.
In those times there was no peace for anyone going out or coming in, for there was great confusion among all the people of the lands.
Nation was crushed by nation and town by town, for God threw them into confusion with every kind of trouble.
But you, be strong and do not give up, for your work will be rewarded."

When Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded, he took courage and removed the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns that he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim, and he repaired the altar of the LORD that was in front of the porch of the house of the LORD.

He gathered all Judah and Benjamin and those from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who were living among them, for large numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
On that day they sacrificed to the LORD from the plunder they had brought seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and all their soul,
and that anyone who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death, young or old, man or woman.
They swore an oath to the LORD in a loud voice, with shouting and with trumpets and horns.
All Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart and sought him with their whole desire, and he was found by them. And the LORD gave them rest on every side.
King Asa even removed his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother, because she had made a horrible image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and crushed it and burned it in the Wadi Kidron.
The high places were not removed from Israel. Even so, Asa's heart was wholly true all his days.
He brought into the house of God the gifts that his father and he himself had dedicated, silver, gold and vessels.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built up Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house and sent it to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

"Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the towns of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the storage towns of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building up Ramah and let his work stop.
Then King Asa brought all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building. With them he built up Geba and Mizpah.

At that time the seer Hanani came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
Were the Cushites and the Libyans not a huge army, with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, he handed them over to you.
For the eyes of the LORD move to and fro throughout the whole earth, to strengthen those whose heart is wholly his. You have acted foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars."
Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks in prison, for he was in a rage with him over this. At the same time Asa crushed some of the people.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet, and his disease was severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.
Asa lay down with his ancestors and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in the tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a bed that was filled with spices and various kinds of perfumes, prepared by the perfumers' art, and they made a very great fire in his honour.
His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.
He put troops in all the fortified towns of Judah and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the towns of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his ancestor David. He did not seek the Baals,
but sought the God of his father and walked in his commands, and not in the ways of Israel.
So the LORD made the kingdom firm in his hand, and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had great riches and honour.
His heart was bold in the ways of the LORD. He also removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah to teach in the towns of Judah,
and with them the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
They taught in Judah, with the Book of the Law of the LORD with them. They went round through all the towns of Judah and taught the people.
The fear of the LORD came on all the kingdoms of the lands round Judah, and they did not make war on Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabs also brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
Jehoshaphat grew steadily greater. He built fortresses and storage towns in Judah,
and had large supplies in the towns of Judah. He had soldiers, brave warriors, in Jerusalem.
This was the count of them by their fathers' houses. From Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, with three hundred thousand brave warriors,
and next to him Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred and eighty thousand,
and next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered for the service of the LORD, with two hundred thousand brave warriors.
From Benjamin: Eliada, a brave warrior, with two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield,
and next to him Jehozabad with a hundred and eighty thousand armed for war.
These served the king, besides those whom the king had put in the fortified towns throughout Judah.
Jehoshaphat had great riches and honour, and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
Some years later he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab killed a great number of sheep and oxen for him and for the people with him, and urged him to attack Ramoth-gilead.
Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me against Ramoth-gilead?" He answered, "I am as you are, and my people as your people. We will be with you in the war."
Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "First, please ask for the word of the LORD."

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to fight against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" They said, "Go up, for God will hand it over to the king."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no other prophet of the LORD here, that we may ask through him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can ask the LORD, Micaiah son of Imla. But I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only bad." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla at once."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself horns of iron and said, "This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore the Arameans until they are finished."
All the prophets prophesied the same: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and win, for the LORD will hand it over to the king."
The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the words of the prophets are all one in favour of the king. Let your word be like theirs, and speak favourably."
But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, I will speak what my God says."
When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to fight at Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" He answered, "Go up and win. They will be handed over to you."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
Then he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, 'These have no master. Let each go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good about me, only bad?"
Micaiah said, "Then hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.
The LORD said, 'Who will persuade Ahab king of Israel to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and another said another.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will persuade him.' The LORD said to him, 'How?'
He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' He said, 'You will persuade him, and you will succeed. Go out and do it.'
So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours. The LORD has declared disaster against you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the spirit of the LORD go when it left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "You will see on the day when you go into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the governor of the town and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and feed him only a little bread and a little water until I come back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you ever come back safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." And he said, "Listen, all you peoples."
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
Now the king of Aram had ordered the commanders of his chariots, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel alone."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "It must be the king of Israel." So they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.
For when the chariot commanders saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from chasing him.
But someone drew his bow without aim and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armour. So he said to his chariot driver, "Turn round and take me out of the fighting, for I am wounded."
The battle grew fierce that day, and the king of Israel was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset he died.
Jehoshaphat king of Judah came back safely to his house in Jerusalem.
But Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this the anger of the LORD is on you.
Yet some good is found in you, for you have removed the Asherah poles from the land and have set your heart to seek God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified towns of Judah, town by town,
and said to the judges, "Consider what you do, for you are not judging for human beings but for the LORD, who is with you when you give judgement.
Now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Be careful what you do, for there is no injustice with the LORD our God, no partiality and no taking of bribes."
In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat also appointed some of the Levites and priests and heads of the families of Israel to give judgement for the LORD and to settle disputes. They lived in Jerusalem.
He commanded them: "This is how you are to act, in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and with a whole heart.

Whenever a case comes to you from your relatives who live in their towns, whether bloodshed, or law and command, statutes and rules, you must warn them, so that they do not become guilty before the LORD and his anger does not come on you and your relatives. Do this and you will not be guilty.

Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the governor of the house of Judah, in all matters of the king. The Levites will serve as officers before you. Act with courage, and may the LORD be with those who do good."
After this the Moabites and Ammonites, and with them some of the Meunites, came to make war on Jehoshaphat.
Some people came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great crowd is coming against you from Edom, from beyond the sea. They are already at Hazazon-tamar" (that is, En-gedi).
Jehoshaphat was afraid and set his face to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
Judah gathered to ask help from the LORD. From all the towns of Judah they came to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of the LORD, in front of the new court,
and said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, are you not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and strength are in your hand, and no one can stand against you.
Did you not, our God, drive out the people who lived in this land before your people Israel, and give it for ever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
They have lived in it and have built in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,

'If disaster comes on us, the sword, judgement, plague or famine, we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is in this house, and cry out to you in our trouble, and you will hear and save.'
Now the people of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you did not allow Israel to invade when they came from the land of Egypt, but they turned away from them and did not destroy them,
see how they repay us by coming to drive us out of your possession, which you gave us as an inheritance.
