Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no power against this great crowd that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
All Judah stood there before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives and their children.
Then the spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the descendants of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly.

He said, "Listen, all Judah and you who live in Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat. This is what the LORD says to you: Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this great crowd, for the battle is not yours but God's.
Tomorrow go down against them. They will come up by the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, east of the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Take your positions, stand still and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out against them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you."
Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and those who lived in Jerusalem fell down before the LORD and worshipped the LORD.
The Levites, from the Kohathites and the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

They got up early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and you who live in Jerusalem. Trust in the LORD your God and you will stand firm. Trust in his prophets and you will succeed."

When he had consulted the people, he appointed singers to the LORD to praise him in holy splendour as they went out in front of the army, saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for his faithful love lasts for ever."
As they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.

For the people of Ammon and Moab rose up against those who lived on Mount Seir, devoting them to destruction and wiping them out, and when they had finished with those who lived in Seir, they helped to destroy one another.
When Judah came to the watchtower in the wilderness and looked towards the crowd, there were dead bodies lying on the ground. No one had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and his people came to take the plunder, and found among them a great deal of cattle, goods, clothing and precious things, which they took for themselves until they could carry no more. It took three days to collect the plunder, there was so much.
On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD. So that place has been called the Valley of Beracah to this day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, went back to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They came to Jerusalem and the house of the LORD with harps, lyres and trumpets.
The fear of God came on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
So Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.
So Jehoshaphat ruled over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
But the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
He joined with him to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.

Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, the LORD will wreck what you have made." And the ships were wrecked and could not go to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David, and his son Jehoram became king in his place.
He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Their father gave them great gifts of silver, gold and valuable things, with fortified towns in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
When Jehoram had taken over his father's kingdom and was firmly in power, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the leaders of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married a daughter of Ahab. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants for ever.
In his days Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of their own.
Then Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. He got up by night and struck down the Edomites who had surrounded him and his chariot commanders.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled against his rule at the same time, because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He also made high places in the hill country of Judah, and led the people of Jerusalem into prostitution and made Judah go astray.

A letter came to him from the prophet Elijah: "This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem into prostitution, as the house of Ahab led Israel into prostitution, and you have also killed your brothers, your own father's house, who were better than you,
now the LORD is about to strike your people, your children, your wives and all your possessions with a great plague,
and you yourself will have a severe illness, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day by day."
The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who live near the Cushites.
They came up against Judah and invaded it and carried off all the goods they found in the king's palace, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest.
After all this the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire in his honour, as they had for his ancestors.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for eight years in Jerusalem. He died with no one's regret. They buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The people of Jerusalem made his youngest son Ahaziah king in his place, for the raiding band that had come with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother advised him to act wickedly.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they were his advisers, to his ruin.
He also followed their advice and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. The Arameans wounded Joram,

and he went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds he had received at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.

But it was from God that Ahaziah's downfall came about through his visit to Joram. For when he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.
While Jehu was carrying out judgement on the house of Ahab, he found the leaders of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's relatives who were serving Ahaziah, and killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him as he was hiding in Samaria, and brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, "He was the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So the house of Ahaziah had no one able to rule the kingdom.
When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she got up and destroyed all the royal family of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being killed, and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and wife of the priest Jehoiada, because she was Ahaziah's sister, hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not kill him.
He stayed with them six years, hidden in the house of God, while Athaliah ruled over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
They went through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah, and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
The whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son. He must rule, as the LORD promised about David's descendants.
This is what you are to do: one third of you priests and Levites who come on duty on the sabbath are to be gatekeepers,
one third at the king's house and one third at the Foundation Gate, and all the people will be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
No one may enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who serve. They may enter, for they are holy, but all the people are to keep the charge of the LORD.
The Levites will surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who enters the house must be put to death. Stay with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

The Levites and all Judah did all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those who were to come on duty on the sabbath and those who were to go off duty on the sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had not released the divisions.
Jehoiada the priest gave the captains the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and were in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, round the altar and the house, to guard the king.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the testimony. They made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they shouted, "Long live the king."
When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with musical instruments leading the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason. Treason."

Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains who were over the army and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
So they seized her, and she went to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house, and there they put her to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king that they would be the LORD's people.
Then all the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed his altars and his images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.

Jehoiada put the care of the house of the LORD under the priests and the Levites, whom David had organised in the house of the LORD, to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, as written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and singing, as David had ordered.
He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any way could enter.

He took the captains, the nobles, the rulers of the people and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the house of the LORD, and they came through the Upper Gate to the king's house. They seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the town was quiet, for Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he ruled for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of the priest Jehoiada.
Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
After this Joash decided to restore the house of the LORD.

He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel to repair the house of your God year by year, and do it quickly." But the Levites did not hurry.

So the king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax that Moses the servant of the LORD laid on the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?"
For the sons of that wicked Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had used even the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
So the king commanded, and they made a chest and put it outside the gate of the house of the LORD.
A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God had laid on Israel in the wilderness.
All the leaders and all the people rejoiced and brought their tax and dropped it into the chest until it was full.

Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king's officials, and they saw that there was a lot of money, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest and take it and put it back in its place. They did this day after day and collected a great deal of money.

The king and Jehoiada gave it to those who were in charge of the work on the house of the LORD, and they hired masons and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
So those who did the work laboured, and the repairs went ahead in their hands, and they restored the house of God to its proper condition and made it strong.

When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made vessels for the house of the LORD, for the service and for the burnt offerings, and dishes for incense and vessels of gold and silver. They offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.
But Jehoiada grew old and full of years, and died. He was a hundred and thirty years old when he died.
They buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, and for God and his house.
After the death of Jehoiada the leaders of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to them.
They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Anger came on Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt of theirs.
Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. They testified against them, but they would not listen.

Then the spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: Why do you break the commands of the LORD, so that you cannot succeed? Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you."
But they plotted against him, and by order of the king they stoned him to death in the court of the house of the LORD.
So King Joash did not remember the faithful love that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him, but killed his son. As he was dying, he said, "May the LORD see and take revenge."

At the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against Joash. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people from among the people, and sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.

Although the Aramean army had come with few men, the LORD handed over to them a very large army, because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So they carried out judgement on Joash.

When they had left him, severely wounded, his own servants plotted against him because of the blood of the son of the priest Jehoiada, and killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
Those who plotted against him were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
The accounts of his sons, the many prophecies against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. His son Amaziah became king in his place.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not with a whole heart.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he put to death the servants who had killed the king his father.

But he did not put their children to death, as it is written in the law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Parents are not to die for their children, or children for their parents. Each person is to die for his own sin."

Amaziah gathered the people of Judah and set them by fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and of hundreds for all Judah and Benjamin. He counted those twenty years old and over and found that there were three hundred thousand chosen men fit for war, who could handle spear and shield.
He also hired a hundred thousand brave warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "King, do not let the army of Israel march with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with all these Ephraimites.
Go yourself, act, and be strong in battle. But God will bring you down before the enemy, for God has power to help and to bring down."
Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what about the hundred talents that I have given to the army of Israel?" The man of God answered, "The LORD can give you much more than this."
So Amaziah dismissed the army that had come to him from Ephraim, to go home. They were very angry with Judah and went home in a great rage.
But Amaziah took courage and led out his people and went to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand men of Seir.
The men of Judah also captured ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of a cliff and threw them down from the top of the cliff, so that they were all smashed to pieces.

But the soldiers whom Amaziah had sent back, not letting them go with him to battle, raided the towns of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon, and struck down three thousand people in them and took a great deal of plunder.
When Amaziah came back from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods, and bowed down to them and burned incense to them.
The LORD was angry with Amaziah and sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you looked to the gods of a people who could not save their own people from your hand?"

While he was still speaking, the king said to him, "Have we made you the king's adviser? Stop. Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but said, "I know that God has decided to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my advice."
Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice and sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let us meet face to face."

Joash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' Then a wild animal of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You say, 'Look, I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has made you proud and boastful. But now stay at home. Why ask for trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen, for it was from God, so that he might hand them over to their enemies, because they had looked to the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah met face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was beaten by Israel, and every man ran home.

Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages as well, and went back to Samaria.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?
From the time that Amaziah turned away from the LORD, they plotted against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They brought him back on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.
All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Amaziah had done.
He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who taught him the fear of God, and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.

He went out and made war against the Philistines and broke down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he built towns in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal and against the Meunites.
The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
Uzziah also built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and fortified them.

He built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had large herds, both in the lowland and on the plain, and he had farmers and vine-dressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

Uzziah had an army of fighting men in divisions, according to the number in the list made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The total number of the heads of fathers' houses, brave warriors, was two thousand six hundred.
Under their command was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, who could make war with great strength, to help the king against the enemy.
Uzziah supplied the whole army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of armour, bows and sling stones.
In Jerusalem he made machines, designed by skilled men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. His fame spread far, for he was wonderfully helped until he was strong.
But when he was strong, his heart became proud, to his ruin. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
The priest Azariah went in after him with eighty priests of the LORD, brave men,

and they stood against King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD. That is for the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who have been set apart to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and it will bring you no honour from the LORD God."

Uzziah was angry. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was angry with the priests, a skin disease broke out on his forehead in front of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.
Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and there was the skin disease on his forehead. They hurried him out, and he himself hurried to get out, because the LORD had struck him.

King Uzziah had the skin disease until the day he died, and he lived in a separate house, because he was cut off from the house of the LORD. His son Jotham was over the king's house and governed the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz wrote.

Uzziah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has a skin disease." His son Jotham became king in his place.
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still followed corrupt ways.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and did a great deal of building on the wall of Ophel.
He also built towns in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers on the wooded hills.

He fought against the king of the Ammonites and overcame them. That year the Ammonites gave him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same in the second and third years.
So Jotham grew strong, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David, and his son Ahaz became king in his place.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done,
but walked in the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made cast images for the Baals,
and he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.

So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram, who defeated him and took a large number of his people captive and brought them to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him with a great blow.
For Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, all of them brave men, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Zichri, a warrior from Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah the second to the king.
The Israelites took captive two hundred thousand of their relatives, women, sons and daughters. They also took a great deal of plunder from them and brought it to Samaria.

But a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded, and he went out to meet the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, "Because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, he handed them over to you, but you have killed them in a rage that has reached heaven.
And now you intend to make the people of Judah and Jerusalem, men and women, your slaves. But do you not have sins of your own against the LORD your God?
Now listen to me and send back the captives you have taken from your relatives, for the fierce anger of the LORD is on you."

Then some of the leaders of the Ephraimites, Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up against those who were coming from the war

and said to them, "You must not bring the captives in here, for you are planning to bring on us guilt against the LORD, on top of our present sins and guilt. For our guilt is already great, and there is fierce anger against Israel."
So the armed men left the captives and the plunder in front of the officials and the whole assembly.

The men who have been named got up and took the captives, and from the plunder they clothed all those among them who were naked. They clothed them and gave them sandals, and gave them food and drink and anointed them, and all those who were weak they put on donkeys. They brought them to their relatives at Jericho, the town of palm trees. Then they went back to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
The Edomites had again come and struck Judah and taken captives.

The Philistines had also raided the towns in the lowland and in the Negev of Judah. They had captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages and Gimzo with its villages, and settled there.
For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had made Judah run wild and had been very unfaithful to the LORD.
So Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came against him and oppressed him instead of helping him.
Ahaz took some of the wealth from the house of the LORD and the king's house and the leaders and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
In his time of trouble, King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD.

He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, and said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram helped them, I will sacrifice to them so that they will help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God and cut them in pieces, and shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and made altars for himself in every corner of Jerusalem.
In every town of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and made the LORD, the God of his ancestors, angry.
The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the town, in Jerusalem, for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east
and said to them, "Listen to me, Levites. Now make yourselves holy, and make the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, holy, and carry out the filth from the holy place.
For our ancestors were unfaithful and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They abandoned him and turned their faces away from the dwelling of the LORD and turned their backs.
They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
So the anger of the LORD came on Judah and Jerusalem, and he has made them an object of horror, of shock and of mockery, as you see with your own eyes.
Our ancestors fell by the sword, and our sons and daughters and wives are in captivity because of this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not be careless now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him and to be his ministers and burn incense to him."

Then the Levites got up: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the descendants of the Kohathites, and of the descendants of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel, and of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah,
and of the descendants of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel, and of the descendants of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah,
and of the descendants of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei, and of the descendants of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
They gathered their relatives and made themselves holy and went in as the king had commanded, in keeping with the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.

The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and they brought out all the unclean things that they found in the temple of the LORD into the court of the house of the LORD. The Levites took them and carried them out to the Wadi Kidron.

They began making holy on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of the LORD. For eight days they made the house of the LORD holy, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, "We have cleansed the whole house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering and all its equipment, and the table for the bread of the Presence and all its equipment.
We have prepared and made holy all the vessels that King Ahaz threw away in his reign when he was unfaithful. Look, they are in front of the altar of the LORD."
King Hezekiah got up early and gathered the officials of the town and went up to the house of the LORD.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah. He commanded the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.

So they killed the bulls, and the priests received the blood and splashed it against the altar. They killed the rams and splashed the blood against the altar, and they killed the lambs and splashed the blood against the altar.
Then the male goats for the sin offering were brought to the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them,
and the priests killed them and made a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel. For the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.

He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps and lyres, as David and Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet had commanded, for the command was from the LORD through his prophets.
The Levites stood with David's instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.
Then Hezekiah ordered that the burnt offering be offered on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song to the LORD began also, with the trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.
The whole assembly bowed down, and the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded. All this went on until the burnt offering was finished.
When the offering was finished, the king and all who were with him knelt and bowed down.
King Hezekiah and the officials ordered the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. They sang praises with joy, and they bowed down and worshipped.

Then Hezekiah said, "Now you have given yourselves to the LORD. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing brought burnt offerings.
The number of burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs. All these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.
The holy offerings were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.

But the priests were too few and could not skin all the burnt offerings, so their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until other priests had made themselves holy, for the Levites were more upright in heart than the priests in making themselves holy.
Besides the great number of burnt offerings, there were the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of the LORD was restored.
Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because of what God had done for the people, for it had happened so suddenly.

Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,
for they could not keep it at the proper time, because not enough priests had made themselves holy and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
The plan seemed right to the king and the whole assembly.

So they decided to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that people should come and keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem, for it had not been kept in large numbers as written.

So couriers went throughout all Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his officials, as the king had commanded: "People of Israel, turn back to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, so that he may turn back to those of you who are left, who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your ancestors and your relatives, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors, so that he made them an object of horror, as you see.

Do not be stubborn as your ancestors were. Give yourselves to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has made holy for ever, and serve the LORD your God, so that his fierce anger may turn away from you.

For if you turn back to the LORD, your relatives and your children will find mercy with those who hold them captive and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and will not turn his face away from you if you turn back to him."
The couriers went from town to town through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and mocked them.
But some from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
The hand of God was also on Judah, to give them one heart to do what the king and the officials commanded by the word of the LORD.
A very large crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month.
They set to work and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and took away all the incense altars and threw them into the Wadi Kidron.
They killed the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were ashamed, and made themselves holy and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
They took their usual places according to the law of Moses the man of God. The priests splashed the blood that they received from the hands of the Levites.
For there were many in the assembly who had not made themselves holy, so the Levites had to kill the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to make them holy to the LORD.

For a large number of the people, many of them from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover not as it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them: "May the good LORD pardon everyone
who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his ancestors, even if not in keeping with the purity rules of the sanctuary."
The LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day after day, singing to the LORD with all their strength.

Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding in the service of the LORD. They ate the festival food for seven days, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Then the whole assembly agreed to keep the festival for another seven days, and they kept it for another seven days with joy.

For Hezekiah king of Judah gave the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for offerings, and the officials gave the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. A great number of priests made themselves holy.

The whole assembly of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and the whole assembly that came from Israel, and the foreigners who came from the land of Israel and those who lived in Judah, rejoiced.
So there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the time of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like it in Jerusalem.
Then the priests and the Levites stood and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling in heaven.

When all this was finished, all the Israelites who were there went out to the towns of Judah and smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah poles and pulled down the high places and the altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites went back to their own towns, each to his own property.

Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites, division by division, each according to his service, the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, for serving in the gates of the camp of the LORD and for giving thanks and praise.

The king gave a portion of his own property for the burnt offerings: the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed festivals, as it is written in the law of the LORD.
He commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, so that they could devote themselves to the law of the LORD.

As soon as the command was made known, the Israelites gave generously the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil and honey and of all that the field produced. They brought in a great amount, the tithe of everything.

The Israelites and the people of Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought the tithe of cattle and sheep and the tithe of the holy things that had been dedicated to the LORD their God, and put them in heaps.
In the third month they began to pile up the heaps, and they finished in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him, "Since the people began to bring their contributions into the house of the LORD, we have had enough to eat and plenty left over, for the LORD has blessed his people, and what is left is this large amount."
Then Hezekiah ordered that storerooms be prepared in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.
They faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes and the holy things. Conaniah the Levite was in charge of them, with his brother Shimei second,

and Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by appointment of King Hezekiah and Azariah the chief officer of the house of God.
Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the keeper of the east gate, was in charge of the freewill offerings to God, to distribute the contributions for the LORD and the most holy offerings.
Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah faithfully helped him in the priests' towns, to give out the portions to their relatives, old and young alike, by their divisions,

besides those males three years old and over who were listed in the family records, all who entered the house of the LORD as each day required, for their service according to their duties, by their divisions.
The listing of the priests was by their fathers' houses, and that of the Levites twenty years old and over was by their duties, by their divisions.
They were listed with all their little children, their wives, and their sons and daughters, the whole assembly, for they were faithful in making themselves holy.

For the descendants of Aaron, the priests, who were in the pasturelands of their towns, in every town there were men appointed by name to give portions to every male among the priests and to all the Levites who were listed.
Hezekiah did this throughout Judah, and he did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.
In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, in the law and the commands, seeking his God, he acted with all his heart, and he succeeded.
After these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah and camped against the fortified towns, thinking to break into them for himself.
When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and intended to fight against Jerusalem,
he consulted his officials and his warriors about blocking the water from the springs outside the town, and they supported him.
A large crowd gathered and blocked all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?"

He worked hard and rebuilt all the broken wall and raised towers on it, and built another wall outside, and strengthened the Millo in the city of David. He also made weapons and shields in large numbers.
He appointed military commanders over the people and gathered them in the square at the gate of the town and spoke to encourage them:
"Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and the whole crowd with him, for there is a greater power with us than with him.
With him is only an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." The people were encouraged by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

After this, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was besieging Lachish with all his forces, he sent his servants to Jerusalem to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem, with this message:
"This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What are you relying on, that you stay in Jerusalem under siege?
Is Hezekiah not misleading you, to hand you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, 'The LORD our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria'?
Is it not the same Hezekiah who removed his high places and altars and told Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before one altar and burn sacrifices on it'?
Do you not know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to rescue their lands from my hand?
Who among all the gods of those nations that my ancestors devoted to destruction was able to rescue his people from my hand, that your God should be able to rescue you from my hand?

So now do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this. Do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue his people from my hand or from the hand of my ancestors. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand."
His servants said still more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.

He also wrote letters to mock the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him: "Like the gods of the nations of the lands who did not rescue their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand."
They shouted it in a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might capture the town.
They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as they spoke about the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.

The LORD sent an angel, who wiped out all the brave warriors and commanders and officers in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he went back in shame to his own land. When he went into the temple of his god, some of his own sons struck him down there with the sword.
So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and gave them rest on every side.
Many brought gifts to the LORD in Jerusalem and valuable things to Hezekiah king of Judah, so that from then on he was held in high regard by all the nations.
In those days Hezekiah became ill and was close to death, and he prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not respond to the kindness shown to him, for his heart was proud. So anger came on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.
Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the anger of the LORD did not come on them in the days of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah had very great riches and honour, and he made treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields and all kinds of valuable vessels,
and storehouses for the produce of grain, new wine and oil, and stalls for every kind of cattle, and pens for flocks.
He also built towns for himself, and had large numbers of flocks and herds, for God had given him very great possessions.
It was this Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and channelled them down to the west side of the city of David. Hezekiah succeeded in all that he did.
But when the envoys of the officials of Babylon were sent to him to ask about the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to himself, to test him and to know all that was in his heart.
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his faithful deeds are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him on the upper slope of the tombs of the descendants of David, and all Judah and the people of Jerusalem honoured him at his death. His son Manasseh became king in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had pulled down, and set up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem my name will be for ever."
He built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and practised soothsaying and divination and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spirit-consulters. He did great evil in the eyes of the LORD, making him angry.

He put the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever.

I will never again remove the feet of the Israelites from the land that I assigned to your ancestors, if only they take care to do all that I have commanded them, all the law, the statutes and the rules given through Moses."
Manasseh led Judah and the people of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
So the LORD brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
In his distress he sought the favour of the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.
He prayed to him, and God was moved by his plea and heard his request and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD was God.

After this he built an outer wall for the city of David, on the west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance at the Fish Gate, and round the Ophel, and he made it very high. He also put army commanders in all the fortified towns in Judah.
He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built on the hill of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the town.
He restored the altar of the LORD and offered peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
Even so, the people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are written in the records of the kings of Israel.

His prayer, and how God was moved by his plea, and all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and the images before he humbled himself, are written in the records of the seers.
Manasseh lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in his own house, and his son Amon became king in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for two years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon sacrificed to all the images that his father Manasseh had made, and served them.
He did not humble himself before the LORD, as his father Manasseh had humbled himself, but Amon became more and more guilty.
His servants plotted against him and killed him in his own house.
But the people of the land struck down all those who had plotted against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of his ancestor David, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David, and in the twelfth year he began to clear Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles and the carved and cast images.

In his presence they pulled down the altars of the Baals, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and cast images, ground them to dust and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He also burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and so cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
In the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in the ruins round about,
he pulled down the altars and beat the Asherah poles and the images into powder and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the town and Joah son of Joahaz, the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the threshold had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin and the people of Jerusalem.
They handed it to those in charge of the work who supervised the house of the LORD, and they gave it to the workers who were working in the house of the LORD to repair and restore the house.
They gave it to the carpenters and builders to buy cut stone and timber for the joints and the beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had let fall into ruin.

The men worked faithfully. Over them were put Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the descendants of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the descendants of Kohath, to supervise. The Levites, all who were skilled with musical instruments,
were over the carriers and supervised all who did work of any kind, and some of the Levites were secretaries, officials and gatekeepers.
While they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, the priest Hilkiah found the Book of the Law of the LORD given through Moses.
Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan took the book to the king and reported to the king, "Your servants are doing all that was entrusted to them.
They have poured out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have handed it to the supervisors and the workers."
Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "The priest Hilkiah has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it in the presence of the king.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go and ask the LORD for me and for those who are left in Israel and Judah about the words of the book that has been found. For great is the anger of the LORD that has been poured out on us, because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD and do all that is written in this book."

So Hilkiah and those whom the king had sent went to Huldah the prophet, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her about this.
She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me:
This is what the LORD says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and on those who live here, all the curses written in the book that was read in front of the king of Judah.
Because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, to make me angry with all the work of their hands, my anger will be poured out on this place and will not be put out.
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask the LORD, say this: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: As for the words that you have heard,

because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and those who live here, and you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me, I have heard you, declares the LORD.

I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am going to bring on this place and those who live here." They took the word back to the king.
Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went up to the house of the LORD with all the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people, small and great. He read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

The king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD to follow the LORD and to keep his commands, his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, and to carry out the words of the covenant written in this book.
Then he made everyone present in Jerusalem and Benjamin join in it. The people of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the territory that belonged to the Israelites and made everyone in Israel serve the LORD their God. All his days they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they killed the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.

He said to the Levites who taught all Israel and who were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. You no longer need to carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
Prepare yourselves by your fathers' houses, by your divisions, as written by David king of Israel and by his son Solomon.
Stand in the holy place according to the groups of the fathers' houses of your relatives the people, with a part of a Levite father's house for each.
Kill the Passover lambs and make yourselves holy and prepare for your relatives, to do as the LORD commanded through Moses."

Josiah gave to the people, for all who were present, lambs and young goats from the flock, thirty thousand in all, and three thousand bulls, as Passover offerings. These were from the king's own property.

His officials also gave willingly to the people, the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the leaders of the house of God, gave the priests two thousand six hundred lambs and young goats and three hundred bulls for the Passover offerings.

Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, gave the Levites five thousand lambs and young goats and five hundred bulls for the Passover offerings.
When the service was ready, the priests stood in their places, and the Levites in their divisions as the king had commanded.
They killed the Passover lambs, and the priests splashed the blood that they received from them, while the Levites skinned the animals.
They set aside the burnt offerings to give to the groups of the fathers' houses of the people, to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses. They did the same with the bulls.
They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire as prescribed, and boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons and pans, and quickly took them to all the people.

Afterwards they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the descendants of Aaron, were offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.

The singers, the descendants of Asaph, were in their places as David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer had commanded. The gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, because their relatives the Levites prepared for them.
So all the service of the LORD was prepared that day to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, as King Josiah commanded.
The Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel. None of the kings of Israel had kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who were present, and the people of Jerusalem.
This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
After all this, when Josiah had set the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

But Neco sent messengers to him: "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, or he will destroy you."
But Josiah would not turn away from him but disguised himself to fight with him. He did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, but went to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
The archers shot King Josiah. The king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."

So his servants took him out of the chariot and put him in his second chariot and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

Jeremiah also composed a lament for Josiah, and all the male and female singers have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made these a custom in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
The rest of the acts of Josiah and his faithful deeds, as written in the law of the LORD,
and his acts, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in his father's place in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months in Jerusalem.
Then the king of Egypt removed him in Jerusalem and imposed on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
The king of Egypt made his brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took his brother Jehoahaz and brought him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him in bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his palace in Babylon.

The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and the detestable things that he did, and what was found against him, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
In the spring King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the valuable vessels of the house of the LORD, and made his relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning back to the LORD, the God of Israel.

All the leaders of the priests and the people were also very unfaithful, following all the detestable practices of the nations. They made the house of the LORD, which he had made holy in Jerusalem, unclean.
The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them again and again through his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
But they kept mocking the messengers of God, despising his words and scoffing at his prophets, until the anger of the LORD rose against his people, until there was no remedy.

So he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and had no pity on young man or young woman, old or frail. God handed all of them over to him.
All the vessels of the house of God, large and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and his officials, all these he brought to Babylon.
They burned the house of God and broke down the wall of Jerusalem and burned all its palaces with fire and destroyed all its valuable vessels.
He took into exile in Babylon those who had escaped from the sword, and they became servants to him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power,
to fulfil the word of the LORD through Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its sabbaths. All the days that it lay desolate it kept sabbath, until seventy years were completed.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, in order to fulfil the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he sent a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom and put it in writing:

"This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build him a house at Jerusalem in Judah. Whoever among you belongs to all his people, may the LORD his God be with him. Let him go up."

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfil the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he sent a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom and put it in writing:
"This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build him a house at Jerusalem in Judah.
Whoever among you belongs to all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

And let everyone who survives, wherever he lives as a foreigner, be helped by the people of his place with silver and gold, with goods and with animals, besides the freewill offerings for the house of God in Jerusalem."
Then the heads of the fathers' houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, everyone whose spirit God had stirred, got ready to go up and build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
All their neighbours supported them with silver vessels, gold, goods, animals and valuable things, besides all that was willingly given.
King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods.
Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
This was the count: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,
thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of a second kind, and a thousand other vessels.
All the gold and silver vessels numbered five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;
of Pahath-moab, from the descendants of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;
of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;
of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
of Bigvai, two thousand and fifty-six;
of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
of Ater, from Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;
of Jorah, a hundred and twelve;
of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
of Gibbar, ninety-five;
the men of Bethlehem, a hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Netophah, fifty-six;
the men of Anathoth, a hundred and twenty-eight;
the descendants of Azmaveth, forty-two;
the descendants of Kiriath-arim, Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the descendants of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, a hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Nebo, fifty-two;
the descendants of Magbish, a hundred and fifty-six;
the descendants of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the descendants of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;
the descendants of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the descendants of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the descendants of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the descendants of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the descendants of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the descendants of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, a hundred and twenty-eight.
The descendants of the gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, of Ater, of Talmon, of Akkub, of Hatita and of Shobai, in all a hundred and thirty-nine.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Siaha, Padon,
Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub,
Hagab, Shamlai, Hanan,
Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah,
Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam,
Uzza, Paseah, Besai,
Asnah, Meunim, Nephisim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda,
Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim and Ami.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
These are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan and Immer, but could not prove that their fathers' houses and their descent were of Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.
Also from the descendants of the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz and Barzillai (who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name).
These searched for their family records among those listed in the genealogies, but they were not found there, so they were put out of the priesthood as unclean.
The governor told them that they were not to eat the most holy food until a priest with Urim and Thummim should rise up.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven, and they had two hundred male and female singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five,
their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
Some of the heads of the fathers' houses, when they came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, gave freewill offerings for the house of God, to set it up on its site.
According to their means they gave to the treasury for the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver and a hundred priests' robes.
The priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants lived in their towns, and all Israel in their towns.
When the seventh month came and the Israelites were in their towns, the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak, with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his relatives, got up and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
They set the altar on its base, for they were afraid of the peoples of the lands, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.
They kept the Festival of Booths, as it is written, and offered the burnt offerings by number each day, as the rule required,

and after that the regular burnt offerings, the offerings at the new moons and at all the appointed festivals of the LORD that are made holy, and the offerings of everyone who gave a freewill offering to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, but the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not yet been laid.

They gave money to the stonecutters and the carpenters, and food, drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as Cyrus king of Persia had authorised.

In the second year after they came to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak made a start, with the rest of their relatives, the priests and the Levites, and all who had come to Jerusalem from the captivity. They appointed Levites twenty years old and over to supervise the work on the house of the LORD.

Jeshua with his sons and his relatives, and Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah, together took charge of the workers on the house of God, with the descendants of Henadad, and their sons and relatives the Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests in their robes stood with trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD, as David king of Israel had ordered.

They sang to each other in praise and thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his faithful love to Israel lasts for ever." All the people gave a great shout in praise of the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers' houses, old men who had seen the first house, wept loudly when they saw the foundation of this house laid, while many others shouted aloud for joy,
so that the people could not tell the sound of the joyful shout from the sound of the weeping of the people. For the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.
When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,

they came to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esar-haddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We alone will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, has commanded us."
Then the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah and frightened them from building,
and hired advisers against them to frustrate their plan, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script and put into Aramaic.
*(From here to 6:18 the original is in Aramaic.)*
Rehum the commander and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows.
