Then Rehum the commander, Shimshai the secretary and the rest of their associates, the judges, the governors, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is the Elamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and the rest of the province Beyond the River, and so on.
This is a copy of the letter that they sent: "To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River, and so on.
Let the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have come to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding the rebellious and evil city. They are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.
Now let the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, tax or toll, and in the end it will damage the royal revenue.
Now since we are bound by the salt of the palace, and it is not right for us to see the king dishonoured, we are sending word to the king

so that a search may be made in the record book of your ancestors. You will find in the record book and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that they have made revolt in it from long ago. That is why this city was destroyed.
We make known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will then have no share in the province Beyond the River."

The king sent this reply: "To Rehum the commander and Shimshai the secretary and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River, greetings, and so on.
The letter that you sent to us has been read out clearly before me.
I gave an order, and a search was made, and it was found that this city has from long ago risen up against kings, and that rebellion and revolt have been made in it.
Powerful kings have ruled in Jerusalem, who ruled over the whole province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax and toll were paid to them.
Now give an order to make these men stop, and this city is not to be rebuilt until an order is given by me.
Take care not to be careless in this matter. Why should the damage grow to the harm of the kings?"

As soon as the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read in front of Rehum and Shimshai the secretary and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem, to the Jews, and by force and power made them stop.
Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped, and it stayed stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak got up and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, and the prophets of God were with them, helping them.

At that time Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their associates came to them and said, "Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?"
They also asked them, "What are the names of the men who are building this building?"
But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they were not stopped until a report could go to Darius and a written answer come back about it.
This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates, the officials of the province Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
They sent him a report, and in it was written: "To King Darius, all peace.

Let the king know that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with large stones, and timber is being laid in the walls. This work is being done with care and is succeeding in their hands.
We asked those elders and said to them, 'Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?'
We also asked them their names, to let you know, so that we could write down the names of the men at their head.
This is the answer they gave us: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.
But because our ancestors made the God of heaven angry, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and took the people away to Babylon.
But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus gave an order that this house of God should be rebuilt.

And King Cyrus took out of the temple of Babylon the gold and silver vessels of the house of God that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon, and they were handed to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
He said to him: "Take these vessels, go and put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site."
Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from then until now it has been in the process of building, and it is not yet finished.'

Now if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the royal archives there in Babylon to see whether an order was given by King Cyrus to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. And let the king send us his decision about this matter."
Then King Darius gave an order, and a search was made in the archives, where the documents were stored in Babylon.
In Ecbatana, the fortress in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and this was written in it: "Record.

In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus gave an order: Concerning the house of God at Jerusalem, let the house be rebuilt as a place where sacrifices are offered, with its foundations kept. Its height is to be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
with three layers of large stones and one layer of timber. The cost is to be paid from the royal treasury.

Also, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, are to be returned and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its place. You are to put them in the house of God."
"Now, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and your associates, the officials of the province Beyond the River, keep away from there.
Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

I also give an order about what you are to do for these elders of the Jews for the rebuilding of this house of God. The full cost is to be paid to these men from the royal revenue, from the tribute of the province Beyond the River, without delay.
Whatever is needed, young bulls, rams or lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine or oil, as the priests in Jerusalem say, is to be given to them day by day without fail,
so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
I also give an order that if anyone changes this decree, a beam is to be pulled out of his house and he is to be impaled on it, and his house is to be made a rubbish heap for this.

May the God who has made his name live there overthrow any king or people who reach out a hand to change this or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have given this order. Let it be carried out with care."
Then Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates carried it out with care, exactly as King Darius had ordered.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of the prophet Haggai and of Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished building by the order of the God of Israel and by the order of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
The Israelites, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the returned exiles, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

For the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They set the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their groups for the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
*(From here the original is in Hebrew again.)*
The returned exiles kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. They killed the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their fellow priests and for themselves.

It was eaten by the Israelites who had returned from exile and by everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land and joined them to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

They kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, for the LORD had made them glad and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria towards them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
After this, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest,

this Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses that the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king gave him everything he asked, for the hand of the LORD his God was on him.
Some of the Israelites, and some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants, also went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
Ezra came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.
On the first day of the first month he had begun the journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was on him.
For Ezra had set his heart to study the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach its statutes and rules in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the words of the commands of the LORD and his statutes for Israel:
*(From here to verse 26 the original is in Aramaic.)*
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Greetings, and so on.
I have given an order that anyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel and their priests and Levites who is willing to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
For you are sent by the king and his seven advisers to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which is in your hand,
and to bring the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have freely given to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
with all the silver and gold that you find in the whole province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings of the people and the priests, given willingly for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
With this money you are to be careful to buy bulls, rams and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
What seems good to you and your relatives to do with the rest of the silver and gold, you may do, according to the will of your God.
The vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
And whatever else is needed for the house of your God that you are called on to provide, you may provide from the royal treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, give an order to all the treasurers in the province Beyond the River: Whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you is to be done with care,
up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.
Whatever the God of heaven commands is to be done fully for the house of the God of heaven. Why should there be anger against the kingdom of the king and his sons?
We also make known to you that it is not permitted to impose tribute, tax or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants or other servants of this house of God.

And you, Ezra, in keeping with the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River who know the laws of your God, and you are to teach those who do not know them.
Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king is to have judgement carried out on him without delay, whether death or banishment or confiscation of property or imprisonment."
*(From here the original is in Hebrew again, and Ezra speaks in the first person.)*
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who put this into the heart of the king, to glorify the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,

and who showed me his faithful love before the king and his advisers and all the king's powerful officials. I took courage, for the hand of the LORD my God was on me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
These are the heads of their fathers' houses and the family record of those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes:
Of the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom. Of the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the descendants of David, Hattush,
of the descendants of Shecaniah. Of the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty men were listed.
Of the descendants of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
Of the descendants of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men.
Of the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
Of the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
Of the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
Of the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen men.
Of the descendants of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty men.
Of the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
Of the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten men.
Of the descendants of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeuel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
Of the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy men.
I gathered them at the river that flows towards Ahava, and we camped there three days. When I looked over the people and the priests, I found no descendants of Levi there.
So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam, who were leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of understanding,

and sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place Casiphia, and told them what to say to Iddo and his relatives, the temple servants at the place Casiphia, so that they would bring us servants for the house of our God.
Because the good hand of our God was on us, they brought us a man of understanding from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel, Sherebiah, with his sons and relatives, eighteen men,
and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his relatives and their sons, twenty men,
and two hundred and twenty of the temple servants, whom David and the officials had given to serve the Levites. All of them were listed by name.
Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask him for a safe journey for us, our children and all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road, since we had said to the king, "The hand of our God is for good on all who seek him, but his strength and his anger are against all who abandon him."
So we fasted and asked our God for this, and he answered our prayer.
Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives with them,
and weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the offering for the house of our God that the king, his advisers, his officials and all Israel who were there had given.
I weighed out into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver vessels worth a hundred talents, a hundred talents of gold,
twenty gold bowls worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine polished bronze, as valuable as gold.
I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
Guard them and keep them until you weigh them out before the leading priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel in Jerusalem, in the rooms of the house of the LORD."
So the priests and the Levites received the silver and the gold and the vessels, weighed out, to bring to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
We set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he rescued us from the hand of enemies and from ambushes on the road.
We came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.

On the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was counted and weighed, and the whole weight was recorded at that time.

The returned exiles, those who had come from the captivity, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and as a sin offering twelve male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
They also handed over the king's orders to the king's governors and to the governors of the province Beyond the River, and they supported the people and the house of God.

When these things were finished, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not kept themselves separate from the peoples of the lands, with their detestable practices, from the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians and the Amorites.

They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed has mixed with the peoples of the lands. And in this unfaithfulness the leaders and officials have been the first."
When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my cloak and pulled out some of the hair of my head and beard, and sat down stunned.
Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel because of the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles gathered round me, while I sat stunned until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I got up from my fasting, with my clothes and my cloak torn, and fell on my knees and spread out my hands to the LORD my God
and said: "My God, I am too ashamed and embarrassed to lift my face to you, my God, for our wrongs have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has reached to the heavens.

From the days of our ancestors until today we have been in great guilt. Because of our wrongs we, our kings and our priests have been handed over to the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder and to open shame, as it is today.

But now for a short time there has been favour from the LORD our God, who has left us a remnant and given us a firm hold in his holy place, so that our God may light up our eyes and give us a little relief in our slavery.

For we were slaves, yet in our slavery our God did not abandon us, but showed us his faithful love before the kings of Persia, giving us some relief, to raise up the house of our God and repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and Jerusalem.
And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have abandoned your commands,

which you gave through your servants the prophets, saying: 'The land that you are entering to take as your own is a land made unclean by the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, by their detestable practices. They have filled it from one end to the other with their impurity.

So do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your children for ever.'
After all that has come on us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt, since you, our God, have held back from punishing us as our wrongs deserve and have given us a remnant like this,

shall we again break your commands and intermarry with the peoples who do these detestable things? Would you not be angry with us until you destroyed us, so that there would be no remnant and no survivor?
LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous, for we are left as a remnant that has escaped, as it is today. Here we are before you in our guilt, for no one can stand before you because of this."

While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a very large crowd of Israelites, men, women and children, gathered round him, and the people wept bitterly.

Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Elam, spoke to Ezra: "We have been unfaithful to our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land, but even now there is hope for Israel in spite of this.

So now let us make a covenant with our God to send away all these women and their children, following the advice of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God. Let it be done according to the law.
Get up, for this matter is yours, and we are with you. Be strong and act."
Then Ezra got up and made the leading priests, the Levites and all Israel swear that they would do as had been said, and they swore.

Then Ezra left the house of God and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib, where he spent the night. He ate no bread and drank no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the returned exiles to gather in Jerusalem,
and that anyone who did not come within three days would, by the decision of the officials and the elders, lose all his property and be excluded from the community of the exiles.

So all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem within the three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. All the people sat in the open square in front of the house of God, shaking because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.
Then the priest Ezra stood up and said to them, "You have been unfaithful and have married foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.
Now make confession to the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
The whole assembly answered in a loud voice, "Yes. We must do as you say.
But there are many people, and it is the rainy season, and we cannot stand outside. It is not a task for one day or two, for we have greatly sinned in this matter.

Let our officials act for the whole assembly. Let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God over this matter is turned away from us."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

The returned exiles did this. Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of fathers' houses, one for each father's house, each named by name. They sat down to examine the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
and by the first day of the first month they had finished with all the men who had married foreign women.
Among the descendants of the priests who were found to have married foreign women were, from the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his relatives: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.
They gave their hands to send away their wives, and for their guilt they offered a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.
From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.
From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Elasah.
From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.
From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem and Uri.
From Israel: from the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah and Benaiah.
From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Elijah.
From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.
From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.
From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Jeremoth.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.
From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
Benjamin, Malluch and Shemariah.
From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh and Shimei.
From the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai and Jaasu.
From the descendants of Binnui: Shimei,
Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah and Joseph.
From the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, when I was in Susa the citadel,
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
They said to me, "Those who are left from the captivity there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days. I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said: "LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and faithful love with those who love him and keep his commands,

let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer of your servant that I am praying before you now, day and night, for your servants the people of Israel, confessing the sins of the people of Israel that we have committed against you. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
We have acted very wickedly against you and have not kept the commands, the statutes and the rules that you gave to your servant Moses.
Remember the word that you gave to your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples,

but if you turn back to me and keep my commands and do them, even if your scattered people are at the farthest edge of the heavens, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place that I have chosen as a home for my name.'
They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your strong hand.

Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name, and give success to your servant today, and grant him compassion before this man." I was cupbearer to the king.
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was in front of him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in his presence before.
The king said to me, "Why is your face sad, when you are not ill? This can only be sadness of heart." Then I was very afraid.
I said to the king, "May the king live for ever. Why should my face not be sad, when the city of my ancestors' graves lies in ruins and its gates have been burned with fire?"
The king said to me, "What are you asking for?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
Then I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favour with you, send me to Judah, to the city of my ancestors' graves, so that I may rebuild it."
The king, with the queen sitting beside him, said to me, "How long will your journey take, and when will you come back?" It pleased the king to send me, and I gave him a time.
I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the province Beyond the River, so that they will let me pass until I reach Judah,

and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the fortress of the temple, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will live in." The king gave me what I asked, for the good hand of my God was on me.
Then I came to the governors of the province Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and horsemen with me.
But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard this, they were very displeased that someone had come to seek the good of the people of Israel.
I came to Jerusalem and was there for three days.
Then I got up in the night, I and a few men with me. I told no one what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the one I was riding.
I went out at night by the Valley Gate towards the Dragon Spring and the Dung Gate and inspected the walls of Jerusalem that were broken down and its gates that had been burned with fire.
Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.
So I went up in the night by the valley and inspected the wall, and I turned back and came in by the Valley Gate, and returned.
The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, and I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials or the rest who were to do the work.

Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in, that Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a disgrace."
I told them how the good hand of my God had been on me, and also what the king had said to me. They said, "Let us get up and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good work.

But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us and said, "What is this that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
I answered them, "The God of heaven will give us success. We, his servants, will get up and build, but you have no share or claim or memorial in Jerusalem."

Then Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests got up and built the Sheep Gate. They made it holy and set up its doors. They made it holy as far as the Tower of the Hundred and as far as the Tower of Hananel.
Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri built.
The descendants of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, bolts and bars.
Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz repaired. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel repaired. Next to them Zadok son of Baana repaired.
Next to them the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles would not bend their necks to the work of their lords.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, bolts and bars.
Next to them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, who were under the authority of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
Next to them Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfume makers, repaired. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired opposite his house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah repaired.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, and the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.
Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it and set up its doors, bolts and bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate. He rebuilt it and set up its doors, bolts and bars.

Shallum son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it and roofed it and set up its doors, bolts and bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the city of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired from the place opposite the tombs of David as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Warriors.
After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
After him their relatives repaired: Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armoury at the Angle.
After him Baruch son of Zabbai zealously repaired another section from the Angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz repaired another section from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of his house.
After him the priests, the men of the surrounding area, repaired.
After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah repaired beside his own house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the Angle and to the corner.
Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the Angle and the tower that projects from the upper house of the king by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh
and the temple servants living on Ophel repaired as far as opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
After them the Tekoites repaired another section opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.
After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his room.
After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room at the corner.
Between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants repaired.
When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was angry and greatly enraged, and he mocked the Jews.

In front of his associates and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life from the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him and said, "Whatever they build, if a fox climbed on it, it would break down their stone wall."
Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunts back on their own heads and hand them over to be plundered in a land of captivity.
Do not cover their guilt, and do not let their sin be wiped out from before you, for they have insulted the builders.
So we rebuilt the wall, and the whole wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

But when Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabs and the Ammonites and the people of Ashdod heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was moving ahead and that the gaps were beginning to be closed, they were very angry.
They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it.
But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.
In Judah it was said: "The strength of the carriers is failing, and there is so much rubble that we cannot rebuild the wall."
Our enemies said, "They will not know or see anything until we are among them and kill them and stop the work."
When the Jews who lived near them came, they told us ten times, "From every place you turn, they are against us."
So I stationed people in the lowest places behind the wall, in the open places, by families, with their swords, spears and bows.

I looked, and stood up and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your relatives, your sons and daughters, your wives and your homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew about it and that God had frustrated their plan, we all went back to the wall, each to his work.
From that day half of my young men did the work, while half held the spears, shields, bows and body armour. The officers stood behind the whole house of Judah,
who were building the wall. The carriers took their loads in such a way that each worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
Each of the builders wore his sword at his side as he built. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.
I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is large and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
So we carried on with the work, with half of them holding the spears from the first light of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also said to the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and workers by day."
So neither I nor my relatives nor my servants nor the guards who followed me took off our clothes. Each kept his weapon in his right hand.
There was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
Some said, "We and our sons and daughters are many. We must get grain so that we can eat and stay alive."
Others said, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain in the famine."
Still others said, "We have borrowed money against our fields and vineyards to pay the king's tax.

Now our flesh is the same as the flesh of our relatives, and our children are the same as their children. Yet we are bringing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We are powerless, for our fields and vineyards belong to others."
I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.
I thought it over, and I accused the nobles and the officials: "You are charging interest, each one to his own relative." I called a large assembly against them

and said to them, "As far as we could, we bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to the nations. Now you are selling your own relatives, so that they can be sold to us." They were silent and could not find a word to say.
So I said, "What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the taunts of the nations who are our enemies?
I too, with my relatives and my servants, am lending them money and grain. Let us stop this charging of interest.
Give back to them today their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses, and the percentage of the money, grain, new wine and oil that you have been charging them."
They said, "We will give it back and ask nothing more from them. We will do as you say." Then I called the priests and made them swear to do what they had promised.

I also shook out the fold of my robe and said, "In the same way may God shake out of his house and out of his property everyone who does not keep this promise. May he be shaken out and emptied." All the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.

Also, from the time that I was appointed their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years, neither I nor my relatives ate the governor's food allowance.

The earlier governors before me had put heavy burdens on the people and had taken from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Their servants also lorded it over the people. But I did not do this, because of the fear of God.
I also devoted myself to the work on this wall, and we did not buy any land, and all my servants were gathered there for the work.
Also there were a hundred and fifty Jews and officials at my table, besides those who came to us from the nations round us.

What was prepared each day at my expense was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me, and every ten days all kinds of wine in large amounts. Yet with all this I did not ask for the governor's food allowance, because the work was so heavy on this people.
Remember me for good, my God, for all that I have done for this people.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that no gap was left in it (though until then I had not set up doors in the gates),
Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let us meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono." But they intended to harm me.
So I sent messengers to them with this answer: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"
They sent me the same message four times, and I answered them in the same way.
The fifth time Sanballat sent his servant to me with the same message, and in his hand was an open letter.

In it was written: "It is reported among the nations, and Geshem says it too, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel, and that is why you are rebuilding the wall. According to these reports you are to be their king.
You have also appointed prophets to announce about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah.' Now the king will hear of these reports. So come, let us take counsel together."
Then I sent him this answer: "Nothing like what you say has happened. You are making it up out of your own heart."
For they all wanted to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done." But now, God, make my hands strong.

I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at his home. He said, "Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you. They are coming to kill you at night."
But I said, "Should a man like me run away? And would someone like me go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in."
I saw that God had not sent him, but that he had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He had been hired so that I would be afraid and do this and sin, and so that they could give me a bad name to mock me with.
Remember Tobiah and Sanballat, my God, for what they did, and also the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to make me afraid.
The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations round us were afraid and lost their confidence, for they saw that this work had been done with the help of our God.
In those days the nobles of Judah also sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters came to them.
For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They also spoke of his good deeds in my presence and reported my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.
When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites had been appointed,
I put my brother Hanani and Hananiah the commander of the fortress in charge of Jerusalem, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many.

I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot. While the gatekeepers are still on duty, let them shut the doors and bar them. Appoint guards from the people who live in Jerusalem, each at his post and each opposite his own house."
The town was wide and large, but there were few people in it, and no houses had been rebuilt.

My God put it into my heart to gather the nobles, the officials and the people to be listed by their families. I found the book of the family records of those who had come up at the first, and I found this written in it:
These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two;
of Pahath-moab, from the descendants of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and eighteen;
of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
of Zattu, eight hundred and forty-five;
of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
of Binnui, six hundred and forty-eight;
of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-eight;
of Azgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-two;
of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven;
of Bigvai, two thousand and sixty-seven;
of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five;
of Ater, from Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
of Hashum, three hundred and twenty-eight;
of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-four;
of Hariph, a hundred and twelve;
of Gibeon, ninety-five;
the men of Bethlehem and Netophah, a hundred and eighty-eight;
the men of Anathoth, a hundred and twenty-eight;
the men of Beth-azmaveth, forty-two;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, a hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, a hundred and twenty-three;
the men of the other Nebo, fifty-two;
the descendants of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the descendants of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the descendants of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-one;
the descendants of Senaah, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the descendants of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the descendants of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the descendants of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the descendants of Hodevah, seventy-four.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, a hundred and forty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, of Ater, of Talmon, of Akkub, of Hatita and of Shobai, a hundred and thirty-eight.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Sia, Padon,
Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai,
Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,
Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,
Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,
Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim and Amon.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
These are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon and Immer, but could not prove that their fathers' houses and their descent were of Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two.
Also from the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz and Barzillai (who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name).
These searched for their family records among those listed in the genealogies, but they were not found there, so they were put out of the priesthood as unclean.
The governor told them that they were not to eat the most holy food until a priest with Urim and Thummim should rise up.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven, and they had two hundred and forty-five male and female singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five,
their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
Some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury a thousand darics of gold, fifty bowls and five hundred and thirty priests' robes.
Some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand darics of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
What the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand darics of gold, two thousand minas of silver and sixty-seven priests' robes.
The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants and all Israel lived in their towns. When the seventh month came, the Israelites were in their towns.
All the people gathered as one in the square in front of the Water Gate. They told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses that the LORD had commanded Israel.
So Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, of men and women and everyone who could understand what they heard, on the first day of the seventh month.

He read from it in the square in front of the Water Gate from first light until midday, in the presence of the men and women and those who could understand. All the people were listening to the book of the law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that had been made for the purpose. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above them all, and as he opened it all the people stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. Then they bowed down and worshipped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah helped the people to understand the law, while the people stood in their places.
They read from the book, from the law of God, making it clear and giving the sense, so that the people understood what was read.

Nehemiah the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.

He said to them, "Go and eat rich food and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for this day is holy. Do not be sad."
All the people went to eat and drink and send portions and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood the words that were made known to them.
On the second day the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the law.
They found written in the law that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the Israelites should live in booths during the festival of the seventh month,

and that they should announce and spread this word in all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills and bring olive branches, wild olive branches, myrtle branches, palm branches and branches of leafy trees to make booths, as it is written."

So the people went out and brought them and made booths for themselves, each on his own roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the square at the Water Gate and in the square at the Gate of Ephraim.

The whole assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in them, for from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day the Israelites had not done so. And there was very great joy.
Day by day, from the first day to the last, he read from the book of the law of God. They kept the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a closing assembly, as the rule required.
On the twenty-fourth day of the same month the Israelites gathered, fasting and wearing sackcloth and with earth on their heads.
Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their sins and the wrongs of their ancestors.
They stood in their places and read from the book of the law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and for another quarter they confessed and bowed down to the LORD their God.
On the stairs of the Levites stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Chenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.

Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah said: "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed be your glorious name, which is lifted above all blessing and praise.

You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, the heaven of heavens, and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You give life to all of them, and the host of heaven bows down to you.
You are the LORD, the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.

You found his heart faithful before you and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites to his descendants. And you have kept your word, for you are righteous.
You saw the suffering of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Sea of Reeds.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh and all his servants and all the people of his land, for you knew that they acted proudly against our ancestors. You made a name for yourself that remains to this day.
You split the sea in front of them, and they went through the middle of the sea on dry ground, and you threw their pursuers into the depths like a stone into raging water.
By day you led them with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire, to light for them the road on which they were to go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven and gave them right rules and true laws, good statutes and commands.
You made known to them your holy sabbath and gave them commands, statutes and a law through Moses your servant.
You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water out of the rock for their thirst, and you told them to go in and take the land that you had sworn to give them.
But they, our ancestors, acted proudly and stiffened their necks and did not listen to your commands.

They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders that you did among them, but they stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to go back to their slavery in Egypt. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in faithful love, and you did not abandon them.
Even when they made for themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This is your God who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great insults,

you in your great compassion did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not leave them by day, to lead them on the road, and the pillar of fire did not leave them by night, to light for them the road on which they were to go.
You gave your good spirit to instruct them, and did not hold back your manna from their mouths, and gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
You gave them kingdoms and peoples and divided them up by regions. So they took the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You made their children as many as the stars of heaven, and brought them into the land that you had told their ancestors to enter and take.

So the descendants went in and took the land, and you subdued the people of the land, the Canaanites, in front of them and handed them over to them, with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they pleased.

They captured fortified towns and a rich land and took houses full of every good thing, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves and fruit trees in great numbers. They ate and were full and grew fat and enjoyed your great goodness.
But they were disobedient and rebelled against you and threw your law behind their backs. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn them back to you, and they committed great insults.

So you handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. In the time of their trouble they cried out to you, and you heard from heaven, and in your great compassion you gave them deliverers, who saved them from the hand of their enemies.

But when they had rest they did evil again before you, and you left them in the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Yet when they turned back and cried out to you, you heard from heaven and rescued them many times in your compassion.

You warned them to bring them back to your law, but they acted proudly and did not listen to your commands. They sinned against your rules, by which a person will live if he keeps them. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their necks and would not listen.
For many years you were patient with them and warned them by your spirit through your prophets. Yet they would not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of the lands.
But in your great compassion you did not put an end to them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.

Now, our God, the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and faithful love, do not let all the hardship that has come on us seem small to you, on our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors and all your people, from the time of the kings of Assyria until today.
You have been righteous in all that has come on us, for you have acted faithfully and we have acted wickedly.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests and our ancestors have not kept your law or paid attention to your commands and the warnings that you gave them.
Even in their own kingdom, with the great goodness that you gave them and in the large and rich land that you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their wicked deeds.
Here we are today as slaves. In the land that you gave to our ancestors to enjoy its fruit and its good things, here we are as slaves.
Its rich produce goes to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress.
Because of all this we are making a firm agreement and putting it in writing, and our leaders, our Levites and our priests are sealing it."
Those who sealed it were: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the descendants of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their relatives Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, Bani and Beninu.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim and Baanah.

The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who have separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to follow the law of God, with their wives, their sons and their daughters, everyone who has knowledge and understanding,

join with their relatives, their nobles, and enter into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God that was given through Moses the servant of God, and to keep and carry out all the commands of the LORD our Lord, his rules and his statutes.
We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.

If the peoples of the land bring goods or any grain to sell on the sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the sabbath or on a holy day. In the seventh year we will leave the land alone and cancel every debt.
We also take on ourselves the duty of giving a third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God,

for the bread of the Presence, the regular grain offering, the regular burnt offering, the sabbaths, the new moons, the appointed festivals, the holy things, the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.

We have also cast lots for the wood offering, the priests, the Levites and the people, to bring it to the house of our God by our fathers' houses at set times each year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the law.
We also take on ourselves the duty of bringing to the house of the LORD each year the first fruits of our ground and the first fruits of the fruit of every tree,

and of bringing to the house of our God, to the priests who serve in the house of our God, the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and flocks.

We will bring the first of our ground meal and our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the new wine and the oil, to the priests, to the rooms of the house of our God, and the tithe of our ground to the Levites, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all the towns where we work.

A priest, a descendant of Aaron, is to be with the Levites when the Levites collect the tithes, and the Levites are to bring up the tithe of the tithes to the house of our God, to the rooms of the storehouse.

For the Israelites and the descendants of Levi are to bring the contribution of grain, new wine and oil to the rooms where the vessels of the sanctuary are, and where the priests who serve, the gatekeepers and the singers are. We will not neglect the house of our God.
The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people cast lots to bring one in ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine-tenths stayed in the other towns.
The people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live in Jerusalem.

These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem (in the towns of Judah each one lived on his own property in his own town: the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants).

In Jerusalem lived some of the descendants of Judah and of Benjamin. From the descendants of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the descendants of Perez,
and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.
All the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight brave men.
These are the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah,
and after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.
Joel son of Zichri was their overseer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in charge of the city.
From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the officer in charge of the house of God,
and their relatives who did the work of the house, eight hundred and twenty-two, and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah,
and his relatives, heads of fathers' houses, two hundred and forty-two, and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,
and their relatives, brave warriors, a hundred and twenty-eight. Their overseer was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni,
and Shabbethai and Jozabad, from the heads of the Levites, who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God,

and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, who was the leader who began the thanksgiving at prayer, and Bakbukiah, second among his relatives, and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred and eighty-four.
The gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon and their relatives, who kept watch at the gates, were a hundred and seventy-two.
The rest of Israel, of the priests and the Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
But the temple servants lived on Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of the temple servants.
The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, of the descendants of Asaph, the singers, in charge of the work of the house of God.
For there was a command from the king about them, and a fixed provision for the singers as each day required.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, was at the king's side in all matters concerning the people.
As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, in Dibon and its villages, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
in Jeshua, in Moladah and Beth-pelet,
in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its villages,
in Ziklag, in Meconah and its villages,
in En-rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its villages. So they settled from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
The descendants of Benjamin lived from Geba onwards, at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages,
Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod and Ono, and the valley of the craftsmen.
Some divisions of the Levites in Judah were assigned to Benjamin.
These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their relatives in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah and Mattaniah, who with his relatives was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.
Bakbukiah and Unni, their relatives, stood opposite them in the service.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada,
Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim the priests, the heads of fathers' houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin and of Moadiah, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses, and the priests too, until the reign of Darius the Persian.
The descendants of Levi, the heads of fathers' houses, were written in the Book of the Records until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their relatives opposite them, to praise and give thanks, as David the man of God had commanded, one group beside the other.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers, guarding the storerooms at the gates.
These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with joy, with thanksgiving and singing, with cymbals, harps and lyres.
The descendants of the singers gathered from the district round Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
and from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built villages for themselves round Jerusalem.
The priests and the Levites made themselves clean, and they made the people clean, and the gates and the wall.
Then I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the right on the wall towards the Dung Gate.
After them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah,
and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah,
and some of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
and his relatives Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the scribe went in front of them.
At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the city of David on the rise of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east.
The second choir of those who gave thanks went to the left, and I followed them with half of the people on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall,
and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Old Gate and the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate, and they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
So the two choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me,
and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah, with trumpets,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam and Ezer. The singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.
They offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.

On that day men were appointed over the rooms for the stores, the contributions, the first fruits and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions required by the law for the priests and the Levites, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who served.
They kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were leaders of the singers and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah all Israel gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers. They set apart the portion for the Levites, and the Levites set apart the portion for the descendants of Aaron.
On that day they read from the book of Moses in the hearing of the people, and in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite was ever to enter the assembly of God,
because they did not meet the Israelites with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them. But our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel everyone of mixed descent.
Before this, Eliashib the priest, who had been put in charge of the rooms of the house of our God and who was related to Tobiah,

had prepared for Tobiah a large room where they had previously stored the grain offering, the incense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, new wine and oil that were commanded for the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.
I was not in Jerusalem while all this was going on, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone back to the king. After some time I asked leave of the king
and came to Jerusalem, and then I learned about the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah in preparing a room for him in the courts of the house of God.
I was very angry, and I threw all of Tobiah's household belongings out of the room.
Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the rooms, and I put back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the incense.
I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers who did the work had gone back each to his own field.
So I confronted the officials and said, "Why has the house of God been neglected?" And I gathered them together and put them back in their places.
Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, new wine and oil into the storerooms.

I put in charge of the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah from the Levites, and under them Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered trustworthy, and their task was to distribute to their relatives.
Remember me for this, my God, and do not wipe out the good that I have done for the house of my God and for its services.

In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs and every kind of load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day. I warned them on the day they sold food.
Men of Tyre who lived there also brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself.
I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, treating the sabbath day as common?
Did your ancestors not do the same, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? Yet you are bringing more anger on Israel by treating the sabbath as common."

When it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the sabbath, I ordered that the doors be shut and told them not to open them until after the sabbath. I put some of my servants at the gates, so that no load could be brought in on the sabbath day.
Once or twice the traders and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
But I warned them and said, "Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will use force against you." From that time they did not come on the sabbath.

I told the Levites to make themselves clean and to come and guard the gates, to keep the sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favour, my God, and have compassion on me according to your great faithful love.
In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of the other people.

I confronted them and cursed them, and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. I made them swear by God: "You are not to give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

Did Solomon king of Israel not sin because of women like these? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet even he was led into sin by foreign women.
Are we then to listen to you and do all this great evil and be unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, because they have made the priesthood unclean and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
So I cleansed them of everything foreign, and I set up duties for the priests and the Levites, each in his own work,
and provided for the wood offering at set times and for the first fruits. Remember me for good, my God.
In the days of Ahasuerus (the Ahasuerus who ruled from India to Cush, over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces),
in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on his royal throne in Susa the citadel,
in the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants. The army of Persia and Media, the nobles and the governors of the provinces were before him,
while he displayed the wealth of his glorious kingdom and the splendour and pride of his greatness for many days, a hundred and eighty days.
When these days were over, the king gave a banquet lasting seven days for all the people, great and small, who were in Susa the citadel, in the court of the garden of the king's palace.

There were white cotton curtains and blue hangings, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings on marble pillars, and couches of gold and silver on a floor of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl and other precious stones.
Drinks were served in golden cups, each cup different from the others, and the royal wine was plentiful, as the king could afford.
The drinking followed this order: "No one is to be forced." For the king had ordered all the officials of his house to do as each man wished.
Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Ahasuerus.
On the seventh day, when the king was merry with wine, he ordered Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar and Carkas, the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus,
to bring Queen Vashti before the king, wearing her royal crown, to show her beauty to the peoples and the officials, for she was beautiful to look at.
But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs. The king was very angry, and his anger burned in him.
