I will take my stand at my watchpost and station myself on the tower, and look out to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
And the LORD answered me: Write down the vision, and make it clear on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
For the vision still awaits its appointed time. It hurries toward the end and does not lie. If it seems slow, wait for it. It will surely come. It will not delay.
See, the proud one, his soul is not upright within him, but the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

Moreover, wine is treacherous. The arrogant man does not abide. His greed is as wide as Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers to himself all nations and collects all peoples as his own.
Will not all these take up a taunt against him, in scoffing and riddles against him, and say: Woe to the one who piles up what is not his own (for how long?) and loads himself with pledges.
Will not your creditors suddenly arise, and those awake who will make you tremble? Then you will be plunder for them.
Because you have plundered many nations, all that are left of the peoples will plunder you, for the blood of human beings and violence to the earth, to cities and all who live in them.
Woe to the one who gains evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high, to be safe from the reach of harm.
You have devised shame for your house by cutting off many peoples. You have forfeited your life.
For the stone cries out from the wall, and the beam from the woodwork answers.
Woe to the one who builds a town with blood and founds a city on iniquity.
Is it not from the LORD of hosts that peoples labour for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
Woe to the one who makes his neighbours drink, pouring out your wrath and making them drunk, in order to gaze at their nakedness.
You will have your fill of shame instead of glory. Drink, you yourself, and show your uncircumcision. The cup in the LORD's right hand will come around to you, and shame will come on your glory.

The violence done to Lebanon will overwhelm you, as will the destruction of the animals that terrified them, for the blood of human beings and violence to the earth, to cities and all who live in them.
What profit is an idol when its maker has shaped it, a metal image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own creation when he makes speechless idols.
Woe to the one who says to a wooden thing, "Awake," to a silent stone, "Arise." Can this teach? See, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in it.
But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him.
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
LORD, I have heard the report of you, and your work, LORD, I fear. In the midst of the years revive it, in the midst of the years make it known. In wrath remember mercy.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. *Selah* His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.
His brightness was like the light, rays flashed from his hand, and there his power was hidden.
Before him went pestilence, and plague followed at his heels.
He stood and measured the earth. He looked and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains were shattered, the everlasting hills sank low. His ways are everlasting.
I saw the tents of Cushan under affliction. The tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
Was your wrath against the rivers, LORD? Was your anger against the rivers, or your indignation against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariot of salvation?
You stripped the sheath from your bow, sworn were the rods of the tribes. *Selah* You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw you and writhed. The raging waters swept on. The deep gave its voice, it lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their place, at the light of your arrows as they sped, at the flash of your glittering spear.
In fury you marched through the earth, in anger you trampled the nations.
You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed one. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying him bare from foundation to neck. *Selah*
You pierced with his own arrows the heads of his warriors, who came like a whirlwind to scatter me, rejoicing as if to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the great waters.

I heard, and my body trembled. My lips quivered at the sound. Rottenness entered my bones, and my legs trembled beneath me. Yet I will quietly wait for the day of trouble to come on the people who invade us.

Though the fig tree does not blossom, and no fruit is on the vines, the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food, the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls,
yet I will rejoice in the LORD. I will exult in the God of my salvation.
God, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and makes me walk on my heights. For the choirmaster: with stringed instruments.
The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.

I will sweep away humans and animals. I will sweep away the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and the rubble with the wicked. I will cut off humankind from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.

I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal and the name of the idolatrous priests along with the priests,
those who bow down on the roofs to the host of heaven, those who bow down and swear to the LORD and yet swear by Milcom,
those who have turned away from following the LORD, who do not seek the LORD or inquire of him.
Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice and consecrated his guests.
And on the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the officials and the king's sons and all who clothe themselves in foreign garments.
On that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, and those who fill their master's house with violence and fraud.
On that day, declares the LORD, a cry will go up from the Fish Gate, a wail from the Second Quarter, a loud crash from the hills.
Wail, you inhabitants of the Mortar. For all the traders are no more, all who weigh out silver are cut off.
At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the people who are thickened on their dregs, who say in their hearts, "The LORD will not do good, nor will he do harm."
Their wealth will be plundered, and their houses laid waste. Though they build houses, they will not live in them. Though they plant vineyards, they will not drink their wine.
The great day of the LORD is near, near and hastening fast. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter. The warrior cries aloud there.
A day of wrath is that day, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the lofty corner towers.
I will bring distress on humankind, so that they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed, for he will make a full and sudden end of all the inhabitants of the earth.
Gather together, gather, nation without shame,
before the decree takes effect (the day passes like chaff), before the burning anger of the LORD comes on you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes on you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who do his justice. Seek righteousness, seek humility. Perhaps you may be hidden on the day of the LORD's anger.
For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation. The people of Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron uprooted.
Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites. The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: I will destroy you until no inhabitant is left.
And you, seacoast, will be pastures, meadows for shepherds and folds for flocks.

The coast will become the possession of the remnant of the house of Judah, on which they will graze. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down at evening, for the LORD their God will care for them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard the taunts of Moab and the revilings of the Ammonites, how they taunted my people and made boasts against their territory.

Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, a land possessed by weeds and salt pits, and a waste for ever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the survivors of my nation will possess them.
This will be their lot in return for their pride, because they taunted and boasted against the people of the LORD of hosts.
The LORD will be awesome against them, for he will famish all the gods of the earth, and to him will bow down, each in its place, all the coasts of the nations.
You also, Cushites, will be slain by my sword.
And he will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria, and he will make Nineveh a desolation, a dry waste like the desert.

Herds will lie down in her midst, every wild animal of the nations. The desert owl and the screech owl will lodge on her capitals. A voice will sing in the window, rubble will be on the threshold, for he has laid bare the cedar work.

This is the exultant city that lived securely, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is no one else." What a desolation she has become, a lair for wild animals. Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
Woe to her who is rebellious and defiled, the oppressing city.
She listens to no voice. She accepts no correction. She does not trust in the LORD. She does not draw near to her God.
Her officials within her are roaring lions. Her judges are wolves of the evening that leave nothing for the morning.
Her prophets are reckless, treacherous people. Her priests profane what is holy, they do violence to the teaching.
The LORD within her is righteous. He does no injustice. Every morning he brings his justice to light. He does not fail. But the unjust knows no shame.
I have cut off nations. Their corner towers are in ruins. I have laid waste their streets so that no one passes by. Their cities are made desolate, without people, without inhabitant.

I said, Surely you will fear me, you will accept correction. Then her dwelling would not be cut off according to all that I appointed against her. But all the more they were eager to make all their deeds corrupt.

Therefore wait for me, declares the LORD, for the day when I rise up as a witness. For my decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all my burning anger. For in the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed.
For at that time I will change the speech of the peoples to a pure speech, that all of them may call on the name of the LORD and serve him with one accord.
From beyond the rivers of Cush my worshippers, my scattered ones, will bring my offering.

On that day you will not be put to shame because of all the deeds by which you have rebelled against me. For then I will remove from your midst your proudly exultant ones, and you will no more be haughty in my holy mountain.
But I will leave in your midst a people humble and lowly. They will seek refuge in the name of the LORD,
those who are left in Israel. They will do no injustice and speak no lies, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths. For they will graze and lie down, and none will make them afraid.
Sing aloud, daughter of Zion. Shout, Israel. Be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.
The LORD has taken away the judgements against you. He has cleared away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst. You will never again fear evil.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: Do not fear, Zion. Do not let your hands grow weak.
The LORD your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness. He will quiet you by his love, he will exult over you with loud singing.
I will gather those of you who mourn for the festival, so that you will no longer bear reproach on account of it.
See, at that time I will deal with all your oppressors. And I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will change their shame into praise and renown in all the earth.

At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you. For I will make you renowned and praised among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.

In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: This people say, "The time has not come to rebuild the house of the LORD."
Then the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your panelled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
Now therefore thus says the LORD of hosts: Consider your ways.

You have sown much, and harvested little. You eat, but never have enough. You drink, but never have your fill. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm. And the one who earns wages earns them to put into a bag with holes.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Consider your ways.
Go up to the hills and bring wood and build the house, that I may take pleasure in it and be honoured, says the LORD.

You looked for much, and see, it came to little. And when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of hosts. Because of my house that lies in ruins, while each of you is busy with his own house.
Therefore the heavens above you have withheld the dew, and the earth has withheld its produce.
And I have called for a drought on the land and the hills, on the grain, the new wine, the oil, on what the ground brings forth, on people and animals, and on all the labour of their hands.

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.
Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, spoke to the people with the LORD's message: I am with you, declares the LORD.

And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and worked on the house of the LORD of hosts, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, and say:
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?

Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD, and work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts,
according to the word that I made with you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit remains in your midst. Do not fear.
For thus says the LORD of hosts: Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.
And I will shake all the nations, so that the treasures of all nations will come in, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of hosts.
The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts. And in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
Thus says the LORD of hosts: Ask the priests for a ruling:
If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with the fold touches bread or stew or wine or oil or any food, does it become holy? The priests answered and said, "No."
Then Haggai said, "If someone made unclean by a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?" And the priests answered and said, "It becomes unclean."
Then Haggai answered and said, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so is every work of their hands. And what they offer there is unclean.
Now therefore consider, from this day onward: before one stone was laid on another in the temple of the LORD,
how did you fare? When one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were ten. When one came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures, there were twenty.
I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight and mildew and hail, yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
Consider from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. From the day that the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, consider.
Is the seed still in the barn? Until now the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not borne fruit. But from this day I will bless you.
The word of the LORD came a second time to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I am about to shake the heavens and the earth,

and to overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I am about to destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations, and overthrow the chariots and their riders. And the horses and their riders will go down, each by the sword of his brother.

On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, son of Shealtiel, declares the LORD, and make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts.
In the eighth month of Darius's second year, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
The LORD burned with anger against your fathers.
So tell the people: This is what the LORD of hosts says. Return to me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.

Do not be like your fathers. The earlier prophets called out to them, "This is what the LORD of hosts says: Return from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they would not listen, and they paid me no heed, declares the LORD.
Your fathers, where are they now? And the prophets, did they live for ever?

Yet my words and my statutes, which I gave to my servants the prophets, caught up with your fathers. They came back and said, "The LORD of hosts did to us exactly what he had planned, because of our ways and our deeds."
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in Darius's second year, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
In the night I saw a man riding a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in the hollow, and behind him were horses, red, brown and white.
I asked, "Sir, what are these?" The angel who was speaking with me said, "I will show you what they are."
The man standing among the myrtles explained, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to roam the earth."
They reported to the angel of the LORD who stood among the myrtles, "We have roamed the earth, and the whole earth is still and at rest."
Then the angel of the LORD said, "LORD of hosts, how long will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, which have felt your anger these seventy years?"
The LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind words, words of comfort.
Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Proclaim this. The LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion, with a great jealousy.
And I am fiercely angry with the nations that sit at ease. I was only a little angry, but they made the disaster worse.
So the LORD says: I have come back to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be built there, declares the LORD of hosts, and the measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
Proclaim again: The LORD of hosts says: My towns will again overflow with good things. The LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.
I looked up and saw four horns.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He answered, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
Then the LORD showed me four metalworkers.

I asked, "What have these come to do?" He said, "The horns scattered Judah so completely that no one could lift his head. These workers have come to terrify the horns, to cut down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against the land of Judah to scatter its people."
I looked up and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
I asked, "Where are you going?" He answered, "To measure Jerusalem, to find out how wide it is and how long."
Then the angel who was speaking with me stepped forward, and another angel came out to meet him
and said to him, "Run and tell that young man: Jerusalem will be a city without walls, spread out like villages, because of the many people and animals living in it.
I myself will be a wall of fire all round her, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within her."
Up, up. Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD. I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven, declares the LORD.
Up, Zion. Escape, you who live with the daughter of Babylon.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: After glory he sent me against the nations that plundered you. Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
See, I will raise my hand against them, and they will become loot for their own slaves. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts sent me.
Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for I am coming to live among you, declares the LORD.
On that day many nations will attach themselves to the LORD and become my people. I will live among you, and you will know that the LORD of hosts sent me to you.
The LORD will take Judah as his own share in the holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for he has stirred himself from his holy dwelling.
Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the adversary standing at his right to accuse him.
The LORD said to the adversary, "The LORD rebuke you, adversary. The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you. Is this man not a stick pulled from the fire?"
Joshua was standing before the angel in filthy clothes.
The angel spoke to those standing before him: "Take the filthy clothes off him." And to Joshua he said, "See, I have removed your guilt from you, and I will dress you in fine robes."
I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head and dressed him in robes, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
Then the angel of the LORD gave Joshua this solemn charge:

This is what the LORD of hosts says. If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, then you will govern my house and guard my courts, and I will give you a place to walk among these who are standing here.
Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your colleagues sitting before you, for they are people of good omen: I am bringing my servant the Branch.
Look at the stone I have set before Joshua, a single stone with seven eyes. I will engrave its inscription, declares the LORD of hosts, and in one day I will remove the guilt of this land.
On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, you will invite one another to sit under the vine and under the fig tree.
The angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, as a sleeper is woken.
He asked, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a lampstand made entirely of gold, with a bowl on top, and seven lamps on it, each of the lamps on top having seven spouts.
Beside it stand two olive trees, one to the right of the bowl and one to its left."
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Sir, what are these?"
The angel who was speaking with me answered, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, sir."
He said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by force, not by strength, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will be level ground. He will bring out the top stone to shouts of 'Favour, favour to it.'"
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation of this house, and Zerubbabel's hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts sent me to you.
Who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel's hand. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, ranging over the whole earth."
I asked him, "What are these two olive trees to the right and left of the lampstand?"
And again I asked him, "What are these two olive branches beside the two golden spouts that pour out the golden oil?"
He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, sir."
He said, "These are the two who are anointed with fresh oil, who stand beside the Lord of the whole earth."
I looked up again and saw a scroll flying.
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

He said to me, "This is the curse going out over the whole land. Every thief will be swept away, as the writing on one side says, and everyone who swears falsely will be swept away, as the writing on the other side says.

I have sent it out, declares the LORD of hosts. It will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name, and it will stay inside his house and destroy it, timber and stones together."
The angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me, "Look up and see what is coming out."
I asked, "What is it?" He said, "It is the basket coming out." And he said, "This is how they look throughout the land."
Then a disc of lead was lifted, and there sat a woman inside the basket.
He said, "This is Wickedness." He pushed her down into the basket and shoved the lead weight over its mouth.
I looked up and saw two women coming, with the wind in their wings. They had wings like a stork's, and they lifted the basket between earth and sky.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"
He said to me, "To the land of Shinar, to build a house for it. When it is ready, the basket will be set down there on its own base."
Again I looked up and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses, the second black horses,
the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses, all of them powerful.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Sir, what are these?"
The angel answered me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of the whole earth.
The chariot with the black horses is going to the northern land, the white follow behind them, and the dappled are going to the southern land."
The powerful horses came out, eager to go and roam the earth. He said, "Go and roam the earth." And they roamed the earth.
Then he called out to me, "Look, those going to the northern land have set my Spirit at rest in the northern land."
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Take silver and gold from the exiles, from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon, and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
Make crowns from the silver and gold, and put them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Tell him: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch. He will sprout up from where he is, and he will build the temple of the LORD.

He is the one who will build the temple of the LORD. He will carry royal splendour, and sit and rule on his throne. And there will be a priest on his throne, and the counsel of peace will be between the two of them.
The crowns will stay in the temple of the LORD as a reminder to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah.
Those who are far away will come and help build the temple of the LORD. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts sent me to you. This will happen if you truly obey the voice of the LORD your God."
In the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chislev, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah.
Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regemmelech and their men to seek the LORD's favour,
and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts, and the prophets: "Should I go on weeping and fasting in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?"
Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
Tell all the people of the land and the priests: For these seventy years you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months. Was it really for me that you fasted?
And when you eat and drink, is it not you who are eating and you who are drinking?
Are these not the words the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was settled and prosperous, with her towns around her, and the Negeb and the lowland were settled too?
The word of the LORD came to Zechariah again:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Judge with true judgement. Show faithful love and compassion to one another.
Do not exploit the widow or the orphan, the foreigner or the poor, and do not plot evil against each other in your hearts.
But they refused to listen. They turned a stubborn shoulder and blocked their ears so they could not hear.

They made their hearts hard as flint, so that they could not hear the teaching and the words the LORD of hosts had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So the LORD of hosts burned with great anger.
"Just as I called and they would not listen, so they will call and I will not listen," says the LORD of hosts.
"I scattered them in a whirlwind among all the nations they had never known. The land was left empty behind them, with no one passing through, and they turned a pleasant land into a wasteland."
The word of the LORD of hosts came:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Zion, with great jealousy. I am jealous for her with great fury.
This is what the LORD says: I have come back to Zion and will live in Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the faithful city, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the holy mountain.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Old men and women will again sit in Jerusalem's squares, each leaning on a staff, so old they are.
The city's squares will be crowded with boys and girls at play.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: It may seem impossible to the remnant of this people in those days, but will it seem impossible to me? declares the LORD of hosts.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: I will rescue my people from the lands of the east and the west,
and bring them back to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in faithfulness and in righteousness.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: Be strong, you who now hear these words from the prophets, the same words they spoke on the day the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, so that the temple could be built.
Before that time there were no wages for people or animals, and no one could come or go in safety because of the enemy, for I set everyone against his neighbour.
But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in the past, declares the LORD of hosts.
Peace will be sown: the vine will yield its fruit, the soil its harvest, and the heavens their dew. I will give all of this to the remnant of this people.
You, house of Judah and house of Israel, have been a curse among the nations. So I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not fear. Be strong.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: I resolved to bring disaster on you when your fathers provoked me, and I did not relent, says the LORD of hosts.
In the same way I have now resolved to do good to Jerusalem and the house of Judah. Do not fear.
This is what you are to do: Speak truth to one another. Give judgement in your gates that is true and brings peace.
Do not plot evil against each other in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for I hate all of these things, declares the LORD.
The word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become joy and gladness, happy festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Peoples will yet come, the inhabitants of many cities.
The inhabitants of one city will go to another and say, "Let us go at once to seek the LORD's favour and to look for the LORD of hosts. I am going too."
Many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to look for the LORD of hosts and to seek the LORD's favour.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: In those days ten people from nations of every language will take hold of one Judean by the hem of his robe and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."
An oracle. The LORD's word is against the land of Hadrach and rests on Damascus, for the eyes of humankind and of all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD,
and on Hamath, which borders it, and on Tyre and Sidon, for all their great skill.
Tyre built herself a stronghold, piled up silver like dust and gold like street mud.
But the Lord will dispossess her and hurl her power into the sea, and fire will devour her.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid. Gaza will writhe in pain, and so will Ekron, for her hope has withered. Gaza will lose her king, and Ashkelon will be empty of people.
A people of mixed blood will settle in Ashdod, and I will cut down the pride of the Philistines.
I will take the blood out of their mouths and the abominations from between their teeth. Those who remain will belong to our God and become a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
I will camp around my house as its guard, so that no one passes through. No oppressor will overrun them again, for now I am watching with my own eyes.
Celebrate loudly, daughter of Zion. Shout in triumph, daughter of Jerusalem. See, your king is coming to you, righteous and victorious, humble, riding on a donkey, on a colt, a donkey's foal.

I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the war horse from Jerusalem. The bow of war will be cut off. He will speak peace to the nations, and his rule will reach from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
And you, because of the blood of my covenant with you, I will free your prisoners from the pit with no water.
Come back to the fortress, prisoners of hope. Today I declare that I will repay you double.
I have bent Judah like a bow and fitted Ephraim like an arrow. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you a warrior's sword.
The LORD will appear above them, and his arrow will flash like lightning. The Lord GOD will blow the horn and march out in the storms of the south.
The LORD of hosts will shield them. They will devour and trample the slingstones, and they will drink and roar as if drunk on wine, filled like a bowl, drenched like the corners of the altar.
On that day the LORD their God will save them, his people, like a flock. They will sparkle like jewels in a crown over his land.
How good and how lovely it will be: grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the late rains. The LORD makes the storm clouds and gives showers to everyone, grass in the field to each person.
The household gods speak nonsense, the diviners see lies, and the dreamers tell false dreams and give empty comfort. So the people wander like sheep, in trouble for lack of a shepherd.
My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the lead goats. For the LORD of hosts will tend his flock, the house of Judah, and make them like his proud warhorse in battle.
From them will come the cornerstone, from them the tent peg, from them the battle bow, from them every ruler together.
Together they will be like warriors trampling the street mud in battle. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and they will shame the riders on horses.

I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back because I have had compassion on them, and they will be as if I had never rejected them, for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their hearts will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and rejoice, and their hearts will exult in the LORD.
I will whistle to them and gather them, for I have redeemed them, and they will be as numerous as they once were.
Though I scatter them like seed among the nations, in distant lands they will remember me. They will live with their children and return.
I will bring them home from Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon until there is no more room.
He will cross the sea of distress and strike down its waves, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. Assyria's pride will be brought down, and Egypt's sceptre will be taken away.
I will make them strong in the LORD, and they will walk in his name, declares the LORD.
Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire eat your cedars.
Howl, cypress, for the cedar has fallen, the mighty trees are ruined. Howl, oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has been cut down.
Listen to the shepherds howling, for their splendour is ruined. Listen to the lions roaring, for the Jordan's thickets are ruined.
This is what the LORD my God said: Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished, and their sellers say, "Praise the LORD, I am rich." Even their own shepherds have no pity on them.

For I will no longer have pity on the people of this land, declares the LORD. I will hand each of them over to his neighbour and to his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hands.

So I became the shepherd of the flock marked for slaughter, for the sake of the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs. One I called Favour and the other I called Union, and I shepherded the flock.
In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. But my patience ran out with them, and they came to loathe me too.
Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die and the perishing perish, and let the survivors eat one another's flesh."
I took my staff Favour and broke it, cancelling the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
It was cancelled that day, and the afflicted of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
I said to them, "If you think it right, pay me my wages. If not, keep them." So they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
The LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter, that splendid price at which they valued me." So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.
Then I broke my second staff, Union, cancelling the family bond between Judah and Israel.
The LORD said to me, Take up once more the gear of a worthless shepherd.

For I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not look after the lost, will not search for the young, will not heal the broken, and will not feed the healthy, but will eat the meat of the fat ones and tear off their hoofs.
Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock. May a sword strike his arm and his right eye. May his arm shrivel completely and his right eye go totally blind.
An oracle. The LORD's word about Israel. A declaration of the LORD, who spread out the heavens, laid the foundation of the earth, and shaped the spirit within each person:
I am making Jerusalem a cup that sends all the surrounding peoples reeling. Judah too will be caught up in the siege of Jerusalem.
On that day I will make Jerusalem a boulder too heavy for any of the peoples. Everyone who tries to lift it will tear himself to pieces, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it.

On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with terror and every rider with madness. But over the house of Judah I will keep my eyes open, while I strike every horse of the peoples blind.
Then the clans of Judah will say to themselves, "The people of Jerusalem are strong, because the LORD of hosts is their God."

On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a firepot among logs, like a burning torch among cut grain. They will burn up the peoples around them, right and left, and Jerusalem will go on living where she stands, in Jerusalem.
The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the splendour of David's house and of the people of Jerusalem will not rise above Judah's.
On that day the LORD will shield the people of Jerusalem. Even the weakest among them will be like David on that day, and David's house will be like God, like the angel of the LORD at their head.
On that day I will set out to destroy every nation that comes against Jerusalem.

I will pour out on David's house and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of favour and pleading. They will look to me, whom they have pierced, and mourn over him as people mourn for an only child, and grieve bitterly over him as people grieve for a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning at Hadad-rimmon in the valley of Megiddo.
The land will mourn, every clan on its own: the clan of David's house on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of Nathan's house on its own, and their wives on their own;
the clan of Levi's house on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of the Shimeites on its own, and their wives on their own;
and all the other clans, each on its own, and their wives on their own.
On that day a spring will be opened for David's house and for the people of Jerusalem, to wash away sin and impurity.
On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will wipe the names of the idols from the land, and no one will remember them. I will also drive the prophets and the spirit of impurity out of the land.

If anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother will say to him, "You will not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the LORD's name." And his father and mother, who gave him birth, will stab him as he prophesies.
On that day each prophet will be ashamed of his vision as he prophesies. He will not put on the hairy cloak to deceive,
but will say, "I am no prophet. I work the soil, for a man has owned me since I was young."
And if someone asks him, "What are these wounds between your arms?" he will say, "I was wounded in the house of those who love me."
Sword, wake up against my shepherd, against the man who stands beside me, declares the LORD of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and the flock will scatter. I will turn my hand against the little ones.
Throughout the land, declares the LORD, two parts will be cut off and die, and one part will be left.

I will bring that third through the fire, refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say, "They are my people," and they will say, "The LORD is my God."
A day is coming for the LORD, when the loot taken from you will be shared out among you.

I will gather all the nations to fight against Jerusalem. The city will fall, the houses will be looted, and the women will be raped. Half the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be removed from the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight those nations, as he fights on a day of battle.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives will split in two from east to west, leaving a huge valley, as half the mountain shifts north and half south.

You will flee through my mountain valley, for the valley between the mountains will reach as far as Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the LORD my God will come, with all the holy ones beside him.
On that day there will be no light; the bright ones will thicken and stiffen.
It will be a day unlike any other, known to the LORD alone, neither day nor night. And at evening there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out of Jerusalem, half toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea, in summer and in winter alike.
The LORD will be king over the whole earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.

The whole land will be flattened into a plain, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will stand high in her place, from Benjamin's Gate to the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
People will live in her, and there will be no more ban of destruction. Jerusalem will live in safety.

This is the plague with which the LORD will strike every people that has gone to war against Jerusalem: each one's flesh will waste away as he stands on his feet, his eyes will waste away in their sockets, and his tongue will waste away in his mouth.
On that day a great confusion from the LORD will come over them. Each will grip his neighbour's hand, and each will turn his hand against his neighbour.
Judah too will fight in Jerusalem. The wealth of all the nations around will be gathered in, gold and silver and clothing in huge amounts.
The same plague will strike horse and mule, camel and donkey, and every animal in those camps.
Then all who are left of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up every year to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
Any of the families of the earth that do not go up to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, will have no rain.
If the family of Egypt does not go up and come in, they too will have no rain. The plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths will fall on them.
This will be the penalty for Egypt, and the penalty for every nation that does not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
On that day the horses' bells will carry the words "Holy to the LORD", and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be as holy as the bowls before the altar.

Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts. All who come to sacrifice will take some and cook in them. And on that day there will be no more traders in the house of the LORD of hosts.
An oracle. The word of the LORD to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
"I have loved you," says the LORD. But you ask, "How have you loved us?" Was Esau not Jacob's brother? declares the LORD. Yet I loved Jacob,
and Esau I hated. I made his hill country a wasteland and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.

If Edom says, "We are shattered, but we will rebuild the ruins," this is what the LORD of hosts says: Let them build, and I will tear down. They will be called the Land of Wickedness, the people the LORD has been angry with for ever.
Your own eyes will see it, and you will say, "The LORD is great, far beyond the border of Israel."

A son honours his father, and a servant his master. So if I am a father, where is the honour due to me? If I am a master, where is the fear due to me? says the LORD of hosts to you, priests, who despise my name. You say, "How have we despised your name?"
You offer polluted food on my altar. You say, "How have we polluted you?" By saying, "The LORD's table can be treated with contempt."

When you offer a blind animal for sacrifice, is nothing wrong? When you offer one that is lame or sick, is nothing wrong? Try giving it to your governor. Will he be pleased with you? Will he welcome you? says the LORD of hosts.
So now, try to soften the face of God, that he may be gracious to us. With gifts like these in your hands, will he welcome any of you? says the LORD of hosts.

If only one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would stop lighting my altar fire for nothing. I take no pleasure in you, says the LORD of hosts, and I will accept no offering from your hands.

From the rising of the sun to its setting, my name is great among the nations. Everywhere incense is burned to my name, with a pure offering, for my name is great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
But you profane it when you say, "The LORD's table is polluted, and its food can be treated with contempt."

You say, "What a burden," and you sniff at it, says the LORD of hosts. You bring what was seized, the lame and the sick, and present these as your offering. Should I accept them from your hands? says the LORD.

A curse on the cheat who has a healthy male in his flock, vows to give it, and then sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great king, says the LORD of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.
And now, this command is for you, priests.

If you will not listen, and will not take it to heart to give honour to my name, says the LORD of hosts, I will send the curse on you and turn your blessings into curses. Indeed I have already cursed them, because you have not taken it to heart.
See, I will rebuke your offspring, and spread dung on your faces, the dung of your festival offerings, and you will be carried off with it.
Then you will know that I sent you this command, so that my covenant with Levi may continue, says the LORD of hosts.
My covenant with him was life and peace, and I gave them to him, with fear, and he feared me and stood in awe of my name.
The teaching of truth was in his mouth, and nothing false was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many away from iniquity.
For a priest's lips should guard knowledge, and people should seek teaching from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
But you have turned aside from the way. You have made many stumble by your teaching. You have ruined the covenant of Levi, says the LORD of hosts.
So I in turn have made you despised and low before all the people, because you do not keep my ways but show favouritism in your teaching.
Do we not all have one father? Did one God not create us? Why then do we break faith with one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
Judah has broken faith, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the holy place of the LORD, which he loves, by marrying the daughter of a foreign god.
May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob anyone who does this, the one who is awake and the one who answers, even one who brings an offering to the LORD of hosts.
And this is something else you do: you cover the LORD's altar with tears, with weeping and groaning, because he no longer looks at the offering or accepts it with favour from your hand.
You ask, "Why?" Because the LORD stood as witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.
Did he not make one, with a remnant of the spirit in her? And what was the one seeking? Offspring from God. So guard your spirit, and let no one be faithless to the wife of his youth.
For he hates sending away, says the LORD, the God of Israel, and he covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. So guard your spirit, and do not be faithless.

You have wearied the LORD with your words. You ask, "How have we wearied him?" By saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the LORD's eyes, and he delights in them," or, "Where is the God of justice?"

See, I am sending my messenger, and he will clear the way before me. And suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his temple, the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight. See, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like the soap of launderers.
He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, until they bring offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD as in days of old, as in former years.

I will come near to you for judgement. I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, against adulterers, against those who swear falsely, against those who cheat workers of their wages, who oppress the widow and the orphan, who push the foreigner aside, and who do not fear me, says the LORD of hosts.
I, the LORD, do not change, and so you, descendants of Jacob, have not been destroyed.
Since the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts. But you ask, "How are we to return?"
Will a human being rob God? Yet you rob me. You ask, "How have we robbed you?" In tithes and contributions.
You are under a curse, the whole nation of you, for you are robbing me.

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house. Test me in this, says the LORD of hosts, and see whether I will not open the windows of heaven for you and pour out blessing until there is no more need.
I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the produce of your soil, and your vine in the field will not lose its fruit, says the LORD of hosts.
Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says the LORD of hosts.
You have spoken harsh words against me, says the LORD. Yet you ask, "What have we said against you?"
You have said, "It is pointless to serve God. What do we gain by keeping his charge, or by walking about in mourning before the LORD of hosts?
So now we call the arrogant blessed. Evildoers are built up, and those who test God escape."
Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another. The LORD listened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before him for those who fear the LORD and honour his name.
They will be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my own treasured possession on the day I act. I will have compassion on them as a man has compassion on his son who serves him.
Then you will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not.

See, the day is coming, burning like a furnace. All the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the LORD of hosts, leaving them neither root nor branch.
But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing will be in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves from the stall.
You will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day I act, says the LORD of hosts.
Remember the teaching of my servant Moses, the statutes and judgements I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.
See, I am sending you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, so that I will not come and strike the land with a ban of destruction.
The record of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
Judah fathered Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar. Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram.
Ram fathered Amminadab, Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
Salmon fathered Boaz, whose mother was Rahab. Boaz fathered Obed, whose mother was Ruth. Obed fathered Jesse,
and Jesse fathered King David. David fathered Solomon, whose mother had been the wife of Uriah.
Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asa.
Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.
Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amon, and Amon fathered Josiah.
Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor.
Azor fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud.
Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob.
Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, and from Mary was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
So the generations from Abraham to David total fourteen, from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen.
This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about. His mother Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they lived together she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband-to-be, was a righteous man and did not want to shame her in public, so he planned to end the engagement quietly.

While he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream: "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife. The child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins."
All of this happened so that what the Lord said through the prophet would come true:
"See, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and they will name him Emmanuel" (which means "God is with us").
When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had told him and took Mary home as his wife.
But he did not have intercourse with her until she gave birth to a son, and he named him Jesus.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, in the days of King Herod. Soon afterwards, magi from the east came to Jerusalem
asking, "Where is the newborn king of the Jews? We saw his star rising, and we have come to bow before him."
King Herod heard this and was shaken, and all Jerusalem with him.
He called together all the chief priests and the scribes of the people, and asked where the Christ was to be born.
"In Bethlehem in Judea," they told him. "This is what the prophet wrote:
'And you, Bethlehem in the land of Judah, are far from the least among Judah's leaders, for from you will come a leader who will shepherd my people Israel.'"
Then Herod called the magi aside in secret and found out from them exactly when the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem. "Go and make a careful search for the child," he said. "When you have found him, bring me word, so that I too can go and bow before him."
They heard the king and set out. And the star they had seen rising went ahead of them until it stopped above the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, their joy was enormous.
They entered the house, saw the child with his mother Mary, fell to the ground and bowed before him. They opened their treasure boxes and presented him with gold, frankincense and myrrh.
Warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country by a different road.

After they had left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. "Get up," he said. "Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is about to hunt for the child in order to kill him."
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother in the night, and left for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod's death. This fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: "I called my son out of Egypt."

When Herod realised that the magi had outwitted him, he was enraged. He sent and had every boy killed in Bethlehem and the whole district who was two years old or younger, going by the time he had learned from the magi.
Then the words spoken through the prophet Jeremiah came true:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and bitter grief. Rachel was weeping for her children, and would not be consoled, because they were gone."
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who wanted the child's life are dead."
He got up, took the child and his mother, and went into the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was king in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he left for the region of Galilee
and settled in a town called Nazareth. So what was said through the prophets came true: "He will be called a Nazarene."
In those days John the Baptist appeared, announcing in the Judean wilderness,
"Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
This is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke of: "A voice shouting in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight."
John wore clothing of camel hair with a leather belt round his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
People went out to him from Jerusalem, from all Judea, and from the whole region around the Jordan,
and in the Jordan river they were baptised by him as they confessed their sins.
When he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said to them, "You brood of snakes, who warned you to run from the coming wrath?
Produce fruit that matches repentance.
And do not suppose you can say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
The axe already lies at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptise you in water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I am, and I am not fit to carry his sandals. He will baptise you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor. He will gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with a fire that cannot be put out."
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptised by him.
John tried to stop him. "I need to be baptised by you," he said, "and you come to me?"
Jesus answered him, "Let it be so for now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfil all righteousness." Then John agreed.
After Jesus was baptised he came straight up out of the water. And suddenly the heavens opened, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and landing on him.
And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I take delight."
Then the Spirit led Jesus up into the wilderness to be tested by the devil.
After fasting for forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
The tester came and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become loaves of bread."
He answered, "It is written: 'A person will not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes out of God's mouth.'"
Then the devil took him to the holy city, stood him on the highest point of the temple,

and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. For it is written: 'He will give his angels orders about you, and they will carry you in their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus said to him, "It is also written: 'You are not to test the Lord your God.'"
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendour,
and said to him, "All this I will give you if you fall down and bow to me."
Then Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan. For it is written: 'You are to bow to the Lord your God and serve him alone.'"
Then the devil left him, and angels came and looked after him.
When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,
so that what was said through the prophet Isaiah would come true:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way to the sea, across the Jordan, Galilee of the nations,
the people living in darkness have seen a great light, and for those living in the region of the shadow of death, light has dawned."
From then on Jesus began to announce, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
As he was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew, throwing a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
He said to them, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of people."
At once they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. He called them,
and at once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
Jesus went all through Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, announcing the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria, and people brought him all who were ill, suffering from various diseases and pains, those possessed by demons, epileptics and paralysed people, and he healed them.
Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan.
Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him,
and he opened his mouth and taught them:
"Blessed are the destitute in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are the mourners, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the land.
Blessed are those hungering and thirsting for righteousness, for they will be fed to the full.
Blessed are the merciful, for mercy will be shown to them.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are those who make peace, for they will be called God's sons.
Blessed are those hounded because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are you whenever people reproach you, hound you, and lie about you, saying every kind of evil because of me.
Rejoice and leap for joy, for your reward in heaven is large. They hounded the prophets before you in just this way.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt goes flat, what will make it salty? It has no more use, except to be thrown outside and trampled underfoot.
You are the light of the world. A city lying on a hilltop cannot be hidden.
People do not light a lamp and set it under a measuring bowl. They set it on its stand, and it shines for everyone in the house.
So let your light shine in front of people, so that they will see the good you do and honour your Father in heaven.
Do not suppose that I have come to dismantle the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to dismantle but to fulfil.
Amen, I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter, not one pen-stroke, will pass from the Law until it has all taken place.

So whoever loosens one of the smallest of these commands, and teaches people to do likewise, will be called smallest in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever keeps and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
For I tell you that unless your righteousness is far greater than the scribes' and Pharisees', you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: 'You will not commit murder,' and 'Whoever commits murder will be answerable to the court.'

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be answerable to the court, whoever says to his brother 'Empty-head' will be answerable to the council, and whoever says 'Fool' will be answerable to the fire of Gehenna.
So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there in front of the altar and go. First make peace with your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Come to terms with your accuser quickly, while you are still with him on the road, or he will hand you to the judge, and the judge to the guard, and you will be thrown into prison.
Amen, I tell you: you will not get out of there until you have paid the last copper coin.
You have heard that it was said, 'You will not commit adultery.'
But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye trips you up, pull it out and throw it away. It is better for you that one of your limbs be lost than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand trips you up, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you that one of your limbs be lost than that your whole body go into Gehenna.
It was also said, 'Whoever sends his wife away must give her a divorce certificate.'
But I tell you that everyone who sends his wife away, except for a matter of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a woman who has been sent away commits adultery.
Again you have heard that it was said to those of old, 'You will not break an oath, but you will give the Lord what you have sworn.'
But I tell you: do not swear at all, not by heaven, for it is God's throne,
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool under his feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Do not swear by your head either, because you cannot turn one hair white or black.
Let your 'yes' be 'yes' and your 'no' be 'no.' Whatever goes beyond these comes from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said, 'Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.'
But I tell you: do not stand against the one who does evil. If someone hits you on the right cheek, offer him the other as well.
If someone wants to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak too.
If someone conscripts you for one mile, go with him for two.
Give to anyone who asks you, and do not turn away from anyone who wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said, 'You will love your neighbour and hate your enemy.'
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who hound you,
so that you may become sons of your Father in heaven. He makes his sun rise on the wicked and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
If you love only those who love you, what reward is there in that? Do the tax collectors not do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing that is out of the ordinary? Do the Gentiles not do the same?
You, then, are to be complete, just as your heavenly Father is complete."
Be careful not to do your righteousness in front of people so that they will watch you. Otherwise there is no reward for you with your Father in heaven.

So when you give to the poor, do not have a trumpet blown ahead of you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, to be praised by people. Amen, I tell you: they have been paid in full.
When you give to the poor, do not let your left hand find out what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving stays hidden. Your Father, who sees what is hidden, will pay you back.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand in the synagogues and on the corners of the squares and pray, so that people will see them. Amen, I tell you: they have been paid in full.
But when you pray, go into your storeroom, shut your door, and pray to your Father in the hidden place. Your Father, who sees what is hidden, will pay you back.
When you pray, do not babble on as the Gentiles do. They imagine they will be heard because of their many words.
Do not imitate them. Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
This, then, is how you are to pray: 'Our Father in the heavens, let your name be treated as holy,
let your kingdom come, let your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today our bread for the coming day.
Release us from our debts, as we also have released those who owe us.
Do not lead us into testing, but rescue us from the evil one.'
If you forgive people their failures, your heavenly Father will forgive you too.
But if you do not forgive people, your Father will not forgive your failures either.
When you fast, do not put on a gloomy face as the hypocrites do. They make their faces unrecognisable so that people will see that they are fasting. Amen, I tell you: they have been paid in full.
But when you fast, oil your head and wash your face,
so that it is not people who see you fasting but your Father in the hidden place. Your Father, who sees what is hidden, will pay you back.
Do not pile up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moths and corrosion eat them away and thieves dig through and steal.
Pile up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moths nor corrosion eat them away and thieves do not dig through and steal.
For your heart will be wherever your treasure is.
The eye is the lamp of the body. So if your eye is generous, your whole body will be bright.
But if your eye is stingy, your whole body will be dark. And if the light inside you is darkness, how deep that darkness is.
No one can be a slave to two masters. Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will stick to one and look down on the other. You cannot be slaves to God and to Mammon.
That is why I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will put on. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothes?
Look at the wild birds. They do not sow, they do not harvest, they do not store food in barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth far more than they are?
Which of you, by being anxious, can add one cubit to his span of life?
And why be anxious about clothes? Learn from the wildflowers, how they grow. They do not labour or spin,
yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his splendour was never dressed like one of these.
If God dresses the grass in the field like this, grass that is alive today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, will he not do much more for you, you of little faith?
So do not be anxious and ask, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we put on?'
The nations chase after all of this, and your heavenly Father knows that you need all of it.
Seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all of this will be given to you as well.
So do not be anxious about tomorrow. Tomorrow will be anxious about itself. Each day has trouble enough."
Do not pass judgement, so that judgement will not be passed on you.
The verdict you give will be the verdict you receive, and the measure you use will be the measure used on you.
Why do you look at the splinter in your brother's eye and not notice the log in your own?
Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me pull the splinter out of your eye,' when the log is in your own eye?
You hypocrite, first pull the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to pull the splinter out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to the dogs, and do not throw your pearls in front of the pigs, or they will trample them and turn round and tear you to pieces.
Keep on asking and it will be given to you. Keep on searching and you will find. Keep on knocking and it will be opened for you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who searches finds, and for the one who knocks it will be opened.
Which of you, when his son asks for bread, will hand him a stone?
Or when he asks for a fish, will hand him a snake?
If you, evil as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him.
So whatever you want people to do for you, do the same for them. This is the Law and the Prophets.
Go in through the narrow gate. The gate is wide and the road easy that leads to destruction, and many are going in through it.
But the gate is narrow and the road squeezed that leads to life, and few are finding it.
Watch out for the false prophets. They come to you dressed as sheep, but inside they are ravenous wolves.
You will recognise them by their fruit. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
So every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a rotten tree cannot bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So then, you will recognise them by their fruit.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father in the heavens.
Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, drive out demons in your name, and perform many mighty acts in your name?'
Then I will tell them openly, 'I never knew you. Leave me, you workers of lawlessness.'
So everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice will be like a sensible man who built his house on the rock.
The rain came down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and hit that house, and it did not fall, because it had its foundation on the rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
The rain came down, the rivers rose, the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell, and its fall was great.
When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching,
for he taught them like someone with authority, and not like their scribes.
When he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
A man with a skin disease approached, knelt in front of him and said, "Lord, if you want to, you can cleanse me."
Jesus reached out, touched him and said, "I want to. Be cleansed." Immediately the man's skin was cleansed of the disease.
Jesus said to him, "Be careful not to tell anyone. Go and show yourself to the priest, and bring the offering that Moses laid down, as evidence for them."
When he entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him and begged him,
"Lord, my servant is lying paralysed at home, in terrible pain."
He said to him, "I will come and heal him."
The centurion replied, "Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof. Only say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I am a man placed under authority myself, with soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come,' and he comes. And I tell my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
Jesus was astonished when he heard this. He said to those following him, "Amen, I tell you, I have not found faith like this in anyone in Israel.
I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
while the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth."
Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go. Let it be done for you as you have believed." And the servant was healed at that very hour.
When Jesus came into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began to serve him.
